Popol Wuj: Book of Counsel; the Council Book

Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij-Ancestral Account

This is the root of the Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij; here in this place known as Kʼicheʼ by name.

Here we shall inscribe it; here we shall implant it as that which is known to all as the Ancient Word; the Ancestral Account-Ojer Tzij.

This then is its being seeded; its being sown; its being rooted here at the origin; here at the beginning of its being told as that which reveals all that was done in the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom by the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ.

Here we shall bring forth its being shown-ukʼutunisaxik; its being revealed-uqʼalajobʼisaxik; and its being told-utzijoxikʼ as that which is known as the Sowing, the Dawning; Ewaxibʼal, Saqiribʼal; the Sowing, the Dawning of Life that reveals all that was hidden in the Shadows-Ewaxibʼal to be brought forth; to be revealed in the Light-Saqiribʼal by those who are known; by those who are named:

as they are known in the Kʼicheʼ Language; in the Kʼicheʼ Word; pa Kʼicheʼ Tzij as the Ancient Word is known; as the Ancestral Account is written.

This, then, was when they gave a full account of everything that was done in the Perfection of Existence; in the Perfection of Being; in the Perfection of the Word; in the Perfection of Way as they are known: Saqil Kʼolem, Saqil Tzij.

Here we shall write it out in these days, in these times that are spoken of as the Word of God-Uchʼabʼal Dios; the Word of God known and named as the next Age; the next Era of Christendom-Christianoil chik as the Sun of Christianity is named; as the Age of Christianity is known.

We shall bring it forth in the Perfection of Being, in the Perfection of the Word-Saqil Kʼolem, Saqil Tzij, in this place, in these times, for no longer can we look upon Precious Painted Picture Books of Counsel-Saq Ilbʼal re Popol Wuj to ponder their Sacred Pictorial Histories that came from Beside the Sea known as Ilbʼal Saq petenaq Chʼaqa Palo.

We shall just bring it forth here in writing because there is no longer a place to see Our Ancient Story; Our Ancestral Account that was once shown to be seen in the Painted Pictographic Histories known as the Ilbʼal; for those Pictorial Histories that came from Beside the Sea-Ilbʼal Saq petenaq Chʼaqa Palo no longer exist.

For our Painted Pictorial Histories-Ilbʼal with their ancient writing and painted pictures that were formed and shaped on the Pounded-Poj Paper-Wuj of the Wild Fig Tree-Poj no longer exist.

body:
THIS, THEN, IS ITS NARRATION; here, then, is its recitation: all is in suspense; all is calm; all is at rest; silent is it all; motionless; immobile; not a murmur; no hum; nothing churns; nothing ripples; nothing moves for all is serene stillness as silence echoes silence through the still calm quiet of the vast vacant void; no motion, no movement; not a sigh, nothing yet stirs, not a whir; nothing there to make a sound to rebound around the vacuous vault of the empty, empty Sky-Kaj.

Kʼakatzʼininoq-suspense; kʼakachamamoq-calm; kʼakatzʼinonik-rest; kʼasilanik-silence; kʼakalolinik-murmur-hum; katolona-empty, vacant, void, vacuous; I write this so that you might receive as sense of the sound of calm quiet silence in this incantation of the motionless murmur of the vacuous vault of the vast vacant void of the still quietude of a silent solitary Sky.

Here, then, is the First Word; the First Speech-Nabʼe Tzij; Nabʼe Uchan when it was first spoken; when it was first said there was not yet a single human, not yet was there a single being since there was nothing yet named; nothing yet known.

For there was not yet One Person-Jun Winaq;

Nor was there yet a being that was named as:

One Animal-Jun Chikop

Bird-Tzʼikin

Fish-Kar

Crab-Tap

Tree-Cheʼ

Rock-Abʼaj-Stone

Cave-Jul-Hole

Ravine-Siwan-Canyon

Grassland-Kʼim-Thatch

Forest-Kʼichelaj-Place of the Many Trees

Just all alone is the Sky; the Face of the Earth cannot be seen for the Face of the Earth has yet to be revealed.

There, all alone, is the still silent Sea; settled, calm and quiet; it alone is wombed over by the vast, vacant void of the empty vault of Sky; separate are the two who are pooled together, a perfect reflection of the One over the Other; the Two seen as just One-xa Jun; a mirrored void of vacant Sky reflected in the shinny shimmer of the silent solitary Sea.

The serene, silent Sky floats upon the placid, pool of Sea; its silent stillness echoes in the emptiness of reflected quiet; the ʼOne revealsʼ the ʼOtherʼ in the mirror Sky; on the mirror Sea.

body:
Nothing yet is there to be gathered together; nothing yet there to sound out; not-a-thing to rise-up; nothing to move around; nothing to move about, for everything is at rest; everything held in place; for there is just nothing there to stand-up; just nothing at all to climb-up; and out; and about.

There is just nothing there that might come to be that which might shoot-up to sprout-out; for there is just nothing there at all that might straighten-up to stand-out: xa ma kʼo wi naki laʼ kʼolik yakalik.

Just pooled Water; just the flat Sea; just they alone are pooled and placid; calm and collected; for all that might exist has yet to come into being; for that which might be has yet to come into existence; for all that might be has simply not yet come into being.

Just calm quiet; just still silence is all there is in the nocturnal darkness; there in the dark; there in the night; there in the darkness of night where all is nocturnal silence; there where all is quiet darkness in the silent dark of night.

They are there; for there they are; in the darkness; in the night.

They who are there are those who are all alone yet together; together as one.

All alone are they who are those who are known as:

Former, Shaper-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol;

Sovereign Plumed Serpent-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz;

Bearer, Begetter-Alom, Kʼajolom;

It is they who are those who are there in the shimmering shine of the sparkling light of the jade green waters; hidden yet there is he who is enveloped in the glittering glint of the gleaming light-saqtetoj the emanates from the sacred turquoise bundle of precious quetzal feathers and lovely blue cotinga plumage.

Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is there with Tzʼaqol-Bʼitol; Alom-Kʼajolom; Former-Shaper; Bearer-Begetter; there they are just out of view enveloped in jade feathers; bundled in turquoise plumage; awash in the sparkling iridescent blue-green waters that shimmer as they shine in the emerald green Sea that glistens as it glimmers as it glitters there in the blue-black darkness of the Sky; there cloaked in the mantel of calm quiet; there in the dark womb of night are they in the Water-Sky.

body:
There they are; they are there amidst the primordial waters where starlight sparkles in the starlit night that shines as it shivers silver slivers of scintillating light that shimmers as it shines bright at mid-night in the glittering waters that glisten as they glimmer; glint as they gleam; flash as they flicker; shake as they shiver to then quake and quiver all-about the Sacred Bundle of his Majesty, Lord Quetzalcoatl; Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; Sovereign Plumed Serpent who now is envelop, enclosed, encased in an emerald cloak that flutters as it floats like cypress bows that ripple in the breeze to cover the Precious Twin Quetzalcoatl in a plumed mantel of jade serpents; wrapped in the soft embrace of the feathery fluff of fine florescent feathers; twinned and coupled; paired and doubled; complementary and complete they gather to greet one-an-other as divine twins who are bundled and bound together in the precious plumage of the Resplendent Quetzal-Qʼuqʼ and Lovely Blue Cotinga-Raxon; emerald green, turquoise blue as two become one in an ancient ancestral embrace that envelops as it embodies the everlasting life of the jade green seed; lifeʼs eternal return;  deathʼs undying renewal.

This is the way Qʼuqʼkumatz received his name Quetzalcoatl which was bestowed upon him because of this Sacred Bundle of Quetzal Feathers preciously twinned with Lovely Blue Cotinga Plumage; perfect complements of one-an-other.

It is this ʼsacred bundle of feathersʼ that bears within its embrace the essence of creation as the resplendent jade green jewel of the maize kernel; the luminous blue mask of watery wet light; emerald reed, the jade seed, the turquoise bead that will soon to be brought forth from the shadowy darkness and into the resplendent light of the Soil, Sky, and Sea; Earth, Air, and Water; the dusty-dirt of the earth, the rich resinous green Cypress bows; Earth-Sky; Water-Sky; Sea-Earth; Sky-Earth paired with one another just as the iridescent green, red, and white Feathers of the Resplendent Quetzal that complements golden amber, earthen brown, and obsidian black of Rattlesnakeʼs Serpent Scales.

body:
These Two beings of Earth and Sea; Sky and Earth; Sky and Sea form as they shape this Precious Twin of blue and green; turquoise and jade; gold and obsidian; silver and corral red; emerald and gold forms and shapes that are molded and modeled together to bring forth the Feathered Serpent; the Plumed Serpent; Quetzalcoatl; Qʼuqʼ-Kumatz whose eternal return will never come too early; whose rising as the Morning Star will never come too late.

Quetzalcoatl is a Creator Deity who also destroys as Heart of the Lake-Sea-Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo just as his Divine Twin is a Destroyer who also creates as the One-Jun known as the Smoking Mirror-Tezcatlipoca-the One-Footed-One-Jun Raqan-Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj spoken of here as Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja. The Popol Wuj is their sacred narrative of Creation and Destruction through Forming and Shaping.

Great Thinkers-E Nimaq Etaʼmanel-Great Knowers were they, great was their intelligence; great too, was their imagination as the Great Seers-E nimaq AjNaʼoj that they were; Seers who saw all there was to be seen; Sages-AjNaʼoj who knew all there was to be known.

For truly their sagacious seeing as Great Seers-E Nimaq Etaʼmanel and their great knowing as Genius Knowers gave them their sight to see all that could be seen as well as the intelligence of their imagination to know all that could be known by seeing all there was to be seen.

So then just the Sky-Kaj alone was there; and so too was the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj which is the name of their Deity, their Divinity known as Kabʼawil, as it is said; as it is spoken. He who is the One-Jun known; he who is the One-Jun named as: Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Heart of the Sky; their Deity; their Divinity; their Kabʼawil.

This then was when his Word-Tzij came together here where Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz-Sovereign Plumed Serpent was in the darkness-chi qʼequmal; was in the night-chi aqʼabʼal.

This was when Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj  spoke with Sovereign Plumed Serpent-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz, when they brought their Word together in Council; when they gathered together their thoughts; when they pondered, when they wondered; considerate was their contemplation of their thoughts.

body:
Concerned then were they when they contemplated their imagination; when they consulted their thinking of thoughts; there, where they came together as One in deliberation; there in the dark; there in the night when they found one another in the nocturnal darkness.

These are those who are known as Heart of the Sky-Ukʼux Kaj; Heart of the Lake-Sea-Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo; these are those who are named Jun Raqan Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo.

And so then it was made clear to them, just as it was revealed to them; when their hearts were made one with the other amidst the light; when they took council together with one-an-other, the two of them there in the Dark; the two of them there in the Night; in the Water, in the Light; when their two minds became Just One: Xa Jun.

This then was when the sprouting forth of people-winaq-humans was revealed to them; and so too was seen by them just how those humans-winaq would be brought forth into being as people who would come to populate the Face of the Earth.

They knew as they thought; just as they saw as they imagined the way in which their creation would be brought forth through the clarity of their thinking.

They knew as they thought; just as they saw as they imagined the way in which their creation would be brought forth through the ingenuity of their imagination with which and through which they were to bring human life-kʼaslem to fruition by bringing forth the creation of human beings-winaqirem to completion.

For it was they, the two Kabʼawil known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj; named Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz who came to an accord as their hearts became one there before the light of dawn-ta xkikʼuxlaj kibʼ xeʼ wi saq.

This was when the thought of their creation of humanity appeared them that was a clear image of the generation of life that was revealed to them through the genius of their imagination.

The image that was revealed to them through the genius of their imagination was that which told them, as it showed them, just how they would bring about the birth of life that would lead to their creation of humanity: utzʼuquxik kʼaslem, winaqirem!

This was the thought that was the image that was in truth a vision of their imagination that showed them, as it told them, just how they would bring about the sprouting out of life that would lead to the sprouting forth of all being that would come to fruition through the sprouting forth of humanity!

This was when creation was revealed to them there in the light so that they came to see it clearly as the formation of life-kʼaslem and the generation of the human condition-winaqirem.

This was when their nawal genius revealed to them a revelation that appeared to them in their imagination as clear as a thought could be. This thought that appeared to them showed them just exactly how to bring forth life that would lead to the sprouting-forth of human beings; human beings that would lead to the sprouting forth of  human lineages that would lead to the creation, formation, and generation of the human condition with all of its needs and desires.

This was when their hearts where made one through their genius thinking-xkinaʼojij; their hearts were made one  through their creative imagination-xkinaʼojij to reveal just how to bring about sprouting-forth of life to bring about the formation and generation of the trees and vines-utzʼuqik, uwinaqirik cheʼ, kʼaʼm.

This was made known to them through their nawal genius as the sprouting-forth of life that would lead to the creation of human beings whose human condition would come to fruition through the generation of the human lineage with its peopling and populating the face of the earth-utzʼuquxik kʼaslem, winaqirem.

It is there, in the darkness; there, in the night, when and where it was done by Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja-the One Footed One, the One Legged One who was the First-Nabʼe of the Three Voices of Thunder-Lightning-Kaqulja who was known as the roar of the storm; cry of the water; call of the rain: Kaquljaʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The first of the three forms of Thunder and Lightning that called down rain was known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja. This was the first of the three shapes taken by Heart of the Sky that was the first form that Thunder and Lightening took as the first shape of the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj; so that the first name of the Nabʼey-First of Thunderers-Tojojila taken by Heart of the Sky was that which was known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

This then was when the Earth was made to sprout forth by them; those known to us as Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo. Just their word alone caused it to sprout forth into being.

To bring forth the Earth, they said: “EARTH!”

Chiwinaqir Ulew: “ULEW!” Xecha!ʼ

Immediately, it sprouted out-winaqirik; instantly, like a cloud, like the mist, it blew-up-pupujeʼik; it just erupted; into the Sky it rose; it stood straight-up; and there it went when it climbed up and up; it just kept going, rising up into the Sky.

This was when it emerged out of the water; immediately it rose up; just like that a Great Mountain was created as it was caused to rise-up and out of the water to climb-up into the Sky.

It was just their Nawal-xa Nawal; it was just their magical powers of transformation-xa Nawal; it was just their giving of sacrifice-xa Pus that made it so.

Truly, it was their way of thinking upon the ʼsprouting forth-xwinaqirikʼ of the Earth the way they did that made it so.

It was just their transformative genius and its creative imagination alone that conceived of their nawal creation as that which would be brought forth to completion; brought forth to fruition as the Forming, as the Shaping; as the Molding, as the Modeling of the Mountain-Plain; Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj.

All of the sudden, just like that, the Face of the Earth was covered with cypress groves; blanketed with pine groves-ukisisil, upachajil-for cypress groves and pine groves sprouted forth all across the mountainside; a mantle of cypress cloaked the mountain just as a mantel of pine blanketed of the Mountain-Plain; Juyub, Taqʼaj.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Thus this Great Mountain was enveloped in Great Many Trees then when it was blanketed with a mantel of Cypress Groves-Kisisil of the Maize Lord Quetzalcoatl; when it was cloaked with a mantel of Torch Pine Groves-Pachajil of Tojil-the Sun Deity-Lord Torch-Lord Lightning-Bolt. Cypress Trees and Torch-Pine Trees formed and shaped the green groves of Cypress and Pine that covered the Face of the Earth with a thick mantel of verdure that cloaked the mountainside with resplendent emerald and jade green perfection. In this way the two Kabʼawil were made present in the form of their Nawal Transforms leaving the Sky-Earth prepared for the forming and shaping of the Providers and Sustainers.

So, then indeed it was Qʼuqʼkumatz who was made content and his contentment called upon him to speak with Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj:

“Is it not good that you have come, you Ukʼuʼx Kaj; you Jun Raqan; and you Chʼipi Kaqulja; and you Raxa Kaqulja?”

“Our Forming, our Shaping has turned out well,” they replied.

And so it did; their Forming and their Shaping did turn out well. First, then was the Earth made to arise as the Mountain-Plain so that then next the natural course of the water found its way down through the mountainside to form the rivers and streams that wound their way down the Great Mountain when it appeared.

Thus the Earth was created-uwinaqirik when it was made to sprout-up and out-xwinaqirik of the Water by Heart of the Sky, Heart of the Earth; Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew as they are known.

They were the first to imagine it so: Sky was made to exist. Earth too was made to exist to then be placed in the Water.

But let us bring forth two alternative translation of this secret sacred mythic language to bring forth the idea that come from this sacred text that defies translation in every way.

They were the first to think upon it like this: Sky was sidled up to one side; Earth was sidled up to the other side to then be placed amongst the Waters.

They were the first to imagine it like this: Sky was brought forth into being; Earth too was brought forth to then be placed amidst the Water.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They were the first to think upon it like this: Sky was made; Earth too was made to then be set within the Water.

These then where their thoughts; this then was their thinking when they considered their work, their work of creation; when they wondered, when they pondered all they had done; when they thought about all they had brought to completion; when they contemplated all they had done to bring their work to conclusion.

This then is how they finished their work bringing forth the Sky-Earth.

The Forming, the Shaping; the Molding, the Modeling of the Ancient

Animal Ancestor by the Former, the Shaper; the Molder, the Modeler

This then was when they thought upon their bringing forth of the Wild Animals of the Mountain Wilderness-Uchikopil Juyubʼ when they imagined; when they envisioned populating the mountainside with Animals; when they thought upon their bringing forth of the Forest Guardians-Chajal re Kʼichelaj; when they considered and contemplated their populating of the Forest with the Keepers and Care-takers of the Mountain Wilderness-Uwinaqil Juyubʼ.

This was when they imagined the forest beings; when they thought upon all the animals of the mountains, the guardians of the forest, in this, their first attempt to populate the mountainside with animals; in this, their first attempt to populate the wilderness with guardians of the forest; caretakers of the wilderness who they imagined to be the many animals that would come to people the wild mountain-plain; animals who would come to populate the mountain wilderness: uchikopil juyubʼ, chajal re kiʼchelaj ronojel uwinaqil juyubʼ.

Before long their imaginative thinking inspired their nawal genius so that it brought forth images of animal protectors who as animal guardians would come to reside among the Trees and Vines; these would be those who they imagined would come to inhabit the many trees of the forest there upon the Mountain-Plain known as the Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj. This then is how these protectors of the mountain were named:

The Deer; ri Kiej

Bird; Tzʼikin

Puma; Koj

Jaguar; Bʼalam

Serpents; Kumatz

Rattlesnake; Sochoj

Bushmaster; Kanti as well all the other

Protectors of the Vines; Chajal Kʼaʼm

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These would be the Guardians of the Forest-Chajal re Kiʼchelaj-Guardians of the Wild Mountain Places-Juyubʼal as well as the Valleys and Plains-Taqʼajal. It was then that the Bearer-Begetter-Alom, Kʼajolom spoke:

“Should there just a din of silence; should their only be a deafening quiet under the Trees and Vines? If so, then it would be best that they have Guardians-Chajal to watch over them!” said the Mother-Fathers; Alom, Kʼajolom.

“Should there be such a din of silence; nothing more than this tranquil rustling of savage serene quiet; that incessant sort of horrendous hush in the bush amongst the brush; just the relentless roar of stillness beneath the branches of the flowering vines and fruiting trees with all their spiny thorns and many stinging leaves; was this the only speech that would ever be spoken here on this Earth that had yet to be awoken?”

And so they imagined them ʼjust soʼ with hoofed feet and feathered wings; this then was when they spoke-up to then speak-out; their speech made it so, immediately these forest beings were brought forth there; instantly, just like that-jusukʼ-they were made to appear: Deer-Kej; Bird-Tzʼikin; the Four-Footed Ones, the Feathery Winged-Ones.

They instantly came into being there in the Mountains; there in the Canyons; down in the Ravine among the Trees and upon the Vines.

Then they were given their abode; the Deer, the Birds, they were given their homes:

“You, Deer, go down there by the river; go sleep in the ravines, in the canyons; there you shall live.”

“Here is where you shall be, in the grasslands, among the wild fruit trees; up in the branches; out on the vines; in the forest, this is where you will grow and multiply. On all four you will move about; on all four you will make your way; this is how it will be,” this is what was said to them; this is what they were told.

So then next, they chose the living places that would become their mountain abode; a place in the valley to build the homes of the Small Birds; Big Birds:

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“You, you Birds, get on up in the trees; there up above in the branches; up, up, on top of the vines, make your nests; build your homes. There, there is where you will multiply to become many. There, there is where you will grow and increase; there on the limbs, there on the branches of the trees; out on the vines is where you will be,” this is what they were told when they were spoken to; the Deer, the Birds; the Four-Footed Ones and those of the Feathered-Wings.

Then they did what was theirs to do; while being given their sleeping places; their burrows; their dens; gathering what was there to make their dwellings, to fashion their houses; to build their homes.

There in their forest they went to live; there in the wilderness is where they fashioned their nests, dens, and lairs; some slept together, others slept alone; some lived with one another, others lived on their own.

This was the way the Animals of the Wilderness; Animals of the Earth were each given a home by Alom, Kʼajolom-Bearer, Begetter as they are known.

Alom, Kʼajolom-Bearer, Begetter

Alom, Kʼajolom were those who were the Mother of Offspring; those who were the Father of Offspring; Giver of Girls; Giver of Boys; Alom, Kʼajolom; Maker of Sprouts; Maker of Seeds; Alom-Maker of Sprouts-Conceiver of Children; Bearer of Children; Kʼajolom-Maker of Skull-Seeds known as ʼEngenderer or Sons-Kʼajolom; Begetter of Sons.

And so it was that they, Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom completed their work of bringing forth the Deer, the Birds; the Four-Footed Ones, those of the Feathery Wings as they are named; as they are called; when they are invoked by name; the name that names them until this very day: Kej, Tzʼikin; Deer, Bird.

When their work was complete; when their work was finished the Former, the Shaper; Bearer, Begetter-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom called upon the Deer and the Birds to do what they were Formed to do; what they were Shaped to do which was to invoke their Former; which was to invoke their Shaper; ʼTheyʼ who Formed were the Formers just as ʼTheyʼ who were Shaped were ʼThoseʼ who were the Shapers.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The Former-Tzʼaqol, the Shaper-Bʼitol were those who Formed; were those who Shaped those who were the Formed Ones; those who were the Shaped Ones; AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit. Now Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom wanted to be remembered by being invoked by those they had Formed; they wanted to be remembered by those they had Shaped.

Now those who were the Former, Shaper; Mother, Father; Bearer, Begetter wished only to hear, in order to feel, their ʼnames being namedʼ by the Animals who they created; these who were the Deer-Kej; Bird-Tzʼikin who were those that were called up to  ʼname the namesʼ  of their Former, their Shaper; Bearer, Begetter-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom. And so they ordered the Animal People to do just this.

This then was when they spoke to the Deer-Kej, the Birds-Tzʼikin; they were spoken to by Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom:

“Speak out! Call out! Donʼt just squawk. Donʼt just warble. Invoke us: each one of you one by one; according to your class, your kind; according to your group, your order; go ahead now just Name our Names!”

This is what was said to them:

ri Kej-the Deer

Tzʼikin-Birds

Koj-Puma

Bʼalam-Jaguar

Kumatz-Serpent

“Name then our names; show us reverence, show us respect; invoke us, name us: We, your Mother; We, your Father-Oj Ichuch; Oj Iqajaw!”

“Go ahead; get right to it; you can do it; nowʼs the time for you to prove it! Go ahead, just do it!”

“Go ahead, just do what youʼve been asked to do, show us regard, show us respect; name our names just like this:”

Jun Raqan, Chʼipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja

Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew

Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol

Alom, Kʼajolom

“Speak forth, speak out! Kixchaʼwoq!”

“Invoke us; remember us; revere us; show us regard; show us respect; worship us in our way; this is all we ask you to say; just give us thanks; just show us praise; Kojiqʼijila!”

“Go ahead, just do it: Name our Names!” they were ordered, when they were spoken to; Xeʼuchaʼxik.

They couldnʼt do it; they could not speak like their Former, Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol asked of them; they just mimicked the sound and speech of others.

body:
And so it was that when they began to speak they just squawked and screeched instead of making proper speech they just shrieked; they just whined, they just whimpered; they just chittered, they just chattered; they just howled and yowled when they wanted growl; they just kept up their shrill squeaking and squawking acting as if they were really talking; they could only moan and groan all alone instead of talking amongst one another as was desired by their Mother-Father; so now it was known, being clearly shown that the Animals could not and would not speak like their Mother-Father: Alom, Kʼajolom.

The Animals could not talk amongst one another as they were asked to do: to speak a common language between one another that sound true; to speak as a group; as class; as an order; as a single kind that could communicate together with one another to then ʼName the Namesʼ of those who formed and shaped them; their Former, their Shaper.

For it was no longer clear as to the nature of the language they spoke since each one of them cried out as they called out in different ways; each one with their own form of speech that was as difficult to speak as it was to repeat.

The expression, the character, the nature of their language never came out clearly. Each one of them cried out in different ways; each according to their kind; all according to their group; each speaking the speech that was theirs and theirs alone.

When Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol heard them, they knew their work had not turned out good, for the Animals, as hard as they tried, could not speak with one another as their creators wished they would and most definitely thought there should.

So Former, Shaper talked it over together as they spoke with one-an-other to then say what they said:

“The Naming of our Names by the formed beings we formed; by the shaped beings we shaped did not turn out well; this is just not right just as it is just no good,” said Alom, Kʼajolom speaking together as companions of one-an-other; chi kibʼil kibʼ.

body:
So, then, they said: “You must be transformed; you must be transfigured, you did not turn out the way we imagined you to be;  as those who speak together in one form of speech. You cannot speak one language together; you cannot speak with one another; like we speak as your Father, your Mother; so why try anymore, why even bother.”

“Now you have forced us to bring you down; we must change our word; we must change what we said about the way you are to live in the forest. We must change your life ways, we must change your sustenance, your sleeping places, your homes, yours lairs; we must change the very living spaces we gave to you as your dwelling place; your earthly abode; your residence here in the world on the Face of the Earth,” they were told.

“All that is yours will come from the canyons and the ravines and from the forest because you could not revere us through the remembrance Our Days,” they said.

“Nor could you worship us by showing us praise through the veneration and reverence that comes with the sacred act of ʼNaming our Namesʼ as you were created to do,” they added.

“You could not invoke us, nor summons us by calling upon us as we formed and shaped you to do.”

“There are those who will come to do what we ask of them; those who will show us reverence through the orderly practice of our orderly ancestral ways; the orderly naming of our names in perfectly ordered sacred ways by giving us praise in ancestral ways that keep the count of our numbered and named days,” said the Bearer, spoke the Begetter; Alom, Kʼajolom.

“For there will be those who will provide for us with sacrificial offerings; offerings sacrificed to us that will provide and sustain us with sacred sustenance.”

“So just bear your fate; this shall be your destiny for the rest of your days: let your flesh be eaten!”

“Ta chuxoq! May it come to pass! Let it be so! This, then, is your beneficial burden, your ancestral debt, your divine duty, your sacred service to all those who will live from your death to thrive from your flesh,” as it was said so they were told.

body:
This then was when the Small Animals, the Big Animals were instructed as to what was their fate when they were given counsel as to what their destiny was here on the Face of the Earth.

This then was when they met their defeat; when their flesh became the meat to feed the hunger and appetite of those who would come to eat them as sweet sort of treat.

This was the ancestral destiny; the divine burden of the Animal People here on the Face of the Earth where the fate of the flesh of Small Animals and the fate of flesh of Big Animals was to be hunted and killed to be eaten as meat; meat to be eaten as the sacred sustenance of other animals here on the Face of the Earth; Chuwach Ulew.

SO IT WAS THEN THAT ANOTHER EFFORT WAS MADE to bring forth the Formed People, the Shaped People-Winaq Tzʼaq, Winaq Bʼit;  by the Former, Shaper;  Bearer, Begetter-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom.

“Let us just try again; let us make another attempt; for is not the Sowing, the Dawning soon upon us?” “Xa kʼu tija chik mixyopij rawexik, usaqirik?”

“Let us make a Formed Being that provides for us; let us make a Shaped Being that sustains us; one who nourishes us; one who nurtures us as Our Provider, as Our Sustainer; those spoken of as a Feeder, those named as a Maintainer Tzuqul, Kʼool as they shall be known.”

“If not, then who; who will Name our Names through our invocation; who then will remember us through the remembrance of our ways here upon the Face of the Earth?”

“Did we not already try with our First Forming, with our First Shaping? Did we not already complete our Molding and Modeling of those who would worship us by being and becoming those who would come forth to count and keep our Divine Days; those who would venerate us in honorable, benevolent ways; those who would regard and respect us by showing us thanks and praise as our Day-Keepers; those who would become our Keeper and Counter of Days-qaqʼijiloxik?”

body:
“Did we not already finish the work of ʼCrafting and Creatingʼ those who would become our Prayer-makers and Worshippers to bring about Our Glorification before our Throne and its Altar Place where we were to receive our adoration; our adulation; our worship and our admiration-qaqʼalajxik”

“Did we not already bring forth those who would glorify and worship us with their adoration and glorification of us as our Prayer-Makers and Worshippers who would invoke us and remember us through showing us praise and glory-qaqʼalajxik in ancestral ways through their worship and praise of us by Keeping the Sacred Count of Our Sacred Days in sacred, sacrificial ways?”

“Did we not already attempt to make an Obedient One-AjNim who was a Humble One-AjXobʼ who was a Respectful One-AjXobʼ who was a Devout One-AjNim who would be those known as Our Provider; Our Sustainer those named: Tzuqul; Kʼool,” they cried as they wept.

“So then, shall we not try again?”

“Let us just try again then to form and shape Obedient Beings-AjNim who are Humble Beings-AjXobʼ. Let us mold and model Respectful Beings who are Dutiful Beings; Devoted and Dedicated beings; Righteous and Respectful Beings; who will provide for us as our Providers; who will sustain us as our Sustainers: AjNim, AjXobʼ; Tzuqul, Kʼool.

This then was when they formed his body from Ulew-Earth. His flesh was made of mud-xoqʼol for it was mud that was the clay-xoqʼol that they molded and modeled the flesh-utyoʼjil of the body of this being formed from Earth-Ulew; this creature created from clay-xoqʼol; this man made of mud-xoqʼol.

So then it didnʼt look so good; Ma kʼu utz xkilo

So then they didnʼt like the way it looked; Ma kʼu utz xkilo

So then they didnʼt look upon it with contentment; Ma kʼu utz xkilo

Just lop-sided, deformed, incoherent, inconsistent; xa chi yojomanik

Just soft, spongy, squishy, squashy, without character; xa tzubʼulik

Just soggy, sopping wet, saturated, it could not move; xa nebʼelik

Just so weak, without strength, limp, it just crumbled; xa lubʼanik

Just one to come undone, it fell apart, it fell to pieces, it fell over; xa wulanik

And it just dissolved in water when it got wet; xa pu chiʼumarik

body:
And so it just melted away; it became soft; it was weak; xa pu chiʼumarik

His head was not round so it drooped to one-side; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom

His head sagged so that he couldnʼt hold it up; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom

Not being round his skull would never roll; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom

His head could not swivel around; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom

He could not turn his head around; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom

He could not spin his head about; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom

Just in one direction could he face; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach

He could just look in one direction; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach

Just lop-sided was his twisted face; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach

He just faced in one direction; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach

His face was just immovable; fixed; motionless; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach

His face was stationary; still; stiff; unmoving: Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach

He could just walk in one direction since he could only see in one direction!

Just blanketed was his vision; Xa kuʼl uwach

Just covered-up was his sight; Xa kuʼl uwach

Just veiled was his vision; Xa kuʼl uwach

He could not see behind him; Mawi chi mukun chirij

He couldnʼt see what was coming; Mawi chi mukun chirij

He couldnʼt see what was coming up from behind; Mawi chi mukun chirij

He couldnʼt look back; Mawi chi mukun chirij

Chi chʼaw nabʼe maja bʼi unaʼoj; xa jusukʼ chiʼumar pa jaʼ.

He spoke at first but he had no genius; just right away he dissolved in water.

He spoke at first but without intelligence; he just crumbled before falling to apart when he was placed in the water.

He could speak in the beginning but was unable to make himself understood for he had no insight; he just instantly softened up before melting away in the water.

At first he communicated but without understanding; he just immediately came undone; to quickly dissolve in the water.

He spoke at first but without insight; he just immediately disintegrated in the water!

Chi chʼaw nabʼe maja bʼi unaʼoj; xa jusukʼ chiʼumar pa jaʼ.

“Heʼs not hard; he will not endure!” said the Former; said the Shaper.

“Mawi Ko!” xechaʼ chi ku ri AjTzʼaq; AjBʼit.

“He will never last; he just isnʼt strong enough,” said Former, said Shaper.

body:
“It is just a sign of what not to do; itʼs a warning of further failures that lie up ahead; it is just an indication of whatʼs to come! So be it!”

“It is just a mistake; he canʼt even walk; it is best he never be allowed to multiply to become a great many more mistakes.”

“This man made of mud; this crafted clay creature; this fallen, failed, flawed formation formed from the flesh of earth is just no good.”

“It is just been a test; itʼs just been another attempt of our ʼforming and shapingʼ that has come to a bad end; itʼs just another failure, another flawed work of crafting creation; itʼs a real flop.”

“It is just a mistake; itʼs just an omen is what it is; just a sign; a premonition: xa labʼeq! So be it! We will just have to think it over again,” they said.

This then was when they destroyed him; this is when they threw him down; when they laid him low; his Molders; his Modelers; they just took their clay creation up in their hands and brought him crashing down to the ground. This was when they smashed their failed formation to pieces on the Earth below!

It was over; they could begin again. And they did by asking:

“What should we do now? ¿Jupa cha ki chiqabʼano?”

A Third Try; A Third Attempt; A Third Endeavor;

To Carve Obedient Ones-AjNim; to Create Respectful Ones-AjXobʼ

To Form the Providers-Tzuqul; to Shape the Sustainers-Kʼool

This then was when they began again; when they wondered; when they pondered; when they thought; when they contemplated upon what was to be done next to bring their work of forming to completion; to bring their work of shaping to conclusion.

“What shall we do to finish our work to form, our work to shape those who will name our names; those who will keep our days; those who will remember us in sacred ways?”

This is what they said when they thought on it again; when they imagined it just so; just so they could bring forth formed beings who were shaped beings who would worship them by giving them praise by keeping their days.

body:
This was what they said when they thought on it again; when they imagined it so they would see how to carve and create beings who would invoke then; so that they would know how to form and shape those who would remember them through ancestral ways of remembrance.

This then is when they thought on their ʼFormingʼ and on their ʼShapingʼ again so that their Providers; their Sustainers would be brought to completion; so that their Formation and their Creation would be brought to conclusion.

And so they went to the Diviners of Destiny; those who formed and shaped the golden seeds of maize and corral red beans of divination; those known and named: Xpiyakok, Xmuqane; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw; Grandfather Possum, Lord of the Dawn; Grandfather Coyote, Lord of the Night.

“Let us just speak with those who are Xpiyakok, Xmuqane; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw; let them make another attempt to see again what must be done to divine the destiny of our Forming and Shaping the Formed Ones, the Shaped Ones; to divine the fortune and fate of our Carving and Creating the Carved Ones, the Created Ones.”

“Letʼs just do what we must do to consult the count of Days; to consult the Ancient Ways; to consult the Forming of the Tzʼite Beans, to consult the Shaping of the Maize Seeds.”

“Let us take up that which is the casting of the Sacred Seeds of Sortilege; let us take up that which is the casting of the Divine Beans of Divination.”

“Which is to say: we must cast the consultation of beans; the divination of seeds to see what shape the forming takes; to see what form the shaping makes so that we can know the form our casting makes; to know the shape our divination takes.”

This then was when those who are known as: Xpiyakok, Xmuqane; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw cast and count the golden seeds of the Maize Tree-Ixim Cheʼ, the red beans of the Coral Tree-Tzʼite Tree, this is when they said:

“With kernels and beans let us cast our destiny; let us count-out our futureʼs fate so that we may see the form, so that we may see the shape of the ʼfaceʼ that our divination takes with the corral red beans of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree; with the golden yellow kernels of Maize Tree-Ixim Cheʼ.”

body:
This is what was said by those who are spoken of as the AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit; the Divine Ancestors of the Forming, the Divine Ancestors of the Shaping; known as the Former, known as the Shaper-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol when they spoke to the Ancestral Couple; the Ancestral Pair; the Ancient Ones-Nawal Winaq; Nawinaq-Ancestral Magicians as they are known and named: Xpiyakok, Xmuqane.

“Let us just speak with Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane; let us just consult with Jun AjPu Wuch, Jun AjPu Utiw-the Ancient Ones-the Ancestral Couple-the Primordial Pair; those who are Seers; those who are Knowers; they who are the Diviners; those who will know just what we must do to bring our Forming and Shaping to fruition.”

“Let us, let them make another attempt to see what there is to be seen through their sacred forming; to know what there is to be known through their sacred shaping.”

“Let us, let them make another attempt to bring forth their Divine Count of Days; the Formation of its Ancestral Ways to see in order to know what form their Sacred Count of Days takes.”

“Let us, let them form and shape their Divination to see what we seek to see; to know what we need to know; so that we come to see and know what we need to do to form and shape Our Forming; Our Shaping to Carve and Craft Our Creation of the Formed Ones; of the Shaped One; of the Carved Ones; of the Crafted Ones. Let it be done.”

“Let us; let them make another effort to bring forth their insight and imagination through their divination; through their counting and their shaping of the divine count and sacred shape of their divination.”

“Let us; let them mold and model their Ancestral Divination  to reveal what is to be known through their powers of revelation that comes through those who are the Diviners-AjQʼij-Day-Keepers; the Knowers-AjNaʼoj-Wise Ones; the Mid-Most Seers-e Nikʼ Wachinel-Sages, those who are known as the Grandmother of the Day, Grandmother of the Dawn-Ratiʼt Qʼij, Ratiʼt Saq as they are invoked by Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; as they are remembered by Alom, Kʼajolom.”

body:
Grandmother of the Day, Grandmother of the Dawn, Ratiʼt Qʼij, Ratiʼt Saq those who are the Diviners-AjQʼij; the Knowers-AjNaʼoj; the Mid-Most Seers-e Nikʼ Wachinel; those who are known and named the Keeper of Days: the Nawal Ones; the Sagacious Ones; the Knowers; the Seers; the Diviners are who they are.

Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane: the Ancestral Couple, the Primordial Pair Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw

Realize dear reader that a great deal of exoteric knowledge is provided here in these names that are introduced without any explanation. So let us introduce again these Nawal Winaq, these Magically Transforming Ancestors who take the form and shape of their Animal Companions, their Animal Souls, their Animal Guides, Spirit Guides of the Dead, of the Dawn, of the Dark, of the Night and its Darkness.

These are those from the Ancient Age of the Animal People where ʼanima-soul-psyche-ukʼuʼxʼ is the very ʼheart and soul and of the word ʼanima-animalʼ which we must develop a sense of if we are to understand how Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane work together as diviners to find out what to form and shape the next attempt of ʼpeopling and populatingʼ the Face of the Earth. For they work as a pair, one is the ʼpillar-raqanʼ and the other is the ʼformer and shaper of destinyʼ who scatters and shapes, counts and forms the seeds and beans of this ancient practice of divination the Maya have practiced since ʼtime immemorialʼ. The two Ancestral Diviners will be introduced and named as ʼGrandmothers of the Dawn, Grandmothers of the Lightʼ and it is they who divine through their ancient ancestral animal soul, animal spirit.

Xpiyakok is known as Junajpu Wuch, the Ancient Ancestral Animal Soul of the Dawn embodied by Junajpu Wuch translated as Old Man Possum-Junajpu Wuch who is a powerful Lord of the Dawn, Lord of the Underworld, for Xpiyakok, as you will come see, is already dead by the time the stories of his sons and grandsons begin. Wuch or Possum smells of the Land of the Dead and the Lords of the Dead.

body:
The Ancestors are the Dead and so it is the Dead Ancestors who provide and sustain their Descendants with Divinatory Knowledge through ʼday-dreaming insightsʼ and ʼnight-dreaming journeys of the soul, the anima, the animal soul-nawal or nagual or nahual-animal spirit of each and every Diviner and Day-Keeper, Prayer-Maker and Petitioner who works on behalf of their people and pueblo to find the path that must be taken to do what needs to be done to bring about creation or destruction.

These Animal Transforms, Animal Companions are known as Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw and spoken of here as Junajpu Wuch, the Ancient Ancestral One Grandfather Possum; Noble Lord and Grandfather of the Dawn: Junajpu Wuch. Whereas Ixmuqane is known to Kʼicheʼ Maya Day-Keepers and Prayer-Makers as Ix-Muq-Qʼanil, or She of the Buried Mazorca; She of the Buried Maize Seed whose womb is the womb of the earth where the maize seed is sown to sprout forth as the milpa in which the ʼmany sonsʼ come into existence as the Four Hundred Boys of the South, where the South is seen as the Place Thick with Abundance because of the Heat and Rain found their when the Sun moves to the South from May to November, the rainy season and growing season of maize. Ixmuqane, like many other Maize Mothers of the Ancient Americas is sacrificed and her body so that it may be buried and transformed into maize and squash, cacao and herb as well as many other fruits and vegetables. The important point to understand is that the Ancient Ancestors bodies become the sacred sustenance of their descendants.

body:
Ixmuqane is also known as Jun AjPu Utiw or Ancient One Grandmother Coyote; Ixmuqane as Jun AjPu Utiw come from the Ancient Ancestral Place of the Reeds spoken of as Jun AjPu, Ancient Ancestral Place Thick with Abundance, Ancient Ancestral Place Thick with Reeds; Ixmuqane in this section we are entering here is known as the Ancient Grandmother Diviner, Grandmother Coyote of the Dusk, Jun Ajpu Utiw is known as Ancient Ancestral Coyote Grandmother, Ruler and Authority of the Night, She feeds off of Death, she transforms as she wishes for she is the Trickster Deity Extraordinaire with Magical Powers of Transformation that when understood are at the very center of the Popol Wujʼs sacred narrative.

Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane as the Primordial Couple of Ancient Ancestral Trickster Diviners are those who know everything there is to know because they come from the Ancient Age, Ancient Sun of the Animal People and this is what makes them such powerful diviners. As the Primordial Couple or Ancient Ones they are rulers of the knowledge of divination that is given to those who see in the ʼdarkʼ and live in the ʼnightʼ while resting in the Light of Day when the Sunʼs power overtakes the powers of diviners who cannot ʼseeʼ when there is so much ʼlightʼ. The Ancient Word says, “Let us speak with them that they might speak through their divination to know what we most need to know.”  This is what is said of them.

It was there were they looked with their ancestral vision to know and reveal what was asked of them by those who sought to see what they saw with their powers of divination.

These were those who were the Mid-Most Seers-Nikʼ Wachinel whose vision saw what there was to see in order to know what there was to be known. What they saw and knew was then revealed as the knowledge they sought with their seeds and stones; with their beans and bones that formed and shaped their divination of all that could be seen to be known.

This is what they revealed to Jun Raqan and Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz when they were spoken to by the AjQʼij; AjBʼit; e NikʼWachinel.

body:
These are those who are known as:  AjQʼij-Day-Keepers; these are those who are the counters and keepers of the Sacred Days as well as those who reveal their revelation of destiny in Sacred Ways; these are those who are the seers and diviners of days that see and divine through their ancient ancestral powers of divination.

These are those known as: AjBʼit-the Former of Divination; the Shaper of Divination; those who form small mounds of seeds for the formation of divination; those who shape small mounds of beans for the creation of divination.

These are those who are known as e NikʼWachinel those who are the Mid-Most Seers of divinatory imagination that is seen to be known as the inner-most vision of the seeing and knowing in the Ancestral Art and Science of Divination.

These are those known as e NikʼWachinel who were the Mid-Most Seers that could see to the very Heart of the Revelation of Divination. It was they who saw into the very Center of the Revelation of Divination.

This then was when the two Kabʼawil known and named Jun Raqan and Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz spoke when they said to the Day-Keepers, Diviners, Formers, and Mid-most Seers the following:

“Just gather it together; gather the knowing that is the knowledge of what can be seen; just find the wood that we need to form Our People who are the Shaped People-Qawinaq Bʼitoj those who are Our People who the Formed People Qawinaq Tzʼaqoj-Our People the Sculpted People, Our People the Carved People, who will be our Providers; who will be our Sustainers-Tzuqul, Kʼool.”

Invoke Us; Remember Us; Maya Prayer-Making; Kʼicheʼ Day-keeping

“Invoke us so that we might be invoked by our Descendants; Remember us so that we might be remembered by those who are the Reverent Ones; by those who are the Worshipful Ones; by those who are the Loyal Ones; those who the Faithful Ones, by those who are the Devout; Devoted Ones; by those who are the Dedicated, Dutiful Ones so that we might be remembered; so that we might be honored by those who are Our Providers; Our Sustainers.”

body:
Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane: these are those who are the Grandmother, Grandfather-Qatiʼt, Qamam who are also known as the Iyom, Mamom-Midwife, Matchmaker who are the Ancestral Couple; Ancestral Pair who bring their Granddaughters; Grandsons into the world as their Descendants known as Iweey-their Descendants; their Teeth! Iyom comes from Eeyʼom: Grandmother; Mid-wife who brings forth her Descendants; her Teeth; Teeth that are Maize Seed that bring forth Descendants of Maize!

Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane are the Grandmother, Grandfather of their Grandchildren who are their descendants who are the replacements of their Grandmother, Grandfather-Qatiʼt, Qamam of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq those who are the People and Pueblo of Maize-Ixim Winaq.

Ixim Winaq are those who live together in their Pueblo of Maize People that is like a Milpa of Maize; a Corn Field whose ancestral story is told here in mythopoetic mythic metaphorical speech known as the Ancient Ancestral Account-Ojer Tzij of those who are known as the Ixim Winaq whose Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij we bring forth here as a remembrance of their Ancient Ancestral Grandmother, Grandfather-Qatiʼt, Qamam; who are none other than Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane who are none other than those known as the Mid-Wife, Matchmaker; Matriarch; Patriarch-Iyom, Mamom of the Ixim Winaq.

This is their story and it is they who are the Diviners and Day-keepers who bring about this entire myth so it is best you meet them now! Ixmuqane will form and shape the First Four Ancestors of the Kʼicheʼ Maya in her hands; the same hands that will now perform the forming and shaping of the divination that is about to happen here.

So now you are well prepared for her hands to move over and about the golden kernels of Maize Tree and corral red beans of the Tzʼite Tree  with which she will form and shape her divination from the ruby red; corral red divining beans of the Corral Tree; the Painted Tree; Erythrina Corallodendron.

This then is our invocation and remembrance; that is our incantation and recitation of the Ancient Truth; Ancestral Tradition known as ʼEntering the Wordʼ which we have entered here; right now. So let us enter the word of Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane; Qatiʼt, Qamam; Iyom, Mamom.

“Invoke us so that we might be invoked!”

“Remember us so that we might be remembered!”

“Enter, then, the Ancient Word; enter, then, the Ancestral Tradition, you who are those known as:

Iyom, Mamom: Midwife, Matchmaker

Qatiʼt, Qamam: Our Grandmother, Our Grandfather

Xpiyakok: He who Sprouts forth from the Tortoise-Shell Earth; X-peya-kok

Ixmuqane: She of the Buried Maize Seed-Ancestral Tooth Ix-muq-kan-eey

“May they come forth into Being at the Sowing, at the Dawning; Chawaxoq, Saqiroq; upon our invocation, upon our incantation, upon our remembrance of the Formed People, of the Shaped People, of the Carved People, of the Sculpted People.”

“So be it! May it come to pass!”

“May your names be shown, may your names be known:

Jun Ajpu Wuch: Ancient One Grandfather Possum, Ancestor of the Dawn

Jun Ajpu Utiw: Ancient One Grandfather Coyote, Ancestor of the Dusk

Jun Ajpu Wuch: Nagual of Quetzalcoatl; Ancestral Lord One Hunter Possum

Jun Ajpu Utiw: Nagual of Tezcatlipoca; Ancestral Lord One Hunter Coyote

Kamul Alom: Twice a Bearer of Descendants; Great Grandmother

Kamul Kʼajolom: Twice a Begetter of Descendants; Great Grandfather

Saqi-Nim Aq: Great White Jabali-Peccary, Old White-Haired Ancestress

Saqi-Nima Sis: Great White Coati-Kinkajou; Old White-Haired Ancestress

AjKʼuwal: Worker of Precious Green Jade

AjYamanik: Worker of Translucent Emeralds

AjChʼut: Artisan Sculptors; Wood Carver

AjTzʼalam: Artisan Woodworkers; Sawyer

AjRaxa Laq:  Maker of the Blue-Green Plate; Sacrificer of the Jade Plate

AjRaxa Tzel: Maker of the Blue-Green Bowl; Sacrificer of Turquoise Bowl

AjQʼol: Incense Maker; Resin Gatherer; Gatherer of Pine Resin

AjToltekat: Toltec Artisan, Toltec Artist; Refined Artists of Toltec Tradition

Ratiʼt Qʼij: Grandmother of the Day; Diviner of the Days

RaTʼit Saq: Grandmother of the Dawn; Diviner of the Dawn

“Pass your hands over the golden kernels of Maize; pass your hands over the corral red beans of the Tzʼite; just show how it is to be done; just make it so it comes out right; just reveal how to chisel it; just reveal how to carve its side, the side of the board; just tell us how to sculpt its face, the face of the wood; just reveal the way to sculpt its mouth; reveal the way to carve it out; its mouth; its face; the side of the plank; the face of the board; uchiʼ; uwach cheʼ; the mouth, the face of the wooden people; the mouth and the eyes of the wooden works of wood to be formed; to be shaped by the Former; by the Shaper.”

This is what was said by those who asked the ancestral diviners to reveal how to bring forth their Forming and their Shaping of the Beings of Wood who would be known as the Wooden Beings; the Wooden People; the People of Wood; Wooden Works of Wood who were Woodwork People of worked wood; just whittle works of worked wood.

How would this wood work be done? How would they bring forth the Wooden Beings, these Beings of Wood who would be sculpt and shaped; scored and scraped; carved, cut, and crafted; fashioned, formed, and finished from the soft knotless amber wood of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree; the Corral Tree.

This is a repetition in the original text to form and shape the divination a second time. This first part was the divination of ʼhowʼ the worked would be done by carving and crafting the ʼwoodʼ to create ʼwooden works of woodʼ to then divine next what would be the essence of the substance that would be the ʼfleshʼ of the ʼwooden peopleʼ who would be crafted and carved from wood.

“Let it be done; let it be known; let the revelation be revealed through the work of divination; let the golden seeds of maize be thrown; let the corral red beans of Tzʼite be scattered to reveal just how these formed being that are shaped being that are carved being that are crafted being will be brought forth into being!”

body:
“Let it be done, let it be finished pass your hands over the scattered Maize kernels, pass your hands over the scattered Tzʼite; …the corral red Tzʼite beans; the golden yellow Maize seeds…let it be seen; let it be known…”

“Let it be done, let it be finished may the golden kernels be thrown; may the corral red beans be scattered to reveal the essence of their nature, the nature of their matter, the flesh of the body; the body of the being. What will be the essence of the substance of the flesh of these molded beings; these modeled beings of molded and modeled matter. From what then shall they be made?”

Let it be done:

“Let us let them perform their forming and shaping in order to divine the work of the Formers, the Shapers in their work forming the Formed Beings; in their work shaping the Shaped Beings.”

“Let us let them try their luck; let us let them consult their Way of Seeing; their Way of Knowing; their Way of Divining;  through the casting and scattering of the seeds; casting and scattering of the beans; the forming and shaping of the seeds; the forming and shaping of the beans; the counting of the seeds; the counting of the beans through which to perform our divination and all that it reveals.”

“Let them make another attempt at bring forth the knowledge; to bring forth the knowing that comes forth from the seeing and knowing of divination; in our effort to reveal what will be revealed through our revelation of our divination with it seeing and knowing of that which must be done.”

“Let it be known; let it be revealed; let it be divined so that we may know what will be the essence of their flesh; the essence of the flesh of their bodies; the bodies of those who will be Formed; the bodies of those who will be Shaped into those who will be known as the Formed Beings; those who will be known as the Shaped Beings.”

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They scattered a handful of Golden Maize Kernels of the Maize Tree, then they cast a handful of Corral Red Tzʼite beans from the Tzʼite Tree; then they began shaping the count from which they could mound-up the little mounds of counted seeds and counted beans. This is how they gave form and shape to their divination without knowing exactly what shape their divination would take.

They performed their work by passing their hands over their work in perfectly Ancestral Ways to assure their vision was clear through which to see their divination to then listen to what it said by what it showed.

“Destiny, Formation; Qʼij, Bʼit!” called out the One Grandmother, One Grandfather; Jun Atiʼt, Jun Mamaʼ as they were named, those Old Ones, those Ancient Ones who implored and pleaded; beseech and entreated the golden kernels, the red seeds to reveal what was there to be revealed of the Forming, of the Shaping of the Wooden People.

This then was when they spoke out to the seeds and beans to begin their divination of what they needed to find and to know; to go out into the forest to then bring home their work of forming and shaping the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings by the Former, the Shaper; Bearer, Begetter: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom.

Here then are the invocations revealed to form and shape these archetypal divination to get a sense of divination in English of a Maya Kʼicheʼ incantation of divination.

“Just go find it; just go feel it; to see it; to touch it; to hear it; to reveal it. Speak, speak out; speak out loud so we can hear it; to hear what you say as to what is the way we must go to see it; to then find it;  to then go get it;  to cut it, to carve it, to create it; to mold it, to model it, to make it.”

“Go ahead and say it; just relay it; just feel it to reveal it so we can know it; to see it; to find it; so we can go get it; go on now and get with it; just do what is yours to divine where to find it so we can go get it; to cut it; to carve it; to create it so we can finish the work we first started.”

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“Just tell us where to go so we will know just where to see that special sort of tree with this special sort of wood from which we will form and shape the Formed Being; the Shaped Beings; AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit who will be formed and shaped by us who are the Formers; who are the Shapers of those who will become the Formed Ones; the Shaped Ones; those who will become the Providers the Sustainers; Tzuqul; Kʼool at the time of Our Sowing, at the time of Our Dawning; Ewaxibʼal; Saqiribʼal.”

“You, Maize; you, Tzʼite; you, Destiny; you, Formation be useful, be helpful by telling us what we need to know to finish our work; our work of forming; our work of shaping that we must bring to fruition; the work we must bring to completion.”

This is what was said to the Maize Seeds; the Tzʼite Beans to bring forth the Divination; the Formation; Qʼij; Bʼit as it is known to those who are the Day-Keeping Diviners; the Shapers of Divination: AjQʼijʼ AjBʼit.

And so it was that the Men were formed from the wood of Tzʼiteʼ where as the Women were shaped from bundles of Reeds from the Rushes-Sibʼaq as there are known; the Reeds that grow in the Rushes beside the Lakeshore of the Great Water; Nim Ya; Nim Jaʼ.

The Wooden People were now called forth as they were invoked as Men carved from Worked Wood; as Women crafted from Bundled Reeds known together as Poy; Ajam Cheʼ translated as the Wooden People.

Xpiyakok: AjTzʼite; Old Man

Ixmuqane: AjQʼiij; Old Woman

That Grandfather was known as an AjTzʼite, a Diviner, a Seer, the Old Man-Mam of the Tzʼite Tree; his name Xpiyakok, the First Father-Grandfather of the Maize People.

His complement and companion, primordial partner was the one known as Grandmother and it is she who was an AjQʼiij, a Diviner, a Day-keeper who is spoken of as the Old Woman, Atiʼt; the First Mother-Grandmother of the Maize People: Ixmuqane.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Yet here she is known and named as the Pillar-Raqan-Post of their divination. Ixmuqane, she is designated as the One Foot-Raqan-One Leg that stands strong next to her partner the Former, Shaper of this Divination known as AjTzʼite-He of Authority, Rule, Insight, Knowledge;  He of the Tzʼiteʼ; He of the Talking Tree: Tzʼi Teʼ for this tree is a tree that speaks to its owner like a Dog-Tzʼi; Tzʼite by name; known by the Traditional Maya as the Friend-Enemy; Amigo-Enemigo. Tzʼite in Maya Kʼicheʼ;  Tzʼajtel in Maya Tzʼutujil  known as the ʼPainted Tree for its brilliant red bean; its bark produces a sedative effect to induce sleep and dreams to guide Seers and reveal knowledge to Diviners who seek visions and insights in their Tzʼite induced dreams.

Tzʼite signifies the Canine who manifests a natural sense of Rule and Authority over the Land. The Maya domesticated the ʼdog as canineʼ as in the taking of the ʼpupsʼ of the wolf and coyote and fox and escuintle and other canine we no longer know as ʼwild dogsʼ who live on the threshold of the Maya Villages and their Milpa and its Forests and Fields. These canines embodied ways just as they enacted the thoughts of their ʼdueñosʼ in nawal ways which is to say humans and canines communicate with one another to provide and sustain one another with sustenance in all the many forms sustenance takes.

Especially the Coyote-Utiw who is the Nagual or Animal Transform of Tezcatlipoca-Jun Raqan Kaqulja, el Mero Corazón del Cielo; the Very Heart of the Sky; Heart of Heaven as some folks name the name of this Celestial Mind with a voice that guided and protected his people. Junajpu Utiw you might remember is one of the ancestral patriarchs of the First Sun of the Animal People; it is he who can devour sustenance that is both living and dead. So realize that this Tzʼite Tree is the Tree of Authority just as it is the embodiment of the spirit and soul of Ukʼuʼx Kaj as Junajpu Coyote; Junajpu Utiw.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
All of which provides ʼhimʼ with great authority over the Sky-Earth and all that will happen there. This First Sun of the Popol Wuj is the Sun of Quetzalcoatl with its Animal People in which Junajpu Wuch-Ancient Ancestral Possum is the Nagual of Quetzalcoatl who is the Precious Twin of Tezcatlipoca who is known in Popol Wuj as Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja whose Nagual is Junajpu Utiw the Ancient Ancestral Coyote; Coyote who is the Nagual of Tezcatlipoca.

Possum is the Lord of the Dawn; Coyote is the Lord of the Dusk and it is they who are called upon here to participate in the divination of Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane that seeks to see in order to know in order to reveal where to go find the essence of the substance of the flesh from which will be carved and crafted the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings. This search here will be taken up again when the Former; Shaper known as Tzʼaqol; Bʼitol seek out the knowledge that reveals to them what substance must be used to mold and model the Beings of Wood; Beings of Reeds; Beings of Clay; Beings of Flesh all of which are failed and fallen creations that must be destroyed. It is only when the Yellow Maize; White Maize are found that the flesh of the Maize Beings is formed and shaped out of ground maize. Ixmuqane will be guided by the Fox and Coyote; Parquet and Crow to the Mountain of Sustenance known as Meʼawan to the sacred treasure chest of sweet sustenance known as Pan Paxil; Pan Kayala where they will find the Maize that will be ground nine times to then be used as the flesh of the Maize People. This divination that seeks to find the essence of Human Flesh begins right here with Junajpu Wuch; Junajpu Utiw who assist Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane in their Forming and Shaping of their Divination.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The Wooden Men of the Third Age of Formed Beings; Shaped Beings will be carved and crafted out  of Tzʼiteʼ wood because the Tzʼiteʼ is a tree that communicate extraordinarily as well. Tzʼite is a Tree with sharp senses of knowing  like all Canines that live in Packs; Canines that must be understood as the Wolf, the Fox, the Coyote, the Escuintle, and any number of other Indigenous Canines of the Americas we have no idea of anymore since all that sort of knowledge of Indigenous America has been erased by the destructive powers European Conquest and Colonization of  Indigenous American.

The Dog-Tzʼi is a nawal animal that was painted by the Maya as life-loving companions of human being. The dog like the tree named after it were deeply loved and revered by the Maya because of their ingenious way of being able to understand the thoughts and intentions; as well as the gestures and language of Human Beings. This  most ingenious dog is both a friend and enemy of human beings; a kind and affectionate companion;  a faithful and loyal friend; a bitter foe, a vicious rival; a fierce and ferocious adversary who ʼguidesʼ and ʼprotectsʼ one on the road; who ʼprotectsʼ and ʼguidesʼ one  in the dark of night and the foggy drizzle of the mountainside.

Dogs are a Huntersʼ guide and protector; Dogs are the Merchantsʼ guide and protector; Dogs are the guides and protectors of  Grandmother, Grandfather; Granddaughter, Grandsons so that in this sense of being guide and protector a Dog is exactly like a Kabʼawil so that a Dog must be seen as exactly like the Nagual of the Kabʼawil because the Dog is the Animal Transform; Animal Companion of who is act divine in the prescient way it knows what will happen next as divinity and humanity seem to communicate with one another through these intuitively intelligent genius so much so that the Divine Ancestors and their Human Descendants work together in complementary companionship as Divine Twins; not unlike Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz and Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“You Maize-Ixim, you Tzʼite-Bean; you Destiny-Qʼij, you Formation-Bʼit make yourself useful, do what must be done; speak; reveal to us how it will be made,” they said to the maize kernels, to the tzʼiteʼ beans.

This is when the Kabʼawil spoke to one another; those known as Jun Raqan and Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz.

“Be self-sacrificing in your way; be sacrificial in your support; show pity, show remorse, show humility, you who are the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj do not chastise; do not belittle the spoken word of the mouth; do not mock the ways of speech nor humiliate the divine countenance; the divine presence of Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz-Sovereign Plumed Serpent,” they said, speaking straight to the truth.

Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz and Jun Raqan Kaqulja

This was when  ʼHeʼ was spoken to there before the divine powers of Ixim-Maize Seed; Tzʼite-Red Corral Bean; Sun-Qʼij; Formation-Bʼit or Sustenance-Ixim; Authority-Tzʼite; Destiny-Qʼij; Existence-Bʼit; who are there to speak with the ʼOneʼ known as Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj. The beauty of this mythopoetic language is that it is so open and ambiguous in its polysemic ways that it provides the reader or listener of the recitation of the Ancient Words with many meanings and significations to each of these words that are names of Ancestral Ways of Divination.

These many meanings and significations of this sacred secret speech cause one to ponder and wonder what these Maya Scribes want to say with: Qʼij; Bʼit other than Divination. And what this is; is something major; because it is calling upon the Sun-Qʼij to provide the light with which to see destiny; while calling on Formation-Bʼit to invoke and remember the Divine Powers of Creation that are being invoked as some sort of non-corporeal powers of Creation through Forming and Shaping; Molding and Modeling; Carving and Creating all that which must be brought into being in the World of the Sky-Earth to Provide and Sustain the Formers and Shapers of the Creation and Destruction of the Ages.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These Ages were imagined as the Maize growing in the Milpa that must be sown just so in order to grow and grow to flower and fruit just so; so that the People of Maize will be provided and sustained by the Maize that they have provided and sustained their Maize growing in the Milpa. This is the story that is told here; the story of providing and sustaining to be provided for and sustained by those who one has nourished and nurtured to fruition. This is also a story of the lifecycle of Maize and the Milpa that begins like all Ages with a great deal of hope that is embodied in the sprouts shooting up and out of the Earth with vim and vigor only to end up dying in the end after flowering and fruiting with great beauty only to end life being complete destroyed through the utter chaos of wailing winds under a desiccating Sun. Yet this is the normal lifecycle of the Milpa just as it is the way of each and every Age with its New Sun and New Moon filled with hope and intention to create great beauty and prosperity only to end up completely destroyed. Creation takes self-sacrifice and this is what the text is telling us here.

This Divine Power of Creation named only as Qʼij; Bʼit is being remembered to be called upon so that these Divine Twins give blood through the self-sacrifice of themselves with maguey spines or kʼix. So that from now on out and for all time hence which means for all of eternity which our Maya Scribes will call ʼSaqil Amaqilʼ blood sacrifice will be given by the Providers and Sustainers. So that all those who are Providers and Sustainers will give Blood Sacrifice through Human Sacrifice which means everyone will give blood sacrifice through Blood Sacrifice.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
For was it not ʼHe-Ukʼuʼx Kajʼ who was the ʼOne-Jun Raqan Kaquljaʼ called upon to give blood sacrifice-katkʼix la uloq to feed the forming, the shaping that was brought to completion by Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz and his creation of the New Sun, New Age of the Wooden People. Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is pleading with Jun Raqan Kaqulja to participate in the Forming and Shaping of the Men of Tzʼiteʼ and the Women of Sibaqʼ in order that their collaborative and complementary Twinship comes to fruition but as you will see something is lacking in the essence of the flesh of these two forms and shapes of creation. They will fail to remember Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

This is why Quetzalcoatl is begging Jun Raqan Kaqulja to sacrifice himself to making the Wooden People in order that they turn out well. When they donʼt turn out well one of the proofs of their failings is that they cannot remember the Heart of the Sky; Ukʼuʼx Kaj as their Creator. It is because of this failure to remember Ukʼuʼx Kaj that he turns against the creative ways of the Forming and Shaping of Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz so much so the Ukʼuʼx Kaj becomes nothing less than the Great Destroyer known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja or Hurricane.  The Animals are brought into existence by Lord Quetzalcoatl as Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo the Primordial Waters of Creation of the Heart of the Lake-Sea to then be destroyed by Ukʼuʼx Kaj and his obsidian blade that feeds upon the flesh of the Animal People. Then come the Clay People who are molded out of Earth and Water to end up to Wet because of the Essence of the Heart of the Lake-Sea; Heart of the Water to be completely eradicated through the total destruction of Heart of the Sky who lays all the Clay People low.

And now we have the Wooden People who are carved from wood and bundled from reeds only to be completely destroyed by the Heart of the Sky as you will come to see while being transformed into Spider Monkeys who are the Nagual of Quetzalcoatl known as Kʼoy. Kʼoy this is a most bothersome trickster animal who disrupts the peace of the jungle forest in every way as he embodies the reversal of what Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz intended with his formal forming and shapely shaping of Wooden Men and Reed Women.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz, Quetzalcoatl, the Creator and Jun Raqan, the One Footed One, Tezcatlipoca the Destroyer, Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj were together again Forming and Shaping the next Age of Sibaqʼ Reed Women and Tzʼiteʼ Tree Men. This polysemic phrase ʼkatkʼix la uloqʼ is difficult to translate with precision since it could mean: give self-sacrifice with maguey thorns; humble yourself; mock yourself; sacrifice yourself to the work of forming and shaping of these Wooden Works of Wood known as Poy and Ajam Cheʼ. Poy signifies: Manikins; Scarecrows; Dolls; Puppets; whereas Ajam Cheʼ means ʼWorked Wood or Wooden works of Wood or Woodworks; literally: Worked Wood People; Ajam Cheʼ.

It also sounds a lot like a word play on the Principal Bird Deity-Wuqubʼ Kaqix who is a Nagual Animal Transform of  Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan.  Yet the significance and sentiment of this playful reprimand is clear which is ʼcome on Ukʼuʼx Kaj donʼt humility or mock the word of the mouth of the countenance of Sovereign Lord Quetzalcoatl. Instead, ʼget with itʼ ʼhumble yourselfʼ to properly ʼsacrifice yourselfʼ to become a collaborative complementary Twin by supporting the divine desire and sacred intention of Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz-Nakxit Quetzalcoatl-Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl-Kukulkan of to bring forth Creation through the Forming, the Shaping of the Wooden People. So let us turn to the Forming; the Shaping of the Wooden People: Poy; Ajam Cheʼ in order to watch the way their Age rises up through the powers of Creation to be brought down low through the powers of Destruction.

Here begins the telling of the Wooden People formed and shaped from the wood of Tzʼite Trees and the Reeds and Rushes of the Sibaqʼ that grow thick beside the water of the lakeshore overflowing with natural abundance and prosperity.

They came out well those who were the Wooden Beings-Poy those who were the Wood-worked Works of Wood-Ajam Cheʼ.

They came out well because of their speech and because of the way the spoke with one another there on the Face of the Earth.

So be it! They said then: May it be so!
