source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
When they spoke their name; in a stroke the Wooden Beings were made; known as the Poy-Manikins is what they were these Wooden Beings that were ʼakin to menʼ known and named Ajam Cheʼ: Wooden Works of Wood.

They looked just like People; they spoke just like People as well. And so then it was that the Face of the Earth became populated by the Wooden Ones who now peopled the Face of the Earth.

They multiplied and became many; they conceived and engendered Daughters; they begot and birthed Sons; they sired and delivered Children. This then was when they were there on the Face of the Earth these who were known as Wooden Manikins-Poy-Wooden Figurines; those who were known as Ajam Cheʼ-Wooden People; those People of Wood who were Wooden Works of Wood.

But they had no heart; they had no soul; they had nothing that one could call feelings much less a touching thought of the heart; for nothing moved their soul.

They had no intelligence; they had no genius; they had no thoughts; they had nothing that might be called imagination; all of which made them about as caring and concerned for others as wooden planks of wood. But that wasnʼt the worst of it because they could not remember who formed and shaped them; they could not name the names of their Former; their Shaper; the Carvers and Creators.

They walk about rather poorly, more or less lost and without direction; they crawled about on all fours.

They had no remembrance, no recollection of the Heart of the Sky their Kabʼawil: Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

Because of this they were judged; and this then was their downfall there on the Face of the Earth. And so it was seen as just another attempt; just another demonstration of the human condition; just another attempt at making and molding Providers; Sustainers:  they did not turn out well.

At first they spoke; but their faces were just so dry; their arms, their legs had no consistency, no uniformity.

No blood flowed in their veins; no vital fluids ran through their dry limbs, the branches of their desiccated bodies.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They did not perspire thus sweat did not drip from their pores; no nice fat greased their skin to give them a chubby oily complexion; they were just so very, very dry; this is how dried up and dried out were they.

Dry were there cheeks giving them hardened masked sorts of rigid façades. Just ʼwoodpecker-stiffʼ were their unbending legs and inflexible arms so that their flesh of their stiff bodies squeaked whenever they moved.

And so it was that they felt nothing before their Former, Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Bearer, Begetter; Alom, Kʼajolom; Giver of Breathe, Giver of Heart; Alay Qech, Kʼuxlay Qech; Inspirer, Heartner of the Bright Life; Inspiration;  Encourager of the Divine Life-Saq Kʼaslem.

They were the First People to grow thick and abundant here on the Face of the Earth. Let us continue on with the end of the Wooden People and their downfall, death, and demise.

This then was when they were finished off; when they were eliminated-kimaʼixik; eradicated-kimaʼixik from the Face of the Earth; because the Poy along with the Ajam Cheʼ were swept clean from where they had started out so well to end up completely decimated; destroyed by those who had formed and shaped them not so long ago.

They were just ground down-kikʼutuxik before being completely ground out-kikʼutuxik; for it was they who were killed off-xekamisax. The end had come for these Woodwork Beings ʼAjam Cheʼ who were wooden works of wood.

These were those who were Poy that had been dressed up and adorned to be seen as Manikins in order to be known as Manikins were killed-xekamisax.

Those who were known as Puppet People who were seen as Doll People: Poy were ground-out-xekʼutuxik.

These Wooden People who began their existence with such promise were all killed-xekamisax just finished off because they did not invoke the name of Ukʼuʼx Kaj who had formed and shaped them; they could not remember Heart of the Sky.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This then was when Heart of the Sky thought of flooding the Face of the Earth; this was when a Great Rain were imagined by Ukʼuʼx Kaj; a rain that would create a flood that would bring about the destruction of the Wooden People for it was he who was the One-Jun named Heart of the Sky who thought-up the Great Flood-Nimaʼ Bʼutik that came with a Great Rain-Nimaʼ Jabʼ that was imagined by ʼHimʼ to bring the ʼendʼ to those who did not remember their Former; their Shaper known as Heart of Sky; named Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

And so it was that this Nimaʼ Bʼutik-Great Flood; Great Hurricane was made to fall upon the Wooden People-Ajam Cheʼ and the Puppet People-Poy that had been formed and shaped just a short while ago.

This Nimaʼ Bʼutik, this Great Flood was made to fall atop the thoughtless Poy and the mindless men made of wood-Ajam Cheʼ whose forming and shaping came to no good.

It was just Tzʼiteʼ wood from the Tzʼiteʼ tree that was worked as the wooden essence; the wooden substance used for the flesh of these Wooden Men formed by the Former; shaped by the Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol. This was the wood used to form and fashion; sculpt and shape the wooden bodies of these Beings of Wood; it came from the Divining Tree: Tzʼiteʼ.

Lakeshore reeds growing amongst the rushes-known as Sibʼaq-were used to mold and model the body of the Reed Women in this Age; in this Sun; in this Era of the ʼWooden Peopleʼ that would be remembered as the Age; as the Sun; as the Era that came to a swift and destructive end.

This, then, is the way they were killed: they were just drowned; they drown in the dark rain; a rain of resin that fell from the heavy sky of Storm drowned the Wooden People: Ajam Cheʼ; Poy.

There came a ʼDark Rain of Resinʼ known as ʼNimaʼ Qʼol-Great Resinʼ that fell thick; that fell dark; that fell heavy from a tarred Sky.

And with that dark rain of resin there appeared the Monster Destroyers known by their names; names that are named here:

Kʼotkʼowach: Eye-Gouger; Gouger of Eyes; xkʼotin ubʼaqʼ kiwachʼ, it was he who gouged out; carved out the eyes of his victims.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Kamalotzʼ Kama Sotzʼ: Killer Bat; Death Bat, this one decapitated the heads of his victims; he just lopped off the skulls of those who were found sleeping out in the dark; known as a ʼDecapitator of Headsʼ he cut-off their heads like a ʼfruit batʼ slicing off his sustenance with his razor sharp teeth in less than a heart-beat; he just chopped off their heads-xqupin ula kijolom.

Kotz Bʼalam: Crushing Jaguar; Crunching Jaguar; Devourer of Flesh this Jaguar chomped and chewed to eat his prey whole; by crunching and crushing their skulls and bones he finished off his meals leaving nothing behind.

Tukum Bʼalam: Dismembering Jaguar; Scattering Jaguar; shredder of bone and sinew, this Jaguar just tore his victim to pieces. Just grounding up to ground down the bones of those who fell into his merciless clasp; the pitiless grip of his fangs and claws from which nothing ever made it passed his demolishing grasp.

There came the One named Kʼotkʼowach who gouged out the eyes his victimʼs face.

There came Kama Sotzʼ the Killer Bat known as Kamalotzʼ or who dropped down out of the Heart of the Sky to lop-off the heads of those who had no idea they were about to die.

There came Kotz Bʼalam who crushed and crunched the flesh and bone; tendons and nerves; grist and gristle that he devoured as he finished off his prey as the One who gulp down everything that came his way.

There came Tukum Bʼalam who dismembered the quarry he hunted and caught what he ate to then make his way through it all piece by piece; part by part. For he ripped his victims to pieces just as he tore them apart; shredding their muscles and tendons; thrashing and slashing their ligaments and veins; as he rip through the sinew as it is known leaving the bodies of his victims dismembered; to scatter their bones about leaving them in tatters as is the way of the Jaguar of the Mountain Places and Canyon Country.

These Wooden People were ground up to be ground down; their body and bones were smashed to pieces, split apart; they were punished to be made examples of because they expressed no feeling; no care; no concern for their Mother; for their Father; for their Mother-Father known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Juraqan.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
And so it was that Ukʼuʼx Kaj created a Great Flood of Black Rain to end the days and destiny of the failed and fallen Wooden People. Their disregard and disrespect for their Former, Shaper caused the Face of the Earth to darken; the dark sky announced the arrival of the Black Rain. The Black Rain began to fall as Dark Rain and this is how it fell; it fell as Day Rain, Night Rain.

The Black Rain, the Dark Rain never stopped falling so that it rained all day; it rained all night. This then was the Dark Rain, Black Rain ended the age of the Wooden People with a Great Flood: Nim Bʼutik.

The Small Animals, the Big Animals they just entered the houses where the Wooden People hid. The Small Animals, the Big Animals they just cut their faces when the faces of the Wooden People were slashed by the limbs; the branches of the trees.

This then was when they were pounded by the rocks that waited for them to catch them wherever they ran; but there was no escape, there was nowhere for Wooden People to hide from the blows that were there to take them down.

The cooking pots; their cooking utensils spoke up as they spoke out against their owners; their dueños; kajawal for the lack of respect and regard; the lack of care and concern for those who worked for them day and night.

Now it was time for them to make their point and have their say; to accuse them in order to condemn them for the infinite ways they mistreated night and day. Those, those who had done so much for them, the Women of Reeds who had used their kitchen utensils and cooking pots without the least bit of concern for the painful sort of pitiful condition in which they left them scalded, scratched, and scorched; burnt, blistered, and blackened so that they ended up chipped and charred; busted and broken. This was no way to treat those molded and molded creations of clay who were put to use every day, to be taken up again beside the hearthʼs fire that burned through the night, just to be brought back to life at dawn.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Those who came forth were kiqʼebʼal, kixot, kilaq, kibʼoʼj, kitzʼia, kikaʼ all of whom were know well as their clay water jars-kiqʼebʼal, their clay comal-kixot, their clay plates-kilaq, their clay cooking pots-kibʼoʼj, their special clay vessels used to boil maize in ash or lime known as nixtamal-kitzʼia and their grinding-stones: kikaʼ. These were those who wanted only to be remembered for all they had gone through at the hands of those Wooden Men and Reed Women whoʼs faulty forming and flawed shaping had left them failed and fallen.

Those who they had used, abused, and misused cried out to be heard when they told of the great anguish; the great affliction they were made to endure because of the scorching heat of their red-hot cooking fires that blazed as they burned within the divine triangle that formed their sacred three-stone-hearth shaped by the ʼthree hearth stones-xkʼubʼ upon which their clay cooking utensils were placed to perform their sacred burden of cooking the sacred sustenance of the Wooden People.

It was then that their heavy grinding stones told their story of how they were never given a moment of rest by those who didnʼt feel a thing for their endless grinding of maize and cacao across their sensitive stone face.

The many instruments, implements, tools, and utensils of the Wooden People that were used to prepare the sacred sustenance that fed in order to nourish their people now came before the Wooden People who had cause them endless pain and suffering.

They came before these Wooden Works of Wood to let it be shown that theyʼd been neglected and abused for much too long and now it was time for that truth to be known. It was time to judge them, to then punish them by making the Wooden People endure the same pain as they had caused their charred pots, plates, ladles, and bowls; their burnt comal, their ground down grinding stones, scorched hearth stones, and lime-caked nixtamal which was everything there was in their ancestral kitchen that had been treated with neglect and disrespect by those who had not a care or concern for those clay beings whoʼd always been left much too long in the fire.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Immediately they threw themselves upon the Wooden People to cut into their flesh; they jumped on them to cut and carve-up their faces. But it wasnʼt just their kitchen utensils and cooking pots that attacked them there.

No, no, no it was their domestic animals that came after them to let them know all they had done to make their lives miserable; always on the edge of starvation; an intolerable existence where they always went hungry.

Now it was time for their animals to rise-up to give them the some of the same. These were their dogs-kitzʼi and their turkeys-kakʼ that were eaten as soon as they fattened up. That was just the way it was for those who were the dogs-kitzʼi and turkeys-kakʼ of the Wooden People; dogs and turkeys who joined in now with the Clay Cooking Utensils to take it to the Wooden People who had caused suffering whenever they could.

They just let the Wooden People have what they had coming to them for the cruelty and neglect they were made to suffer when they were made to endure hunger; what else could they do?

The end of their days had arrived so that something new could come through; now it was time for the truth to be spoken; it was time to come true about who the Wooden People grew to become and how they came to treat those who they were responsible to take care of there on the Face of the Earth.

And so their Dogs and Turkeys spoke-up as they spoke-out against those who were there to give them care and show them concern as their providers and sustainers; nourishers and nurturers:

“You really made us suffer, you truly caused us harm, you bit into us, so now we will bite into you; you chewed on us, so now it is time we chewed on you,” growled their Dogs-Kitzʼi, gobbled their Turkeys-Kakʼ.

Then it was their old grinding stones who spoke:  “On our faces you ground down maize until it was fine and silky; cacao too. You did this every day, day after day; from dawn to dusk, your grinding never stopped; grinding-down endless kernels of maize; grinding-up infinite nubs of cacao; you just ground down our face with your infinite, endless grinding that was never enough.”

What the sacred secret speech says: joli, joli; jukʼi, jukʼi.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Now it was time for them to continue speaking-out now that everyone was listening to these ancient, ancestral stones speak their piece: “After nightfall; before sunrise, it didnʼt matter, it was always the same for us; always the same sound of grinding maize, grinding cacao, on your grinding stones, upon our face: scrape, scrape, grind, grind; the same orders spoken over and over:  joli, joli, jukʼi, jukʼi; letʼs go girl-jo ali, letʼs go girl-jo ali; our one ground drink of maize-jun ukʼej; our one ground drink of maize-jun ukʼej; letʼs go girl get our ground maize drink; letʼs go girl get our ground maize drink;  joli, joli, jukʼi, jukʼi was all you ever said because that is all we ever heard you say. And knowing this was our burden and tribute to be paid to you we just kept up our grinding from sun-up to sun-down like good girls are taught to do.”

Jukʼi, jukʼi; Joli, joli; Jo ali, jo ali

This play on the sound of grinding maize-joli, joli; jukʼi, jukʼi-is just as much as play on words that tell of the Women and Girls who grind that Maize. This play on sound that is a play on words says everything about how sound speaks to us in order to say something vital about the relationship between the grinding stone and the ʼstrong, hardʼ Women and Girls who must work in the patios and kitchens of their Female Lords or Ixqi Ajaw who are responsible for the feeding of their Great Houses. Noble Women learned to grind maize and cacao on their Grandmothers Grinding-Stones-Ka just as they spun cotton thread with their Great-Grandmotherʼs Spindle-whorls-Bʼatzibʼal to then dye those threads in order to then weave them into the cloth that became to clothing that gave both cultural identity and magical protection to their families and relatives who wore them.

Jo ali jo! Joli, Joli; Jukʼi, Jukʼi! Our sweet drink; our sweet drink; our one sweet drink that is the drink that is ground down to satisfy the Mayaʼs appetite for sacred sustenance that is the drink that is first ground down to be drank up as their most roasty-toasty ancestral sweet drink there is: joli, joli; jukʼi, jukʼi. Let us listen to what the Grinding Stones say.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This then was when the Grinding Stones spoke up to tell of their plight before those who left them with constant work grinding maize; work that never ended since the sacred sustenance of the Ixim Winaq asked to be transformed from hard kernels of maize to the soft sustenance that could be eaten. This transformation of  hard grains into sweet food was brought to fruition through the continual work of Maya Women and Girls who were called upon to feed their people four times a day:  twice with maize drink-once at dawn, once before sleep and twice during the day with tamales and tortilla.

And so it was that this endless work of women was remembered in mythic ways; this continuous work of cooking corn in clay pots of nixtamal water everyday-juta qʼij; to then strain and rinse it in their clay sieves; to then grind it on the grinding stone xqʼek-dusk; saqirik-dawn in order to then cook it up again in great big pots-kukubʼ as tamales or on the hot comal-xot as tortilla.  Truly, the work of Maya women to feed the People of their Pueblo knows no end.

“We were never given any rest, just grinding and grinding is all you gave us to do, maize and cacao, grinding and grinding, night and day. This was our cargo to carry; our debt to life; our burden to bear; that which is ours at birth to bear; the work we constantly had to perform for you. This was our sacred burden-qapatan our divine office; our duty you set upon us to pay as our tribute-qapatan; just debt, just tribute paid to you when ʼyou were still people-ix ta na winaqʼ who lived on earth as they say.”

“Now it is you who will try out our strength when we grind you down. Now it is our turn to take a bite out of you, when we grind down your flesh,” said their grinding stone-kikaʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Then their dogs; kitzʼi said what they had to say: “Why didnʼt you give us our piece; our portion; our bit; just a bite, a taste? You saw us standing there hungry; you just kept us there; kept us waiting like that, waiting patiently; we wanted just a bite to eat but still you ran us out; you just drove us away; always with your stick-yakal at the ready to give it to us while you ate. Is that any way to treat your companion; your best friend?”

“We almost died of hunger because of you. But how could you have known that, when you canʼt feel a thing? Perhaps you might have thought it over; with you as our masters we almost died. Now itʼs time you try out our teeth; qabʼaq just the ʼbonesʼ here in our mouths-qachiʼ. We are going to take a bite out of you before the end of the day!” growled their dogs before they tore into their faces.

Next, it was their comal-kixot; their tortilla-toasting griddles-kixot and cooking pots-kibʼoj who said:  “You caused us pain, the way you burnt our mouths, charred our faces; always cooking with us over your hot fire, could you have not known! You tested us well when you left on your blazing fire. Why so hot; why so long? You didnʼt think we felt pain? Then you try it. Now we will burn you!” cried their pots; cried their comal. They went after them, they pursued them; they caught up them and burnt them good as any self-respecting worker would.

Their fire-stones-abʼaj that were their hearthstones-xkʼubʼ that were burning red-hot in the fire just flew up and out of the flames hitting the Wooden Ones in the head. Those hearthstones of theirs shot right out of the flames to hit them on their skulls-jolom as if one had aimed them directly at their skulls-taqal chi kijolom.

That was it! They knew what had hit them until it was over; those Wooden Men, Reed Women werenʼt as innocent as they pretended to be. It was then when those Wooden People ran as fast as they could run, running from all that was scattered about the ground; that which was thrown at them.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They tried to scramble up on top of their houses to escape but their houses collapsed beneath them when they tried to make their getaway. It was no use their destiny was sealed; their fortune that was their fate that they should die on that very same day.

They tried to disappear by hiding up in the trees, but they were easily defeated by the limbs and leaves of those trees and vines they had treated without the least bit of regard and absolutely no respect.

But that didnʼt stop them from running through the Many Trees-Kiʼcheʼlaj of the Forest where they were attacked by the limbs and branches that beat them bad and cut them to pieces. Those branches, limbs, and twigs they had cut and chopped now gave them more of the same: the People of Wood; the Wooden People realized now who they were and where they come from leaving theme nothing more to do then accept their fate that now surrounded them to then begin closing in on them from all sides.

The Tree People now remembered and recognized these Men-made of Wood; these trees with their branches, trunks, and limbs who would never forget those who had once wounded them even though they knew what they were doing was no good. Those who were now on the run were those same shameless woodcutters who had once carelessly cut firewood in the forest by chopping down the trees to then cut-up their branches without the least bit of concern for the trees of the forest.

Those who once did whatever they wanted in the wilderness; those who once did whatever they pleased to the vines and trees now received the wrath of the vines and the revenge of the trees.

It was then that they-the Wooden People-tried to hide inside of the caves but the caves slammed shut in their faces leaving them no option but to turn about to receive what was theirs in life: the complete death and destruction of their fallen lineage with its failed ways.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This, then, was the destruction of the Formed People, the Shaped People. They were the lost ones; the fallen ones; those of the great reversal of their destiny; their luck had changed forever; they were transformed completely because they could have cared less about the rest of life with who they shared the Face of the Earth.

The Wooden People are no longer what they once were. They were made examples of by being transformed in their speech and in their looks; for their language and appearance were changed forever.

So now, today, it is said that the Spider Monkey-Kʼoy is just a memory of them; a sign, a symbol to remind everyone of their fallen, failed, and flawed ways especially those who act ʼas ifʼ they were their descendants: descendants of the Wooden People known as Kʼoy who we will meet up down the road and up in the trees.

Those Kʼoy, those Spider Monkey, who live in the forest today live as a remembrance of their sorrowful and sad existence, perfect examples of how not to act, just signs of the Wooden People with their disastrous, destructive, and defective ways of existence.

These Kʼoy live on as the kʼexel-replacements of a lost-sach generation of Formed Beings, Shaped Beings who were failed beings and fallen beings-sachnaq winaq who made very good examples of very bad examples for their human descendants who would come to learn from them through their regret, remorse, and repentance.

Truly, the Wooden People taught those who came after them how to behave like kind and caring, considerate people since bad examples always teach how best not to act and speak than good examples show how to succeed.

It was just soft, knotless wood from a spiny tree full of color that was used to form and shape their flesh by the Former, the Shaper; the Maker, Molder; the Woodworker, Whittler of the Wooden People.

Kʼoy: the Spider Monkey; Wooden People

Today it is the Spider Monkey that acts like these poorly behaved Wooden People; and so it is they, the Wooden People, who are remembered as the descendants of this lineage of Spider Monkey People; the remembrance of Quetzalcoatl whoʼs Nagual or Animal Companion is the Spider Monkey.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They were just Puppet People; Poy, just Doll People; Poy who were the People of Worked and Whittled Wood known as Ajam Cheʼ who are just Men made of the Wood of the Tzʼite; the Tzʼite and its Magical Talking Wood and Divinatory Beans that are used every day to divine the order and count of the Days. Tzʼite is a knotless wood that is used amongst the Maya to sculpt and shape the many Masks of Mam; the Ancestor; the  Grandfather; the Old Man; el Viejito known as Rilaj Mam; the Ancient Old Man who lives on today as a remembrance of this story that is so well told here.

And so too the Women of the Rushes and Reeds-Sibʼaq are remembered and recalled by the great bunches of reeds cut on the lakeshores of the Maya world where they are dried in the Sun to then be gathered up and brought home. Then they are woven in the patios of the lineages of those People who weave reed mats. Reeds that are worked with flat, round stones held in the hand just right to flatten the reeds so they can then be woven into the noble reed mats known as Pop; Pop the root that is the origin of the name Popol Wuj; the Council Book of the Noble Reed Mat of Noble Rule and Authority.

Pop are the embodiment of Female Authority; Female Rule of the Matriarch who was and continues to be the Ruler of the Maize Peopleʼ lives. Pop or Petate are those Reed Mats upon which the Maya enter the world at birth and exit life at death.  Maya people were once rolled up in the Pop upon which they died to return again on the Pop upon which they returned to life as their own replacements who would be born into the world as their Descendants: Ketal; Kitzijel. This is the story told here; as it is said: Just the Half of It. The story of the Reed Women is hidden away in the shadows for it is too powerful to be revealed here in the light of the public eye; the public sight; for that story reveals the Ancestral Soul that reveals the Ancient Perspective of the Ancient Ones: los Nawales.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These stories that are written out to be recited here are just revealed stories that demonstrate in order to manifest the truth and tradition; the work and the word; the word and the way of these Mythic Archetypes; Mythic Figures known as Poy as Ajam Cheʼʼ These were those who were just Works of Wood; these were those who were just the Wood-Worked Wooden People. You will see how they reappear in another place down the road on top of the Mountain Jaqawitz; the Open Mountain; the Mountain of Lord Jaqawitz; this is where the Poy, the Ajam Cheʼ will play a most significant role of the Kʼicheʼ Maya over the Mountain People; the People of the Canyon Country who will fall to the Nawal Powers of the Jaguar Lords introduced to you here.

These Wooden People who were whittled works of wood continue to exist until this very day as those people who do not know how to care of others nor have concern for the world they live in with the many things that must be shown respect and regard for they are tools and instruments formed and shaped in the hands of working people.

The Wooden-People never learned to protect the world they lived in, its wild and domestic animals, its people, and all the many tools, art, and things those people made. This is how these disrespectful beings are remembered and known today: as Wooden People with No Heart; No Soul.

They are seen as the fallen ones-sachnaq, poqnaq winaq-the lost ones who experienced the great reversal of their destiny and its fortune, its fate. They are seen today as Spider Monkey swinging through the forest canopy, high, high up in the many trees that grow and multiply in the forest of the Kʼicheʼ.

Ukabʼ

Second

Wuqubʼ Kaqix: Lord Seven Macaw: Great Bird Deity

The Big Man and his Big Sons

Volcano Boy   Earthquake Boy   Seven Macaw   Shield Bearer

Sipakna        Kabʼraqan           Wuqubʼ Kaqix      Chimalmat

Age of the Giants; Sun of the Giants; Era of the Giants

The Boys, the Sons, the Twins

Junajpu Ixbʼalamkej

Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu

Four Hundred Boys: Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
We have entered the middle of this story of the Ancestors of the Maize People, which is a story that is already in progress; a story in which the mythic narrative is already moving; En Medias Res as it is known. This is why I must introduce you to this traditional Kʼicheʼ Maya narrative that the Kʼicheʼ Maya knew by heart as the ʼmotherʼs milkʼ that provided and sustained their lives with sacred sustenance at the ʼmid-pointʼ of the ritual year with this myth was played out as ritual drama enacted as rite of passage. Popol Wuj as myth went with the ritual renewal of the New Year and its sacrificial fires that were fed with sacrificial offering to feed the Sky-Earth and its Divinities-Kabʼawil that hungered to be fed.

This ritual drama and its sacred narrative nourished and it nurtured those Kabʼawil you know as Qʼuqʼkumatz and Jun Raqan Kaqulja who as Heart of the Lake-Sea; Heart of the Sky-Earth would provide reciprocal rains to feed the maize recently sprouted-up and out of the Dry-Earth of the Milpa. These Rituals of Sacrifice will be played out here in this Sacred Narrative we have just stepped into a narrative the Maya knew by heart; the mythic narrative I must introduce you to in order that you are firmly established in your knowing what exactly is going on; which is to say I must introduce you to its protagonist and antagonist; allies and enemies; friends and rivals.

What follows is not ʼrequired readingʼ so those who would rather move ahead to the telling of this mythic history then by all means do so. But for those who would benefit from more background knowledge in the form of mythic perspective and culture context to develop deeper understand this section of the Popol Wuj then by all means make your way through these next few pages of interpretive introduction into the story of the Hero Twins-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej and their archenemy, the Principal Bird Deity: Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The exemplary speech and actions of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will teach as its manifests the courage and cunning; genius and insight; self-effacement and sacrifice; daring and decisiveness needed to be  Great Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom, el Reino Kʼicheʼ  in the place known today as Quicheʼ.

This is their story that begins here. A story that begins with a short Introduction that is not the original Popol Wuj yet replicates the original sense and cadence; pace and poetics; sound and sentiment of the original Ancient Word; Ancestral Account.

My greatest hope and deepest desire for the reader and listener is that this translation is as enjoyable to listen to and comprehend as it is edifying and instructive as a expression and revelation of the imaginal realm of the mythic mind of the Maya-Nahua Culture of Mesoamerican World and that Mythical Realmʼs Cosmo-Magical thought and imagination.

This section begins with a dreamy white light that settles over the Sky-Earth to create an atmosphere of being ʼbetween and betwixtʼ the world of the Ancestors and the world of their Descendants. This calm pre-dawn light has name that expresses a feeling that we have entered a world that exists between the Sun of the Wooden People and the Sun of the Maize People.

This, then, was when soft white light enveloped the Sky-Earth in the calm quiet glow of Dawn; its luminous warmth of smooth silver moon like sort of light blanketed the Face of the Earth in an ancient, ancestral remembrance recalling the moment when the Ancient Ones, the Divine Ancestors watched and waited for the First Dawn; a memory of an Age; a recollection of a Sun that had come and gone: Saqnatanoj. Saqnatanoj was the time that was the moment just before the arrival of the shimmering, shining, sparkle of the bright white light of Dawn. Saqnatanoj; embodiment, ensoulment of the resplendent recollection and remembrance, the radiant recuerdo y recolección of the first rays of sunlight of Sunrise; the glistening gleam of the glossy glow of Dawn,  just named, just known as: Saqnatanoj.

body:
So let us take up ʼthe good fightʼ alongside the Two Boys, the Two Sons, the Twin Brothers known as the Hero Twins as they lead us down the road to where we must be to see all there is to see; to known all there is to know; to speak and act as the First Mother-Fathers who showed their Descendants just how to speak and act in order to know just where to go!

Popol Wuj asks us to invoke the Divine Ancestors and Kabʼawil by ʼNaming their Namesʼ just as it calls upon us to remember the Ancient Ones known as the Nawal Lords of Tollan Tzuy-Wa who we will come to know extremely well by the time we come to the end of this Sacred History of the Popol Wuj we know as the Mayaʼs Myth of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq. But it does ask us to open our hearts to clear our vision to awaken and engage our imagination in order that we are provided with the Nawal Perspective of the Mayaʼs Ancestral Soul through which to see the Imaginal Realm with ancestral sight.

This Nawal Perspective of the Ancestral Soul is what will open up our Mythic Imagination to the Imaginal World of Myth that is waiting within us to reveal the mythic beauty to be found in this Ancient, Ancestral Account.  Let us take up this Mythic Masterpiece of the Maize People; Ojer Tzij Ixim Winaq to follow in the footsteps of the Hero Twins, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej, as they ʼorderʼ the Sky-Earth as they make their way walking and talking around the Four Corners; Four Sides of the Sacred World placing their sacrificial offering in the North-South; West-East with their Sacred Cosmogonic Acts of Ritual Sacrifice. This then is Sacred History that tells of the Destruction of Sacrifice required for the Creation of Abundance and Prosperity that is the essence and condition of the Good Life: Utzilaj Kʼaslem; the Sacred Life, Saq Kʼaslem.

body: Wuqubʼ Kaqix is about to be ʼplacedʼ in the Northern Quadrant of the Night Sky as the One-Legged-One; Jun Raqan or the One Legged-Big Dipper of Ursa Mayor; the Four-Hundred Boys-Jobʼ Much Kʼajolabʼ will be placed after their death by Sipakna-Volcano Boy the Southern Quadrant of the Night Sky; Sipakna-Volcano Boy will be placed in the West to become the Mountain of Sustenance known as Meʼawan-Bent-Over; Broken-in-Half Cane where great quantities of Maize are found stored within the Maize Mountains of Pan Paxil, Pan Kayala found here at Meʼawan; Kabʼraqan-Earthquake will be ʼplacedʼ in the East after his ʼsacrificeʼ at the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij to become the Dawn Mountain of Saqiribʼal or Sajribʼal: Dawning Mountain. This Primordial Mountain of the Dawn-Saqiribʼal is where the Sun continues to be welcomed into the World of the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew every New Year on February 19th-20th when the Cargador del Año or Year-Bearer-Mam is set on his Path of Walking the Four Corners; Four Sides of the Sky-Earth during the Solar Year of Eighteen-Twenty Day Months or Eighteen-Months of Twenty-Day Months plus the One Five Day Month of the Five Dangerous Days of the Wayebʼ. This is that story being told here.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Popol Wuj is the Ritual Drama formed from Five Ritual Acts played out on the Five Starlit Nights of the Wayebʼ: First Night of Cosmogonic Creation of the Earth-Ulew then the telling of the Animal People, Clay-Creature, Wooden Men, Reed Women; Second Night of the Defeat of the Giants by the Hero Twins (told here); Third Night of the  Hero Twinʼs Descent into Xibʼalbʼa and Defeat the Lords of Death; Lords of Xibʼalbʼa; Fourth Night IxMuqane Molds and Models the First Four Mother-Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom and the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun of the Ixim Winaq, Pilgrimage to Tollan Tzuy-Wa; Fifth Night is the telling of the Invocation and Remembrance of Kʼicheʼ Noble Lineages and their Peregrination through the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom to Settle Mountains to Abandon Mountains; this Ancestral Path of the Kʼicheʼ Realm Comes to it Inevitable End with the Dawn of the Kaxlan Qʼij-Castilian Sun with the Arrival of Don Pedro de Alvarado known as Donadiu –Tonatiuh-Nahua Sun that issues in the Beginning of Krixtianoil-Dominican Catholic Christianity with the  New Word-New Story-New Account of God and his Son Jesukristo spoken of as Chʼabʼal Tiox: Word of God.

We have taken up the ʼInvocation and Remembranceʼ of this Ancient Ancestral Account told with the Ancient Ancestral Word known as Ojer Tzij Popol Wuj: the Ancient Word of the Council Book of Ancestral Counsel; Ancestral Advice. Let us pick-up the pace by moving on from where we left off to get ourselves well situated En Medias Res-In the Midst of Things which is to say Amidst its Being Told; in the Middle of its Recitation: Right Here in the Middle of Things that Shine Bright like the Sun and Moon as well as that Great Big Star that Sweeps the Road to Open the Way so the Sun can Rise-Up in order to Walk-On with Wuqubʼ Kaqix who isnʼt as ʼBrightʼ as he imagines himself to be!

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The Principle Bird Deity of the Maya Cosmos who is the major opponent and adversary of the Maize People will make his own introduction of himself in the calm white light before Dawn; there in the nostalgic glow of possibility that simmers in the Sky and upon the Earth just before Sunrise.  Lord Seven Macaw known as Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kaqix is a False-Face Noble Lord whose name is translated as Lord Seven Macaw; Lord Seven Red Feathers or Wuqubʼ-Seven Kaq-Red Kʼix-Feathers: Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix; Seven Macaw is an ʼarrogant oneʼ and his self aggrandizement gives him a view of himself as a Big Man; Nimalaj Achi. Wuqubʼ Kaqix imagines himself to be the Great Lord which is a name perfectly in sync with the mythic archetype of a Principal Bird Deity;  a Noble Lord of the Jungle Forest with a Treetop Throne in mythic Tree of Abundance from which he rules over his Ancestral Sun while gorging himself on its fruit from which ritual drunkenness is rooted in the ʼfermented liquorʼ known as ʼthree day sweetʼ that is potent mind-altering medicine once used in ritual initiation of the rites of passage for which it was once made.

Every element of the Popol Wuj is connected to everything else; and, so it is that the Nance Fruit Tree-Tajpal that provides the Sacred Sustenance of Wuqubʼ Kaqix is also the fruit used to make the liquor that the Four Hundred Boys will come to drink to become drunk to then die crushed here in this Sacred Narrative of Popol Wuj. Once they are drunk the First Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix known as Sipakna brings their initiation hut-kabʼal down on them killing workers, messengers,  and advocates of the Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja on the Face of the Earth: Uwach Ulew. This is the Mesoamerican Myth of the Maize People that tells of the movement of the Sky-Earth through mythic figures and archetypes that personify the Forces of Nature spoken of in mythic ways.

Maize People: Ixim Winaq

body:
The Hero Twins as Cultural Heroes of the Maize People must prepare the Sky-Earth for the arrival of the Maize People who are of course led by the First Mother-Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Maya; the Kʼicheʼ Maya who will come to know and name themselves as the Ixim Winaq; the People of Maize; the Maize People: Ixim Winaq.

The Maize People will eventually take over the Forest Kingdom of Wuqubʼ Kaqix but before that takes place the Cultural Heroes of the Maize People, JunAjPu, IxBʼalamKej must take Wuqubʼ Kaqix out of his ʼThrone set upon his Tree of Sustenanceʼ because he prides himself as being a Great Lord while being seen by those below as being a pretentious self-aggrandizing Lord who is an ʼarrogant oneʼ  by nature of his red plumage and the ʼfineryʼ of Silver Throne; his Turquoise adornment; his Jade embellishment all of which leads to his self-aggrandizement-nimarisaj rib-self-magnification.

Wuqub Kaqix only says he is a Noble Ruler because of the his ʼtrappings and trimmingsʼ that are  nothing more a manifestation of material wealth which begs one of the principal questions asked in the Popol Wuj: what does it take to be a Great Lord and Noble Ruler of oneʼs People and Pueblo? The Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Maya will answer that question through their Courageous Acts and Regal Speech; just as they will make themselves out to be perfect examples-saqetal-precious pathway for the People of their Pueblo to follow by becoming the perfect path-saqetal that is exemplified by the divine way the Noble Lords act and speak through their Noble Ways and Noble Words.

body:
Wuqubʼ Kaqix saw himself as a Nawal Winaq which, is the way he wanted to be seen by those who would follow him who embodied and ensouled the Perfect Path-Saqetal-Perfect Way to be copied perfectly; to be followed precisely on his path and mirrored exactly  in his way while being imitated flawlessly in his speech as the Perfect Ancestral Exemplum-Saqetal to be followed as a Nawal Winaq who as a Divine Ancestor embodied and ensouled their magical powers of transformation known as ʼancestral geniusʼ that was the very essence and condition of the nawal nature of being of Nawal Winaq who would come to transform the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea once the Wooden People  followed the exemplary path that was what Wuqubʼ Kaqix imagined to be his perfect way of being in the world of the Sky-Earth.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix as a Great Lord; Nim Ajaw wanted only that the Wooden People would do as he did; to speak as he spoke; to act as he acted; to think as he thought; to be as he would always be; to become as he always was; to be as he had already become which according to Wuqubʼ Kaqix was a Perfect Example-Saqetal because of the way he spoke and acted; walked and talked; reflected and respond  just like a Divine Ancestor who changed and transformed just like a Nawal Winaq who communicated and connected with other with concern and care just like an Ancient Ancestral  Magician who came to show the Wooden People the sacred way to be in order to  become perfect Descendants who would come to transform into the perfect Replacements of the Divine Ancestors who showed them the way to be in life by expressing their transforming nature, condition as well as their transformative  essence and way of being that was Nawal in every way. This is what Wuqubʼ Kaqix did and said when showed one and all that he indeed was the sacred path that was the sacred way of being and becoming: Saqetal in every way.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
JunAjPu, Ixbʼalamkej will act in opposition to the ways of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who will always act and speak alone as a single, solitary lord without a companion; without a complement; without a partner to balance his weakness and correct his mistakes; improve his faults while saving him from his failings. This arrogant Bird Deity rules without a Co-Regent with who to reign over his Noble Kingdom like all the Kʼicheʼ Lords will come to do. Kʼicheʼ Lords will always rule with a companion who will complement their ways as rulers who will always rule in a regal form of Twinship that is a noble kind of Companionship.

This is something you will come to see in order to know about the Kʼicheʼ Lords who like the Hero Twins will come to their rule and sovereignty in perfectly complementary ways; ways that will strengthen and protect one another like Junajpu is strengthened and protected by Ixbʼalamkej; like Ukʼuʼx Kaj is balanced by Ukʼuʼx Ulew; like the Heart of the Sky is harmonized by the Heart of the Earth; just as Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is inspired by Jun Raqan Kaqulja so it is that Jun Raqan enlivens the competitive essence of Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz.

This Ancient Ancestral Account of Twins and Twinship is formed and shaped by the balance and harmony of the Ancestral Word; Ancestral Way of Ancient Maya who knew their World as a Primordial Pair that brought forth prosperity out of the Divine Twinship of the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew. The Maya Hero Twins come from this Primordial Couple that becomes Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane who are the Grandfather and Grandmother of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

body:
JunAjPu, Ixbʼalamkej are the Original Ones; they are Ancient Ancestral Ones; they are the First Ones; they are those who embody Hunter and Hunted as the Jaguar hunts the Deer; as the Deer is hunted by the Jaguar. Their blowgun is the ancient, ancestral weapon used in their hunting that will cause the world to move and transform as they perform the work of Cultural Heroes by putting the Giants of the Past Fallen Age in their place to order the world of the Ixim Winaq. JunAjPu, Ixbʼalamkej act and speak as hunters who are Cultural Heroes so they can begin their lives with the Sowing and Dawning of their Bright Life; Saq Kʼaslem experienced as the Perfect Life; Saq Kʼaslem lived out as the Divine Life; Saq Kʼaslem in the world known as Kaj-Ulew; Sky-Earth.

This is that story of the Twins and Twinship told here where Jun AjPu and IxBʼalamKej are twinned within themselves as hunter and hunted just as they are twinned with one-an-other as hunter and hunted as Jaguar hunts the Deer; as the Deer hunts the Maize; as the Blowgunner Boys protects their Maize growing in the Milpa where the Jaguar hunts the Deer that devours the Maize that comes to fruition in the Milpa.

The symbolic soul and essence of the character of Junajpu is his emblematic ʼcerbatana-blowgun-pubʼ who will protect the Maize flowering and fruiting in the Milpa from all the many Birds and Animals who only want to devour its sweet cane, leaves, and kernels as their own sacred sustenance.  This gives us Pubʼ and Pu that  come together in the name Jun-Aj-Pu  who is from the Noble Reed Place of Abundance and Sacred City of Artists, Priests, Calendars, Observatories, Scholars, Painters, and Rulers known as Tollan or Pu.

body:
So Junajpu might be best thought of as Noble Lord of the Sacred City of Pu or Ancient Noble One of Tollan Tzuy-Wa. But Pu comes from Puj as in pustule as Professor Oswaldo Chinchilla Mazariegos sees in his understanding of this story of the ʼPustule One or AjPujʼ who will throw himself into the sacrificial fire to become the Sun and indeed AjPuj is seen with round pustules ooze pus that must tell yet another story of these warrior ball-playing hunting twins who may develop pustules from the ʼmosquitoʼ bites spoken of in this story or some other such narrative.

AjPubʼ, AjPu, AjPuj, AjPus is born with his brother Ixbʼalamkej to his Mother, IxKikʼ on the Mountain and in the Wilderness as a Blowgun Boy or AjPubʼ giving him his name: Junajpubʼ the young hunter who will become the older hunter who will become the hero and defender of his lineage the Junajpu lineage of the Maize People: Ixim Winaq.

Ixbʼalamkej: Little Jaguar Deer

Junajpu has a Twin Brother Ix-Bʼalam-Kej or Ix Bʼalam Kiej to form Ixbʼalamkej who is known as Little Jaguar-Deer, the Hunter and the Hunted, who is Lord of the Animals, Lord of the Wilderness. Both are depicted with their Father Jun Junajpu in an iconic image of the twins bringing their Father the Maize Lord back to life on the Resurrection Plate found in Boston Museum of Fine Arts and in the Blom Plate of Museo de Chetumal in Quintana Roo, Mexico.

In this scene IxBʼalamKiej is named by a named glyph as Yax Bʼalam and this is how he is known throughout in the Classic Period. In the image found on the Resurrection Plate Yax Bʼalam-Ixbʼalamkej pours water from his Grandmotherʼs water jug over his Father while his twin brother Jun Ajaw attends to the sprouting image of his Rising Maize Father forth as maize sprout from a ʼskull-seedʼ that transforms into the body of the descendant rising up and out of the ʼskull-seedʼ of the Ancestor of the Maize Lord to then rise up and out of the carapace of the Tortoise Shell Earth as the Maize Deity Grandfather Jun Nal Yeey-Xpiyakok brought back to life by his Grandsons Jun Ajaw, Yax Bʼalam; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

body:
The two-kabʼ of them are attending the ʼrebirthʼ of the Maize Deity; Jun Ajpu with a ʼhand gestureʼ that speaks of ʼrebirthʼ and Yax Bʼalam with his Tinaja or Qʼebʼal-Water Jug taken from Ixmuqane the Grandmother of the Ixim Winaq. But one wonders is it their Father and Uncle; Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu or is it their Grandfather; Xpiyakok-Jun Nal Yeey who rises up and out of the tortoise shell earth: Xpi-ya-kok.

Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkejʼ are perfect examples of Nawal Winaq giving them miraculous powers of transformation and it is their powers to transforms the Sky-Earth that continues the work of the Formers and Shapers. This work of Forming, Shaping will then be taken up by their descendants just as the forming, shaping of this translation expresses the molding, modeling of the written word in order that this story can live through further transformation through translation and the necessary interpretation needed for its words to be understood on Maya terms, in Maya context, and in Maya ways of knowing-feeling the Ancient Word. The name Junajpu suggests a variety of different yet congruent meanings for he is the First One from the Place of Reeds which makes him the Ancient One Blowgun Boy who becomes the incarnation of the last day of the twenty day names of the two hundred and sixty day divinatory calendar.

Junajpu as One Blow-gun Boy is a magical hunter who is the ʼfirstʼ of ʼtwoʼ twins. He is the one who gets the two into the right kind of transforming trouble while his brother Xbʼalankeʼ is their protector, savior who gets them out of challenging trouble that change the world once and for all. IxBʼalanKeʼ uses his miraculous powers as Lord of the Animals which he inherits from his mother IxKikʼ the Moon Maiden, Moon Mother, Goddess of Blood, Rubber, Resinous Sap in all the forms it takes.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Ixbʼalamkej calls on IxKikʼ in hidden, magical ways. Xbʼalamkiej means he-she of the Jaguar-Deer making him the hunter and hunted all at once and all in one being. As Xbʼalankeʼ he becomes the face of the Jaguar looking out upon the world to the South from the Full Moon as she-he sets upon the Western Horizon. In this aspect Xbʼalankeʼ is known as the ʼhidden Sun, Jaguar moonʼ and so it is that Xbʼalankeʼ will become the Night Sun as Full Moon at the end of their lives and story as blow-gunning hunter boys sent to the world to keep it from dying dead.

I have decided to use the name Ixbʼalamkej because of the way it forms a female gender balance with name of male Jun Ajpu which is the proper way of balancing and harmonizing the genders in twins, couples, and pairs. I also asked many, many Maya Day-keepers about the pronunciation of this name in the contemporary world of Day-Keeping; Prayer-Making. All of which were adamant about their pronunciation of  IxBʼalamKej in which-as you know with the past examples of poj going to po; and,  koj going to ko so that kej moves to ke. Makes sense; sounds right; looks good; feels goods which is enough reason for me to write kej not keʼ in the name written as Ixbʼalamkej; or, even as IxBʼalamkiej as is pronounced and written among Maya Tzʼutujil speakers who live out their Traditional Maya ways by dancing the Jaguar-Deer Dance known as ru Xojo Ixbʼalamkiej.

So it is Ixbʼalamkej that I have chose as the proper way to ʼspellʼ in order to invoke, in order to enchant the Number Two Son, Twin Brother of Number One Son Jun Aj Pu or Jun Aj Pubʼ: Jun Ajpu who is the Ancient Ancestral One of the Place Thick with the Abundance of the Reeds and Rushes who is Jun AjPubʼ One Hunter Blowgun Son; Jun AjPus who is he of the ʼOneʼ mark of pustules of death identifying as being the Son of Grandfather from Xibʼalbʼa who is Kuchuma Kikʼ the Blood Gatherer; Rubber Gatherer; Incense Gatherer of the Underworld Real of Death and Disease of Xibʼalbʼa. This then is a partial naming of the names that name these Maya Hero Twins.

body:
This knowledge that I must provide you with here is the knowledge all Maya would have known at the opening of this scene so now you know what you need to know to move down the road with the Boys, the Sons, the Twins known to all as the one set of twins that speak as one formed, shaped by twin souls that is suggested in the naming of the names of Xbʼalamkej and Junajpu: the hunter and the hunted. Junajpu is pronounced in English as Hoon-ah-pooh and in Spanish as Jun-aj-pu just like it sounds.

The pronunciation of Xbʼalamkej spoken in English is sounded out as Ix Bʼalam keh or Xbʼalankeʼ Ix Bʼa-lan-kay or in Spanish as Ix-Bʼalam-kej or Ix-Bʼalan-keʼ just as it is sounded out phoneme by phoneme. It is important to grasp these names and their pronunciation right from the very beginning because these two will be with us all the way through to the end. It would be a shame to not be saying their names properly as I have heard done so many times in the past.

IxBʼalamKej: He-She of the Jaguar Deer Dance is he who creates the archetypal movement of the hunter and the hunted; as Ixbʼalamkej transforms into the movement of the wind who coaxes the movement of the Wind Jaguar with the Deer Dance that awakens the Wind Jaguar who takes up the chase of an enchanting Deer Women whose beguiling dance entices the sleepy Wind Jaguar to take up the hunt. This then is the mythic metaphor of the Sun chasing the Moon or Venus as the Deer Hunter chasing the Sun as a Deer Women who drops into the Sea as Venus follows the falling celestial sphere; the flaming solar ball plunging into the cosmic chaos of the watery wet world of the Dead Ancestors.

The name Junajpu suggests a variety of different yet congruent meanings for he is the First One from the Place of Reeds which makes him the Ancient One Blowgun Boy who becomes the incarnation of the last day of the twenty day names of the two hundred and sixty day divinatory calendar that flowers and fruits with this sacred day known as Junajpu; Jun Junajpu; Ajaw Junajpu; or just, Ajaw: Noble Lord.

Junajpu as One Blow-gun Boy is a magical hunter who is the ʼfirstʼ of ʼtwoʼ twins. He is the one who gets the two into the right kind of transforming trouble while his brother Xbʼalankeʼ is their protector, savior who gets them out of challenging trouble that change the world once and for all. Xbʼalankeʼ uses his miraculous powers as Lord of the Animals which he inherits from his mother IxKikʼ the Moon Maiden, Moon Mother, Goddess of Blood, Rubber, Resinous Sap in all the forms it takes. We will come to know her well when the time comes to take the stage to show the strength and genius of Young Maya Women who as the Moon Goddess shine through the intuitive genius of the dream of the Underworld and Night.

Xbʼalamkiej recalls the Underworld ways of his Mother IxKikʼ in hidden, magical ways. Xbʼalamkiej means he-she of the Jaguar-Deer making him the hunter and hunted all at once and all in one being. As Xbʼalankeʼ he becomes the face of the Jaguar looking out upon the world to the South from the Full Moon as she-he sets upon the Western Horizon. In this aspect Xbʼalankeʼ is known as the ʼhidden Sun, Jaguar moonʼ and so it is that Xbʼalankeʼ will become the Night Sun as Full Moon at the end of their lives and story as blow-gunning hunter boys sent to the world to keep it from dying dead.

Junajpu, Xbʼalamkej or Xbʼalamkiej are perfect twins, as one person they act in perfect collaboration with one-an-other to bring about the transformation of the Sky-Earth. These twins act as one, speak as one, shoot as one, and dance as one in a world where twins and twinship, couples and colleagues, pairs and partners form and shape the metaphor of divine collaboration that brings the Sky-Earth to fruition. Watch the way these two work together just as you watch your spirit and soul, mind and body, persona and anima, conscious and unconscious as they work together with one another to bring about the necessary changes needed to understand this story through reflection and introspection that creates perspective that in turn helps one change and transform this world through our understanding of ourselves through Maya perspectives of self and shadow, actor and reflection.

body:
There is no end to our revelation of the understanding of these perfectly polysemic names: Jun AjPu; IxBʼalamKiej whose meaning depends on the context in which they are found. You will be drawn to fire-up your own imagination to find other meanings that arise from the mythic metaphors created by different cultural contexts and natural realms in which these Boys find themselves. It is you engage in a dialogue with the Imaginal Realm of the Twins through the mythic imagination as the place of initiation on this mythic journey of self-knowledge and its quest for ancestral transcendence experienced as the unity of psyche and myth.

JunAjPu, IxBʼalamKej: Cultural Heroes who act as Guides and Protectors of the Maize People

These Divine Twins, JunAjPu, Ixbʼalamkej originate from the Sacred Place of Tollan once known as Place of the Reeds; Pu or Place where the Reeds grow thick with abundance. This is the place known as Pu that will become the great cultural nexus of the Mesoamerican Civilization known today as Teotihuacan where humanity becomes divinity.

This is the Ancient Ancestral Place where the First Sun and First Moon were brought to life and into movement through their self-sacrifice which meant throwing themselves on the sacrificial fire. This is the Myth of the Sun and Moon in which the humble Nanahuatzin and arrogant Tecuciztecatl or Tecciztecatl immolate themselves on the sacred fire that burned in Teotihuacan. This becoming of the Sun and Moon is identical to the sacrifice of JunAjPu, IxBʼalamKej who immolate themselves by throwing themselves on the Sacrificial Fire burning there in Xibʼalbʼa to become the Sun and Moon of the Age or Era of the Ixim Winaq.

body:
Teotihuacan is where Humanity is said to have transformed into Divinity which perhaps means that it was the Sacred Place of Transformation or Divine Heart of Initiation where Human Descendant became the replacements of their Divine Ancestors. Just like in the Popol Wuj Kʼicheʼ Maya Initiates  once made this Ancestral Peregrination to Tollan Tzuy-Wa so where  Young Noble Lords took up their Divine Ancestorsʼ Paths of Initiation just as described here in Popol Wuj. By learning the Dances and Singing the Songs; Playing the Ballgame and Practicing Blood Rites of Self-Sacrifice the Kʼicheʼ Maya Youth became Kʼexel or Replacements of their Divine Ancestors.

Thus we must recognize in order to realize that the Popol Wuj is a Book of Counsel that shows the way to carry out Rites of Initiation that were carried out through Rituals of Transformation. Thus the name of the First Hero Twin Junajpu; the Ancient One from the Reeds and Rushes of Teotihuacan: AjPu or XJunAjPu: He the Ancient Ancestral One from Tollan Tzuy-Wa.

JunAjPu thus is well understood as the Ancient Ancestral One of the Ancient Ancestral Place of Abundance-Pu-Place of the Reeds but he is also the One Blow-gun Boy, Lord of the Hunters, Lord of the Warriors, Lord of the Ballplayers, Lord of Transformation, Creation, and Destruction as his is complementary, collaborative, and cooperative Younger Brother Little Jaguar Deer who is his ʼsavior-protector-healerʼ spoken of always as the Second of Two who is the Twin Brother of Junajpu known always as named always as Ixbʼalamkej

Ixbʼalamkej: Little Jaguar-Deer; Lord of the Hunter and Hunted; Lord of the Mountain, Lord of the Wild; the Second One of Two who heals and resuscitates the First One; Junajpu whenever he becomes wounded by being dismembered. Junajpu is the Guide of his Young Brother Ixbʼalamkej who is the Protector of his Older Brother Junajpu; the ʼTwoʼ who work together as the ʼOneʼ: the ʼTwoʼ in the ʼOneʼ Hero Twins who are the Cultural Heroes of the Maize People.

body:
These are the Two Maize Deities who are the one face of the Maize Lord, their Father Jun Junajpu; the First Father of the Maize People. Jun Junajpu begets his ʼEngendered Sonsʼ Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej in the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa who grow upon the One Cane-Jun Aj that is the body of their Mother IxKikʼ who, like One Cane of Maize-Jun Aj, sprouts-up and out of the Underworld to grow and grow before flowering to fruition on the Face of the Earth.  In this way these Boys who are the Sons of their Father-Jun Junajpu are born from their Mother-IxKik who bears them up and out of the Underworld carrying them to safety in her womb. This womb of IxKikʼ becomes ʼone big net of maizeʼ that IxKikʼ must harvest just as she bears her Boys-the Maize Twins on her back until they are born.

IxKikʼ is a Cane of Maize who bears her Sons-the Replacements of their Father the Maize Lord on her back as the Moon Mother of Maize-IxKʼik who carries her twins as  two swaddled heads of maize that grow on her  as the ʼengendered sonsʼ of the First Father of Maize: Jun Junajpu. This is their story; the story of Maize Deities; the story of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej the Sons of the Maize Lord-Jun JunAjPu that is the Sacred Narrative of the Maize People: Ixim Winaq.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Before any of this happens these Two Cultural Heroes of the Ixim Winaq must ʼorderʼ the Sky-Earth to ʼprepareʼ it for the coming of the Maize People. This is the work of blowgun boys who are the primordial hunters of birds who are the primordial enemies of the Ixim Winaq in a world where maize is the preferred food of the birds. This is why Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej must take Wuqubʼ Kaqix down from his throne that sits in his Great Tajpal Tree that stands above and over his Great Kingdom of the jungle forest that the Maize People wish to take for themselves in order to settle down beside it along its lakeshore and waterways in order to grow their Milpas of Maize and their Milpas of Cacao as it is said. This struggle between Wuqubʼ Kaqix and the Hero Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej is the central part of the Popol Wuj introduced to you here. It symbolizes the eternal struggle the Maize People have with the Bird People who are happy to eat the food the Maize People have apparently grown for them.

The Maize People must control the Bird People through superior magic and so it once was that the Kʼicheʼ Maya who knew themselves as Ixim Winaq performed this Ancient Ancestral Account as Ritual Drama at the time of sowing their Milpas with Maize. The Maya performed this ritual drama as a magical means of controlling the birds and animals who like nothing more than eating the sweet canes of maize to then devour the sweet kernels of corn. This then is the story of that eternal struggle between Maya maize growers and the wilderness that surrounded their fields. This will play itself out in beautiful ways as you will come to experience for yourself. A story that begins with this very dramatic line: “This then is when it begins; here then is where it begins; the story of the defeat of Wuqubʼ Kaqix by the Boys, the Sons: Jun Ajpu, IxBʼalamKej.”

body:
The imaginal mythical realm we are now about to enter is an Ancient Ancestral World that is remembered here in deeply nostalgic ways; ways that recall remembrances when the Hero Twins of the Maize People ʼordered and preparedʼ the Face of the Earth for the Creation of the Maize People. The Popol Wuj is the story of the defeat of the Animal People; the creation and destruction of the Clay People, and now the last of the Wooden People who do not know what it takes to rule as a Noble Lord; Noble Lords who learn how to act through the ways and words of Junajpu and Ixbʼalamkej. The sacred narrative of these Divine Twins begins here so do realize this story taught the way of being and becoming a Noble Lord through the forming and shaping of the ways and words of the Hero Twins.

Kabʼawil

Kabʼawil these are Divine Twins-Kaʼibʼ Kabʼawil who are those whose ʼtwo-kabʼ way vision of the kabʼawilʼ allowed them to ʼsee-ilʼ with two-way vision that allowed them to see everything, everywhere, both near and far; above and below; past and future; truth and deception; they saw-il all there was to see-il on the Face of the Earth; Kabʼan. This two way vision of Kabʼawil is the ʼcapacityʼ that makes Kabʼawil the Two Way Seers of the Sky-Earth: Kabʼawil. Kabʼawil are those who see everything to know everything to be able to do everything they come to do.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The Twins will pull of tremendous acts of magic because they are Kabʼawil who are Nawal Winaq; Nawal Winaq who are of a nature-kʼojeʼik-condition that enables them to transform whatever they wish to transform with the intention of bring some sort of greater transformation in the World. Kabʼawil need a bit of time and space to understand them because they will be with us and have been with us from the first utterance of this Ancient Account for it kabʼa means ʼnameʼ so that Kabʼawil are those who are named by the naming of their names; which is how Popol Wuj is begun with the naming of the names of the Kabʼawil who I call Divine Ancestors. These Kabʼawil are those who embody the voice and ensoul the soul of the narrator of the Ancient Word;  the voice of the narrator who is omniscient as all Kabʼawil always are. Letʼs take this name as far back as I have been able to do with the compilation of a ʼglyphic dictionary of Classic Chol Maya.

This potent name-kabʼa in the language of Classic Chol or Cholan or Chorti Maya means much more than name-kabʼa  for the name Kabʼawil manifests sweet abundance-kabʼ awa a word formed from kabʼ-honey and wa; sustenance which in the case of Kʼabʼawil is seen as the ʼsweet abundanceʼ to provide sweet sustenance for the Queen of the Hive. Were Maya Queens seen as Queen Bees? Yes, I believe they must have been since Bee Hives are well organized societies that produce sacred sustenance to feed and sustain those who feed and sustain the multiplying and growing of the People of the Pueblo. Bees are vital for the pollenization of the Maize growing in la Milpa so that the more Bees that exist the more honey is produced along with the production of more kernels of corn on each head of maize. In this sense Kabʼawil are those who ʼfill-outʼ in order to complete everything that is made and manufactured in by the Maya People of a Maya Pueblo.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Kabʼawil is said to be the ʼfull and completeʼ abundance of the kingdom that is distributed in perfect reciprocity between the Kabʼawil who provide the Rain and Wind for Maize and Cacao that provides abundant sustenance for the Maize People-Ixim Winaq who provide sacred sustenance to sustain the Kabʼawil through rituals and rites of sacrifice that shape the clouds that form the lightning and thunder that provide rain for the Cacao and Maize. It is then the Sky is cleared of clouds as the North Wind is called in to bring forth the flowering and fruiting of the Maize growing in la Milpa. This is the way of the Kabʼawil, Maize in la Milpa and the Ixim Winaq who form this triangle of reciprocity that creates great abundance in the World…

Kabʼawil are Deities that are complete-kabʼal in the sense they are those who are completely filled with sustenance through the reciprocal relation between Divinity; Kabʼawil and Humanity; Winaq and the Earth; Kabʼan-Ulew. Kabʼal signifies the idea of the fullness of abundance; the completeness of an order; the wealth of a people; the richness of a land; kabʼal-complete as in the head of maize replete with grain; the cacao pod filled with seeds; fruit trees burgeoning with fruit; clouds filled with water; nets teaming with fish, shrimp, and crabs.

The complete definition of Kabʼawil is more than enough for you to take up a deeper search into the meaning of this most enigmatic name-kabʼa of these Divinities-Kabʼawil-Deities-Kabʼawil.  Kabʼawil are those who might best  be understood as the ʼNamed Onesʼ who only want to hear their names named through their ritual remembrance and  invocation of the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ spoken in divine ways. These names of the Kabʼawil ask to be pronounced in sacred ways in which the sacred names the Divine Ancestors and Kabʼawil were first pronounced at the very beginning of the Popol Wuj with the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ of the Divine Ancestors and their Kabʼawil known as the Divine Twins: Kabʼawil by having the number Two-Kaʼibʼ being transformed into a ʼdivine agentʼ by adding the suffix –il at the end of the name as in Kabʼawil.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Kʼabʼawil are those who are brought into being through the Nawal Powers of Transformation that is one of the divine capacities of the Twins and Twinship that are the Powers of Creation that are experienced as the Nawal Powers of Transformation of Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ukʼuʼx Ulew as  Jun Raqan Kaqulja who  become Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz, Nikʼaj Taqʼaj and Ukʼuʼx Cho-Ukʼuʼx Palo Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz who become Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatzʼ who becomes Nakxit Qʼuqʼkumatz who becomes Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij Quetzalcoatl of Tollan Tzuy-Wa who becomes a Nim Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz who the Ancient Word says changes and transforms in magical ways as the Nim Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz who is a Kabʼawil who is Nawal Winaq or Nawinaq!

To be a Kabʼawil is to exist through the Nawal Ways of Transformation that are also seen and known as Ancestral Change within Change in order to transform and change the Sky-Earth in divine ways that are magical ways. The prime of example of this is the Maize Plant as it changes on the outside of the husk as the cane, leaves, tassel, corn silk, and roots change to transform on the outside while the heads of maize change and transform in the inside within the husk in which the ʼone seedʼ that was planted has become 800 seeds on each and every head of corn. This change within change is known as ʼjaloj-kʼexojʼ and is a true manifestation of the divine nature of maize because of the way great abundance is created from just one small spark of life so that ʼone becomes manyʼ which is exactly what essence of being a Kabʼawil is all about!

Kabʼawil then emanate a sense of ʼTwo-ness-Kaʼibʼʼ that gives them the sense of ʼcompletenessʼ found in the divine sense of ʼtwinsʼ and complimentary ʼtwinshipʼ as coming from Two-Kaʼibʼ as  the Two that is deified to become a Kabʼawil.

Kabʼawil are those who are the very essence from which comes all the Forming and Shaping of Creation through the Formation-Generation that sprouts forth in the Sky-Earth through the balancing and the harmonizing of the Twinning of Duality and all the endless forms it takes in the Sowing and  the Dawning of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea; Kaj-Ulew; Cho-Palo.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
It is the Two-ness of the Kabʼawil that bring forth the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings into the light of existence out of the darkness of non-existence to bring forth the sprouting out of  the Trees and Vine; Men and Women; Maize and Cacao; Sun and Moon; Heat and Moisture; Wind and Rain; Life and Death; Earth and Sky; Sky and Water; Rain and Sun; Dew and Drought; Mother and Father; Word and Story; Song and Dance; Day and Night on and on and on as the manifestation, revelation, and expression of  Two-ness of the Kabʼawil with their Dual Powers; Twin Powers found throughout  this  Book of Counsel; this Council Book with its many names both sacred and profane of the Sacred and Divine that lead to the Creation and Formation of  Divinity known as Kabʼawil.

Let us move quickly into a deeper understanding the Divine Twins who are the Hero Twins of Popol Wuj who are named by this Sacred Text as Kabʼawil for it is they who are Two who speak and act as One those making them divine in every way.

En Media Res: In the Middle of the Myth

So let us place ourselves in the middle of this myth that is a plot in order for you to understand where we are before taking up the road with the Hero Twins in the direction they are moving. And where we are moving is down the road with the Hero Twins each shouldering a blowgun on their way to take Wuqubʼ Kaqix out of his Nance Tree; his Tapʼal Tree where he takes his mid-day meal of bitter, tart coastal fruit a top the giant Nance Tree where he is perched upon his throne above the Jungle Kingdom over which he reigns as its Sovereign Lord and Ruler.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Wuqubʼ Kaqix sees himself as the light of both Sun and Moon. He imagines himself so because of his bright shining wealth and bejeweled adornment. This is the Lord of Bling who loves to show off his Silver Nose that shines like the Moon. His Turquoise Eyes that shimmer like splendid pools of turquoise water. His Jade Necklace and Jade Earrings that provide him, Seven Macaw-Wuqubʼ Kaqix with a most resplendent reminder of his eternal existence as a Noble Lord of a Noble Lineage of Maya Lords who as a Divine Ancestor will always be replaced by his beloved Descendants who remember him through songs of praise and incantations of remembrance.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix is a much adorned being as arrogant as he is vain. And then there are his bright red, yellow, and Maya blue feathers; his splendid, spectacular feathers that give him his ornithological name: Scarlet Macaw; Ara Macao. Ara Macao; Scarlet Macaws are Lords of the Jungle Canopy and Wuqubʼ Kaqix knows that he gorgeous to look upon, especially in flight. He will tell you as much for he is a braggart. And so it is in the wild where flocks of Scarlet Macaw make it know to all by their incessant call that ʼwe are hereʼ ʼwe are hereʼ ʼwe are hereʼ ʼlookʼ ʼlookʼ ʼlookʼ ʼlook at usʼ ʼlook at usʼ ʼare we not beautifulʼ ʼare we not magnificentʼ ʼare we not gloriousʼ  ʼlook at usʼ ʼlook at usʼ ʼlook upʼ ʼlook upʼ  ʼlook, look, lookʼ ʼlook, look, look at us flyʼ ʼlook at us fly across  the Heart of the Skyʼ? “Do we not rival the light of the Sun with our divine radiance?”  This is the way it can be with a large flock of Scarlet Macaw when they are at home in their Jungle Forest where they are safe and free to be whom they are; and whom they are; are those who are the Lords and Rulers of the Jungle Forest!

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Just look at his fine emerald jewels that he wears in his diadem that manifests his status as a divinity for he is the Nawal Transform of Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Heart of the Sky. Popol Wuj doesnʼt just come out and say it but we know it; we know it because of way this mythic figure acts and speaks. As a trickster deity Wuqubʼ Kaqix could not embody the Nawal of Tezcatlipoca more perfectly for the way he falls from grace to end up losing his wealth and power as is the way of Mesoamerican Trickster Figures who like Wuqubʼ Kaqix are given great power by Heart of the Sky to then lose it all through trickery to then end-up dying dead as it is said because he is not brought back to life to be placed as an Celestial Ancestor in the Night Sky.

Lord Seven Macawʼs power and rule are founded only in material wealth that he adorns himself in as a pretentious ruler whose authority is grounded in his being a boasting braggart who elevates himself over all others through his own self-aggrandizement. This is not the way of Lord Quetzalcoatl who is a hard working conscientious and caring ruler, which is the way it must be for those who wish to be practicing Noble Lords of the Empire of Quetzalcoatl known as Qʼuqʼkumatz to the Kʼicheʼ Maya and Kukulkan to the Yucatec Maya of Tollan Tzuy-Wa of the Great Post-Classic Maya World of Chichen Itza, Mayapan, Uxmal, Cobaʼ, Cozumel, Tulum, Chetumal, and the turquoise blue sea from where the Sun rises at Dawn from that sacred most place known as: the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij.

Lord Quetzalcoatl requires his Noble Lords to be initiated into the Noble Tradition of Tollan Tzuy Wa by ʼEntering the Wordʼ through acts of initiation that change and transform a Young Noble Prince through fasting and performing self-sacrifice.
