body:
Sipakna was by now completely inside the mountain. Only his kneecaps were showing, as if he had disappeared.

Just then the mountain came undone: it collapsed on his chest. No longer was he able to move. Right then and there, Sipakna turned to stone. The mountain swallowed him whole.

This then was the defeat of Sipakna by the Boys, by the Sons, ri Kʼajolabʼ: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Sipakna was the one known as Bʼanol Juyubʼ which is what made him the Maker of Mountains according to the ancestral meaning of the Ancient Word, Ancestral Account.

It was he, Sipakna, the Spiny One, the Smoking One who was known as Caiman Boy, Volcano Son; it was he that was the First Born Son-Nabʼeyal Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

It was he who was turned to stone beneath the mountain of Meʼawan, and there he continues to lay beneath this Broke-back; Bent-back Mountain of Maize, Meʼawan-Doubled-over stalk of Maize-Meʼoj Awan-Broken Cane is its name; the place where Sipakna was lured to his defeated to meet his death laid-out on his back.

It was just their ancestral powers of transformation-xa nawal- that brought about the ingenious deception that led to the defeat of the First Born Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix whoʼs conceit and deceit led to his own being deceived by those who conceived of a plan that was inspired by he who was known as the Mocker of Men; Heart of the Sky One-Footed Lightning Bolt Thunderer-Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja is just one of his many, many names of the Invisible One; the Invincible One who knew how to lose to win.

It was their nawal powers of enchantment that gave them the victory over the second one who manifest himself as the Big Man-Nimalaj Achi through Self-Magnification-Nimarisay ribʼ who was the Second One to be defeated; to be destroyed and disappeared by the Boys.

He who was the First Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix; he who made himself out to be greater than he was through his Self-Aggrandizement-Nimarisay ribʼ this was Sipakna who was transformed into a mountain of stone; he who was left to lie where he was led to die beneath the Mountain of Maize: Meʼawan.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
He who was lured inside a mountain a deceptive trap set by the Boys to be turned to stone because of his arrogant pride; his self inflation; Self-Glorification-Nimarisay ribʼ that brought about the end of his days.

ONE MORE ANCESTRAL TALE THEN SHALL WE TELL, this one speaks of Kabʼraqan; Earthquake Boy; the Two-Footed One; the Third of Three; the Second of Two Sons who said they were better than all the rest to then be set to the test to see if in truth he was the best of the Best.

Earthquake is his name; Kabʼraqan as he known, the One who came next, the Third of Three; Kabʼraqan is he who we shall speak of now to complete the telling of their death and defeat by the Boys, the Sons, known and named; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Earthquake or Kabʼraqan

This then is the Last of another Ancient Account of another Arrogant One of another filled with Pride and Conceit; One more False-faced Son; of the Three False-faced-Ones; Earthquake or Kabʼraqan is he who is the Last of Three.

It is of He that we shall relate of those who did vociferously state that they were the Greatest of All those who were Greater than Great; the Third of the Self-Magnifying Ones; the Second Son of the First One who said he was the Light of Sun; Light of the Moon when in fact he was the False Light of the Moon; False Light of the Sun; Wuqubʼ Kaqix was his name.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix is  the One who was taken out of his Tree; the arrogant Father of the Two Arrogant Sons; Wuqubʼ Kaqix, Sipakna, and now Kabʼraqan the Second of Two Sons of Seven Macaw the First of this Three to be defeated by the Hunters; the Hunted; the Hero Twins; this then is the Last Story of all Three; here we shall tell of  the Second Brother of the Big Three: the Giants of the Age of the Wooden People; the Sun of the Men of Tzʼite; Talking Tree; the Moon of  Women of Sibʼaq-Reeds that grow thick beside the Lakeshore abundant with life.

“I am the Leveler of Mountains-In yojol juyub-I am the Destroyer of Mountains; I am he who ʼfells mountainsʼ thus a ʼFeller of Mountainsʼ am I who takes Mountains from the very Heart of the Sky,” he said.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
But it was just Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who defeated Earthquake-Kabʼraqan-Two-Footed One, the Second Born Son of Seven Scarlet Macaw-ukʼabʼ ukʼajol Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

Those who spoke were Jun Raqan; Chʼipi Kaqulja; and Raxa Kaqulja when they spoke for Ukʼuʼx Kaj who told Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej just what to do next:

“The Second Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix, the Second Son of Seven Macaw is just another one, another one who must be defeated.”

“This is just my word-xawi nutzij, for it is no good what he does there on the Face of the Earth. They wish to surpass the Sun in power and importance, strength and majesty; and this is something that just cannot be.”

“Bring him down then, just take him down when you persuade him to accompany you over to were the Sun comes up; convince him to walk East with you over to the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij-the Place of Dawn as it is known!” said Juraqan when he spoke to the Two Boys, Two Sons.

“Very well then, You-Lal, oh Noble Lord; it is he, then, who must go. It is no good what we see in him. Do you not exist? Are you not the exalted one? Are you not the one who rises up higher than all the rest, you, oh Heart of the Sky-Lal Ukʼux Kaj?” said the Boys when they heard the word of Juraqan, the one known; the one named Jun Raqan-One-Footed One: Heart of Sky-Ukʼux Kaj-Heart of Heaven as his name is heard spoken.

And there Kabʼraqan was; out ʼLeveling Mountainsʼ across the land. It was just with the ʼSlightest Tap of his Footʼ on the ʼFace of the Earthʼ that he was able to ʼBring Downʼ Big Mountains, Small Mountains leveling them right ʼDown to the Groundʼ there wherever it was that he shook and shake the Earth causing it to quiver and quake as Kabʼraqan performed the task that was his to perform as the One who was the Second Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix: Earthquake his name; the Second of Two who knew what was his to do on the Face of the Earth: Uwach Ulew where he caused the Sky to shake and the Earth to quake as Earthquakes are called to do. This then was when the Boys met up with him:

“Where are you going there, you, oh Son; you, oh Boy-At Kʼajol?” they asked Kabʼraqan.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“Iʼm not going anywhere; Iʼm just bringing down the mountains; just leveling them down; just taking them down to the ground ʼfor All Time; for Eternityʼ chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; on the Footpath of the Sun; on Footpath of the Dawn as they say,” said Kabʼraqan thundering his voice real, real loud.

Chi Bʼe Qʼij, Chi Bʼe Saq

The saying: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq might be translated as ʼfor as long as Dawn Comes; for as long Sun Risesʼ it is a Traditional Maya oath or spell that makes folks know ʼthis is what I do and Iʼm not going anywhereʼ and Old Women and Old Men still say it when they take a ritual shot of liquor, letting it rip with a roar: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; for as long as Dawn walks the Path of the Sun; which is often heard in another version of the same: Raqan Qʼij; Raqan Saq which signifies: Footpath of the Sun; Footpath of the Dawn as a play on the expression performed throughout this recitation of Popol Wuj: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; ʼon the Path of the Sun; on the Path of the Dawnʼ which is to say for all time; which is to say for all eternity!

Which is to say: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; On the Footpath of the Sun; On the Footpath of the Dawn which is what Kabʼraqan roars to make the Earth quake and the Sky shake to let the Boys know that he is right there; which means he is right here; and, he isnʼt going anywhere: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq! Which is a truly Nawal Way to set up the story of his own death and destruction by letting everyone know from the start that this Boy known Earthquake is as tough as his Older Brother, Sipakna, who was the Number One Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who went down doing what was his to do in a world where oneʼs hunger and appetite tells us who we are by telling us what is ours in life to bring to fruition.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Popol Wuj, when it comes right down to it, is an Ancient Ancestral Account of Noble Lords fasting while walking on pilgrimage in Sacred Ways in accordance with the Sacred Count of Days while giving worship and praise to their Kabʼawil and Divine Ancestors by performing self-sacrifice to nourish and nurture the Kabʼawil to sustain them with their Sacred Sustenance of the body and blood of human beings; human being who were formed and shaped from the divine essence of maize and water; flesh and blood. These were used by the Former; the Shaper to form and shape the body and blood of the First Four Men who were then called to perform self-sacrifice with Maguey Spines and Stingray Spines.

So do realize the Boys are performing sacrifice that is founded in hunger for that which creates the flesh and blood of Wuqubʼ Kaqix: the Golden Yellow Fruit of Tapaʼl; the fish and crab of Sipakna-Cipacatli-Crocodile-Caiman Boy and now Kabʼraqan-Earthquake who eats Birds; Birds that will be what the Older Brothers Jun Bʼatzʼ; Jun Chowen; Birds that Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will hunt for them to provide them with their Sustenance!

Two-Footed One-Kabʼraqan-Earthquake:

One of the Eternal Ones of the Sun and the Dawn

So it was then when Kabʼraqan spoke with Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej:

“Where are you Boys from?  I donʼt know your faces; I donʼt know your names. What do they call you? When then are your names?” asked Kabʼraqan.

“We have no names; we are just hunters; we are just blowgun boys, we snare birds with our gypsum line; indeed, we are those of the Mountain; we just trap up on the Mountainside. Just poor orphans is all we are-xa Oj Mebʼa. There is nothing that is ours, you, Boy, you, Son, At, Kʼajol,” said the Boys before continuing on.

“We just wander along from place to place shouldering our blowguns. We just pass through the Small Mountains, the Big Mountains, wandering and walking is our way,” said the Boys.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“Well, for one who levels mountains, we can tell you for certain that way over there-pointing with their blowgun-there is one really Big Mountain that we watch grow and grow; it just keeps growing, just keeps goinʼ up; it just grows taller and taller all the time; it never stops it just climbs and climbs, that mountain over there, it is real big,” said the Boys staring off in the direction of the Coming Out Place of the Sun; just tapping the soft silky dust making it jump-up; puff, puff.

“Over there, well, we have no luck over there; over there, there arenʼt even one or two birds that weʼve snared for ourselves, You, oh Boy-At Kʼajol. Is it really true that you bring down ʼallʼ the mountains, Boy? ” asked Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej defiantly, doubtfully to which Kabʼraqan responded just the same.

“Is it really true that you ʼsawʼ this mountain that you speak of? Where is it? I want to see it for myself. I will take it down. I will shake it down. I will just grind it right down to the ground. Where did you say you saw it?” asked Kabʼraqan-the Two-Footed One-Earthquake as this Destroyer Mountain was known; as this Leveler of Mountains was named.

“It is just a little bit over that way, it just grows and grows up above all the rest; truly high does it climb that mountain there; it just puffs and puffs its way up into the Sky; it just climbs and climbs way up high; itʼs over there towards the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij-Place of the Dawn,” said Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

“Utz! Great! So then show me our road so we can be on our way!” he said to the Two Boys, the Two Sons; chi Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ.

“Not so fast, you must just come over here to walk between the two of us. One to the left side; one to the right; after all we have our blowguns so if there are any birds to be had, then, we will be ready to take a shot,” they said.

Happily, contentedly they went along testing their blowguns as they made their way but when they blew on their blowguns no earthen clay shot came out of their tubes it was their puff, puffing on their blowguns that took the birds down;  which left Kabʼraqan truly astonished.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They just puffed on their long wooden tubes; they just blew hard on the mouth of their blowguns and…puuj… puuj…They just blasted bursts of nawal breath through their enchanted blowpipes, and the birds fell from the limbs of the trees fluttering down to the ground; poof in the dust…chimalmat…flat on their back.

This simply astonished Kabʼraqan who was truly astounded by all the Boys said and did. And so it was they went along towards the Coming Out Place of the Sun hunting all along the way, taking their time enjoying the fine day.

It wasnʼt long before they had all the birds they needed to do what they were called to do by the One-footed-One there in the Heart of the Sky; Jun Raqan Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

So this then was when they went to work drilling fire and in no time their birds would be ready for roasting over the fire they drilled with cunning and skill.

They blanketed one of the birds with a sacred sort of soft silky soil known as ʼsajkabʼ white-earthʼ which when wettened with water it becomes a curious class calc; a gypsum coat that serves as a simple sort of plaster. But, when it is left to dry it becomes a fine, fluffy kind of divine dusty dirt similar if not the same as a tasteless, odorless, plain, pallid talc; really itʼs just deadly white earth and that is why they call it: sajkabʼ.

Once they basted the bird with sajkabʼ they placed it with the others to roast ever so slowly over the bright burning coals of their red hot fire.

“This one is for him, so that he might hunger for it, so that he might devour it. We will just whet his appetite, then, when he takes in the aroma to awaken his desire for a nice piece of meat,” said the Boys.

“So then it shall be the white earth-sajkabʼ with which we cover his bird that shall be his defeat; for the earth that we cook his bird will be the same earth we cover him up when we bury him beneath the Earth.”

“Indeed, great wisdom comes to us through the Great Sages, the Great Knowers-Nima Etaʼmanel, those known; those named One Former, One Shaper-Jun Tzʼaq, Jun Bʼit.”

“May it be so! May it come to pass! To the Sowing! To the Dawning! Ta Chawaxoq! Ta Saqiroq!” said the Two Boys, the Two Sons.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“Because it is just our heartsʼ desire to take a bite of meat. Truly, itʼs natural to enjoy a bit of roasted flesh. This is just the longing of the heart; like that of Kabʼraqan that longs for a tasty treat; Kabʼraqan who craves for nothing more than to eat a juicy piece of roasted meat,” said Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej when they spoke to one another there watching over their beguiling birds that simmered so sweet over their enchanting fire.

Kabʼraqan just stood there staring, salivating as he took in the captivating aroma that sparked his appetite that was soon set on fire.

The Boys just turned the birds over ever so slowly in the reddish-orange flames that glowed with the rich warm heat of their fire; those birds were just roasty-toasty, browning so easy as they cooked to perfection; juicy fat just dripped from their crispy, crackling backs; truly, the sweet smelling grease just sputtered and spattered to flame up out of that delectable fire to release an enchanting aroma of an ancient, ancestral kind of primordial desire.

It was just because of the delicious aroma of the roasting meat and the spellbinding scent of those sweet smelling birds with their sumptuous grease that Kabʼraqan now hankered for so ravenously for just a bite of this brazed birdʼs succulent meat.

If only he could just try a taste of that tantalizing treat; if only he could calm his fierce longing; his ferocious hankering hunger for now his mouth watered for just a itty-bitty bite of the roasting meat with its crackling gristle and fizzling fat that fizzed and sizzled as the birdsʼ golden backs browned; as their skins crackled as the grease spattered and  sputtered over the fire that now ignited a profoundly primitive flame that now burnt bright as some sort of ancient ancestral fire of primordial desire.

A desire lit by the primal power of fire that now burned as an ancient ancestral desire; a desire that hungered to devour all that was within reach of Kabʼraqanʼs will to fulfill that ravenous longing for what the Boys brazed on their fire; their fire that now bloomed like a flower whose succulent scent had Kabʼraqan in the grasp of its power.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
For now Kabʼraqan was not only caught but captured in their trap: the trap of appetite. The trap of appetite the Boys had set just for Kabʼraqan; the trap of appetite that now had Earthquake in its grip; the trap of appetite that Kabʼraqan could no longer slip.

Kabʼraqan now just swallowed his drool; he just downed his dribble, as he began to drown in his very own spittle; as the meat grilled, as the fat sizzled; the grease spat and then lit in the flames of the fire that burned in the pit over which the roasting birds were turned on the spit. Now there was no turning back; no way to quit so they kept up with the plan that had become quite fun as spun those birds little by little as the fire popped and fizzled.

This spellbinding spinning of their spell was spun; for Kabʼraqan was now completely undone by their clever cunning; their ingenious craft of luring in their prey.  Which was easy to see was working by the devastating way the poor Boy that leveled mountain was now knocked flat by his destructive powers that now took the form of his ferocious hunger and the humiliating way he was left low by the way his heart now hankered for the least piece of meat.

Now it was he who was destroyed by his desire to destroy the work of his older brother the Maker of Mountains; for it was now those who made mountains and destroyed mountain should be made to become mountains by these Boys who laid these arrogant ones as low as low can be.

All of this had been contemplated to be brought to completion by these two charming beguilers those Ancient Ancestral Hunters; the Blowgun Boys known as the First One and Second Son Little Jaguar Deer. It was just through their enchanting words spoken over their beguiling fire that bewitched those birds that they hunted with their ancestral powers.

So then, they, the Boys, asked Kabʼraqan something that spoke to him in a visceral sort of primal way; a question that spoke to the truth that he bore within him as the essence of his soul; a truth that now bound him to the Earth in an essential sort of elemental kind of way; a question and an answer that would name him in a simple yet substantial sort of way.

body:
This then was when they asked: “What then is your food; what then is your sustenance; what is it that is yours, Kabʼraqan?”

The poor Boy just answered wantonly as he was now completely transfixed by his ancient ancestral appetite: “Truly delicious do I find the aroma that I smell now. That which is roasting here before me is truly what I desire to eat. Why donʼt you just give me a little taste; just a bit of this sweet smelling meat?” he replied with such humility.

Earthquake Boy, Earthquake Son was now utterly humbled by his horrific hunger; Kabʼraqan found himself to be totally devastated, destroyed by his desire; knocked down; laid low; just leveled was he, the Two-Footed-One, who was now overwhelmed by his own appetite and its craving for meat.

Kabʼraqan was definitively demolished his false sense of superiority that had always ruled his self-aggrandizing delusion of grandeur and his grandiose illusion of power and majesty.

This, then, is when they gave Kabʼraqan that browned basted bird that they had expressly prepared for him to eat, which was his destruction and defeat as the destroyer of mountains; Kabʼraqan, the shaker and quaker of the Earth who was the maker of Earthquakes.

This then was when he finished off that whole bird without saying a word. Kabʼraqan devoured the specially brazed bird he was give to eat without ever tasting his defeat.

An Alternative Telling of the fall of Kabʼraqan

He just smacked his lips; he just sucked his teeth; he just licked his fingers as he wiped his cheeks; never had he ever tasted something as delicious as the nicely coated back of that brazed bird and its roasty-toasty meat.

He took what was given just as he ate all that was offered; the bird they gave him was the one they plastered with the white-earth-sajkʼabʼ and that gypsum baste might be what gave that the rich taste to that roasted bird in white-earth leaving it succulent and sweet.

When they finished eating and they continued on walking until they came to the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij-the Dawning Place of the Sun, in the East; there where the Big Mountain, the Dawning Mountain stood high above all the rest of the Mountain-Plain.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This Dawning Mountain is known as Saqiribʼal or Sajribʼal. Now they stood at its feet; at the Foot of the Mountain; PaRaqan Juyubʼ is where they stood, the three of them there.

This, then, was when Kabʼraqan could go no farther. This is where he felt that his strength had abandoned him; the vigor within his two feet was now complete; for his strength was gone.

Just like a pile of rocks was the way he now felt in his feet, in his hands, then his knees; his ankles they buckled; his body seized; then ever so slowly he began to fall as he completely collapse. Before he knew it, it was he that was brought down without making a sound; just demolished, destroyed like a Great Mountain Kabʼraqan was knocked to the ground.

No longer was he capable of making his way. It was the sajkabʼ with which they blanketed his bird, the divine white dirt; the sacred white earth that was his downfall; the doing of the Boys the calling of their Father; their Lord and Ruler in the Heart of the Sky; Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

Kabʼraqan couldnʼt do a thing to the Great Mountain that stood before them. He did not destroy it as he wished he could. He did not demolish it like he thought he would. He didnʼt even try to level it as he thought he should. It was over; his power and strength were gone; gone for good.

Just like a captive was he bound by the Boys, the Sons. They tied his arms behind his back; they coupled his hands together to then knot them at the wrists.

Then they bound and tied his ankles together like a war captive; like a slave; like an offering to be offered up for sacrifice was he subjugated.

This then was when they threw him down and buried him in the ground; in the White Earth; under the Dawning Mountain: Sajribʼal.

Thus was the defeat of Kabʼraqan; it was the doing of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who did innumerable, uncountable things here on the Face of the Earth; waral Chuwach Ulew.

Now we shall tell of the birth of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej; since we have first told of the defeat of Wuqubʼ Kaqix-Seven Scarlet Macaw along with Sipakna-Volcano Son, and Kabʼraqan-Earthquake Son here on the Face of the Earth; waral Chuwach Ulew.

Rox

Ixim Winaq   Maize People

body:
Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu: One and Seven Ancient Ancestors of Tula-Tollan, Ancient Hunter of the Blowgun, Blowgun Hunters of the Sacred Place Thick with Reeds, Ancestral Fathers of the Land Thick with Abundance, Place Thick with Life living in the Reeds: known and named as Pu-Tula-Tollan; the Mythic City of Ancestral Perfection where the Arts and Sciences of the Mesoamerica reach a State of Sublime Intelligence; Aesthetic Beautification, Scientific Sophistication, Astronomical Precision, Calendrical and Architectural Perfection, Mythical Imagination, Theatrical Tradition, Song and Dance Drama, Performance of Mythic Recitation, Ancestral Practices of Initiation through Peregrination, Long Distant Warrior-Merchant Tradition. These are aspects of Mesoamerican Social and Cultural Traditions found here in the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj that come from Olmec Origins on the Gulf Coast and from Teotihuacan in the Central Highlands of Mexico and Guatemala as well as Mixtec-Zapotec Tradition of Oaxaca. All of these Mesoamerican Traditions will influence the Maya of Southern Mesoamerica who will adopt and adapt Social and Cultural influence they find in the Mesoamerica World through Long Distant Trade and Cultural Exchange. This is adoptive and adaptive way of the Maya continues to amongst the Maya of Southern Mesoamerica to this very day. The Popol Wuj is an expression of this cultural capacity and adaptive capability of the Maya to his very day.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu and their sons Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are those of Teotihuacan the First Tula-Tollan; these are those of Cholula-Chollan; these are those of Chichen Itzaj and Mayapan; these are those of Palenque, Tikal, el Mirador, and Copan. These are those of an Ancient Mesoamerican City of Great Splendor where the ancestral image of ancestral perfection was realized by the Splendid Sublime City and its Rulers and those Rulersʼ Vassals and Subjects known as Daughters and Sons who worked and played with their Noble Lords to reach a state of precious perfection right here on the Face of the Earth.

body:
These are those who are Protectors of Maize, Guardians of the Sacred Sustenance as they are named; the Father, the Uncle as they are known; One Ancient Ancestral Father of Maize, Seven Ancient Ancestral Father of Maize known from here on as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. These Two are the First Fathers of the Maize People or Ixim Winaq: Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are their names, the names of the Fathers of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

These then are the names of their Parents-kikajaw-the Parents, the Primordial Pair, the Ancestral Mother-Father known as Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane; the First Father, the First Mother, the Parents-Kikajaw: Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane are the Divine Ancestral Pair; Grandmother, Grandfather of the Maize People, those of the Saq Kʼaslem-Divine Life, Sacred Life, Bright Life for they are those of the Face of the Earth, those of the Milpa and Maize, these who are those who are empowered with the magical powers of transformation and creation: Nawal Winaq.

Nawal Winaq are Divine Ancestors who embody the transformative energies of renewal and regeneration on the Face of the Earth. They embody the ancestral powers of the mythic imagination and initiatory transformation of the life affirming forces of light and life; they are Divine Ancestors of the Living Light of the Sun and Moon; warmth of the Sun and pull of the Moon; the constancy of the Sun and transforming essence of the ever-changing Moon.

The personified image of the Sun and the Moon  live on in the face of the Ancestors  seen in face of their Descendants as well as  their harvest of Maize and Cacao that is transformed into sacred sustenance through the work and care of the Men and Women; Boys and Girls; Grandmother, Grandfathers; Chuch-Qajaw. The ʼhard kernelsʼ of maize and ʼhard beansʼ of cacao live on as replacements of the original ʼkernels of maizeʼ and ʼbeans of cacaoʼ in a world where and in which Maize and Cacao are personified by Maize Deities and Cacao Divinities.

body:
These Divinities of Sacred Sustenance are known in Popol Wuj as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu for it is they who are reborn in the shape and form of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who will become the Sun and Moon of the Era and Age of the People of Sacred Sustenance: Ixim Winaq known as People of Maize; Maize People

Their ancestral soul that lives within the Maize Beings is eternal, it does not die; their transforming essence is experienced as their Nawal embodied in the sparkling green resplendence of a jade bead; the blood red remembrance of a Tzʼite bean; the Maize Shoot of the Sprouting Seed all of which are manifestations of the eternal return of the Divine Ancestors through their ritual renewal as the Descendants known as ʼkʼexel-replacementsʼ as ʼketal-signsʼ as ʼkitzijel-word-spark-essence-flowerʼ all of whom will be with us all along the way.

This Ancestral Essence of Maize is alive within Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu and their Boys, their Sons: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. Their essence is Life and Rebirth and so they embody the eternal return of the bright life of the Dawning and the Sowing for even if they are killed their Nawal essence, character, or nature known as ʼukʼojeʼikʼ will find a way to come back to life through some sort of magical means of transformation.

THIS THEN IS WHEN WE WILL NAME THE NAMES NEXT OF THE FATHERS OF JUNAJPU, IXBʼALAMKEJ; let us name the names of their Fathers; the names of the Fathers of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Let us drink to him; let us just make a toast to it being told; to its being spoken; to its being said; the telling of the tale that tells of the begetting of the Boys, the Sons, the Twins; the account of Jun Junajpu and his engendering of the ʼMagical Transformingʼ Twins; of his begetting of his ʼNawalʼ Sons: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Just the ʼhalfʼ of it we shall tell; just a part of their ancestral story we shall tell; the ʼhalfʼ that gives an account of their Fathers is what we shall tell.

Here then is itʼs telling; here then is itʼs being told; the Ancestral Story, the Ancient Account of those who are named Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

body:
In the darkness, in the night-chi qʼequmal, chi aqʼabʼal-were they born, the Boys, the Sons; those who were born Twins; Twin Boys, Twin Sons known as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. These Boys, these Sons were begotten to their Father Xpiyakok while being born to their Mother IxMuqane.

So then this Jun Junajpu had just two children and the two of them were Boys, his Sons: Jun Bʼatzʼ known as One Monkey is the name of the First-born-Son; Nabʼeal, while Jun Chowen spoken of as One Artisan is the name of the Second-born Son; Kabʼal.

Here then is the name of their Mother: IxBʼaqiyalo; White Egret Woman of the Great Water Sea; IxBʼaqiyalo-White Bone Woman of the Delta Sea; White Egret Woman of the Great Estuary Sea-Yalo-Palo as she is spoken of, as she is named, the First Woman, the First Wife of Jun Junajpu as she is known.

Now this Wuqubʼ Junajpu had no Wife, he was just a Single Man. And being the second born it was just in his nature to remain a Young Man of marrying age.

Great Thinkers-E Nimaʼq AjNaʼoj-Great Sages were they; great then was their Knowing and great, too, was their Understanding-Ketamabʼal-Genius, for it was they who were Great Diviners-E Nikwachinel-Mid-most Seers here on the Face of the Earth.

Seers who were known to be Knowers; Seers who were Knowers who were seen and known to be Diviners; Diviners whose sight reached both far and near; for truly vast was their vision; for truly infinite was their sight so that endless was  their knowing here on the Face of the Earth.

They were good-natured and they were well-trained; properly instructed were they in all they came to say and do; perform and create. They taught their arts to their Boys; they passed on their skills-nawikil-their knowledge to their Sons Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen: the First Sons of Jun Junajpu known as the Older Ones.

They were Flute Players; e AjSuʼ

They were Singers; e AjBʼix

They were Blowgunners; e AjPu

They were Scribes and Painters; e AjTzʼibʼ.

They were Carvers, Sculptors, and Mask-makers; e AjKʼot

They were Jade-workers; e AjXit and Silversmiths; e AjPuwaq, as well.

body:
This is what became of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; One Monkey, One Artisan as these Boys were known to be: flautists, singers, shooters, blow-gun hunters, scribe, painters, sculptors, carvers, jade-workers, jewelers, artists, artisans, performers, dancers, and musicians.

This is how these Twins were known, those who were the Boys of Jun Junajpu as these first two Sons are named: Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; One Spun Thread; One Ancestor; One Howler; One Monkey, One Artisan.

Now as for Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; well, they just Played-Dice; xa Sakʼ, they just Played-Ball; xa Chaaj; everyday they threw dice, everyday they played ball:  xa Sakʼ, xa Chaaj.

Just two-on-two did they play their games; in duos as doubles, in pairs as partners, in twos as twins they played every day, day after day they played in a complementary sort of way; as balanced pairs they played; as caring companions is the way they played; as they played in harmony; competitive yet collaborative                 is the way they played day after day.

It was the four of them that gathered together to play two-on-two; it was those who were the First Fathers of the First Sons who played together as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen to compete with one another everyday in astounding and astonishing feats of play on their ancestral ballcourt that they called-Jom-Ballcourt-Burial Groundsʼ pronounced just like ʼhomeʼ.

One day Wok-Laughing Falcon landed there above their Ballcourt-Jom, and seeing that they were playing he stopped to watch the way they play their rubberball game as they played one another as complementary companions-kikʼulelaj kibʼ.

Wok, Laughing Falcon, was a Seer-Ilol ke-making him the Worker-usamajel-the Messenger of Jun Raqan, Chʼipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja, these were those known as the Heart of the Sky; Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

Now for Wok, this Laughing Falcon, it was not far for him to arrive on the Face of the Earth; nor was it distant for him to descend there to Xibʼalbʼa: Place of Fear, Place of Intimidation, and Place of Initiation.

body:
In an instant the Messenger-Wok-Laughing Falcon arrived there in the Heart of the Sky Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Heart of the Sky where he acted as the Messenger-Samajel-Worker of Jun Raqan, Chʼipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja Wok who he arrived with there in the Ukʼuʼx Kaj as great Seer-Ilol who saw everything that went on in the land of the living and the land of the dead; on the Face of the Earth just ʼbelow the Skyʼ and in Xibʼalbʼa just ʼbelow the Earthʼ.

For Wok, being a Falcon, it wasnʼt far to fly from here in the Heart of the Sky to there on the Face of the Earth; nor was it far to fly from here on the Face of the Earth to down there in Xibʼalbʼa.

In an instant Wok could fly up into the Sky with Jun Raqan; and so it was that Wok could fly back and forth from up in the Sky with Jun Raqan and then down into Xibʼalbʼa with those of Xibʼalbʼa seeing everything there was to see with the vision of a ʼSeer-Ilolʼ which was the work and way of Wok who saw all their was to see as Wok the Ilol; Wok the Seer.

Now it was Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who remained on the Face of the Earth for a long time after the death of IxBʼaqiyalo-White Egret Woman, the Mother of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen, the Monkey Twins, the Artisan Twins: One Howler, One Artisan as they are known.

IxBʼaqiyalo: White Bone Woman of the Great Water

IxBʼaqiyalo is also known as White Bone Woman of the Great Water, in which Ya-Lake and Palo-Sea combine to create Yalo-Great Water in the form of a Lake or perhaps in the shape of an Estuary where the Snowy White Egret People live out their lives.

Their light white bodies are formed from weightless hollow bones and bodies conformed from almost no flesh; these divine ancestral birds are avian beings that live by the shores of large bodies of placid pacific water.

These birds canʼt take much wind and live almost like ghost beings because they are so light consisting of bodies shaped with puffy fluffy snowy white feathers and a yellow beak that spears minnow and fish like true warriors.

body:
Because IxBʼaqiyalo was a Snowy White Egret she lived up on the Highland Lakes alongside the lakeshore reeds and down on the Seaside Estuaries where there was nice calm water for her to fish amongst the thick reeds. These lake and estuary reeds were teaming with a great multitude of minnows, snails, shrimp, langoustine, and crabs which is the sacred sustenance of Mesoamerican women and men.

It was the women in particular and old men and children who created ʼfish traps or corral-kokʼ amongst the reeds where the minnows and crabs and shrimpʼ were rounded up and harvested by old men and boys in dugout canoes that drove and corralled the minnows, fish, shrimp and crabs into the fish traps or weirs or corrals formed in the reeds.

This is where IxBʼaqiyalo would go to get her fill of what the people gathered together form themselves.  IxBʼaqiyalo dies but we donʼt know why but we do know she is the embodiment of sacred sustenance for she must become the white bone of white maize or some such nawal transformation of the Divine Ancestors being transformed into sacred sustenance.

Since the rubber ballcourt-jom where the Fathers and Sons played their rubberball game was there beside the road to Xibʼalbʼa where the ball players up on the Face of the Earth were heard playing ball all day long with the bouncing about of their rubberball.

They were heard playing ball by Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame-Lord One Death, Lord Seven Death, the Noble Rulers of Xibʼalbʼa who did not  like their jumping up and down and running all about.

There is a ubiquitous pun formed continuously with this formation of  ʼon the road to Xibʼalbʼa or pubʼeʼel Xibʼalbʼa-and the blowgun of the Boys written both pubʼ or ubʼ  so that the contraction that is formed by ʼon the roadʼ or  ʼpa ubʼeʼelʼ becomes  ʼpubʼeʼel-on the roadʼ  and ubʼ blowgunʼ which is heard as the pun throughout the telling of the story of the Boys walking on the road shouldering their blowguns as they make their way to and then through Xibʼalbʼa.

body:
I mention this so the reader gets a taste of all that is constantly lost in translation that we will continue to put on the table when able so you get a sense of constant and continuous word play that takes place throughout the endless play-on-words in this masterpiece of Ancient American Indigenous Literature that is formed and shaped from Sacred Secret Speech that makes the Popol Wuj one of this Worldʼs Masterpieces of Mythic Literature and Language.

“What is going on up there on the Face of the Earth? Who are they to jump up and down the way they do; running up and down yelling and screaming causing such a racket; I just canʼt take it; I just canʼt hack it! Go up there to send for them so they can come down here where they can play ball with us. Just let them be defeated by us here on our court with our play, that is all I have to say,” said those of Xibʼalbʼa.

“We just arenʼt respected by them; they show no humility, no regard for who we are; they have no consideration for us anymore with the way they beat their ball over our heads,” said all of those there of Xibʼalbʼa.

This then was when they gathered their thought together when they made Council with one another, those who were named Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame those who were the Supreme Judges of the Word; those who were the ʼsupreme judges of the word-e nimaʼq qʼatol tzijʼ as it is said.

This then was when they gathered together to consider and contemplate their thoughts in council there in Xibʼalbʼa. These were those named Jun Kame-One Death, Wuqubʼ Kame-Seven Death.

It was they who were the supreme judges of the word; Lord One Death, Lord Seven Death; they were the ultimate authority over the judgment of the truth which made them those with the authority to ʼweigh the word-qʼatabʼal tzij-measure the truthʼ and this power to ʼweight the word; judge the truthʼ gave them the power to judge and rule all others with their word and its weight to balance the truth; which was the balance of the word.

body:
As for all the other Lords of Xibʼalbʼa, they were each assigned a sacred cargo that was carried out as a divine obligation; that was borne out as an ancestral burden to bear as the Lords of Death and Disease who performed their duties and obligation under power and authority of  the Lords One Death, Seven Death-Ajawabʼ Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; who carried the fate of the living on their shoulders and fulfilled their sacred burden as the ʼsupreme judges of the wordʼ  by bearing the destiny of the Living to its natural fruition in Death.

It was they, the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa, who bore upon their shoulders the burden of the ancestral offices and hierarchical ordering of the divine offices of death and disease with their sacred order of authority and rule over a particular realm of disease and specific dominion of death.

The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were paired in pairs and coupled in couples who were called upon to fulfill their sacred obligation and divine burden as the Noble Lords and Rulers of Death and Disease who ruled over the lives of the living on the Face of the Earth.

It was this ancestral power of rule and authority over death and disease that each of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa exercised over the living on the surface of the earth that came to the direct attention of the Supreme Lords of Xibʼalbʼa known as Ajaw Jun Kame, Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kame spoken of as Lord One Death, Lord Seven Death.

Let us then name their names of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa so we can move on to their playing ball with the innocent ones and naive ones who lived on the Face of the Earth in the Land of the Living; those known as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; they of the Mountain Places; they of the Canyon Country; Settled and Sedentary not knowing their Ways were not the Ways of Others; and, the Ways of the Other was Not their Way of Life, Death, and Rebirth. This then is the Ancient, Ancestral Account of the Living and the Dead.

The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were given their power and authority over their Sacred Burden of Divine Office of Death and Disease; each and every Lord of the Underworld was appointed Sovereign Rule-Ajawarem over Illness and Accident by those who were named Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame.

body:
There were those Lords named Xikʼiri Pat; Kuchuma Kikʼ whose Divine Office; Sacred Burden pertained to ʼletting or drawingʼ blood and ʼgathering or collectingʼ blood to heal those whose blood was ill.

So then came next Ajal Puj-Lord Pus and Ajal Qʼana-Lord Jaundice; these Lords-Ajawabʼ were given the authority over the swelling up of people; they caused pus to ooze from their legs; they caused their face to turn yellow;  Jaundice is the name of the disease of their domain.

That then is the rule and authority; the burden and cargo of the rule and sovereignty of Ajal Puj; Ajal Qʼana; Lord Pus, Lord Jaundice.

The next Lords of Xibʼalbʼa named here are those known as Chʼamiyabʼaq, Chʼamiyajolom; Lord Bone Staff, Lord Skull Staff; they are the guardians and gatekeepers that act as the wardens of Xibʼalbʼa: their scepters, their staffs-chʼamiy are made of skulls-jolom and bones-baq.

These are the staff-bearers of Xibʼalbʼa whose cargo it is to make people grow thin; to then transform them into skeletons; these unfortunate souls just end-up as bones; they just end-up as skulls so that at the end of their life they just end-up as ʼskull and bonesʼ known as ʼjolom, baqʼ with no flesh at all.

When these skeletal beings died it was just their skeleton that was taken away. This then was what they reigned over as Lords of Disease; whose cargo; whose duty; whose office-upatan was that of the skeletons: skull and bones.

Chʼamiyabʼaq; Chʼamiyajolom were the Staff Bearers of Xibʼalbʼa: they bore the Staff of Bones, Staff of Skulls for the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Ajawabʼ Xibʼalbʼa.

These Lords of Xibʼalbʼa where known as the Staff Bearers of Xibʼalbʼa; Skull-Jolom and Bone-Baq were their emblem of office, Jolom; Baq were just the symbols of their Divine Office as the Guardians and Gatekeepers of Xibʼalbʼa; Chʼamiyabʼaq, Chʼamiyajolom were the Wardens of the Land of the Dead.

These were their positions of power and authority over Death borne out in their names Lord Bone Staff, Lord Skull Staff; Chʼamiyabʼaq, Chʼamiyajolom, as they are invoked, as they are named, as they are known.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Those that came next were Ajal Mes; Ajal Toqʼobʼ Lord Filth-maker, Lord Back-stabber they were those known as Lord Slander, Lord Favor who created conflict wherever they were called. Their burden of office was just causing hostility and hatred amongst people by digging up filth on oneʼs rival either behind the house of an adversary or in front of the house of an enemy. They were there to make a ʼmessʼ of anotherʼs life by doing some nasty ʼfavorʼ or just sowing-strife to create enmity and ill-will.

No matter where it was that these slanderers met they created mocking malice, ill-will, and cruel ridicule by bating friends into becoming bickering enemies.

These endless wars of hatred and hostility were always founded in ʼtrash-talkingʼ and ʼback-stabbingʼ activities that came to fruition in low-life, low-life filth that called for fatal sorts of favors; favors that asked somebody to cause somebody else to ended-up laying face down in the dirt or face-up by the side the road; perfectly still because of being perfectly dead at the bottom of a ravine or some out of the way place like a gully or a gorge or a gulch.

This is the authority given to Ajal Mes; Ajal Toqʼobʼ, as they are called. They were true Trash-Talkers completely competent and capable of completing evil-errands, and doing others a fatal favor!

Next comes the naming of those rulers of death and disease known as Ajaw Xik; Ajaw Patan; Lord Hawk, Lord Wing, Lord Messenger; Lord Merchant, Lord Cargo-Carrier, Lord Tribute-Bearer-Ajaw Patan.

Ajaw Patan was just the Lord of the Pack-strap of Merchants; Patan-Tump-line of Porters, Pack-strap of Bearers, of Cargadores, of Tamemes as they are known: Aj Patan.

This name named Ajaw Patan as a Death Lord Merchants; a Death Lord of a Cargador. This is the name that named Ajaw Patan as a Merchant Lord of Violent Death who was encountered in and upon the Road as a malicious and malevolent murderer Merchants who robbed them blind.

Ajaw Patan is the name that names those who were killed by killers while being robbed by robbers who left these unfortunate merchants with little choice in desperate situations where there is nowhere to run and nowhere to hide.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These Underworld Lords were those who ruled over the deaths of people who died on the road from sudden death-xa rax kamik as it is known and named because of the way blood pours forth from these ill-fated merchantsʼ mouths after being waylaid on the road. These were Merchant Lords who were just ambushed from above or taken down from below; both of which are violent ways to go.

These are those who die spitting-up blood after being beaten bad by murderous thieves who take advantage of those who walk with their tumpline on the top of their head not being able to see where they are going as they walk down the road.

Ajaw Xik, Ajaw Patan; Lord Hawk; Lord Bearer of Burden or just named as they often are: Xik, Patan. These are those who are they that cause Sudden Death, like a Hawk, these Lords of Death just swoop down from above; just like a thunderbolt of sudden lightning these victimsʼ attackers are there to plunder what is carried on the merchant back by their pack-strap or tumpline thatʼs been torn asunder to then take its bearer under.

Truly there is no crueler ruler of a disease as is Xik, Patan for usually it is not poverty and need that is the seed to these sort of violent deaths. No, it is always avarice and greed that are the root of this deadly disease that feeds the need to kill Merchants like this lighting quick form of death known as Xik: Sudden Death.

These two, Xik, Patan, strike far from home without warning to finish off all those unfortunate long distant merchants who bear their cargos with tump-lines slung over the crown of their heads.

These are those who are slain by the side of the road and then left to die in a pool of blood in the most violent form of death the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa call: Xik or Hawk because of how ʼQuickʼ one dies without ever being sick.

These are those that take hard-working folk by the throat to choke them out by throttling them hard. These killers just crush the chests of merchants-warriors-ballplayers who are destined to die far from home. They make this happen either walking about or sitting-down in the middle of the road; nobody knows where their lives will be cut-short in this most brutal of all ways to go.

body:
This then was the traditional power and authority that ruled those who went by the names: Xik, Patan.

So then they gathered together to celebrate council with one another to consider and contemplate their thoughts. These were those who were the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who were known as the Lords of Death and Disease.

They decided to persecute Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu in order create conflict to cause trouble with those known and name Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. Those of Xibʼalbʼa wanted the Ball-playing equipment and adornment of Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu; their desire alone called them to invite the Ballplayers down to Xibʼalbʼa to play on their Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice: Pusbʼal Chaaj. So this is what they did by sending their Messengers up to call them down.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu

AjPus were those of sacrifice; AjPubʼ were those of the blowgun; AjPuj were those of weeping pustules of pus; Ajpu were those ancient ancestral ones from the place of pu the cattail reeds and rushes; AjPuuh were those of the shamanic breathe that transformed the soul and spirit of the nawal to heal the ill, to cleanse the poisoned, the polluted, to transform the Sky-Earth and its beings with a powerful ʼpuuhʼ of breathe.

These were those spoken of as One Ancient Ancestral One of the Blowgun and Seven Ancient Ancestral Blowgun Man from the mythical Place of the Reeds thick with abundance where the Ancient Ancestors lived magical transforming lives defined by endless play, contentment, and ease.

But now Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu have awoken the anger and wrath of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame with their bouncing ball and stomping about while yelling and shouting out on their ballcourt that is said to be right there beside the Road of Xibʼalbʼa which says something about where these Ancient Ancestral Ones come from.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Now the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa want to take for their own the prized possessions of these two innocent twins; these two ball-playing brothers; these two ball-playing fathers who have what the Lords of the Underworld do not have but want very much for their own because of their ʼbad-styleʼ ways where envy and avarice are what have ignited this passionate problem of asking them to bring their ʼball-playingʼ equipment with them down to Xibʼalbʼa; but Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu will not do as they are commanded to do by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu will asked to bring down to Xibʼalbʼa that which is theirs to pass down to their sons as inheritance. The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa want to take from Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu the splendid adornment and special ball playing equipment from those who the Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame are inviting down from the Face of the Earth.  Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame do this because they have nothing of their own to adorn themselves as ballplayers on their ballcourt for they  are nothing but skeletal beings with no clothes, no jewelry, no jade, no ball gaming equipment,  or adornment to call their own.

And you know how False-face Lords are. They need adornment to show everyone they are legitimate entitled lords with insignia and emblems of investiture that identifies them as Noble Lords with the power and authority to rule.

And so it is that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu have brought their ball playing equipment to the attention of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame.  And so it that the ball-playing gear; their ball-playing equipment of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu will be named here along with all of its valuable paraphernalia.

The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa wanted what was not theirs yet the very source of the envy and jealousy that they now suffered; the jealousy and envy they suffered was formed and shaped by their desire to possess for themselves the beautiful ball-playing equipment and adornment that was not theirs yet had become the very object and origin of the ferocious longing and fierce desire that they now suffered.

body:
And so it is that the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa now want for themselves the ball-playing equipment-ketzʼabʼal of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; for it is Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who have caught the attention of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa with their loud and continuous ball-playing on the Face of the Earth.

This then is the Ball-Playing Equipment-ketzʼabʼal-Ball-Playing Adornment of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu:

Kitzʼum-their animal pelt apron-armor-ri kitzʼum-their skins, their covering, their protection they wore that transformed them into Animal Lords of the Ballcourt

Kibʼate-their ball-playing yokes worn on their hips-kibʼate-the wooden yokes to ʼbeat-bʼa-hammerʼ the   rubberball; hip-yokes made from the wood-teʼ-cheʼ-trees; yokes covered in puma or jaguar pelts

Kipachqʼab-their arm guards-kipachqʼabʼ to protect their arms from being bruised and broken by the heavy rubber ball

Kiyachwach- their penachos or coronas-kiyachwach-headdress that express the ʼface-imageʼ of their nawal-nahual-nagual that comes to life on the ballcourt as the soul-spirit-essence of the Ballplayer; the Animal Companion-Nagual-Animal Transform are embodied through these finely finished feather headdresses and embellished wooden masks

Wachzut-their emblematic head-scarf and skull-protectors-wachzut-the ʼzuteʼ or ʼhead-scarfʼ that all ballplayers wore as a way of showing ʼfaceʼ on and off the ballcourt so that everyone knew their place

Kikawubʼal-their gemstone adornments-kikawubʼal-jade beads that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu wore as the essence of their lineageʼs eternal life; the eternal life embodied in these gemstones and jade that empowered those who wore them with the power of renewal and regeneration of the lineages from which the ballplayers came as the flowering fruit that grew in the limbs and branches of their lineagesʼ ancestral tree with its ancestral trunk, limbs, and branches from which flower and fruit through the generations

The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa are determined to take for themselves what they are ʼdead-setʼ on taking from Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu:  the fine ball-playing regalia of those who play their rubberball game over their heads.

body:
Let us tell next of when they journeyed to Xibʼalbʼa to play Ajaw Jun Kame, Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kame and how they left behind Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen, the sons of Jun Junajpu.

Their mother had already died for Ixbʼaqiyalo was already dead before the defeat of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen by JunAjPubʼ, IxBʼalamKej!

It was then that they, the messenger and emissaries-samajel-worker and servants arrived on the Face of the Earth after being sent by their Lords, Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; One Death, Seven Death. These were those known as the messengers-ajsamajel-workers who were the servant emissaries of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame who sent them with a message to summons Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu with a message, with a summons while being told to do the following:

“Go you Warrior Messengers of the Noble Reed Mat-AjPop Achij; go with this summons to bring back Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu!” said Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame.

“Say this when you arrive there with them: ʼCome! Kepetoq!ʼ say the Lords for us to say to you: ʼDown here is where you must descend; here is where you must come to play with us, so that we might liven-up our lives with you! Truly we are amazed by you; truly we are astounded by all you do; and, that is why we wish for you to arrive here to play with us!ʼ say the Lordsʼ you will say,ʼ” they said when they left their instruction with their Messenger Warriors of the Noble Reed Mat of the Noble Lords; AjPop Achij.

“You will say to them, ʼBring along your ball-playing gear; just bring along your gaming things; your ball-playing regalia so that you shall be well prepared to play on our ballcourt, just bring what is yours: bring your waist yokes-kibʼate, to beat the ball; bring your arm protectors-kipachqʼabʼ; and your rubber-ball-kikikʼ-your blood-kikikʼ as well!ʼ say the Lords.ʼ This is what you must say to them when you arrive with them up there,” said the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa when they spoke to their Messengers-AjSamajel-Workers-AjSamajel.

And so these were the Messengers, the Owls-ri Tukur, were their Messengers, Kisamajel:

Chʼabʼi Tukur, Arrow Owl;

Juraqan Tukur, Juraqan Owl;

Kaqix Tukur, Macaw Owl;

Jolom Tukur, Skull Owl spoken of as the Messengers of Xibʼalbʼa

body:
Chʼabʼi Tukur-Arrow Owl moves fast like an arrow that arrives out of nowhere.

Juraqan Tukur-One-Legged Owl has just one leg; but he has wings, he has feathers.

Kaqix Tukur-Macaw Owl is colored fire-red; he has wings, just as he has feathers.

And then there is this Skull Owl-Jolom Tukur; Skull Owl is he who just has a skull, he has no legs, he just has wings, he just has feathers; Jolom Tukur-Skull Owl is a Skull Being with no legs, only wings and feathers are what he has as a messenger of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; One Death, Seven Death, the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

There were four Messengers-Workers known as Samajel Rajpop Achijabʼ they were of high rank known as the ʼWarrior Messengers of the Woven Reed Mat of the Noble Lordsʼ.

They had status that went with their rank so that people took notice wherever they were sent to arrive with the messages they delivered for their Lords to be listened to as the very same message of the Lords to be followed as the Lordsʼ very same orders that were sent with their Messenger Warriors of the Noble Reed Mat of Noble Rule and Authority: Samajel Rajpop Achijab.

These were those Messenger-Workers-AjSamajel who were respected as the ʼveryʼ embodiment of the word of the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

The Owls flew up and out of the cave underworld of Xibʼalbʼa that was down below the surface of the earth to arrive instantly up above the Ballcourt where they perched themselves over the ballplayers who were playing ball on their ballcourt they called Jom, ancestral place of burial, ancestral place of the deceased ballplayers; dead Lords; dead and deceased Noble Lords buried there beside the Jom: the Ballcourt Burial Grounds.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu were playing ball on their ballcourt there, they called their ballcourt Nim Xol Kar Chaaj which was a Great Hollow of Fish Ballcourt from a previous Age and its sacrifice. This Ballcourt of Karchaaj is there in a ʼhollowʼ out on the plain before the road to Xibʼalbʼa that drops down to the Lowland limestone caves. Nim Xol Kar Chaaj is the opening that leads down into the cave world leading into the underworld caves of the Divine Ancestors.

body:
“Could it be true that this was said by Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame?” asked Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

“Truly it is so-Qitzij bʼa la,” they said, said the Owls, “Oj na! Letʼs go!  We are to accompany you! Bring along all of your ball-playing equipment-chikʼam uloq ri ketzʼabʼal-your ball-playing gear with all your ceremonial adornment! Say the Lords.”

“Utz bʼa la! Very well then! Just wait for us since we must first take leave of Our Mother: QaChuch,” they said then to the Owls-ri Tukur-the Messengers of Xibʼalbʼa.

This then was when they went back home, returning to speak with their Mother-Ixmuqane. Their Father-Xpiyakok was already dead; Xpiyakok had already died which made their Father Xpiyakok a Dead Ancestor as it is said-xkaminaqoq kiqajaw.

“Joʼna! Ix QaChuch-We must go! You, Our Mother; Joʼna! Ix QaChuch. We will return soon; donʼt cry Mother we will soon come back home. It is just the Messengers of the Noble Lord-usamajel Ajaw it is just they who have come to summon us so that we might go with them; and so weʼve been asked to ready our things so that we might return with them. It is they who have come to guide us; it is they who have come here so that we may depart with them; those who our guides who now await us; it is they the Owls who will show us the way; they are those who await us so that we might leave with them.”

ʼ“Kepetoq! Come along!ʼ say the Lords-ri Ajaw,” said those who were sent to summon us.

We will leave behind our rubber ball-qakikʼ, as our remembrance, as our sign” they said, those named Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu, when they took leave of their Mother IxMuqane.

Straight-away they left their ball tied up in the rafters of the house-puwi ja.

“Qojul na! We will return! We will come back! Then we will take up our ball again to play with it once more!” said Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

Then they gave instructions to the Boys Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen before taking leave of their home:

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“Just play your flutes, just sing your songs; just paint and write, just sculpt and carve. Make our home warm by warming the heart of your Grandmother,” is what they said when they gave their counsel; when they took their leave of Jun Bʼatz, Jun Chowen, their Artisan Sons, the Monkey Boy Twins: One Howler Monkey, One Artisan Monkey.

Bitter tears did she weep-qʼusqʼus choqʼ kichuch-their Mother, IxMuqane, upon their taking leave of her.

“Joʼ na! Come now! We are not going to die. Donʼt be sad-Maja bʼi kojkamik. Mixbʼisonik.” said Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu when they left.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu in Xibʼalbʼa

And so it was that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu left. They were guided down their road by the messengers, the emissaries, the Owls-Tukur.

This then was when they descended down the ʼblowgunʼ road of Xibʼalbʼa-xeqaj kʼut pu ubʼeal Xibʼalbʼa. They dropped down the steep face of the flight of stairs there-xuluxuj uchi kumuk-and then down, down, down they went in their steep, steep descent.

When they arrived at the bottom of the steep face of the flight of stairs the ball-players came out to where the canyons split off from one another arriving at a place spoken of as the junction of the river canyons where they came to the turbulent river rapids of the Changing, Transforming River-Jal Ja that formed the Blowgun Canyon-Siwan Ubʼ that was there at the entrance of the two great canyon rivers that went underground like a ʼblowgunʼ as in Narrow Canyon; Echo Canyon-Nubʼ Siwan creating the roaring noise of Kʼulku Siwan the Call of Quetzal Canyon.

Now they must pass through the rushing-roaring rivers and their wild-whirling waters they-Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu-known and named Jal-Jal Jaʼ Simaj-the Turbulent River Rapids crowned by sharp spears that resemble spiny stakes standing up straight; spikes set pointed in their way.

For truly there were innumerable spike-like spines-simaj-shooting up to be standing-up before them. But the fearless ballplayers were not speared, they were not stabbed, they were not spiked, and so they moved on undaunted by the challenges they encountered on their way.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Theyʼd been summoned by the Lords-Ajaw so they did whatever was demanded of them in order to do as they were commanded; and so it was that they took up the narrow road north to then follow it to where it landed them and that is where they appeared to be stranded before two deadly rivers that gave them no other option then to make their way across.

They came upon the side of a river, Blood River-Kikʼ Aʼ; they passed right over without drinking a drop.

They came upon another river, where pus-puj ran like water; they werenʼt defeated there either, they just crossed over without being poisoned by its deadly filth.

It was then that they arrived at the Crossroads-pa Kajibʼ Xalqat Bʼe where four roads from the four directions came together to then cross over one another to create the Crossroads.

This is where they were defeated, at the Four Crossing Roads; the place where Four Roads Crossed: Kajibʼ Xalqat Bʼe.

There at the Center of the Crossroads the Four Roads met:

One Red Road; Jun Kaqa Bʼe

One, then, Black Road; Jun kʼut Qʼeqʼa Bʼe

White Road One; Saqi Bʼe Jun

One, then, Yellow Road; Jun kʼut Qʼana Bʼe

Four Roads; Kajibʼ Bʼe

This then was when it spoke; the Black Road-Qʼeqʼa Bʼe spoke; “I am the one to take up, I am the road of the Ruler; I am the road of the Noble Lord-In ubʼe Ajaw!ʼ” said the Black Road-Qʼeqʼa Bʼe.

Right there is where they were defeated; they were defeated when they took up the road of Xibʼalbʼa-ri ubʼe Xibʼalbʼa. This is the road they took up, the Black Road-ri Qʼeqʼa Bʼey the Black Road of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

It was then that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu arrived at the Council House of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa-Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa.

It was there that they were defeated again by being tricked again; for it was they who were deceived by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa: Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame-One Death, Seven Death.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The first seated ones there at the entrance of the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa was just a Decorated Decoy; just a Dressed-up Dummy-kawutalik Poy, kawutalik Ajam Cheʼ just a Decked-out Doll; just Adorned Works of Wood were all that these wooden decoys; wooden deceptions were; Embellished Works of Wood; just Adorned Wood-Works is what they were and all that they would ever be.

These carved men, sculpted men were dressed up and decorated before being set-up seated right there beside the entryway of the Entrance Hall of Xibʼalbʼa-Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa:

They were just Decorated Dolls, xa Poy, xa Ajam Cheʼ, just Whittled Works of Wood placed right there at the entrance of the Popobʼal Rajawal: the Council House Place of the Noble Lords and Rulers of Xibʼalbʼa.

It was they; it was just them, those Wooden Men who were greeted first by Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; these Seated Figures just Formed, just Shaped from Wood who were greeted by those known and named Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

This then was beginning of the end for them; and this would be the root of their ruination; the origin of their humiliation, for it was just the sowing; just the seeding of their defeat by those of Xibʼalbʼa: Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame.

“Qʼala! Saqarik; Greetings! Good Morning, One Death-Jun Kame!” said Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu as they greeted the First-Seated-One seated there at the entrance hall of Xibʼalbʼa. The Decorated-Decoy; the Decorated-Doll-Poy sitting there; he was just a Wooden Manikin who sat there silent and still; the ʼWooden-kind-of-Manʼ who sat there and said nothing at all.

“Qʼala-Saqarik, Good Morning, Seven Death, Wuqubʼ Kame!” they greeted the second-seated-one; the second wood-worked work-of-wood: Ajam Cheʼ.

They did not speak-maxechaʼkowik-they did not say a thing; no, those they greeted who were seated there at the entrance of Xibʼalbʼa did not say a word; they didnʼt say a thing; those Wooden-Works-of-Wood didnʼt make a peep because they couldnʼt speak being Works of Wood: Ajam Cheʼ just Worked-Wood was all they were.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This was when a roar of laughter thundered through the entrance hall as a horrendous howl reverberated through the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa: Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa.

The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa just yowled hysterically for they had defeated Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu by besting them with this first testing of them that ended their chances of taking one step further towards their Ballcourt; not one foot farther would they make it to take up play in Xibʼalbʼa on the Ballcourt known as Pusbʼal Chaaj.

For Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame defeated them-xechʼakomajik right there; right there at the entrance of Xibʼalbʼa; truly, Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu were defeated for they had lost heart while losing face by being humiliated here at the entrance place; they were ridiculed as fools for not knowing who to greet at the entry-way of the Popobʼal of  Xibʼalbʼa.

It was then that those of Xibʼalbʼa spoke and those who spoke were Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame:

“Utz bʼa la! Very well then, at least you arrived here with us, at least you came down here below to be among us. Tomorrow you will have an opportunity to put into play your hip-yokes-kibʼateʼ, your arm guards-ipachqʼabʼ,” they said, when they spoke to Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu there in the Council House of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa.

“Just take a seat then, just take a seat there upon our bench,” they were told. It was just a searing slab of stone; the seat that the Lords offered Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu was just a burning bench.

It was then that they were burnt badly; they were just seared sadly there atop that blistering bench; they just did what little they could do to move about atop that scorching seat that had been offered to them so graciously; but they got no relief, no relief at all atop that blazing bench of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
When it was too much for them to bear they no longer pretended to care and shot straight up off the bench into the air; for truly their bottoms were burnt and burnt badly from sitting upon that burning bench of those ever-so-clever Lords of Xibʼalbʼa; the flat cooking stone that was placed there with such care was just to defeat Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who now just wanted to get out of there.

Truly, these cunning trickster Lords of Xibʼalbʼa could not get enough of their deceptive ways of mocking their guests to make fools of those who knew nothing of disgrace for they had never, ever lost face caused by deception like this that was crafted to cause them nothing but shame.

And so it was that the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa just burst out laughing until they fell on the floor to then fall to pieces for truly they couldnʼt take much more of their laughing; they just came undone from never having laughed so hard as they now laughed there in the  dark of the entrance hall of Xibʼalbʼa.

They cramped up inside from their endless laughter so that it seemed they would soon die from laughing as they writhed in pain from so much laughter; their blood; their bones seized up as they laughed at anything and everything their invited guest did; it no longer mattered the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa just laughed to then laugh even harder; and so it was that the Lords of Death laughed and laughed and laughed until they fell on the floor; they just couldnʼt laugh any harder; they simply could not laugh anymore it hurt too much so they sent Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu away; out of the Popol Ja to enter another House of Xibʼalbʼa.

“Xa jix chi ja! Just go now; go ahead outside of the Council House so you can enter Dark House. Go then, go receive each your pine-torch and cigar there before your sleeping quarters,” they were told.  It was then that the two arrived at Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja-House of Darkness. Just darkness alone filled this first house of tests and trials of Xibʼalbʼa.

So then they arrived there at Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja; darkness alone was the inside of that House; House of Darkness its name: Qʼeqʼuma Ja.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Right away those of Xibʼalbʼa gathered together their thoughts; and so those of Xibʼalbʼa said what they were thinking: “Letʼs just sacrifice them tomorrow, it is just a bad sign, it is just a wrong sort of indication; it is a mistake-labʼe-a nettle road; a road of nettles is what it is. It is just a mistaken path that we have taken.”

“So let them be sacrificed straightaway with our gaming implements-ri qetzʼabʼal by playing our game; our way of playing on our court with our ball in our way of play; by the way we play our game of sacrifice.”

“Let it be our way of ball-playing and our ball-playing equipment-ri qachaajibʼal-that brings them a quick and sudden death. Let us just sacrifice them tomorrow,” said those of Xibʼalbʼa speaking there together in council with one another.

Indeed their ball-kichaaj-was just a round obsidian stone-kʼolokʼik cha-with its own name-Saqi Toqʼ-White Flint Knife of Sacrifice was the name of their ball, the name of the game-ri chaaj-the ball, the game, the name of their game was sacrifice; sacrifice was the game played by those who were Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

Their ball was just a razor sharp obsidian blade; the game of sacrifice they played was just played with a polished stone blade. And so it was that their blade made of obsidian is what would be put in play the very next day.

For their ball, the ball of Xibʼalbʼa, was just a round obsidian ball-kʼolokʼik cha that was just a sharpened, polished blade of sacrifice-xa juqʼul kichaaj; and so the ballgame of sacrifice they played and the sacrificial way they played; as well as the sacrificial ball with which they played their game of sacrifice was as a sacrificial ball of ballgame sacrifice that was a polished blade which was a sharpened  blade that was a well-honed, sharp, and shiny obsidian blade of sacrifice-xa juqʼul kichaaj.

This razor sharp obsidian blade of sacrifice was their ball and their game and their way of playing their game which made their game just the game of ball-game sacrifice.

And so then they entered there where they were led.  Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu entered Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
It was there they were given their torches-kichäj of burning torch-pine. This is to say they were given their burning torches-kichäj tzijom-torches that were burning since Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame had lit them to then give them to their porters-yaʼol to then pass them on to Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

And so it was that they were given burning cigars to accompany their burning torches; each of them-Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu-was given a lit cigar that was already burning-kisikʼ tzijom chik-when the porters-yaʼol were given them already lit by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. These already lit cigars and already lit torches were delivered to Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu, already burning!

This then was when they were there in Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Jaʼ crouched down in a squat-chʼokochʼoj-sitting on their heels in the dark; they were just left waiting in a crouch-chʼokochʼoj like war captives; like slaves; like captives captured for ritual sacrifice. This all happened when they were there in Dark House: Qʼeqʼuma Ja.

This was when the porters-yaʼol came in to give Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu their torches-kichäj along with their cigars-kisik; torches and cigars that were already lit when they were given to them already burning.

Truly, their torches were ablaze-kajuljut-resplendent when the porters entered there; they entered Dark House with their torch-pine torches lit; they were burning; they were ablaze; each was given a cigar; each of their cigars was lit; they were burning; the torches they were given were just like their cigars that were given to them burning; they were ablaze-kajuljut.

Then they-the porters of the torches and cigars-spoke for the Lords: “ʼtomorrow you must return them just as they are given to you as a burning torch, as a burning cigar; so return them just as you have received them. Donʼt finish them off; donʼt burn them down because you must return them just as they have been given to you; we will gather them from you just as you have received them from us; so return them to us at Dawn just as we give them to you now,ʼ say the Lords to say to you,” they were told, those known and named Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
So then they were defeated-xechʼakataj for those two who were left in Dark House were finished off for they finished off their burning pine torches-chäj just as they finished off their burning cigars-sik.

And so it was that the two of them there were finished off; they were finished off when they went before the Lords to give them what was theirs; when they went to give their cigars and torches that were finished off.

This was when daybreak broke after watching and waiting for Dawn all night long in Dark House where the dark of nightʼs darkness is so very dark there in that Dark House that was a House of Darkness-Qʼeqʼuma Ja.

Thick with trials is Xibʼalbʼa-tzatz utijobʼal Xibʼalbʼa thick with tests-tzatz utijobʼal many are the trials found there in Xibʼalbʼa where one encounters many heaps of tests-kʼya molaj chi tijobʼal that must be confronted as the countless tests that are trials that are always an ordeal because truly one was made to overcome the great many trials and tests that are encountered there in Xibʼalbʼa.

The first one is Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja; just darkness alone is there inside that dark, Dark House.

The second house of ordeal then is Xuxulim Ja-Shivering House-Xuxulim Ja is its name this Cold House-Tew Ja thick with cold is it there inside that House; unbearable cold drafts of icy winds blow there; intolerable whistling gusts of penetrating cold are met there; fearful freezing frosty gales drive through the inside of that frigid, icy abode of Shivering House-Xuxulim Ja; Tew Ja-Cold House is its name.

The third place of trials, the thirds place of tests goes by the name of Jaguar House-Bʼalami Ja as it is named-chuchʼaxik-as it is spoken of.  Nothing but Bʼalam-Jaguar are there inside, tangled up, squeezed together in a rage, furious are they, closed up are the Jaguar-Bʼalam in the House of Jaguar-Bʼalami Ja; Jaguar House is its name.

Sotzʼi Ja is the name of the fourth house of tests-ukaj utijobʼal-the fourth house of trials, the fourth house of ordeal. Just Bats alone are in that house: Xa utukel Sotzʼ kʼo upam chi Ja.
