source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Perhaps this is the remembrance of the places known as los Bajos or the Low-laying areas that form inland seas out in the Petén Jungle. These areas would have to be ʼpassed overʼ by walking pilgrims. Many areas such as these lay between Northern Yucatan where Mayapan and Chichen Itza are found and the distant Kʼicheʼ Highlands; if one were to take a relatively straight line towards the Highlands of Guatemala then one would be forced to pass over these low-lying areas that the Maya must have created their Saq Bʼey or Sacred Road that ran north-south. Is this what the Popol Wuj is talking to us about here in very simple yet revealing ways?

They suffered deep affliction; truly, they felt anguish in their hearts when they took council together as they contemplated what it was that they were obliged to do next. There was nothing for them to eat; but there was something for them to drink as their sustenance; the name of this one drink was ju ukʼ known as jun ukʼi or jukʼi an ancestral drink that came from just one kind of maize-xa juna ixim. Just ʼone kind of maizeʼ was ground fine to create their sacred sustenance that they drank as their one drink of maize: ju ukʼ is its name; jukʼi as it is known.

This line of text is so very, very interesting as it takes us back to the Wooden People and their grinding stones that spoke out to them in significant signifying ways that become significant now as we hear of this primordial maize drink that enables the survival of the First Four Fathers. The First Fathers who are now leading by being led by Tojil their Kabʼawil; the Kabʼawil of the now multiplying-Tamubʼ, Ilokabʼ, Qʼaqʼchikelebʼ, Aj Tzʼikina Ja Pueblos who are growing in number as the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo.

These are those who will always remember their ancestors when they drink their ʼone drink of sustenanceʼ that is remembered when they sow their maize in their milpa and drink this ʼone drink of one variety of maizeʼ in a very subtenant significant sort of way through the spoken phrase: “Ju ukʼ chikiqumej ri xa juna ixim-One drink is what they drank of only one kind of maize.”

body:
Remember, remember the grinding stones calling out joli, joli, joli…jukʼi, jukʼi,  jukʼi now you know where this comes from: the one primordial maize drink to stave off hunger:  jun ukʼ juna ixim or one beverage of one kind of maize; the one maize drink of one kind of maize; one kind of sustenance: jukʼi, jukʼi,  jukʼi.

This is when they bore on their back the ʼsacred burdenʼ that they carried to the top of the mountain, the mountain known as Chi Pixabʼ spoken of as Place of Council, Council Place.

They just bore the burden of their divine cargo up the mountainside; those Kabʼawil that they carried were those known and named: Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz.

A Great Fast-Nima Mewajik was carried out by Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ with his woman-rixoqil-his wife Kaqa Paluna-Red Sea Turtle Woman was her name.

The same Great Fast-Nima Mewajik was performed by Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ with his wife-rixoqil-his woman Chomi Ja-Shrimp House, Prawn House as she is named.

Majukʼutaj completed his Great Fast-Nima Mewajik with his woman-rixoqil-his wife Tzʼununi Ja-Hummingbird House as she is named, his partner; rikʼulel as she was spoken when she was named as his wife, his partner: rixoqil, rikʼulel.

Ikʼi Bʼalam kept a Great Fast-Nima Mewajik like the others; Ikʼi Bʼalam fasted with his woman, his wife, his partner; Kaqix Ja who was known as Scarlet Macaw House.

These ancestral couples carried out their Great Fast-Nima Mewajik there in the dark; there in the darkness that anticipate the coming forth of their Sun; there before the dawning of their Dawn.  Great was their affliction; weary with worry were they for their great concern  there up on the mountain top known today as Chi Pixabʼ that was their Place of Council known as the Council Place of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo; Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ: Chi Pixabʼ.

So they spoke again with their Kabʼawil there. This is what was said by: Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz to those known and named:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam.

body:
This then was when their Kabʼawil counseled them on what they were to do with these words of counsel that were words of advice when they celebrated council together on the mountain top of Chi Pixabʼ; the place they that they left when they took leave of this Place of Taking Leave: Chi Pixabʼ.

“We should just get going; we must ʼrise-up-yojyakatajikʼ and take leave of this place that is not of our essence; our character; our nature; this place that is not of our way of being; the way of becoming that is our way of being. This place is not our place to be and become who we shall come to be! So let us take leave of it to go somewhere that is of our way of being and becoming!” said the Kabʼawil.

“Let us find a place to hide ourselves away. Will not the Dawn soon be upon us?  Will not the Dawn of Our Sun soon appear at the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij?”

“Would it not be a disgrace for you-the First Four Fathers-if we-your Kabʼawil-were to be taken as ʼwar captivesʼ by the Warrior People; AjLabʼal? We should be hidden away in a hiding place we ourselves make; or maybe just be kept out of sight behind some kind of hideaway we create: chi tzʼaq!”

“You might then just hide us beside a temple wall-chi tzʼaq. This is where we should be placed for you who are those who perform rituals of sacrifice with Maguey Thorns-Ix AjKʼixbʼ; and, you Ix AjKʼajbʼ who perform penitential acts of sacrificial punishment with your Obsidian Blades. You must make yourselves ready. Each one of us Kabʼawil with their own place; each one with a place of their own,” they said when they spoke; when the Kabʼawil spoke to those who bore them on their backs as their sacred burden.

“Utz bʼa la. Let us just pull ourselves up to get going so we can move out of here to find a place in the forest among the ʼmany trees-kʼechelajʼ for each one us to have our place to hideaway,” said all those who were there to speak to one another while taking council together at Chi Pixabʼ.

Each one of them carried their deity upon their backs; each group bore their sacred burden of their Kabʼawil.

body:
And so it came to pass that Awilix entered a canyon known as Ewabʼal Siwan; Hideaway Canyon as it is spoken of by all. It was a grand canyon amidst a great forest.

Pa Awilix is the name of this hidden sort of hiding place now; Pa Awilix is the name of this hideaway as this hidden hiding place is known today; the hiding place of Awilix where Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ left his Kabʼawil there in a Hidden Canyon in a Great Forest: Ewabʼal Siwan; Hideaway Canyon; Hideaway Ravine; the Hidden Hideaway in the Hidden Canyon; Ewabʼal Siwan as it is known.

Each of the Kabʼawil from Tulan Tzuy Wa was left in their own hiding place in an orderly fashion:  these Kabʼawil of the First Fathers were hidden one after another:  Awilix was first.

Next came Jaqawitz who was brought to a mountain-top where there stood a mountain-top temple; this mountain-top temple was One Great Red House-Jun Nima Kaqa Ja.

This is where he, Jaqawitz, was left; when Jaqawitz was left upon this one great temple house that stood upon this one mountain-top known for its one great red house. This is the mountain-top known as Kaqajawitz: Red House Mountain.

Jaqawitz was the second deity that was hidden by them; but they did not hide him in a forest because they hid Jaqawitz on top of a Great Red Temple House-chuwi Jun Nima Kaqaja.

Jaqawitz is the name of the mountain today; the mountain upon which was founded the town known as Jaqawitz.

Majukʼutaj was left here along with his Kabʼawil that he carried known as Jaqawitz. This is the name of the deity that will become the name of the mountain citadel known and named Jaqawitz.

body:
Jaqawitz was the second deity that was hidden by them; they did not hide him in a forest but up on top of a ʼcleared-off; cleaned-offʼ mountain known as  saqi juyubʼ or cleared-off mountain. This ʼcleared-off; cleaned-offʼ mountain top is where they placed Jaqawitz which was an open mountain that was cleared of all the trees and vines; it was just a cleaned off mountain top known and named Saqawitz for it was a ʼcleared-off mountainʼ which made it a ʼOpen Mountain or Jaqawitzʼ because it was a mountain-top that was completely ʼcleaned-offʼ to be completely ʼopened-upʼ upon on top so they called it Jaqawitz: open mountain since ʼjaqʼ is to ʼopenʼ up. Today it is known as ʼChuwi Juyubʼ or ʼMountain Topʼ that is remembered by all as a Sacred Mountain; Saqawitz.

And so it was that Jaqawitz the Kabʼawil of Majukʼutaj was left on top of a cleared-off kind of cleaned-off sort of mountain-top where there was a Great Temple known as the Red House that was a Sacred Temple House placed up on this wide-open mountain-top where Majukʼutaj stayed alongside his Kabʼawil  Jaqawitz on a sacred mountain-top that was an open mountain-top that was a cleaned-off kind of cleared-off mountain-top that in time would be known as: Kaqawitz, Jaqawitz, Saqawitz because of how Jaqawitz was left there with Majukʼutaj.

Jaqawitz; Kaqajawitz; Saqawitz; Qʼaqʼawitz; Jaqʼawitz; Witz-Mountain; Open Mountain Top or Chuwi Juyubʼ or the Above the Mountain;  Up-Upon the Cleared-off  Red Temple Mountain

Jaqawitz becomes the mountain citadel known as Jaqawitz where Majukʼutaj leaves his Kabʼawil Jaqawitz that is also known as Kaqajawitz and Saqawitz and Jaqawitz in master play Nawal Transformation combined with the ʼinvisibilityʼ of Majukʼutaj: Nobody Is Here who seems to be coming in and out of sight.

body:
All of which brings us to the following inconclusive conclusions as to name of the place known as Chuwi Juyubʼ or Atop the Mountain or Mountain Top and itʼs the multiple connections regarding the nawal name Jaqawitz: Jaqawitz the Kabʼawil of Majukʼutaj; Jaqawitz the Open Mountain Place that is where Great Red House Temple was placed on its Mountain-top Place of Nima Kaqa Ja Witz or Great Red House Mountain of the Nima Kaqa Ja, Great Red Temple House of Sacrifice, Kaqajawitz that stood-out on the Saqawitz; Cleared-off; Cleaned-off Mountain Place that was an Opened-up Mountain ;  Jaqawitz which will become the First Kʼicheʼ Citadel built by Majukʼutaj; the First Father of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ lineage that was the Sacred Mountain-top Stronghold of the Kʼicheʼ People that was protected and ruled over by the  Sacrificial Priest AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ of the Great Red Temple House; Kaqaja where the Kabʼawil Jaqawitz was set to take dominion over this first place of conquest of the  First Father known as: Ajaw Majukʼutaj. None of which one could possibly understand from a ʼliteralʼ translation and interpretation of Popol Wuj!

So there you have it; right here, a clear, clean kind of open understanding of Jaqawitz where soon there will be great conflict that will lead to a ʼmagical battleʼ in which Great Pots of Bees and Wasps that are Sacred Pots of Bees and Wasps will be ʼopened-jaqaʼ by being broken open-jaqʼaʼ which is to say smashed open-jaqʼaʼ to release these vicious vindictive flying insects with a deadly sting who are the embodiment of the ʼanimal companionʼ or  ʼnagualʼ or ʼanimal transformsʼ of the Warlord Majukʼutaj who along with his Kabʼawil Jaqawitz will become the Noble Lord and Ruler of  Jaqawitz the mountain top citadel of Jaqawitz.

Majukʼutaj is the Third-Rox of the First Four Fathers who receives Jaqawitz as his Kabʼawil at Tulan to then leave Tulan by abandoning Tulan when leaving Tulan Tzuy-Wa.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
I suspect there is some sort of auspicious kind of propitious type of confusion created here in the ʼhidingʼ of the Kabʼawil in the hidden mountain places by leaving one of the Kabʼawil in the open in plain sight. This is Jaqawitz who is left on the ʼOpen Mountain-Saqawitzʼ as the Kabʼawil of Majukʼutaj-Black Panther of the Western Cardinal Direction of the Black Night; the Falling Down Place of the Sun in the West who is the Invisible One-Majukʼutaj.

It is he who leaves us with a great many mythic names and images to fire-up our  imagination that is fully engaged in the mythic metaphors formed by the mythic figures and mythic archetypes  that bring to life an imaginal realm as alive with mythic images as one could ever wish or want for. Yes indeed,  our mythic imagination is now burning bright as we open up to a most fascinating imaginal world atop this cleared-off Mountain Top where the Kʼicheʼ Winaq will establish themselves for the first time a People who are a Pueblo of Warlords who do not conquer the Mountain People. No, the Kʼicheʼ Lords known as los Tojiles will only defend their Women and Children; Daughters and Sons; Vassals and Subject atop the Primordial Mountain known and named as Jaqawitz and this story of their defending their Mountain Place is what shall be told here.

But there is more because there will soon be built a ʼgreat walled palisadeʼ atop Jaqawitz the Mountain that will form and shape the Citadel of Jaqawitz of the Kabʼawil Jaqawitz on the Mountain Jaqawitz so that Jaqawitz the Kabʼawil who was ʼjustʼ left with Majukʼutaj on the Mountain of Jaqawitz will become the Lord and Ruler of the mountain-top citadel of Jaqawitz. Jaqawitz the Mountain Citadel that is established on the Open-Mountain; Jaqa-Witz that is the place once known as Kaqajawitz because of the Great Red House Temple of Sacrifice that made this a Saqawitz; Sacred Mountain that is a Dawning Mountain-top; Saqiribʼal that opens to a clear view of the Relebʼal Qʼij to watch and wait for the Great Star; Nima Chumil that is the very same place where the Great Red Temple House; Nima Kaqaja was built upon the Open Cleared-Off Mountain of Saqawitz.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
I hope this detailed explanation is of some benefit to your enriched understanding of this most esoteric section of Popol Wuj. One must come to appreciate the ability of the Maya Scribe to create a kind of nawal sort of confusion as a person becomes a place to become a divinity to become a citadel to become a mountain top that is named one name than another all in order to hide the Kabʼawil Jaqawitz in a net of confusion in order to create the sense of everything coming out of nothing to return to nothing.

For some reason the Kabʼawil say there are very good reasons to think and believe they might be captured. So it would be best that they are hidden from those who ʼmightʼ be ʼtrackingʼ them. And so it is the Kabʼawil Jaqawitz is best hidden in a Great Red House and being it a Red House it is a Temple of Sacrifice giving the name of the Mountain Top: Kaqa Ja Witz or Kaqajawitz. All of which will ʼthrow offʼ those ʼinvisible enemy forcesʼ in search of the First Four Fathers and their Kabʼawil who have returned to the Mountains of the Kʼicheʼ as Noble Lords of Tolan Tzuy-Wa who want to settle themselves among the ʼMountain Peopleʼ mentioned earlier in our mythic narrative.

Now we are in those Mountains with Majukʼutaj which is best translated as the ʼInvisible Oneʼ which is one of the names of Tezcatlipoca which the name of Heart of the Sky; Ukʼuʼx Kaj that is the name of Jun Raqan Kaqulja; the One Footed One; the Smoking Mirror: Tezcatlipoca. You get the idea; I hope you get the idea because it isnʼt at all obvious.

But once you ʼgetʼ a ʼsenseʼ of ʼitʼ ʼoneʼ canʼt help but ʼfeelʼ the ʼgeniusʼ of this ʼnawalʼ of ʼinvisibilityʼ and ʼbeingʼ going ʼpoofʼ into ʼthin airʼ which is quite wonderful but more than likely best pulled off through the ʼperformanceʼ of ʼstorytellingʼ by Kʼicheʼ Maya Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word: Chuch-Qajaw Ojer Tzij.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These Masters of the Ancient Word played with this ʼnaming of the namesʼ that forms as it shapes the ʼInvisible Senseʼ that comes forth from the name of Majukʼutaj. Majukʼutaj the One; Jun who is Ma-Jun; No One that becomes Maju; Not One to create the invisible name ʼNo One is Hereʼ Ma-Jun-Kʼo-Taj that become Majukʼutaj.

Nothing is here to find or to track so that there is ʼNothing to Showʼ or ʼNo Sign to be Seenʼ or the ʼInvisible One; Titlacauanʼ all of which makes one think of Tezcatlipoca as Titlacauan; Invisible One and his wily ways as the beguiling Lord of Mysterious Comings and Goings and Ruler of Nawal Trickster Deities such as these Four Jaguar Lords of the Kʼicheʼ. Tezcatlipoca is the ʼObsidian Mirror that smokesʼ in a mirror of divination into which everything can be seen by this Changing and Transforming Trickster Deity Extraordinaire: Tezcatlipoca.

Tezcatlipoca is also known as ʼHe who makes Himself; Moyocoyaniʼ who is he who gives great wealth in the form of ornamentation and embellishment and it is he who takes them away. Remember this, oh please do remember this: the one who gives prosperity to then take it away from those who do not respect him and his way!

So do not get confused while watching how the ʼbreaking open or jaqaʼ of the ʼSacred Pots; Kukʼubʼ once translated as ʼGod Potsʼ that are the ʼTamale Potsʼ that are ʼbroken openʼ inside the entrance of Jaqawitz; the Citadel. This ʼbreaking open; jaqaʼ is really a ʼsmashing open or jaqʼaʼ which is just a change in the inflection of the guttural sounding q to occlusive sounding guttural qʼ that for the Maya is heard loud and clear!

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This smashing open of the Sacred Pots or the jaqʼa Kukʼubʼ is when and where and what causes the deadly stinging Metallic Black Wasps-Sitaʼl and blistering bite of Big Bad Bees-Wonon come out of nowhere like the unseen, unnamed Tezcatlipoca who is known as  the Invisible Enemy and/or the Enemy on Both Sides to win the conflict that is the battle that is the war of Jaqawitz or Jaqʼawitz when the Sacred Pots of Sustenance where tamales are cooked up are ʼopened upʼ by having the tops being ʼsmashed open or broken open to name the name of his sacred mountain as Jaqʼawitz not just  Jaqawitz.

This is when the United Forces of the Kʼicheʼ will be attacked by the United Forces of the Pueblos; ri Amaqʼ; the Tribes of the Mountain Places and Canyon Country who will be defeated by Tojil. Tojil as the protecting and guiding Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ who will provide counsel in the form of strategic advice to the Lords of Kʼicheʼ on how to gather  together  the Sitaʼl and Wonon; Black Stinging Wasps and Big Round Bees to destroy and devastated the Pueblos and Tribes of the Mountains and Canyons.

This shamanic transformation of the Kabʼawil Jaqawitz into becoming his Nagual Animal Transform of Wasps and Bees is one Mesoamericaʼs greatest archetypal examples of Nawal Winaq controlling the natural world and the Ancestral Beings that exist within it to be called upon as the ʼmagical alliesʼ of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ.

This is not the only time these bees and those wasps will be brought to life by Tojil to take revenge on the arrogant, self-aggrandizing enemies of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq and their Kʼicheʼ  Kabʼawil: Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz and Nikʼaj Taqʼaj.

Enough is enough with all of this interpretive narrative as valuable as it is; it isnʼt the original Ojer Tzij; Ancient Word of this Book of Council; Popol Wuj.

body:
This was when Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ came there-xul chilaʼ to a place a Great Forest: Nima Kʼicheʼlaj, this was when Tojil was hidden by Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ in this Great Forest where Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ arrived with his Kabʼawil Tojil; Pa Tojil; Place of Tojil is the name of this mountain today; Pa Tojil is the Place of Tojil in the Great Forest Nimaʼ Kʼicheʼlaj where Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ left hidden the Kabʼawil Tojil;  Tojil the Kabʼawil left hidden away by Ajaw Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ in his hiding place which was the hideaway of Tojil known and named: Pa Tojil.

This was when they named this Hidden Canyon Place-ri Ewabʼal Siwan; ri Kunabʼal Tojil, the Medicine Place of Tojil this was the hiding place of Tojil where Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ went to hide Tojil in a hidden place named Kunabʼal Tojil.

Thick with Serpents; tzatz chi Kumatz was this hiding place of Tojil; thick too with Jaguar, Rattlesnakes, Fer-de-Lance; tzatz chi Bʼalam, Sochoj, Qʼanti thick with venomous vipers, lethal serpent, poisonous snakes was this Medicine Place of Tojil known as Kunabʼal Tojil; Tojilʼs Medicine was the hiding place of Tojil on the Mountain named Pa Tojil where Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ came upon a hideaway in a Great Forest-Nim Kʼechelaj where Tojil was hidden away in his hiding place named Hidden Canyon-Ewabʼal Siwan.

It was there in that Great Forest-Nim Kʼechelaj where Tojil was hidden by the AjKʼixbʼ; AjKʼajbʼ; those known as Nahualli who were ʼBlood-letting Priestsʼ who bled blood with the Maguey Thorn and Stingray Spine; these were the Sacrificers of the Obsidian Blade who were the Punishing Penitent Priests of Sacrifice known as AjQʼij; AjKin those who were of the Sun. They were just ʼOneʼ were they there together with those known as:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

Alternative Translation: Pa Tojil; Pa Kunabʼal Tojil; Pa Nima Kʼicheʼlaj; Ewabʼal Siwan Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ

This was when Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ came to where there was a Great Forest-Nima Kʼichelaj it was there that Tojil was hidden by Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

body:
Pa Tojil; Place of Tojil is the name of this mountain today; Pa Tojil was where the Kabʼawil Tojil was hidden when he was hidden in his hiding place by Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ. This was when Tojil was hidden on the mountain known as Pa Tojil in a Great Forest: Nima Kʼichelaj.

They gave a name to this hiding place of Tojil on the Mountain known as Place of Tojil: Pa Tojil. The name they named this hidden place that was the hiding place of Tojil on the mountain known as Pa Tojil this was the name of the hidden hiding place of Tojil who was hidden in a Great Forest, on a Great Mountain known as Pa Tojil.

The place where they hid Tojil was in a hidden hiding place; the place where they hid Tojil was on the Great Mountain known as Pa Tojil where there was a Great Forest; Nima Kʼichelaj where the hiding place of Tojil was known as Medicine of Tojil; Kunabʼal Tojil.

Kunabʼal Tojil; Medicine of Tojil or Healing Place of Tojil is the name given to this hidden hiding place where they hid Tojil on the Great Mountain of Pa Tojil named by the First Fathers as Kunabʼal Tojil: Medicine Place of Tojil or the Place of Medicine of Tojil.

This place Kunabʼal Tojil is known as the Mountain Place; Juyubʼal spoken of as Pa Tojil; Pa Tojil, a mountain thick with Serpents-Kumatz; Pa Tojil, a mountain thick with Jaguar-Bʼalam, Rattlesnake-Sojchoj, and Qʼanti-Barba Amarilla.

There in the forest they left their Kabʼawil Tojil; they left him hidden in the forest.  Kabʼawil Tojil was hidden in the forest by the AjKʼixb; those of Maguey Spine, those of the Stingray Spine, the Blood-letters; and the AjKajbʼ Temple Priests, Sacrificial Priests, the Punishing Penitent Priest of the Obsidian Blade. They were the ones who left Tojil hidden in the forest.

In just one place were those named: Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam. It was they who came together as one in the forest as AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ; for they were one now with one-an-other as when they left; yet they did not return as they had gone away in search of ʼsomeoneʼ who could guide and protect them along the way.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These are those who journeyed to Tollan Tzuy-Wa for a reason; so when they returned they were not the same as when they left. They left as Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam to return as the AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ from Tollan.

As ʼOneʼ they watched and waited for the Dawn up above on the mountain Jaqawitz, as it is named; Jaqawitz then was the name of the Mountain-top upon which they watched and waited for the Dawn: Saqirik.

Those who were there were the AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ known as the First Four Fathers: Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam.

ʼXa Junʼ; As ʼJust One-Xa Junʼ they awaited the Dawn there above atop the Mountain Jaqawitz is its name: Jakʼawitz ubʼi.

At a short distance between where they were gathered together at Jaqawitz were hidden the Kabʼawil of the Tamubʼ and Ilokabʼ. The Tamubʼ hid their Kabʼawil at the place named Amaqʼ Tam; Pueblo of the Tree Trunk; Tribe of the Tree Trunk: Amaqʼ Tam.  This is where the Kabʼawil of the Tamubʼ was placed; and, there is where the Kabʼawil of the Tamubʼ or ʼTree Trunk Peopleʼ celebrated the Dawn; chiriʼ xsaqir wi-there they celebrated the Dawning of the Dawn together as a People; as One; together as Pueblo; those whose name is named: Tamubʼ.

The Ilokabʼ who were the ʼHoney Huntersʼ hid their Kabʼawil in the place known as Amaqʼ Ukʼin Kʼat-ʼthe Burn of the Sunʼ or ʼWhere the Sun Burntʼ or ʼthe Maize Drinkʼs Fireʼ ʼFire to Cook the Maize Drinkʼ or ʼWarp of the Weave of the Harvest Netʼ or ʼHarvest Net of the Jocoteʼ Ukʼin Kʼat is the name of the hiding place of their Kabʼawil. It was they who watched for the Dawn, Saqirik a short distance between one another.

The Sun dawned upon them here in a place named after their name known as the Pueblo of the Trunk:  Amaqʼ Tam. Amaqʼ Tam is their name, the name given to their home, the home of the Tamubʼ.

Amaqʼ Uqʼin Kʼat is the place where the Ilokabʼ watched for the Dawn, and this is where the Kabʼawil of the Ilokʼabʼ was placed there just a short distance between; betwixt the mountains-xa kok uxol juyubʼ of the other Tribes known as the Pueblos; Amaqʼ who were ʼJust One-Xa Junʼ with those of Tojil.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
It was there that the Rabʼinalebʼ, Qʼaqʼchekelebʼ, Aj Tzʼikina Ja gathered together with the Small Tribes-Chʼuti Amaqʼ and Big Tribes-Nima Amaqʼ. In just One Place they came to a halt; they stopped there together; the detained themselves there as Just One People and, as Xa Jun-Just One together they gathered together to celebrate council as Just One Pueblo-Xa Jun Amaqʼ to watch, to wait for the Dawn.

In just one place they waited for the coming out of the Great Star-relik uloq Nima Chʼumil-Morning Star, the Great Star that they called Ikʼoqʼij by name.

This is the Great Star known as: “First to come out before the Face of the Sun-Nabʼe chel uloq chuwach Qʼij. ¡TA SAQIROQ! When Dawn Came! When the Dawn of the Sun Came!”

“Here comes the bright-shining Star; the Sun-Bearer-Ikʼoqʼij that rises just before the Dawn,” they said.

They were ʼJust One-Xa Junʼ there: Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam.

They could not sleep, nor did they rest for the worry of their weary souls; for their restless hearts were filled with woe; they just felt an anguished agony there before its imminent arrival; distressed, distraught were their anxious souls as they watched waiting before the Dawn; as they watched waiting there before the Rising Sun.

And that is how it was when one of them said: “It is not so sweet this place that we have come to here. ¡Aqʼaroq! ¡Aqʼaroq!”

“If only we could see the birth of the Sun! What have we done, we were once the same as one another on our mountain place-qajuyubʼal-from where we come; from where we came.”

“We just abandoned it; we just divided up and separated when before we lived as if we were one,” they said when they spoke together with one another.

This is when they spoke to one-an-other as they pondered their pitiable plight; as they faced the fear, as the faced their fright; as they cried out into the deep dark of night there before the Dawn.

This is when they spoke; for their hearts were now desperate to see the Dawn: Saqirik.

Their hearts could not be consoled, for they grieved to see the Dawn with the Rising of the Sun.  Maja kʼut chi kubʼaroq kikʼux chi re usaqirik.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The ones that were tranquil, the ones who felt contentment were the Kabʼawil in the Canyons-pa taq Siwan, in the Forests-pa taq Kʼechelaj among the flowering bromeliad, among the hanging moss; there amongst the Many Trees of the Great Forest is where there Kabʼawil were in a contented state of great tranquility.

It was not upon wooden pedestals that they were placed; it was in the forest that they felt at home.

So then they were the first to speak, those named: Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz.

Great was their destiny; they were strong of heart; ancestral anima animated their ancient souls; this is why they were greater than all other Kabʼawil of all the other Tribes; of all the other Pueblos;  of all the other People; truly, great was the destiny of the Kabʼawil: Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz.

And so truly great was their destiny before all the other Kabʼawil of all the other Pueblos. Great were their ancient ancestral powers of transformation that was their nawal essence; that was their nawal condition; that was their nawal character and nature; the nawal nature of these Kabʼawil that were Nawal Ancestors in every way, shape, and form; whose magical changing and transforming nawal ways made these Kabʼawil who they were and how they were known and named: Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz.

They were those who moved about in the world on two legs and on four legs to open the way; to lead the way; to guide the way to become who they need be at the moment in order to move about as they wished and willed themselves to appear among the People of the Pueblos; at first to cause amazing wonder and astonishing awe; but then to create shocking fright and surprising fear.

For truly their presence caused fearful fright in all the Pueblos and all their People whose hearts; whose souls could only be calmed by: Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam.

Yet their hearts found no bitterness towards the Kabʼawil they had carried for so long on their backs ever since their departure when they walked away from Tulan Tzuy Wa; the place known as Relebʼal Qʼij: the Coming Out Place of the Sun.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
It was just there in the Forest; pa Kʼechelaj when the Dawn; Saqiribʼal came for Tojil, pa Tojil; for Awilix, pa Awilix; for Jaqawitz, pa Jaqawitz as it is said today.

Xawi kʼu chiriʼ xkʼoje wi pa Kʼechelaj are Saqiribʼal pa Tojil; pa Awilix; pa Jaqawitz; kuchaʼxik wakamik.

It was there in the forest atop their Place of Dawn-Saqiribʼal-Dawning Mountain when the Dawn came for Tojil; for Awilix; for Jaqawitz as it is said today.

This then was the Sowing; this then was the Dawning of Our Grandfathers; QaMam, Our Fathers-Qajaw at this Place of Sowing, Place of Dawning; Ewaxibʼal; Saqiribʼal.

For there it was there in the Forest; Kʼicheʼlaj of Saqiribʼal; of the Mountain of Dawn that Sunrise came when Dawn arrived for Tojil, for Awilix, for Jaqawitz as they are spoken of today. This was the Sowing-Ewaxibʼal; this was the Dawning; Saqiribʼal of Our Grandfathers, Our Fathers:  QaMam, QaQajaw.

Xa kʼu Jun Xechawax wi; Xsaqir wi ronojel Amaqʼ.

There was just One Sowing; just One Dawning for all of the Pueblos.

Waʼe chiqabʼij chik Saqirik; uwachinik Qʼij, Ikʼ, Chʼumil.

Here we shall tell next of the Dawning; the Appearance of the Sun, Moon, Star.

Here now we shall tell next of the Dawning; when we tell of the appearance of the Sun, Moon, and Star.

Here then is the telling of the Dawning; the telling of the Emergence of the Face of the Sun; of the Moon; of the Star.

Great was the contentment of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj,  Ikʼi Bʼalam when they saw the Morning Star-Ikʼoqʼij-when it came out first, sparkling in the Sky it sprouted forth as it came up and out First-Nabʼe before the Sun.

This then was when they unbound to unbundle their Incense-Pom-Copal that came all the way from the Relebʼal Qʼij; these were bundles of Copal-Pom-Incense that they carried back from the Coming Out Place of the Sun.

Their hearts delighted in their untying to unravel the three different bundles of incense given as gifts of gratitude; given as gifts of thanks; given as gifts that came from the thankfulness of their hearts and souls:

Mixtam Pom; Mictlan Pom was the incense that Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ brought.

Kawistan Pom was the incense Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ carried with him.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Kabʼawil Pom was the incense that Majukʼutaj bore on his back.

These three Noble Lords of these three Noble Lineages brought back three varieties of Pom: Mixtam Pom; Kawistan Pom; Kabʼawil Pom.

This is what they burned their Pom in the direction of the Sunrise, when the Sky brightened; when it whitened; when it lightened with nostalgic reminiscence; xesaqbʼisanik; with the heartfelt remembrance of the Oriente at the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij.

So this then was when they wept with happiness; sweetly they wept with contentment when the Sky began to brighten the Face of the Earth.

This was when they thought upon the Dawn at the Coming Out Place of the Sun; when they contemplated from where they had come there before the arrival of their first Dawning of their Sun.

This then was when they burnt their beloved incense; their sacred incense; their blessed incense; their precious incense: Loqʼolaj Pom. They burnt it there in the direction of the Rising Sun.

So this then was when they wept again; this time they wept because they did not see it; for they did not see the Birth of the Sun-Ralaxik Qʼij. They did not see it yet despite the Sky whitening as began brightening to then begin lightening up the horizon without the Sun ever being born.

And then it came; the Sun came up; when at first it began show it came up nice and slow; and then up it rose as it rose up and up; and as it rose up and up it grew and grew; this then was when it began to grow and grow when the Sun came up to show its face at the Coming Out Place of the Sun, Relebʼal Qʼij; when the Sun finally rose it climbed up into the Sky up and above  the House of the Dawn; there at the Coming Out Place of the Sun...chilaʼ pa Relebʼal Qʼij.

They were all made content; content with the rising Sun were they all; all those who were there; the Small Animals; the Big Animals; Chʼuti Chikop; Nimaʼ Chikop; they were just so very content with the emergence of the Sun; with the sunrise there at dawn  the Animals were all made content.

All of them came out to the waterʼs edge; there beside the streams; there beside the rivers; they came out and on to the rims of the canyons and ravines.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They were there on the points of mountain; they came right out upon the outcrops of the rocks there on the mountains; they were there in the mountains out on the points, promontories, and peaks.

Just as one they gazed upon the direction of the rising Sun; there in the direction of the Dawn, in the direction of the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij they just held their gaze watching with great delight as the rising Sun rose in the Sky.

So then Koj-Puma and Bʼalam-Jaguar roared with the first cries of the Guarda Barranco Chajal Siwan; this Brown-backed Solitaire the primordial birdsong of the dawn she sang like a flute, Kʼeletzu is her name, she sang like a flute of the canyon; like a flute did she sing as she sang her song into the canyon with its chasm of silence there at dawning place of the Sun; at the sunrise place of the Dawn.

Guarda Barranco-Cotora Parlanchin-Chajal Siwan-Guardian of the Canyon is this beloved birdʼs name; this Brown-backed Solitaire sung her long sonorous song; she sang  like a flute; she sang her song a dawn; she woke-up singing and kept singing all morning long as she sang her song echoing up and down the canyon walls; just singing as she moved along as she sang her song that she began singing when she rose at dawn to sing her  song that rose up and dropped down with its jingle-jangle sort of metallic flute sound; she sung out at the first sight of the dayʼs bright warm light that arrived with the first rays of dawn of all the days that rose up just for her so she could sing her song there at dawn in the first light of the sun and its ancient way of waking the day with birdsong  at dawn and again at dusk when Chajal Siwan sang her song in the rising and falling Sun;  in the first and last light of the Day this is when she sung: saqnatanoj.

Truly, all the animals were filled with contentment; so, so sweet were their hearts made by the light; by the warmth of the Sun.  They opened their wings wide: Eagle, Kot; White Zopilote, Kuch;  Small Birds, Chʼuti Tzʼikin; Big Birds, Nima Tzʼikin they stretched their wings out wide to welcome home the Sun.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
There on their knees kneeling-xukuxinaq before the presence of the Sun were they, those of the Maguey Spine-AjKʼixbʼ those of the Obsidian Blade-AjKajbʼ. They were there on their knees kneeling-xukulem; mejlem-kneeling on their knees giving thanks with great respect; giving praise with high regard they knelt to give thanks and praise for the Dawning Sun at the Break of Day; as it is said; as they say.

The AjKʼixbʼ knelt there; those who performed blood sacrifice with spines knelt before the Dawn; those who performed sacrifice with their Stingray Spines knelt their before the Sun; those there with their Maguey Thorns were made content with the emergence of the Sun; with the arrival of the Dawn.

The AjKʼajbʼ knelt with their Obsidian Blades; those who practiced sacrifice with Obsidian Blades knelt on their knees showing their gratitude for truly content were they with the arrival and appearance; entrance and emergence of the Dawning Light of the Rising Sun.

Great was their contentment; great was their satisfaction those who were filled with gratitude; those who were filled with thanks; those who were they of the Maguey Thorn; those who were they of the Stingray Spine: AjKʼixb.

Great was their contentment; great was their satisfaction those who were filled with gratitude; those who were filled with thanks; those who were they of the Obsidian Blade: AjKajb.

Those who performed punishing penitential acts of self-sacrifice; those that practiced the blood-letting; blood-gathering ways of self-sacrifice each in their own ancient ancestral way; each with their sacred sacrificial way were there together as Just One-Xa Jun face to face with  radiant, resplendent Face of the Sun.

These AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ were of the Tamubʼ, Ilokʼabʼ who were as happy and content as those of Rabinal, Qʼaqʼchikelebʼ, Aj Tzʼikina Ja; who were happy and content as those of Tujal Ja, Uchabʼa Ja, and those of Kibʼa Ja, AjBatena Ja; and, Yaki Tepew.

How many People; how many Pueblos who were there now that stood before the Dawn!

Innumerable people were there now standing before the Sun but there was only One Dawn for all the many Tribes; Amaqʼ when the Sun rose that Day at Dawn.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
For the Dawn had dawned at the Coming Out Place of the Sun: pa Relebʼal Qʼij; it had come; the Sun rose up as all watched and waiting while pleading and praying that it would and now the could say: Our Dawn has come for Our Sun.

And so it was that the Face of the Earth dried up immediately because of the Sun, just like a person was the Sun when he showed his burning face; when his scorching face appeared it instantly dried the Face of the Earth-Uwach Ulew; the Face of the Earth was toasted dry; it was baked dry as soon as he-the Sun-showed his hot burning, blistering Face; the searing face of the sweltering hot Sun dried the Face the Face of the Earth leaving it completely dried out; burnt to the bone.

Before the searing, scorching Face of the Sun came-out the Face of the Earth had always been a wet, watery place; before the emergence of the Sun the Earth had been a mushy kind of marshy place. This is how the Earth was before the Sun came out; before the Sun came up the Face of the Earth was as very soggy, swampy place.

But then the Sun rose just like a human being, like a person did the Sun rise; and when it rose the Sun was so hot and dry that no one could endure its red hot heat, one could not survive the sizzling heat of the Sun. But he only showed his face when he was born; so that later on all that remained of him was his mirrored reflection; the Sun mirrored his reflection once he passed the mid-point of the Day when the Sun stood straight-up over the Face of the Earth.

“Itʼs not the same Sun that appears to us today,” says their Ancient Word.

And so, just like that, in an instant, they were turned to stone: Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz with all the other Kabʼawilal, with all the other Divinities that took the form of Puma, Koj;  Jaguar, Bʼalam; Rattlesnake, Sochoj; and Fer-de-Lance-Qʼanti-Barba Amarilla spoken of originally: Koj, Bʼalam, Sochoj, Qʼanti the most dangerous devourers of human flesh in all the land; those whose poisonous venomous bite was more than enough to kill one dead.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This was when Saqi Kʼoxol, the Lord of the Mountain-el Dueño de la Montaña-hid himself up in the branches of the trees when the three of them appeared there; there at emergence of the Sun, Moon, Star; Qʼij, Ikʼ, Chʼumil.

This then was when the Sun, Moon, and Star appeared before all of them there who were the dangerous, deadly ones who when struck by the burning, blistering rays of the Sun were turned to stone; the Deadly Animals were turned to stone for they were transformed by the Sun and turned to Stone. The wild animals and guardians of the trees; the vipers there in the vines were petrified, they were left hard as rocks; they were turned to stone by the hot, dry Face of the Sun.

Had these wild voracious animals not been turned to stone we might not be here today: Koj-Puma, Bʼalam-Jaguar, Sochoj-Rattlesnake, Qʼanti-Qʼantil are all ravenous animals who were innumerable before the Dawn; before emergence of the Sun; before the Coming out of the Dawning Sun.

Without Saqi Kʼoxol perhaps we would not be alive today; had the First Animals-Nabʼey Chikop-Original Animals not been turned to stone by the petrifying heat of the Sun, we might not be here at all.

Their hearts filled with great joy and happiness; their souls filled with great contentment and ease the moment the Sun sprouted out of the Earth; when Dawn illuminated the Face of the Earth with its bright shining light; the Dawning Sun just shimmered as it shined for all those who were there at the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij.

Great was their delight; great was their satisfaction, those known as:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam; they were made content; finally at ease for their hearts were made sweet; with the peace they felt with the Dawn of their Sun-Xsaqirik.

Mythic Time; Mythic Belonging; Mythic Divinity

Being At Home in the World of the Divine Ancestors

Being at Home in the Imaginal Realm of Myth

body:
This is the mythic power of ʼentering the word to enter into the mythic momentʼ by stepping out of the terror of history to step into the transcendence of the mythic present. There is a sense of belonging to a place and a people that provides human beings with a sense of being at home in the world. This sense of being at home in the world is to feel that one belongs in this world comes through myths of that come from the place and people that form and shape the myth of being and belonging in the world; the myth that forms and shapes the place and peopleʼs sense of being and belong in the World.

This is the ʼcontentmentʼ that the Popol Wuj speaks of when it says, “they were happy, they were contentʼ yes they were because they felt at home in the world in which the Sun Rises and the Dawn comes so the seed sprouts and cane grows so that the People of the Maize are at one with Maize that is One with the Sun with its nourishing light and its nurturing warm. When human beings live in a myth that lives within them and that myth tells of the ways of the people and the ways of the place then you can be sure a Human Being feels at Home in the World that is the World they also feel they belong to through the myth of being and becoming that gives a person a sense of belonging.

Perhaps best of all myth teaches us compassion for other as it opens up to a deep knowledge of the People and Places from where and who the myths we read and engage with comes from. In this sense myth is perhaps the most valuable source and resource for understanding the way the People see and understand the World that the myth comes from. What could be more valuable than this in ones study of myth?

This must be how the Popol Wuj was once lived by the Kʼicheʼ Maya and all these other Tribes mentioned here that are the Maya People; Maya Pueblos who lived through this Ancient Ancestral Account of the Sowing and the Dawning.  This feeling of being at Home in the Word in order to belong in the World is brought forth in a very subtle way through this Ancient Account that brings forth a sense of temporal transcendence.

body:
This entering into transcendent time is made possible by the performer of the Ancestral Account and the audience of the Ancestral Account enters mythic time through the continue refrain watching and waiting for the Dawn. This Dawn of the Sun that is anticipated through the text repeating over and over  that the Dawn was getting closer and closer for the time was coming nearer and nearer to when the Sun, Moon, and Star were about to cross over head of Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol.

And then it happens the Dawn comes and suddenly we enter the warmth and light of the first rays of the Sun as our nostalgic remembrance takes us back to the very first page of Popol Wuj where the Maya Scribe say this is the description, revelation, and manifestation of the expression of the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of the Sowing and the Dawning of Life and the Peopling and Populating of the Face of the Earth. Here we are with the Pueblos being named at the Sowing and the Dawning.

IxMuqane brought for the Sowing-Ewaxibʼal by naming  the names of the Place where the Maize Harvest are sown in the Middle of the House; Middle of the Harvest and now the Sun has Dawn and its heat has dried out a very mushy marshy Face of the Earth. We are at Home in the World for we have formed and shaped it through the Former, the Shaper-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol. We have become Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol through the mysterious magic that is a miracle of our mythic imagination with its capacity to mold and model the Imaginal Realm of the Maya Myth of the Sun and Maize.

We have entered the imaginal realm of a very real natural world of the Kʼicheʼ Maya with their Mountains and Plains and their Mountain Place and Canyon Country. Here we are at Home in a World in which we very much belong because we know the story that tells of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea that is the Natural World that Formed as it Shaped the forming and shaping of this Ancient Ancestral Narrative of the People of Maize: Ixim Winaq. This you know only too well ʼas ifʼ it were the most important aspect of this Interpretation of this Translation of Popol Wuj.

body:
We are made to feel ʼas ifʼ we were the Former, the Shaper through the transformative power of the mythic imagination through its capacity and capability to release us from the present moment by entering the mythic moment when the Sun, Moon, and Star are about to pass overhead in the Imaginal Realm to announce the arrival of the Dawn in our mythic imagination that is fed by our life experience in the real world of the Face of the Earth and its relationship with the Sun, Moon, and Stars both Day and Night; Dawn and Dusk as well as Mid-Day and Mid-Night. We have entered all these times in our Mythic Imagination imagining this very real imaginal world of myth that reflect reality in this reality that reflects myth. Enter Trickster with his Obsidian Mirror with plenty of smoke and even more mist.

This brings up the perennial idea that ʼmyths are things that never were but always areʼ which is to say myths exist in the present through our mythic imagination and its ability to bring to life the imaginal realm of myth so that we might transcend reality by transcending ordinary time and space by entering the word of myth to enter the way of myth leading to the world of myth: the Imaginal Realm of the Divine Ancestors.

This is how we create an ecstatic experience that takes transports our soul by entering myth through the ʼeyeʼ of the mythic imagination in order to exist in mythic time and mythic space. This is where we find a deep sense of belonging as the landscape we live in is reflected in the sacred landscape we imagine in myth; just as the people we live with such as the Maya we live with here in the Highlands mirror the Nawal Ancestors and Mythic Figures that live in our mythic imagination to feel a deep sense of belonging in this world that we feel very much at home.

body:
This is the beauty of myth; it tells the deepest truths of human relationships and those human relationships connection and communication with the real world in which we live. Myths speak to us of the most important aspects of life and we can be sure the truths we find in myth have been contemplated by human beings and their divinities for tens of thousands of years. Yet we doubt all of this because of the arrogant and pride of the self-aggrandizing mind of the rational, lineal, analytical, sorts of materialist minds that think they are the end all to all of human conscious which is what it is and what is a joke if it were not so very psychologically infirm. But we give myth the benefit of the doubt in order to really enter into its original genius then we come to realize the highly level of civilizing content that exists within myth.

This is how this Ancestral Account comes to move our soul as we become more and more familiar with this Mythic Masterpiece of the Sowing and the Dawning that has the power and genius to move oneʼs soul by opening oneʼs heart through its mythopoetic language that create mythopoetic metaphors that bind us to the Sacred Landscape while its mythic images and mythic intuitions knot us to the Ancestral Sky with its Ancestral Constellations the embody as they outline the Mythic Figures that move through the Night Sky in the same direction as this Mythic Narrative unfolds.

body:
This is where myth is played out through the movement of the Constellations of the Night Sky that tell us of the mythic events; mythic figures; mythic places that are brought to life through the mythic narratives told by Ancient Ones who shine as bring lights in the dark of the Night. This is why the Dawn is so bright because that is when the Ancestors speak to us through the movements of Nature and the ancestral language of the dawn song and its being sung to speak and communicate with us through the language of the birds; language of the breeze; language of light; language of the sunlight as it plays with the sparkling spectrum of light that twinkle as iridescent colors on the dewdrops at the tip of the leaves in the Sun at Sunrise with its magic white light of the calm and collected; settled and silent; still and quiet sky at Dawn.

This is the language of myth spoken in the landscape to connect with the descendants and their infinite ways of communicating with those who want to connect with the Ancient Ones who transform into whatever they must to connect with their replacements on the Face of the Earth; the Nawal Ancestors in all the forms and shapes that connection and communication takes.

In this way we come to feel at home in the world through our developing a deep sense of belonging to this Place and its People known as Kʼicheʼ Maya and the many Maya Amaqʼ that they name in their naming of the names of those who were there at the Dawn of their Sun. The One and Only Dawn experienced by all the Tribes-Amaqʼ who were their watching and waiting for the Sun, Moon, and Star at this Origin of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Sun.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These are the Original People of this Dawn that was experienced by all as their Dawn; People of Pueblos who came to live in this Sacred Landscape that comes to life through this Ancient Ancestral Account that awakens us to the wisdom that awaits us through walking this myth we come to live by in order to transcend the past in order to live empowered lives in this continuously transforming world. We are just about to enter this Sacred Landscape as reflected in the Imaginal Realm of this Mythic Masterpiece spoken of as the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj. The Dawn of the Kʼicheʼ Sun has risen and so the power and authority of Kʼicheʼ Maya Sovereignty and its Rule will now begin on the Mountain Top Citadel of Jaqawitz.

Jaqawitz

There werenʼt many people in existence up there at the time; there were just a few of them living up on top of the mountain Jaqawitz.

It was there where they met the Sun at Dawn. It was there atop Jaqawitz where they burnt their offerings. There on Jaqawitz the Sunrise shined bright for them at Dawn; there at Dawn the Sun rose upon Jaqawitz; Jaqawitz was the place of their Sun and its Dawn; and this is what made Jaqawitz their Dawning Place; their Dawning Place of their Sun.

There in the East, there at the Coming Out Place of the Sun-chi Relebʼal Qʼij is where they walked away from when they walked away from the place of their origin there in Tolan Tzʼuy Wa.

They were those who walked away from Tolan Tzuy-Wa to abandon it and that is how they came away from that place in the East known as the Relebʼal Qʼij.

That was their Mountain Place; that was their Place of the Plain; that was their Place of the Mountain-Place of the Plain: Juyubʼal, Taqʼajal, their Mountain; their Plain.

Relebʼal Qʼij; there in the East at the Coming Out Place of the Sun was their Mountain Place; their Plain Place; Kijuyubʼal, Kitaqʼajal.

That was their Place of Origin; their Place of Sprouting Forth into the Sky-Earth known as their Mountain, their Plain: Juyubʼ, Taqʼaj.

That is where they come from, those known as:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They grew there on the Mountain Top-Chuwi Juyubʼ; there up above on their Mountaintop is where they grew to become many, many people. Their fortified citadel-kitinamit-came forth there in that place on top of the Mountain-Chuwi Juyubʼ-where they built a palisade known as a kʼoxtun. That is where their Tinamit; Citadel was first made to be built up and brought forth; when their citadel-tinamit was built by a multiplying population of people; a growing population of people who lived there in a village-chinamit on top of the Mountain known as Chuwi Juyubʼ.

Tinamit is a walled enclosure while a Chinamit is a group of people or a village but the signification of these words seems to move about with changes of meaning depending on the way they are used and the context in which they are found.

A Tinamit can be used to talk about a Territory or a Realm or a Kingdom of a People when speaking of the Tinamit Kʼicheʼ one is speaking of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom or the Realm of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ.

Whereas chinamitl comes from the cane of maize or carrizo cane to signify a village that is enveloped by its milpa or chinamitl that is a cane enclosure or cane wall known as a chinampa a word derived from chinamitl. It is no small thing that mitl is an arrow used to defend the People of a Pueblo who are set upon from an attacking force from the outside. A chinamit also defines a group of people who make-up a village that lives within the fortification of a tinamit which is a fortified citadel that is defended with chimalli-shields-pokobʼ and mitl-arrows and tlacoltl-bow.

We will enter into battles where the shield and the bow-sting and bows and arrows will enter into the story-telling; myth-making Epic Conquests of Kʼicheʼ Maya Warlords and Captains and the Mountain People; Mountain Tribes they must vanquish and subjugate by defeating and destroying them in battle. This is all a preparation for those bellicose mythic narratives.

There upon Chuwi Juyubʼ is where they were when they appeared up above in the Sky overhead. It was there where they were at the time of their emergence; those that appeared were the Sun, Qʼij; the Moon, Ikʼ; and the Star, Chʼumil.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This was their place of emergence when they appeared there at Dawn; they appeared there when the Sun rose to light-up the Face of the Earth; when the light of the Sun lit-up and illuminate everything there was in existence beneath the Sky.

That is the place on the mountain top where their singing of their song began; Qamuku is the name of their song.

They sang it; they sang that song and when they sang it they began to weep in their heart; this song that made them weep is the song they sung from deep within; the song they sung was their song: Qamuqu. And this is what was said when they sang their song Qamuqu; Qamuku the song that they sung together as one; the song that was sad; the song they sang as one that made feel sad yet strong:

“¡Aqʼaroq! Ay de nosotros! We lost our way in Tulan, gone astray from one another we went our separate way in Tulan, in Tulan. It was there where we split-up, it was there we went our way, when we divided up and went astray from one another in Tulan, in Tulan.”

“That was when we lost our way, when we lost our way in Tulan, in Tulan. It was there we left our Older Brothers abandoned when we left them there on their own in Tulan, in Tulan.”

“It was there in Tulan, in Tulan where we left behind our Younger Brothers; when we left our Older Brothers; when we left them alone and moved on and moved; when we left our Young Brothers behind when we abandoned Tulan, when we left Tulan; we moved on; we moved on from Tulan, from Tulan.”

“It was there we went wrong; we went wrong in Tulan, in Tulan! We went our own way when we moved on to leave our Older and Younger Brothers long gone, long gone; in Tulan, in Tulan.”

“Where could it be that they watched and waited for the Dawn? Where were they when they saw the Dawn; where we they when they saw the emergence of the Sun; where were they when came the appearance of the Sun?”

“Where could they have been at the Coming of the Dawn; when Dawn shone for all; when the Sun shone for all at Dawn; at Dawn; when the Sun came to shine upon us all; when the Sun shined upon us all; where were they at the Dawn; at the Dawn?”

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“Where were they at the Coming of the Dawn, the Dawn; our Older Brothers, our Younger Brothers of Tulan, of Tulan?” sang the AjKʼixbʼ; sung the AjKʼajbʼ of the Yaqui Winaq when they sang that Sad Song; when they sang that Sad Song Qamuku; Qamuqu when they abandoned Tulan; Tulan; Tulan!

Qamuqu; Qamuku Qamuqu; Qamuku

Qamuqu: Our Burial, Our Death and Burial, Qa-Our, Muquj-Burial to create a mourning song of departure, a sad weeping song of drinking; a sad song sung upon abandoning the place they once called home Our Drinking, Our Toasting: Qamuku. Qamuku: our vision, our sight, our seeing; Qamuku Our Sight that we lost when our eyes were veiled like mist on a mirror by Our Formers; Our Shapers who did not want us to see-muku as Kabʼawil can see close and far and through rock and trees and stones and mountains…Qamuku: what happen to our vision, we no longer can see our Older and Younger Brothers to known where they are and how they are! ¡Aqaroq!

We never find out just exactly what Qamuqu means but it signifies many deep and important things when it comes to the Sowing and the Dawning because muqu is to sow seeds just as it is to bury the dead. And now that we have experienced the Dawning perhaps it is time to experience the Sowing; to bring forth the Sowing and Dawning.

Qamuqu is when the Maya milperos work their milpa after the last yearʼs harvest they must bury the dried-out rotten cane known as qʼumaraq aj. In this way last yearʼs leaf and canes are buried in long straight rows dried out, decimated, disintegrating rotten canes.

These canes are buried in long straight rows that that the workers of the milpa; Abʼixik who are very orderly working their milpa cover with earth to form and shape what look exactly alike long burial mounds about two varas wide and as long as the milpa which is traditionally a cuerda or kʼaʼm long. This long, relatively thin mound of buried cane is named just exactly what it looks like: Qamuqu, Our Burial.

body:
Once these long rows of buried cane are left to decompose for a month or more then the next yearʼs seed is sown in between the rows of ʼqamuquʼ so that the seed is sown down below in the trough formed and shaped between the rows of buried cane; rows of qamuqu where the moisture from the dew collects all night long. This is down in the trough or swale when and where the first rain falls to catch all the first downpours of Jun Raqan Jabʼ or One Footed Rain water that falls with the first rain fall. This is what qamuqu signifies when it comes to the milpa.

But sense Qamuqu is sung when thinking upon Tulan and how it all went wrong then perhaps it is a ʼdrinking songʼ meant to provoke tears of remembrance that bring on weeping and wailing of regret upon leaving oneʼs older and younger brothers behind in Tulan: Qamuquj as ʼourʼ drinking songs makes a great deal of sense since we have already been asked to drink to the telling of the names of the Fathers of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

We must pause for a moment to attempt an understanding of what is going on here with this name Qamuqu that could mean many things but the text does not tell us assuming everyone will always know what it means to be singing our song Qamuku, or Qamuqu.  There is the phrase used in this section when talking about who the ʼdeer skinsʼ must be protected because they are useful in hunting to deceive the prey that says:  are e ri umuquwach; these are deceptive; these are for deception!

Qamuqu most likely signifies our being deceived at Tulan; Tolan; Tollan; Tullan but that doesnʼt mean this word doesnʼt mean all the other possible meaning because the ʼwordʼ itself is a form of ʼmetaphorʼ that shapes the idea of deception. And we are about to enter into a beguiling narrative of tricksterʼs deception. So allow the meaning to open up because they are meant to be multiple indeed! This maybe the most fascinating section of the Popol Wuj because the way that it is written is ʼcompletely otherʼ than anything else we have seen.

body:
No translation has clarified this and because of that we enter the rest of reading of the Popol Wuj confused as to ʼwho is whoʼ and why exactly they ʼdo what they doʼ so let us briefly bring forth what we know so you can move through your reading of Popol Wuj bolstered by our knowledge of language and custom that we know to be truer than true. This was written specifically for you and your deeper comprehension of this ancient ancestral song: Qamuqu or Qamuku.

Qamuqu: Our Burial, Our Death and Burial, Qa-Our, Muquj-Burial to create a mourning song of departure, a sad weeping song of drinking song upon abandoning the place once called home Our Drinking, Our Toasting: Qamuku.

We never find out just exactly what Qamuqu means but it signifies many deep and important things when it comes to the Sowing and the Dawning because muqu is to sow seeds just as it is to bury the dead. And now that we have experienced the Dawning perhaps it is time to experience the Sowing; to bring forth the Sowing and Dawning. Sowing of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ Chuwi Juyubʼ on the Mountain Top of Jaqawitz

“Tojil was just the name of the Kabʼawil of the Yaki Winaq. Yolkwat Kitzalkwat is his name known as Heart of the Serpent Quetzalcoatl or in Maya Kʼicheʼ Ukʼuʼx Ulew Qʼuqʼumatz was the name of Yolkwat Kitzalkwat Quetzalcoatl back in Tulan.

“It is just because the name of our deity Yolkwat Kitzalkwat is he who was our Kabʼawil when we split-up from one another back in Tulan; back there in Tzuy-Wa when we left our Kabʼawil behind in Tulan Tzuy-Wa. They left with us as one, we were all there together as one; just one and the same when we left with our brothers, when we left Tulan-Tzuy-Wa,” they said when they spoke with one another.

They remembered their Older Brothers; they remembered their Younger Brothers, the Yaki Winaq who watched the sunrise there in México, as it is called now. There was a few of those Méxica Yaki who stayed right there at the Coming Out Place of the Sun Relebʼal Qʼij.

Those who stayed there were the Tepew Oliman is their name. They are those known as the Sovereign Lords of Rubber Lands; they of the Noble Rule of the Lands of Rubber: Tepew Oliman.

body:
This is the name of those of the rubber groves beside the water there on the Gulf Coast of Campeche; Gulf Coast of Tabasco as the Land of Rubber is known: Tepew Oliman.

“They became known as the Ones we Left Behind-Xeqakanaj kanoq,” they said, the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ known as AjKʼixb, AjKajbʼ. Great was the affliction that they suffered in their hearts; great was the suffering that afflicted their souls there upon the mountain of Jaqawitz.

They felt the same as those known as the Tamubʼ, Ilokabʼ. They were just there in the forest: kʼechelaj.

“Amaqʼ Tʼan, Amaqʼ Dan,” is the name of the Amaqʼ Tamubʼ; Pueblo Tamubʼ and it was their sacrificial priests, AjKʼixb, AjKajbʼ of the Tamubʼ who were there with their Kabʼawil who was also Tojil.

There was just one name for the Kabʼawil of all three branches of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ People: Tojil.

Tojil was the same name as the Kabʼawil of the Rabʼinalebʼ only these Rabʼinal People spoke of their Kabʼawil Tojil with a name that changed just a bit: Jun Toj, as it is said; the name of the deity of the Rabʼinalebʼ; the Kabʼawil of the Rabinal Winaq was Jun Toj; the day name Jun Toj, One Rain; One Storm; One Debt; One Sacrificial Debt. One drop of Blood; for one drop of water that is the sacrificial debt exchange between humanity and divinity Jun-Jun; One to One: Blood for Rain. And that is the reason they call him Jun Toj which is the name of Tojil among the Rabʼinalebʼ because their language known today as ʼAchiʼ was so very close to being the same as the other ʼKʼecheʼ language.

Maya Achi is the language known today as the spoken and written Kʼiche language of Rabinal. This language is were similar to the Kʼicheʼ of the Central Kʼiche but different enough to create a separate language that is known as Maya Achi of Rabinal where the Dance Drama of the Rabinal Achi continues to be danced out telling the story of Jun Toj similar to the way Dance Dramas were danced out long ago; similar to the long performance of this production of the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

body:
But this is just what is said, because the Kʼicheʼ language that is spoken by the Rabʼinalebʼ is almost exactly the same as that which is spoken by the other Kʼicheʼ people.

Now what changes most is the speech spoken by the Qʼaqʼchekelebʼ or Kaqchikelebʼ and this is because of the difference in the name of the Kabʼawil when they left Tulan Tzuy-Wa.

Sotzʼi Ja Chimalkan is the name of their deity, because of this there is a difference in their ways of speech today. It is just because of the name of their deity that created the changes in the naming of their Pueblos; Chinamit  known as the AjPop Sotzʼil, AjPop Xajil, as they are named, as they are known; the names of their Pueblos:  AjSotzʼil, AjXajil; the People of the Bat; the People of the Dance.

It is just their Kabʼawil that created the change in their speech, in their language. This happened when these people were given their Kabʼawil in Tulan.

The language with which they spoke together changed the way the people, the Kaqchikel People, spoke with one another.

It was their stone images of their Kabʼawil that caused the difference in speech, the speech of the stone images that the people were given; these were the stone images of the Kabʼawil that they carried away with them when they left Tulan in the dark of night amidst the darkness: Ta xpe Tulan chi qʼequmal.

But there was only One Sowing, One Dawning for all of the Pueblos.

Xa kʼu Jun Xawax wi; Xa Jun Xsaqir wi ronojel Amaqʼ.

Yet each group that came away from Tulan came away with their Kabʼawil that spoke their own language; all of the Pueblos left with Kabʼawil that spoke their own form of speech.

Now let us speak of the places where they stopped and stayed there on the mountain. In just one place were the four of them when they stopped to stay in a resting places on their way; their names were Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam; those were their names.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Their hearts wept for Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz who they left in the bromeliad; in the hanging moss in the great forest; in the deep canyon is where they left them; their Kabʼawil were left hidden in their hideaways in the Hidden Canyon; Ewaxibʼal Siwan and the Great Mountain; Nimaʼ Kʼechelaj.

Origin of the veneration of Tojil

This was when they went to perform sacrifice with their sacred fire where they gave sacrifice with burnt offerings. This was the origin of the veneration of Tojil; this was the beginning of their rituals of sacrifice when they came before the divine presence of Tojil, Awilix.

This was when they went to see them, to visit them in the forest, in the canyons; when they went to invoke them; to worship them; to give them thanks and gratitude; the show them praise and worship them there by prostrating themselves by bending down-low before them there in the forest at dawn.

It was just through their nawal presence that they spoke; that is to say through the Stone Images becoming ʼYoung Menʼ.

The AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ took positions of reverence-wonowoj-kneeling down low ʼas ifʼ  to demonstrate a traditional form of veneration through subjugation to oneʼs Divinity or oneʼs Kabʼawil.

This was a traditional way of to show worship and veneration by kneeling down doubled-over there before their Kabʼawil; prostrating themselves before their Stone Images; Abʼajil as they were known. With their chin upon their knees-wonowoj to demonstrate the highest regard, deep respect for their Kabʼawil who they wished to show reverential adoration by worshipping them by providing them sweet, sweet smell offerings and to sustain them with burnt offering of sacrifice that were the sacrificial offerings they offered up in the round altars of sacrifice.

These Stone Images-Abʼajil were there in the forest but now only their Nawal Spirit spoke to their AjKʼixbʼ, AjKʼajb who came before Tojil there in the Great Forest.

body:
What the AjKʼixibʼ, AjKʼajibʼ brought with them to burn was no great gift; they just brought pine tree resin-qʼol and the blood of the Sun that bleeds as pine sap-xa rachaq noʼj from the wounding of Pine Trees. They brought these gifts along with Iyaʼ which is Pericón to burn before their Kabʼawil there where they made their Ceremonial Fire that was known as a Flower; Kotzʼij with the Power, Qʼaqʼal to change and transform both Sky and  Earth.

The AjKʼixibʼ, AjKʼajibʼ burnt ʼjust pine resin, just pine sap; xa qʼol, xa rachaq noʼj along with pericón flowers-iyaʼ this is what they brought to the mountain to be burnt as sweet smelling, fragrant offerings of the Mountain-Plain; Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj; they brought them to be burnt there before Tojil their Kabʼawil.

So now Tojil spoke through his Nawal to give the knowing that was the knowledge that he need to give the them his AjKʼixibʼ, AjKʼajibʼ

Tojil spoke through his Nawal to provide his Providers, Sustainers-Tzuqul, Kʼool with the knowing-naʼoj of their knowledge-naʼoj so they-the Priests of Tojil-could do what they needed do which was what needed to be done to bring forth the divine will of Tojil the Kabʼawil of those known as AjKʼixibʼ, AjKʼajibʼ those who gave sacrifice with Maguey Spines, those who gave sacrifice with Obsidian Blades.

The greater his Tzuqul, Kʼool became the greater his priests AjKʼixibʼ, AjKʼajibʼ for they were one and the same in this Nawal game of changing faces to mirror changing names. It would be they AjKʼixibʼ, AjKʼajibʼ who were AjKʼixibʼ, AjKʼajibʼ who were Bʼalam Kiʼ Tzeʼ; Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam who were the First Four Father known and named Our Grandfather, Our Fathers; QaMam, QaQajaw who will make the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo the Great People, Great Pueblo; Nimaʼ Winaq, Nimaʼ Amaqʼ that they wil become because of their Promising Birth and Propitious Destiny. All of which we shall enter into now.

body:
This is what he-the Nawal of the Kabʼawil-said when he spoke to them-his Priests; his Providers; his Sustainers-who listened to the Nawal of Tojil their Kabʼawil of those who were there on the Mountain with Tojil who now spoke his words that were his will; the will of Tojil the Kabʼawil of those who were there. This is to say when Tojil spoke to the AjKʼixbʼ, AjKʼajbʼ:

“This here; this here will come to be our mountains, our plains; qajuyubʼal, qataqʼajal chuxik, it will become ours; our mountain-plain; qajuyubʼ-taqʼaj. It will become ours to become yours; yours to rule; for what is ours to rule must be yours to rule,” said Tojil, Awilix.

“Our destiny is great; our birth sublime because all of the Tribes here are now yours, yours to rule,” said the Nawal of Tojil, Awilix.

“We are only going to be your companions, your friends; you allies here in your enclosed cities, your walled towns-itinamit-your fortresses, your strongholds. This is why we must just give you your knowing, your knowledge-xawi chiqayaʼinaʼoj,” said Tojil, Awilix.

“Never reveal our existence before the Pueblos, before the Tribes when we show our power to cause affliction because now they are so many, these People who make-up these Pueblos who create the great plenty of Mountain Tribes for they multiply more and more to become great many.”

“Never reveal our whereabouts before the populous Pueblos, before the bountiful Tribes when we show our preponderance for power and our powerʼs preponderant potential and possibility to cause anguish and affliction amongst the profuse populations of people and pueblos because now they are so many now.”

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“These prosperous prolific People who make-up the plentiful populations of these populous Pueblos of plentiful and prodigiously productive people whoʼs prolific productivity has produces a populous of profuse plenty,  so that these providentially prodigious Pueblos of plentiful People are so many now that they come the Mountains and Plain as never before; for they have multiplied and multiplied to become more and more through some sort of divine providence found in the maize and cacao the eat day and night that has led them to become a great, great many People of a great quantity of Pueblos of People of Maize; of People of Cacao.”

“Make certain that we should never be captured by them. Meanwhile, provide us with the little creatures that live in the bunch grass and seedy brush, like the offspring of the deer; clutches of birds; the brood of the animals,” they said, those who were now known as los Tojiles; those who made-up the Kabʼawil of the  Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz.

“Just come give us a taste of blood, just give us a little taste of blood as a bit of sacred sustenance; just one drop. Show us a little consideration; just show us a kindness by favoring us in this way. This is what we ask of you; this all we ask of you,” said the Tojiles.

“May the skins of the deer remain with you, take care of them, the deerskins, for they can be useful to deceive in the hunt; so just flay them so you can wear them since they are always so very useful in the art of deception.”

“May the deerskin embody us as an exchange for our essence; may they embody our nature before the eyes of the Pueblos; the Tribes; ri Amaqʼ. Deerskins are what one needs most when one is called to provide for others; when one must sustain others with their sustenance,” said Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz.

“When they ask: ʼWhere is Tojil?ʼ”

“Show them the Sacred Bundles of Deer Skin-KʼuʼKej-Sacred Cover of Deer Skins, but do not show who you are.”

“There is much that you will come to do; and truly great will become your destiny; superior to all the rest; truly sublime shall be your condition; ikikʼojeʼik when your true nature; ikikʼojeʼik is brought forth,” said the Tojiles.
