source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Those of all the Pueblos were now made content-kekikot; they could clearly see that those of the Jaqawitz were not so very many. On the other hand those of the Pueblos consisted of a great multitude; innumerable were the People there; those who were Warriors; those who were Assassins; those who were the Executioners of those known as: Bʼalam Kʼitzeʼ; Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; Majukʼutaj.

This is how the Tribes saw them and this is what made the Pueblo rejoice; for truly the Pueblo was molded and modeled from a proud People who had populated and peopled the Face of the Earth as the formed people; as the shaped people that they were imagined to be; as they were dreamed to be such a long, long ago. And now the Sky-Earth was populated with People who continued on their primordial quest of searching to find what was theirs…

This then was when all the many Mountain People of the Mountain Pueblos were now so very happy; just content were they made for what they saw atop the Mountain of Jaqawitz; and so, they rejoiced because they could see there were not so very many of them up there; there were not so many warriors up on top of that mountain fortress. It was clear there were not so many enemy soldiers protecting the defenses of this mountain stronghold; not so many at all to defend its palisade wall.

And since they were not so many, the Pueblos felt victorious because the Pueblos consisted of many Mountain Tribes who together amount to a great multitude of invading warriors; innumerable were they who now made-up the marauding masses of warrior people who came from the many Mountain Pueblos.

These were Pueblos of aggressive armed warriors who were now made their final preparation before their assault on Jaqawitz. That open mountain they now planned to attack to capture if not kill the Noble Lords who were the Providers, Sustainers; Tzuqul, Kʼool of the Kabʼawiles named Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz, Nikʼaj Taqʼaj who were Providers, Sustainers known as AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ  named:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

body:
And it was they, the First Fathers, who were the Providers, Sustainers; Tzuqul, Kʼool of the Kabʼawiles; Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz, Ikʼi Bʼalam who were the Kabʼawiles of those we know as the First Four Fathers:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

These were those, who were those who were they who were known as the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ; they who were the Providers, the Sustainers; Tzuqul, Kʼool  of those who were named; as those who were known as the Kabʼawil who were given and received at Tulan Tzuy-Wa who were those known; who were those named Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz, Nikʼaj Taqʼaj who were those who guided; who were those who protected those First Four Fathers who were the  Formed Ones; who were the Shaped Ones: AjTzʼaq; AjBʼit.

It was they who were named the Formed Ones, the Shaped Ones; AjTzʼaq; AjBʼit who were those that were the kʼexel-replacement-kʼexuwach of the Former, of the Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol who were now there on top of the mountain citadel of Jaqawitz; Jaqawitz, the name of the Mountain Stronghold; Tenamit surrounded by the Wooden Palisade; Kʼoxtun that is Mountain Fortress known today as Chuwi Juyubʼ.

This is the ʼMountain Place; Juyubʼalʼ where the Pueblos invaded with their many, many warriors; and this is the story we will tell now of those known and named as:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

They were there gathered together all as one at war with one another against those of the Pueblos; they were ready now for the combat; for the conflict in the battle to be waged there on top of the mountain of Jaqawitz.

They were there all together with their wives; with their children watching and waiting for their enemy to come to them on the mountain top of Jaqawitz; watching and waiting for the Pueblos, the Tribes who were now on their way; as they came up climbing; as they came up by making their way up the steep mountainside that rose up to Jaqawitz.

body:
And then they climbed as they came; all of them came climbing; all the many soldiers came climbing up the mountain; the warriors, the killers, the assassins; the avenging armed aggressors; the aggressive armed avengers they came in one massive attack against the citadel city that was now completely surrounded by the spiked wooden walled of the palisade known as a kʼoxtun.

They were no less than 16000-xa kachuy enemy on their way;  nor less than 24000-xa oxchuy warriors of the Pueblos that came to surround the Mountain Stronghold; the Great Walled Citadel; Nim Tinamit of Jaqawitz.

The multitudes of Mountain Tribe warriors now encircled the mountain citadel; they completely enclosed the wooden-wall palisade as the masses of warriors encased as they enveloped those who were now trapped inside. Like a great serpent they would squeeze and squeeze to then swallow their prey whole.

This then was when those of the Pueblos just burst their lungs as they called out in a truly chaotic way all with the intention to create a cataclysmic kind of cry that was chaotic call to the chaos and catastrophe of conquest. This was the feeling that now engulfed the mountain top citadel of Jaqawitz.

Jaqawitz was the mountain place-juyubʼal where they, the Mountain Tribes were most certain they would bring down death and destruction upon the bodies and minds; souls and spirits of those who were guided and protected by los Tojiles who now prepared themselves behind the kʼoxtun of Jaqawitz by doing nothing more than readying themselves for the timely opening of the Four Great Big Ceramic Pots known as the Kajibʼ Nimaq Kukubʼ that were placed strategically behind the wooden fortress that formed the palisade of wooden planks and pointed posts that gave shape to the mountain stronghold of Chuwi Juyubʼ.

body:
The Warlords and their War Captains along with their vassal subjects and vassal warriors knew in their hearts this would be the definitive end; that would be the disastrous end of los Tojiles. Those of the Pueblos; those of the Tribes knew of  this most assured destruction and defeat of their enemy inside of their own fortress of Jaqawitz; all at the hands of the boisterous Pueblo and its innumerable angry and armed warriors.

They were coming and they wanted those inside to know that they were coming; and, they wanted those inside to know that they would soon be arriving to where they would begin killing those who refused to be taken captive to be enslaved or sacrificed upon the command and instruction of the Noble Lords of the Pueblos.

This would be when the destiny of their war captives would be decided when that time to decide their destiny would inevitably come; and that inevitable time would inevitably come as the People of the Pueblo were so very certain.

But for now the time of watching and waiting had passed because the moment of destiny had come; the invasion and conquest of Jaqawitz had arrived; a a matter of fact it was well underway.

And so it was that thousands of Pueblo warriors continued coming to prepare for one great wave of attack announced by the uninterrupted calling and crying out of their earsplitting screams as they began their invasion of the mountain fortress of Jaqawitz that sat above by coming at it from below.

And so they came above as planned from down below; just screeching, just screaming;  just squealing, just shrieking  as they roared up the mountain blowing their sharp shrill bone-whistles with their trimmer and trill; while trumpeting their ancestral conchs to inflict deed intimidation by igniting fear; by inciting terror in those of Jaqawitz who were there to hear it all long before the battle began.

Those inside those wooden walls of the great kʼoxtun wall were calm; they were cool; and, they were collected since they knew they were all well protected.

body:
The wives and children of those of Jaqawitz were safe there where they were lined up right behind well-armed and well-adorned works of wood who were the finely dressed and highly embellished wooden warriors knowing they were ready to repel the attack sent to take them captive.

They had no fear because they were told not to be afraid because they knew what to do and were prepared to do it after theyʼd watched and waited for those to climb up the mountainside of Chuwi Juyubʼ in order to do what they were order to do right there before them; there on the rampart walls of the wooden palisade.

The wooden palisade wall that the killer;  assassins of the Pueblos were about to come up and over  to break through this great wall of defense after clawing their way up the steep, steep slopes of Jaqawitz.

There the warriors of the Pueblos were; standing there before the wall and the entrance to Jaqawitz after climbing up to where they were now. Hungry to finish what they began in the road down below; hungry to destroy their enemy los Tojiles; los Tojiles being those of Jaqawitz; those of Tojil; those of the Kaweq of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom that was born there on top of the mountain: Chuwi Juyubʼ the Mountain Top they were all on at this most pivotal crossroads moment of mythical space and time of this sacred history of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

The moment theyʼd been waiting for had finally come but especially for the avenging warriors who had been made to suffer great humiliation. Now they were here; they were here, they were there; they were everywhere; suddenly there wasnʼt anywhere that they, the Warriors of the Tribes-ri AjLabʼal Amaqʼ were not.

And so it was that by seeing the Warriors were everywhere around Jaqawitz and knowing those Warriors now surrounded the palisade wall-kʼoxtun of the citadel city that this was the sign to ʼsmash-open the great big potsʼ which is to say: xjaqʼ uwi ri kukʼubʼ.

And so then was when were broke-open the four great big pots atop the citadel; atop the Chuwi Juyubʼ; atop the mountain of Jaqawitz.

Kʼate puch ta xjaqʼ uwi ri kukʼubʼ, kajibʼ kʼo wi chi tinamit; chi tinamit Chuwi Juyubʼ; chi tinamit Jaqawitz.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They had not come through the fortress gate when they broke open the tops of the great big pots-xkijaq uwi ri kukubʼ.

This was when they just opened-xjaq the four big pots there amongst the marauding warriors.

They just broke open the lids of the great big pots-xjaqʼ uwi ri kukubʼ when they smashed open-xjaqʼ the lids of the great big pots and when they did so they released the angry captives inside the great big pots standing there in the hot face of the morning sun.

Jaqawitzʼ is the mountain citadel where the Kʼicheʼ Lords were when they opened-jaqa the heads-uwi of the four great big pots kukubʼ or kokobʼ placed in four perfectly chosen places around the fortress wall of the citadel just inside the kʼoxtun of this tinamit of the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

Open-up the Heads of the Great Big Pots-Jaqa uwi ri kukubʼ

Jaqa uwi ri kukubʼ or kokobʼ is the way the mountain Jaqawitz is remembered for all time as the place where the heads of the great big tamale pots were opened to release the Big Round Bees-Wonon and Big Black Wasps-Sitaʼl.

Jaqawitz is where the Dawn is experienced by the Sun ʼbreaking openʼ the Face of the Earth ʼas ifʼ the Earth was the ʼhard tortoise shellʼ that must be ʼbroken openʼ so that the Sun can ʼbreak throughʼ into the Day to create the Destiny of his Mother-Fathers.

Just as the seed must be broken open by the ʼhair-wiʼ of the ʼsprout-alʼ so the maize sprout can shoot-up and sprout-out of the hard ʼFace of the Earth-Uwach Ulewʼ which is the image ʼcomes upʼ over and over and over again in our recitation and revelation of the Ancient Word that forms the Ancestral Way that shapes the truth and tradition of Popol Wuj: the Book of Council that is the Book of the  Sprouting; the Dawning of Life and its People and their Populating the Face of the Earth. Jo, jo, jo junam jo!

This was when they came out; the Big Round Bees-Wonon, Sitaʼl-Black Metallic Wasps came out like smoke-sibʼ; they came out of each one of the pots; ta xel chi upam ri jujun chi kukubʼ; just like smoke they just poured out of the Four Big Pots.

Like Smoke; Like a Cloud

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They appeared like a cloud; they appeared like smoke; they rose-up just like mist; they rose-up just like a cloud, a cloud of smoke; like a smoke-cloud. And like a cloud of smoke they poured forth from each of the four opened pots.

Like ʼsmokeʼ says the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account when it could have said ʼcloudʼ or ʼmistʼ or ʼfogʼ but it is sacred text that tell of incense smoke rising up to spread out in order to cover the mountain top of Jaqawitz that is now covered with swarm of bees and a cloud of wasp that are seen as smoke: sibʼ.

But ʼwhat ifʼ we read the Popol Wuj as it was once heard as a bilingual expression of the Yaki Méxica who were Nahua People who spoke Nahuatl in Tolan Tzuy-Wa. Tolan is the heart and soul of the Mesoamerican World where we know for fact that the Maya Nobles and their Merchant-Warriors spoke the ʼword-tzijʼ that was the ʼchʼabʼal-languageʼ of their Chuch-Qajaw Ojer Tzij; Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word and the Nahua Language of the Great Noble Lords of Tulan Tzuy-Wa; Nim AjAwabʼ chi Tulan Tzuy-Wa. Maya Kʼicheʼ Lords were bilingual just a Maya speakers of Spanish continue to speak their Ancestral Language that is their Mother Tongue. The Maya are and have always been a bilingual people.

There are so many Nahuatl words and phrases found throughout the Popol Wuj that when one knows them comes to realize that Maya Scribes were playing another game with their translation of Ojer Tzij. Let us take a moment speak of smoke-sibʼ in Maya Kʼicheʼ that in Nahuatl translates to popoca; smoke or poctli. And if we contemplate the word smoke and its derivations our mythic imagination is sparked alive because where there is smoke there is fire. And where there is fire Tojil must be close at hand and where Tojil is the presence of the Invisible One is all about in a Mesoamerican world where Tezcatlipoca is said to be the deity of the ʼclose and nearʼ which is to say he stirs the soul as he lives within the heart.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This is a world in which the clouds of incense given as sacred sustenance to Tojil as Storm embody those clouds of mist and rain that will fall from the mirrored Face of the Sky upon the mirrored Face of the Earth. This is the smoke that forms the cloud that shape the rain that falls as sacred sustenance to feed and sustain la Milpa of Maize; la Milpa of Cacao.

Let us take a look nothing more to open up the lid of meaning on this word that is mentioned to mean a great deal more: popoca; smoke ʼsmoking-popocaʼ…popochcomitl-incense vessel…popochtli-incense, perfume…Popoloca-speak a foreign language…popolcatl-barbaric, mountain people…popoquitli- firefly-popoyacatl…popoyotl-blind…popozoctli-foam, suds, froth, jolomax; Tezcatlipoca from the intransitive verb; popoca; to smoke; smoke-poctli; pocatl.

The Maya Scribe chose ʼsmokeʼ not ʼcloudʼ not ʼmistʼ not ʼfogʼ no they chose ʼsmokeʼ so they are talking to us about the ʼsmokeʼ of ritual sacrifice and the popoca-smoking tezcatl-mirror into which one looks to find oneʼs destiny. Popochcomitl is the incense burner or Saqilaq or Sacred Vessel from which issues forth the popochtli-perfume, sweet smoke to sustain the Kabʼawil…Smoke; Sibʼ but also Popoca of the Smoking Mirror of Tezcatlipoca; the Popol Wuj then might best be seen as the Book of Smoke of Tezcatlipoca and his Precious Twin; Quetzalcoatl to create the idea of the Book of the Fire and Power of the Precious Twins.

The warriors were just finished off by these little animalitos, chikopil; as the Bees; the Wasps did the Warriors in.

They just attacked them, they just stung them to then sting them again and again; to then go on stinging them until they did them in by finishing them off once and for all by just stinging and biting them until they killed them dead so that in the end the Warriors of the Pueblos; the Soldiers of the Tribes were laid out on the ground to be left for dead.

They, the bees; they, the wasps just began by stinging the warriors in their eyes; to then sting and bite them on their noses; to then sting them on and around their mouths; to continue stinging and biting them all over their faces.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
It was then when the wasps and bees stung and bit the warriors up and down their arms and legs before moving on to stinging them again on their swollen faces before moving on to give them deadly stings and killer bites in more hidden places; their more intimate spaces.

They just stung them to continue stinging and stinging them again and again so that those of the Pueblo were stung and stung;  over and over by the biting bees and stinging wasps who attacked them who were those who attacked those of Jaqawitz while never stinging; while never biting those of Jaqawitz.

Wherever the warriors of the Pueblo ran, the bees and wasps went after them to sting them there; to then sting them here; to end up stinging them everywhere they could sting as they chased after the warriors who had nowhere to run; nowhere to hide.

Everything and everyone that was of the nature and essence of the attacking Pueblo was soon covered by the swarm of round black bees and cloud of the black metallic wasps. Bees and wasps knew what was theirs in life since they knew exactly who to sting; just as they flew to those they knew who were theirs to bite.

Diving-down at the enemy the bees and wasps fell to stinging the now completely defenseless warriors of the attacking Pueblo who now just ran for their lives in their struggle to survive.

They tried to hide but as soon as the bees and wasps sensed them they then saw them to quickly dive down upon them to sting and bite them.

There simply was no end to this lethal kind of stinging that was a fatal sort of biting; that was a most deadly way of dying. There was no way to stand-up and face this invisible enemy; this deadly adversary known as the ʼenemy on two-sideʼ only this was the enemy on ʼall-sidesʼ that now surrounded them as they swarmed all around them as this great cloud of smoke that was there buzzing all about to induce fear like nothing the Pueblo; the Tribes had ever faced before...this purring; humming; this whining whirring; this bustling buzzing of these busy bees and watchful wasps.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The warriors now appeared drunk because of the way they staggered about swinging and swiping at the bees and wasps that swarmed all around them. They no longer could hold-on to their bows and arrows nor grip their shields so they left them fall to the ground where the warriors quickly followed as they threw themselves upon the earth.

There the warriors curled up in the dirt; they just balled up in the dust doing their best to survive this terrible ʼsmokeʼ of the swarming bees and clouds of wasps. This was when those of Jaqawitz came out from behind the kʼoxtun wall to begin cleaning-up and clearing-off the warriors who lay about on the ground stung blind by the bite of the Bees; left silent by the sting of Wasps.

They just gave themselves up; while those who tried to escape were rundown; grabbed hold of; to then be quickly finished off. Devastated and destroyed the defeated warriors now only wished to survive by finding a way to stay alive since staying alive was staying alive and that was enough for them now because now the only thing in life that matter to them  now was how to not die.

And so it was that the multitude of the warriors of the Pueblo abandoned the struggle as they gave up the fight and ran for their lives.

Some of them fell off the side of the mountain into the great abyss, no longer conscious of where they were or what they were doing.

Others didnʼt feel a thing when they were shot through with arrows, chi chʼabʼ; they no longer knew what was happening when they were finished off with obsidian blade axe, chi ikaj; they were knocked out cold; they were just bludgeoned to death with clubs; les dieron una buena paliza, xa bʼolaj cheʼ.

The disorienting affect of the troublemaking trickery of the beguiling bees and bewildering wasp was so utterly mystifying that it left the enemy more vulnerable to the attack of Jaqawitz who moved about like smoke to finish off their rivals like never before.

Just tree-limbs were used as clubs by Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ to knock down the blinded warriors before knocking them out.  Their wives became deadly killers: xok kixoqil e kamisanel who finished off their attackers with their great strength.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Not just a few people died there on Jaqawitz, they werenʼt killed by those who wished to do them harm. It was just the insects, the little animalitos-xa kʼu chikop xok chike-that killed them there.

Those who didnʼt perish on the mountaintop were chased by the bees and wasps that soon caught up with them running down the mountainside.

There were no great acts of mannish valor. Not by bow and arrow; not by wielding the shield did they die for it was just the biting of the  big round bees-wonon; it was just the stinging of the black metallic wasps-sitaʼl that did the Pueblo in; xa wonon, xa sitaʼl, just bees, just wasps were those who finished them off.

This is when all the tribes were defeated; when they were subjugated; so this then is when the Pueblo, the Tribes, the Amaqʼ were made to humble themselves before them; the Noble Lords.

This was when they gave themselves up to the Noble Lords; when the Mountain Pueblos were made to humble themselves; to bow down low before:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj.

“Pity us; just forgive; please, donʼt kill us!”

Pueblos of the Mountain Tribes

This is what they cried when they begged for their lives; all those who were there who were those of the Pueblo who came to turn themselves in to deliver themselves over to the rule and authority of their new Lords and Rulers.

It was those of the Pueblos of the Mountain Tribes who came in as the many vassals, as the many subjects who were now ruled by the power and sovereignty of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords of Jaqawitz.

The supplicants sought a way to save themselves from the edge of the sacrificial blade of the white flint knife of sacrifice by asking those who they had just given themselves up to as war-captives if there was a destiny that they might find for them other than those to be sacrificed.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
For they did not want to be named amongst the dead, disappeared and departed: kamnaq chik; sachnaq, poqnaq chik as it is said to this day. This is when one is finished off; lost in the dust just dried up and dead like a withered cane; like shriveled leaves; like desiccated roots; like a milpa and its maize that is long past the hope that comes with tassling up to flower out to fruit and become many again. Kamnaq chik; sachnaq, poqnaq chik a Maya saying that says it all about the end that suggests the beginning of those who are lost-sachnaq and in the dust-poqnaq: dead then-kamnaq chik.

It was then that they responded as Noble Lords always do when acknowledging the humbled state of those who have just lost the power and freedom to choose their destiny as the path that leads to knowing that which is oneʼs in life to bring to fruition: like a rubberball and ball playing gear; like an axe, a hoe, and a planting stick; like blowgun and a bag full of shot; like a grinding stone, three hearth stones, and a few clay pots; like weaving sticks and balls of handspun cotton…

And so it was that the Noble Lords of the Jaqawitz spoke as the addressed those the Pueblos of the Mountain Tribes when they said:

“Utz bʼa la! Very well! Very well, indeed! Utz bʼa la!”

“Xax ix wi kamel chuxik. Ix AjPatan chi bʼe qʼij, chi bʼe saq!” Xeʼuchaʼxik.

“Even though you should be counted amongst the dead; it is your destiny to be pay us tribute for all time; as in the saying: Chi Bʼe Qʼij; Chi Bʼe Saq!

“Since you have humbled yourselves before us you will not be sacrificed; instead you shall become those who pay us tribute as our subjects; our vassals; you who will remain subjugated to our power and authority; our rule and sovereignty by remaining devoted subjects of ours;  dutiful vassals of ours; our daughters and our sons for all time; which is to say for eternity; which is best said as follows: For as long as the Sun walks on the Footpath of the Dawn; For as long as the Dawn walks on the Footpath of the Sun; Chi Bʼe Qʼij; Chi Bʼe Saq; Raqan Qʼij; Raqan Saq!

Our Bearers of Tribute; Our Providers of Sacrifice;

Ix AjPatan chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Which is that great Maya metaphor for the Footpath of the Sun; Footpath of the Dawn! For all Eternity; for as long as the Sun rises; for as long as the Dawn comes you shall be Our beloved Sons; Our beloved Daughters; You our Vassals; You our Subjects of Noble Lords; of Kabʼawil who you shall provide and sustain so that they in turn provide and sustain you for all time: Chi Bʼe Qʼij; Chi Bʼe Saq.

Your destiny is to humble yourselves before us to become our vassals and out subject so that you shall deliver us our tribute; which is our recompense for your making us suffer; so that our tribute may be your sacrificial payment to provide and sustain our Kabʼawil as our subjects who will remain as you are: conquered subjects, subjugated vassals who will become Our Bearers of Tribute; Our Providers of Sacrifice: Ix AjPatan chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq.

For you shall be the Bears of our Burden-IxPatan for as long as the Sun walks his Sacred Road across the Face of the Earth; for as long as the Sun walks his Sacred path of Dawn across the Face of the Sky.

Which is to say: for all time, forever, eternally, you will be those who bear us tribute as well as those who carry our tribute to others; for you shall become ʼour tumpline, our pack-strapʼ who will be our porter; our bearers of wealth and its reapportioning across the Face of the Earth.

This is who you shall be which is the quintessential image of subjugated subjects; venerable vassals sign and symbol of a dutiful subject and devoted vassal who revere and venerate their Noble Lords as Divine Ancestors; and those Divine Ancestors Divinities; Kabʼawil who will be provided with tribute in order to be sustained with sacrifice for all time, for eternity: chi Bʼe Qʼij; chi Bʼe Saq.

And thus was the defeat of all the Pueblos; Amaqʼ by Our First Mothers, Our First Fathers; Our First Mother-Fathers: Nabʼe Chuch-QaQajaw.

There it was done atop the mountain Jaqawitz; Chuwi Juyubʼ Jaqawitz is its name today.

This is where they established themselves; this is where they settled themselves there upon the Sacred Mountain; Dawning Mountain: Jaqawitz, Jaqʼawitz, Qʼaqʼawitz, Saqawitz, Kaqajawitz.

body:
They grew there; they multiplied there; they just populated themselves there, where they became many people there; there on Jaqawitz.

They brought forth vassal daughters; they brought forth subject sons on top of Jaqawitz. They bore and birthed daughters; they engendered and begot sons there atop Jaqawitz.

They rejoiced again; they were made content again by their defeat of their enemies there atop of their First Mountain; Nabʼe Juyubʼ: Chuwi Juyubʼ Jaqawitz.

The Noble Lords of Mountain Tribes; the Noble Lords of the Pueblos; ri Amaqʼ are those Noble Lords who went to Jaqawitz to defeat the First Four Fathers;  Our First Grandfathers; Our First Fathers; Nabʼe QaMam; Nabʼe QaQajaw. But it was they, the Noble Lords of the Pueblos, who were those that met with their own defeat at the hands of those First Four Fathers who they went to Jaqawitz to attack in order to kill and destroy on top of the Chuwi Juyubʼ.

All those Mountain Tribes of all those Mountain Pueblos who went to conquer those of Jaqawitz were conquered by those of Jaqawitz; there on Jaqawitz is where the Pueblos, the Tribes, ri  Amaqʼ met their death; met their defeat for they were defeated there; they were conquered there; they the vanquished, they the defeated were those known as the Mountain Pueblos; Juyubʼ Amaqʼ; Juyubʼ Winaq. We will tell their story now; we will tell of their being conquered by the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ; this is the Ancestral Story; Ojeroq Tzij we shall tell next.

It was then that they did it; the First Mothers, First Fathers; Nabʼe Chuch, Nabʼe Qajaw. They conquered them all; all the Mountain Tribes-ronojel Amaqʼ-all the many Mountain People of all the many Mountain Pueblos were conquered, they were conquered there on Jaqawitz, one and all were subjugated to the power and rule; sovereignty and authority of the First Mothers, First Fathers; Nabʼe Chuch, Nabʼe Qajaw.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
And so then their hearts were made content when they felt the great satisfaction of defeating all of the Pueblos; for truly they felt great contentment because of their victorious ways of conquering and subjugating the others who were the first to come to conquer and subjugate the First Four Fathers on top of Jaqawitz; Chuwi Juyubʼ Jaqawitz.

This was when they told their sons that the time of their death was fast approaching; finally, after so many had wanted them dead; after so many had wanted to kill them their deaths had finally arrived. They told their sons that the time had come for their deaths; the time had come for their dying; soon they too would be dead.

Indeed, their lives had come to fruition; finally, the time for their dying, the time of their death had arrived; it was time for them to go.

So next we shall recount the deaths foretold of:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

For they knew of their deaths and their dying; they knew that soon they would no longer be anymore. They knew they would soon be dead and gone-kikamik, kisachik-as it is said-dead and disappeared; dead and forgotten; dead and no longer here anymore: deceased and lost to others forever more except for these words of remembrance recounted here of the death of:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

This was when they left their final instructions with their Sons advising them what to do when they were dead and gone; for it was time that they took leave of their Boys; their Sons; Kikʼajolabʼ since it was time for them to go; since the time for them to die had come; truly, the time for them to go had come.

They were not sick nor were they suffering; nor did they complain of pain or illness; they were not tired; they were not fatigued nor where they without breath.

When these Old Men left their last wishes with their Sons it was because they knew they were dying; they knew it was time for them to move on.

And so they took leave of their Sons in preparation for their departure from the ones they brought into the world who were their Boys, their Sons; Kikʼajol. Kikʼajol; the Sons; the Boys whose names are named here:

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
There were two noble sons engendered by the Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ: Kʼo Kaʼibʼ and Kʼo Kawibʼ are their names; the names of the two noble sons of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

Kʼo Kaʼibʼ was the name of the first born son: nabʼey al.  Kʼo Kaʼibʼ ubʼiʼ nabʼeyalʼ; Kʼo Kaibʼ is the name of the Noble Lord known a Noble Lord Two.

Kʼo Kawibʼ was the name of the second born son. Kʼo Kawibʼ ubʼiʼ ukabʼal; Kʼo Kawibʼ is known as Noble Lord Investiture; Nobel Lord of Noble Installation; Noble Enthronement; Noble Inauguration; Noble Coronation.

Kʼo Kaibʼ and Kʼo Kawibʼ are the two noble sons of the Noble Lord Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ who is the Grandfather, the Father of the Kaweq People; Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ umam, uqajaw Kaweqibʼ.

Then there were two sons engendered by Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ and these are their names: Kʼo Akul was the name of his first born son of the Noble Lord Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ: Kʼo Akul ubʼiʼ nabʼe ukʼajol of Noble Lord Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ.

Kʼo Akutek is the name of the second son of the Noble Lord Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; Kʼo Akutek ubʼiʼ ukabʼ ukʼajol Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ who is the Grandfather and Father of the Nimaʼ Jayibʼ People.

Kʼo Akul and Kʼo Akutek are the names of the two noble sons of Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ of the Nijaʼibʼabʼ.

There was just one engendered son of Majukʼutaj; Kʼo Ajaw-Noble Lord is his name.

The Three Noble Lords known as Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj all engendered sons of their own but Ikʼi Bʼalam had no sons of his own engendering; there was no son of the Kʼicheʼ Lord Ikʼi Bʼalam: Many Jaguars; Moon Jaguar; Wind Jaguar; Jaguar Lord of the South.

And so it was that Ikʼi Bʼalam engendered no sons of his own or they did not survive to sit on his throne; so that he left no noble sons to bear the sacred burden of his noble lineage with its noble rule and sovereign reign.

Truly these are the First Fathers of the first three lineages of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ known as the Kaweq, Nima Jayibʼ or Nijaʼibʼab, and Ajaw Kʼicheʼ lineages that provided for and were sustained by the Providers, Sustainers-Tzuqul, Kʼool who were Sacrificial Priests known as AjKʼixbʼ AjKʼajb.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These were those of the Maguey Spine; those of the Obsidian Blade who performed rituals of sacrifice to provide and sustain the Kabʼawil with sacrificial blood through rituals of sacrifice.

They are known as: AjKʼixbʼ AjKʼajbʼ they carried out their ritual performance of ritual sacrifice when they carried their Kabʼawil on their backs; when they abandoned Tulan Tzuy-Wa; when they walked away from the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij at Tulan Tzuy-Wa where they watched and waited for the Sun, Moon, Great Star; known as Qʼij, Ikʼ, Nimaʼ Chumil. This was when they were there watching the horizon there at the Relebʼal Qʼij-Coming Out Place of the Sun; the place of the emergence of the Sun; the place of the appearance of the Dawn: Saqirik.

And these are the names of their Engendered Sons-Kikʼajol from whom they took leave of at the time of their death and disappearance; once they were dead and gone-kamnaq, sachnaq.

These are the names of their Sons with whom they left their word; their Sons with whom they left their instruction; when they left counsel their Sons so they knew what to do when they were dead and gone: kamnaq, sachnaq.

The four of them were together as the four companions who gathered together in just one place with just one voice when they sang their song with their hearts burning with sadness; for truly their heart wept with sadness when the four of them sang together their one song as companions for life.

Just One-Xa Jun was all they were, since all they were, was Just One: Xa Jun.

The four lineages; the four divisions were in just one place together when they remembered from whence they came; truly their souls knew sorrow for truly their hearts wept in their song; their hearts, their souls wept in their weeping while singing their ancient ancestral song of their Sacred Burial; Holy Burial upon their Death Divine: Qamuqu-Our Burial; Kamaku-Divine Death of a Noble Lord known as a Holy Lord, Divine Lord: Kukʼul Ajaw.

Kamaku or Qamuqu was the name of their song, the song they sung was Kamuqu: our burial song of remembrance of our love-maq for one another; the remembrance of our burial song and the pardon they extend to one another.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Kamaku is the song they sang when they sang their song of death and departure. Kamaku was the song they sung when they took leave of their sons by singing them the song they sung: Qamuqu.

This was when they left them with these wise words of counsel before they died and left their Sons with these ancestral words of advice:

“Oh our sons, we are going now, but we shall return. So we shall take leave of you by leaving you with the divine word, divine truth; sacred counsel, sacred instruction spoken of as Saqil Tzij, Saqil Pixabʼ. These are our sacred words of departing; these are our precious words; perfect words of taking leave of you. These then are our words of ancestral counsel; our words of ancestral instruction left for you, our wise-words of advice, our wise-words of counsel; our last words of departure that we leave with you upon taking leave of you, Our Sons.”

Saqil Tzij, Saqil Pixabʼ Qapixabʼ chi we:

Saqil Tzij-Sacred Word, Sacred Truth; Perfect Word; Precious Word; Perfect Truth, Precious Truth; Divine Remembrance, Divine Tradition

Saqil Pixabʼ-Sacred Advice; Sacred Counsel; Precious Advice; Perfect Advice; Perfect Instruction, Precious Instruction

Qapixabʼ chiwe: Our Advice for you; Our Instruction for you; Our Taking Leave of you; Our Giving Counsel to you; Our Sons; Our Replacements

“And you, Our Women-Ix Qixoqil-Our Wives; Our Partners-Qa kʼulel-Our Companions; You, Our Beloved Women; Our Beloved Wives have come far, far into the mountains you have come to arrive here at this place, Our Mountain Place, Qajuyubʼal; Oh You, Our Wives-Ix Qixoqil-Oh You, Our Women,” they said to their Wives, to each of them, taking leave of them as they took up their road of departure. As they took leave of them; their Women-Ix Kixoqil; Oh You, Our Women saying their names as they did; as they took leave of them upon their departure by leaving them with sacred words; precious words left as precious words of departure; precious words of remembrance. These were their wise-words:

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“We are going to our Pueblo-Qamaqʼ; we are going to our Death. It is already divined in the ordering of the Days, of the Year Lord Deer-Kej, just a sign of our Lord Deer reflected in the Sky. It is only the return we must make. Our work here is complete, our days here are fulfilled: our sacrifice satisfied, our burden complete-qapatan-our cargo completed, our destiny brought then to fruition. Truly our lives were fruitful lives; lives lived to completion, lives lived to conclusion. You know us, you will feel our presence. You sense us, you will not forget us, do not wipe clean your remembrance of us; do not wipe clean the mirror of us; do not wipe clean the reflection of us; do not sweep away the memory of us; do not clean away the image of us. Now the time has come for you to look for your home, on your mountain place; your home on your  mountain place where you can establish yourself; where you can settle yourself. Ta chuxoq! So be it! May it so be! Go forth on your road and look back upon where youʼve come,” this is what they said when they left their word with them; when they took leave of their wives and sons.

So then they took their leave of their wives and sons but they left their sign; retal and so it was that their sign was left as their recollection, that was their remembrance, that was their replacement, so that it remained there; there with their replacements; there with their kʼexel to live on; it was there that was left their natural essence, their ancestral nature-kʼojeʼik-their nawal essence; their nawal character; the condition and nature of their ancestral soul; ancestral spirit.

This was the nawal soul and essential nature of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ that was left behind as his ʼsign-retal-symbolʼ for his descendants to remember him by. Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ was he who left the heart, the kernel, the seed, the soul of his nawal nature of magical transformation as the divine essence of his transformative character; his transformative nature of his nawal soul this is his ancestral soul which he had left behind as what would always be remembered as his sign-retal the sign of remembrance of his nawal spirit of his ancestral soul:

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Wrapped in this Sacred Bundle was the remembrance-kʼuʼxulal-commitment of the First Father that remained burning in the heart and soul of his descendants as calling of their ancestral soul and the commitment to their ancestral memory of him in the remembrance of their ancestral heart of the Sowing; of the Dawning; the heart that is sown; the heart that sprouts as the heart and soul that dawns of those who are of the Kaweq Lineage. The Sacred Bundle of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ embodied the memory of their First Father that burned like an undying ancestral ember; like an eternal ancestral flame of ancestral remembrance it burned with the remembrance, recollection, and commitment to the First Mother-Father; Nabʼe Chuch-Qajaw. Like a Sacred Fire-Loqʼolaj Kotzʼij it burned as the divine day of Kʼat; day of the Harvest; day of the Sacred Fire: Loqʼolaj Kotzʼij.

It was in his sacred word; sacred truth that formed the sacred history, sacred narrative that molded and modeled the ancestral imagination that framed the imaginal realm found in and created by the mythic map of meaning of the ancestors and descendants imagination that formed and shaped the ancestral mind of the First Fatherʼs replacements;  his beloved descendants so that his descendants could always find their way through the words and images of ancestral remembrance of the Divine Ancestorsʼ imaginal realm of their ancient word; ancestral stories that were his sacred stories; his ancestral account; his ancient narratives, those of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

These are the ancestral stories brought forth here through the commitment to their remembrance; their recollection before the sacred altar upon which burns the sacred fire; sacred fire that come from the ancient embers that burn like the first fires burnt in the stone oven of the Lords of Death; fires of transformation that transform the Nawal Twins, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej; Grandsons of IxMuqane; IxMuqane the Former, the Shaper of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
IxMuqane, Xpiyakok as the First Mother-Fathers of the Ixim Winaq are a great success. Their People seen as their Maize growing as a Pueblo seen as a Milpa has matured through its own flowering and fruiting that has led to bountiful abundance so that  this Ancestral Couple has become a great many People; a profuse plentiful Pueblo.

These First Two; Kabʼawil are the Mother-Fathers of the Maize People; Nabʼe Chuch-Qajaw Ixim Winaq have brought forth the Sowing and the Dawning of Life for the Peopling and Populating the Face of the Earth. It is they who burn the first fire to search and sift the seeds to find answer to their divination in their divinatory fire of divination. This is the sacred fire that burns today as it burnt yesterday; the same ancestral fire that will burn tomorrow and the next day and all the other days in the Sacred Count of Days that forms and shapes the Footpath of the Sun; Footpath of the Dawn: Chi Bʼey Qʼij; Chi Bʼey Saq.

This is why the commitment to remembrance is of monumental importance because it is the ancestral word and ancient way that the Ancestorsʼ Descendants will take up the path of pilgrimage and its sacred narrative are what forms and shapes their mythic imagination to bring to life the imaginal realm of the First Mother-Fathers whoʼs lives form and shape the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account. And be doing so awaken the life of the Descendants to deep purpose and profound meaning by bring the ancestral world back into existence to once again feed the ancestral soul of the human being that is always on a quest to find the sacred sustenance to feed the human soul that hungers for ancestral authenticity in mythic masterpieces such as this that it hungers for today like nothing else. And so goes our quest for remembrance of that which can sustain our human soul with authentic ancestral images in a world that is so filled with inauthentic reinterpretations of myth.

body:
The seed for this remembrance is right here in the Sacred Bundle that Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ leaves to his descendants through which to remember him by but not only that because he left it so that his descendants could communicate with him through the burning ember that burned within the sacred bundle of flames. For that flame-tzij is the word-tzij so that the remembrance of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ or is that Bʼalam Kʼi Tzij Many Word; Sweet Words was the remembrance of the ancestral word; ancestral way; ancestral truth; ancestral tradition that  burned through the Sacred Word he left for the world to invoke his nawal powers of transformation.

This nawal power of transformation was that through which oneʼs petitions were formed and shaped through words and images that create a life worth living upon a mountain place worth living it; a livable mountain place worth living upon which to find a livable mountain place where one can live out a life worth living. This is what the Ancient Word says as it lives on through the remembrance of the Sacred Bundle of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ; the Smiling Jaguar; the Laughing Jaguar; this Mocking Jaguar that is a Trickster Jaguar. This is his story told here.

This is the ʼSacred Bundled Ember-Pisom Qʼaqʼal-Ember of the Sacred Bundleʼ that burns as the ancestral remembrance of Ajaw Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ for those who follow in the footsteps of his memory found in his nawal word, in his nawal truth as the nawal sign of his nawal ancestry with its power-qʼaqʼal-strength and authority-tepewal-rule and sovereignty brought forth here as his ancestral memory-natabʼal, naʼojʼ-the remembrance of: Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Bʼalam KiʼTzeʼ known as Sweet Smiling Jaguar; Jaguar Lord of Sweet Laughter; Lord Jaguar Great Laughter Bʼalam KiʼTzeʼ create by IxMuqane who could never contain or control her sweet, sweet uncontrollable laughter: Lord Jaguar Mocking Laughter. Did not IxMuqane infuse her forming and shaping of the First Four Fathers with her essence? Of course she did because she is the Great Mother; she is the Creatrix just as she is the Matrix as the Great Mother of the Ixim Winaq. The Kʼicheʼ are a Pueblo who lives their lives surrounded by smiles and laughter. The Kʼicheʼ are a People who place great value on showing oneʼs gratitude by showing happiness to warm the hearts of those with who they live.

It is through her hands that the maize of the People of Maize is ground down nine times to create a very, very fine dough. Dough that is then formed and shaped to then be molded and modeled in the Four First Fathers of the Four Principle Lineages of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ all of which are touched by the nature, character, condition, essence, soul, spirit, and nawal essence of transformation of IxMuqane.

Yet it is the Matriarchs forming and shaping of her first formation who she names Jaguar Lord of the East; He of the Great Laughter; Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ that makes him the Playful Jaguar Lord that he is that enjoys both Creation and Destruction as the elementary movements of this World of the Sky-Earth in which Twins and Twinship bring about the fun-loving complementary collaborative relationships that form the foundation of the ʼGood-Lifeʼ of the Maya who we see smiling all the time.

No translator in the past has ever taken IxMuqane as seriously or as importantly as she should be taken as the Divine Matriarch and Creatrix-Matrix of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Sky-Earth for she is the Former just as she is the Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol who exists at the center of this Sacred Myth of Creation and Destruction of the Lifecycle of Maize and Humans; the Sowing and Dawning; the Sprouting and the Growing; the Flowering and Fruiting; the Harvesting, the Shelling of the Dried Seeds from the  Mazorca, in order to select the Kernels; the Seeds, the Grains.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Jun Raqan Ukʼuʼx Kaj is the destroyer his is in life is death, defeat, demise, destruction, and disappearance for that is what is his in life. But IxMuqane, she is different she is the Former just as she is the Shaper she is love with the sowing and sprouting; the flowering and fruiting. She wants to see here people bring home the harvest so the beautiful grains can be gathered to together out on her patio in the Center of Her House; In the Center of the Harvest as it is said by her: IxMuqane.

So what does this mean? One thing is that her first creation Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ laughs sweetly just like IxMuqane whose sweet, sweet laughter ʼqus, qusʼ can still be heard today.

This was the Sacred Bundle filled with the transforming power of the Forming, of Shaping; Making, Modeling of the Nawal Winaq and the divine essence of transformation burning in their sacred sacrificial fire with its power and authority to guide and protect; nourish and nurture; provide and sustain the endless creativity of this realm known as the Reino Kʼicheʼ; the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom that indeed it was when one asks those who know.

The Sacred Bundle, this ʼPisom Qʼaqʼalʼ was just bound tight, not even could its sewing be seen because no one had seen how it had been bundled and bound together as a Sacred Bundle.

This is how they took leave when they left their advice before disappearing from there on the mountaintop of Jaqawitz. They were no longer seen by their wives, they were no longer seen by their children. Their disappearance was not clear, when they disappeared is not known.

But their instructions were clear; they were clear to the oneʼs they left with their Sacred Bundle that held the memory of their First Father Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

The Pisom Qʼaqʼal instantly became sacred to them, for it was the remembrance, the recollection, the commemoration that was the sacred sign of their memory of their Qajaw, Mam; Father, Grandfather: Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

body:
At once they burnt offerings there before the Sacred Bundle of their Father: Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ. This is when began the progression, the succession of the generations of the Lords that came one after the next from the Great House of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ or Nim Ja Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

This is the origin of the Grandfather; Mam and the Father; Qajaw of the Kaweq as a People; Winaq and as a Pueblo; Amaqʼ known as the Kaweqibʼ, this is to say the Kaweq Winaq; Kaweq Amaqʼ. This was never forgotten by his sons who were named Kʼo Kaʼibʼ and Kʼo Kawibʼ.

And thus they died; those who were the First Four Grandfathers, First Four Fathers, the First Four Companions of One Another at Tulan Tzuy-Wa, Relebʼal Qʼij they died.

They were Our First Grandfathers, Our First Fathers: e Nabʼe Qamam, Qaqajaw.

Now they were gone, while their sons remained atop Jaqawitz, they waited and wondered there; they lingered on and contemplated their past; they contemplated their future there upon their Fatherʼs mountaintop citadel: Chuwi Juyubʼ Jaqawitz as it is known today.

The Mountain Pueblos, the Amaqʼ, the Mountain Tribes had fallen here; humbled, and ridiculed were they in their subjugated days there when they agreed to bringing loads of tribute, cargos of tribute to their New Lords: the Tojiles.

Truly humble was their destiny; truly humble was the destiny of all the Tribes of Mountain People that were conquered there, one and all, once and for all.

No longer was the power and rule that was there, theirs; no longer was the power to rule that was there, theirs. For their fire, their power; their rule, their authority; their ritual, their sacrifice was now given to them by the descendants of the First Four Fathers.  It was they who controlled the Pueblos through the sacrifice they gave to their Kabʼawil Tojil who the Pueblo now embraced.

They were just surviving there without their own fire up on top of their mountains where they gathered together among themselves as the subjugated vassals of the Kʼicheʼ Lords.

So they assembled themselves, every day at dawn they gathered together to remember their Fathers before the Sun; there at the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij; there at the Place of the Dawn-Saqiribʼal-the Dawning Place they remembered their Fathers as they kept the sacred count of the days and named the names of their Divine  Ancestors; as they gave praise in ancient ancestral ways of showing great respect and high regard for their Former; for their Shaper; their Bearer; their Begetter known as Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom.

Truly great was the destiny of the Sacred Bundle; Pisom Qʼaqʼal, but they did not untie it; they did not open it. It was just bundled; just wrapped; bundled up, wrapped up was the way they kept their Sacred Bundle; that they just kept bundled, wrapped; bound, knotted. And they came to call it Sacred Bundle of Fire, Sacred Bundle of Power: Pisom Qʼaqʼal.

It was venerated in secret by them, just as it was named there in secret by them; those who named it were those who venerated it as the Sacred Bundle; their Sacred Bundle:  Pisom Qʼaqʼal. This was the remembrance given formally to them by their Fathers, it was just a sign of their essence, a memory of their existence and all that they did.

This then is just the recollection and remembrance of their disappearance at the end of their lives and the ancient ancestral account of them here, those who are named:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

They were the First People, Nabʼe Winaq to come from there Beside the Sea-chilaʼ chaqa Palo; there Beside the Sea; there where the Sun rises out of the Sea; the Coming Up Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij.

Long Ago, in the Ancient Days, it was they who came here. Long, long ago it was they who arrived here-Ojeroq keʼul waral.

When they died they were already old, they who were the  Sacrificial Priests of the Maguey Spine; they the Sacrificial Priests of the Obsidian Blade; AjKʼixibʼ AjKʼajbʼ, as they were known, as they were named.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Now they are dead and gone but they are not forgotten for these Ancestral Words are a remembrance of them; their memory lives on still; just as their names live as an ancestral remembrance of them and all that they did when they walked the Face of the Earth on the Sacred Path of the Sun; on the Sacred Path of the Dawn.

Ro

Fifth

Remembrance of Tulán Tzuy-Wa: Sustenance Mountain

Memory of Pilgrimage to Tula-Tolan as Rite of Initiation;

Ritual Investiture of Young Noble Lords

Remembrance of Ojer Tzij; Ancestral History as Sacred Myth;

Epic Mythic Literature of Noble Heroes and Warlords of the

Kʼicheʼ Maya Kingdom: el Reino Kʼicheʼ

Tulán-Tzuy-Wa: Relebʼal Qʼij.

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam at the time of their death and departure make a last request that is their final wish for their descendants to commit to their ʼnoble remembranceʼ through their  carrying out the sacred act of ʼreturnʼ to Tulan Tzuy-Wa.

These First Four Fathers ʼtook leaveʼ of their Descendants; their Engendered Sons to return to the ʼRelebʼal Qʼij-Coming Out Place of the Sunʼ as their ancestral commitment in fulfillment of their ʼʼsacred obligationʼ to the Kabʼawil of Tulan Tzuy-Wa from whom the First Four Fathers received their power and authority to rule as Noble Lords.

This ʼsacred obligationʼ of ʼreturnʼ would be borne out as an ancestral commitment of the Engendered Sons of their Fathers who were the Great Lords of the Kʼicheʼ known as Nima Ajaw Kʼicheʼ who were Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam. Their Engendered Sons would be made Entitled Sons were those who would be named as Entitled Lords in order to rule as Noble Lords through Rites of Investiture that were Rites of Enthronement that were Rites of Entitlement of the Engendered Sons of the First Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ who received their ʼpower-qʼaqʼal-fireʼ from Great Lord; Great Ruler of Tulan Tzuy-Wa: Nima Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl; Great Sovereign Lord of Tulan Tzuy-Wa.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The Engendered Sons of the First Four Fathers committed themselves to fulfillment of the one and only request made by their Lords-Qajaw-Fathers and that was to return to Tulan Tzuy-Wa to assure their noble rule with its power and position of entitlement and sovereignty as Nima Ajawabʼ Kʼicheʼ Winaq before the Nima Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz who was the Sovereign Lord and Noble Ruler of the Nahua-Maya Empire of Tulan Tzuy-Wa.

These Engendered Sons were committed to taking up the road of their Fathers to do as their Fathers did and return to the Place of the Dawn known as the Coming Out Place of the Dawn to participate in the Rites of the Bestowal of Noble Power and Authority known as Rites of Entitlement.

These Rites of Entitlement of the Engendered Sons were Rites of Investiture of these Noble Sons as the Successor of their Fathers who were Nim Ajaw who had gone to Tulan Tzuy-Wa to go before Nima Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz; Great Lord of Quetzalcoatl who was a Holy Lord; Kʼul Ajaw who remained upon the throne Tulan Tzuy-Wa.

These Rites of Entitlement that were Rites of Investiture that were Rites of Enthronement that were Rites of Inauguration of Noble Lords were preceded by grueling Rites of Initiation that were life changing Rites of Transformation.

These Rites of Transformation were brought to fruition through the Rite of Initiation that was the Engendered Sons ritual return to Tulan Tzuy-Wa. This Rite of Initiation that brought about the ritual transformation of the Noble Sons by surviving the initiatory ordeals by the Boys, the Sons, ri Kʼajolabʼ overcoming the tests and trials they faced in their passage from the Kʼicheʼ Highlands down to the Lowlands and on to the Splendid City of Tulan Tzuy-Wa. By surviving the many Houses of Ordeal that initiates entered to survive proved they had what it took to become the ʼReplacements-Kʼexuwach-Kʼexelʼ of their Noble Fathers.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Like the Hero Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who survived the Houses of Xibʼalbʼa at Night and the Ballgames by Day so too did the Engendered Sons of Noble Lords-just like Jun Junajpu-would show the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo that these Noble Sons of Noble Fathers were worthy of the entitlement and investiture as Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

These Noble Sons of Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ would then be revered and venerated as the Replacements of their Fathers. These Engendered Sons of the First Fathers were then known as the ʼReplacements-Kʼexelʼ or ʼReturn Face-Kʼexuwach-Replica Imageʼ of their Fathers. Fathers who embody the sacred power and divine authority-ajawarem and tepewal that were bestowed upon them as their sovereign reign and noble rule that originates on the One Sustenance Mountain-Jun Juyubʼ Wa known as Tulan Tzuy-Wa where the Ixim Winaq come from; the Mountain of Origin of the Ixim Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Winaq.

And this then was when they took to heart their commitment-kikʼuxlan to undertake the journey back to the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij.

This was when they remembered their soulful promise; when they had vowed their heartfelt remembrance of their Fathersʼ last wishes that would by their obligation to take-up the road upon which to make their journey of return to their Fathersʼ Place of Origin; their journey to the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij.

The verb used in this section is kikʼuxlaj and kikʼuxlan which is the heartfelt remembrance that was a promise and commitment to their Fathersʼ last wishes that their Sons promised commit to return to the Relebʼal Qʼij.

Kʼux is the heart, the soul, the core, or the center that creates a beautiful verbal metaphor to be committed in oneʼs soul-kʼux to a heartfelt, soulful memory of the Noble Sons for their Noble Fathersʼ wishes that they do now remember to fulfill as they once did long ago when they were young when they promised; when they pledge to return East to the Coming Out Place of the Sun; there to the House of Dawn.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This was when their hearts; when their souls felt certain the time had come for them to fulfill their promise to journey East towards the Rising Sun.

This was when their remembrance called them from within to return to their Fatherʼs Place of Emergence; to return there to their Ancestral Place of Origin; to return to the House of Dawn; to return there to the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij.

They, the Noble Sons, did not forget their Noble Fatherʼs instructions; the instructions left to them when the time came to take leave of them upon their death.

They, the Noble Sons, did not forget the words of their Noble Fathers when their Noble Fathers took leave of their Engendered Sons by leaving them instructions to be kept as a promise to return to where their Noble Power and Authority came from at the Coming Out Place of the Sun.

The Noble Fathers left instructions to their Noble Sons upon their taking leave of their Sons; instructions left by the Noble Fathers to their Engendered Sons at the time of their death and disappearance when they left their Noble Sons with instructions to return to the Coming Out Place of the Sun in East.

The instructions left by the Noble Fathers were the words they left their Noble Sons upon taking leave of them at the time of their Death. The instructions the Noble Fathers left with their Engendered Sons took the form of a request that asked of their Sons to promise to return to the Coming Out Place of the Sun.

The instructions left by the Noble Fathers to their Engendered Sons was the promise the Sons made to their Fathers; the promise was a pledge that was commitment to return to their Place of Origins known as Relebʼal Qʼij: the Coming Out Place of the Sun: the House of Dawn; the House Dawn where Sons returned as an Ancestral Remembrance of their Noble Fathers by their Noble Sons who fulfilled their commitment of return to the Coming Out Place of the Sun there at Dawn when the Sun returns to the Face of the Earth.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The Noble Sons remembered their Noble Fathers as the Noble Lords they were who died long ago but were not forgotten. They were not forgotten because of the Women they were given as gifts by the Noble Mountain Lords who gave their Noble Daughters as the Women who became the Wives of the Noble Lords of the  Kʼicheʼ Maya.

Noble Mountain Daughters of Noble Mountain Lords

These Noble Mountain Lords of the Mountain Tribes; Mountain Pueblos gave their beloved Daughters to the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords to form marriage alliances made through the gift giving of daughters who became the Noble Wives of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords.

These marriage alliances were made through the ancestral practice of the Noble Mountain Lords giving their Noble Daughters of the Mountain Pueblos as gifts given to the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords.

These Noble Lords of the Mountain Pueblos gifted their Daughters to those Noble Kʼicheʼ Maya Lords who had defeated them in battle to then subjugated the Mountain Pueblos to the sovereign rule of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Lords settled together upon the Mountain of Jaqawitz.

And so it was that those Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords who conquered the Mountain Pueblos were those who received Noble Mountain Daughters as Noble Mountain Wives from Noble Mountain Fathers who became Father-in-Laws of the Kʼicheʼ Maya People; Kʼicheʼ Maya Pueblo and by doing so formed long lasting marriage alliances through the Engendered Sons who were born and begot from these fruitful marriage alliances.

This is very, very important to remember because there will be a great many of Noble Daughters and Engendered Sons born to these Mountain People; Mountain Pueblos who the Original Kʼicheʼ Maya Lineage will come to conflict with once again in the distant future as we shall read in this very detailed translation of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Book of Council; Maya Kʼicheʼ Book of Counsel.

These marriage alliances made by the Mountain Lords of the Mountain Pueblos were brought to fruition through the gift giving of Women specially selected to become the Wives of these Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This is how they, the Kʼicheʼ Lords became Father-in-Laws of the Mountain Pueblos when these Three Principal Kʼicheʼ lineages were gifted Women who were chosen to be the Wives of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords.

These Wives were selected from the Young Women of the defeated Mountain People; these Young Women were selected from the many Maidens who were Daughters of the Lords of the Mountain Pueblos: Amaqʼ.

Mountain Pueblos; Mountain Tribes

The Mountain Pueblos; Mountain Tribes who were defeated by the First Four Fathers were those who became known as the conquered Mountain Pueblos and subjugated Mountain Tribes whoʼs Noble Lords gave their Daughters as Wives to the Noble Lords of the Kʼiche who had conquered and subjugated them to their sovereign rule and noble power and authority.

In this way the Mountain Lords came to call their Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords by the name of Father-in-Law because of the marriage alliances they made with their Noble Daughters. This is how the Kʼicheʼ Lords and Mountain Lords became One People that lived together as One Pueblo on One Mountain. This is their Ancestral Story told here.

And so it came to pass that the Mountain Lords of the Mountain Tribes of the Mountain Pueblos gave their Noble Mountain Daughters to the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords who came to call the Mountain Lords of the Mountain Pueblos ʼFather-in-Law or Ajiʼajʼ so that those who are named here as their Engendered Sons were those who were formed and shaped as a People who became a Pueblo through their making of marriage alliances in the ancient ancestral way of gift giving of Daughter of the Lords of the Mountain Places-Rumeʼal Ajawal Juyubʼal; the Daughter of the Lord of the Mountain  Place.

And so it was that these Daughters of the Lords became the Noble Mothers of the Engendered Sons; Kʼajolaxel of the Three First Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ who survived to beget sons.  Ikʼi Bʼalam did not beget sons therefore he has no Engendered Sons to be remembered here.

The Kʼicheʼ Lords were well embraced by the Pueblos and now they were intent on following the advice and counsel; instruction and direction left to them by their Fathers when they said:

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“We are going there to the Relebʼal Qʼij; it is from there that our Fathers come,” said the Three Sons of the Three Kʼicheʼ Fathers. They were Three Honored and Entitled Noble Sons who took up the road to Tolan-Tzuy Wa.

ʼNoble Lord Twoʼ known as Kʼokaibʼ named Kʼo Kaibʼ was the name of the First Born Son, he was the First Son; Nabʼeyal Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ of all the Kaweqibʼ.

Lord Kʼoʼakutek known as Kʼo Akutek was the name of the Noble Son, Honored Son of Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ who was the Father; Qajaw, Grandfather; Qamam of the Great House People:  Nijaʼibʼabʼ known and named Nima Jaʼibʼabʼ

Noble Lord Kʼoajaw spoken of as Kʼo Ajaw was the name of the Honored Son, Noble Son of Majukʼutaj of the Lord Kʼicheʼ lineage: Ajaw Kʼicheʼ.

These then are the names of those who journeyed to the Dawning Place beside the Sea: Xebʼe chilaʼ chʼaqa Palo.

Three of them took up the road together. These were men of great wisdom-kinaʼoj and deep understanding-ketamabʼal; they were those of great genius; they were those of deep imagination they were not just people in their nature; they were not just people in the essence of their existence-mana xa e ta winaq kikʼojeʼik.

They were there to ʼtake leaveʼ of their Older Brothers, their Younger Brothers. It was then that they gathered together to take council with one-an-other in order to provide advice to their Older Brothers, Younger Brother with whom they left instructions-pixabʼaj: this is how they took leave of their Brothers when they took up their road of remembrance; when they took up their road of return as a promise made to their Fathers to whom they were committed as Nawal Sons of Nawal Fathers.

They rejoiced to be on the road to where they promised their Fathers they would return as an ancestral obligation to do as their Fathers had done before them; to follow in the footsteps of their Fathers was their heartfelt, soulful desire to complete the ancestral commitment asked of them by their Noble Fathers.

And so they said as others had said before them:  “We wonʼt die; we will return; mawi kojkamik; kojulik!”

This is what they said when the Three of them left on their way to return to the place of their Fathersʼ origin.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They just crossed right over the sea-chuwi palo arriving there at Relebʼal Qʼij.

Xawi xere xeʼikʼowik chuwi Palo-They just crossed over the Sea

So these Three Sons must have taken a large Maya trading vessel which was a large dug-out canoe that was paddle across the relatively passive waters of Pacific Littoral. We are now asked to imagine these Three Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords making their way paddling up the Pacific Coast of Soconusco then Chiapas up to Juchitán in Oaxaca to then climb up into the Highlands of Mexico to arrive at Cholula-Chollan in Puebla.

Or to have walked down through the Rio Negro to Lake Izabal to then be paddled down the Rio Dulce before crossing the Gulf and then up over the water through passage between the mainland of Belize and the Islands until arriving right there at Chetumal or Tulum or Cozumel or beyond to Cerritos or to walk inland to Chichen Itza; there Beside the Great Cenote of the Itzaj.

These are possible ways one would go in a large dugout canoe headed to Tollan Tzuy-Wa where the Relebʼal Qʼij is to be found where the Sun sprouts up and out of the Sea at Dawn to then burn the Face of the Earth with its scorching rays of sunlight.

They went to receive the signs of power; the symbols of authority; the emblems of investiture; the insignia of Rulership-Ajawarem, as they are known: entitled signs of power; sacrosanct symbols of authority; holy insignia of divine investiture of the noble rule that will empower them when they return to the Kʼicheʼ Highlands to take up their Sacred Burden and Divine Office of their Noble Rule; Noble Sovereignty: Ajawarem.

The name of the Great Lord of Sacred Sustenance there was: Rajawal Aj Relebʼal Qʼij-Noble Lord and Ruler of the People and Pueblo of the Dawn; they went straight to him there when they arrived then at the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They arrived before the Noble Lord and Ruler who was there before them and known by the name: Ajaw Nakxit; Nim Ajaw: Lord Four Footed Deer; Nakxitl Traveler; Conqueror; Voyager for he was a Great Four Footed One who walks on four feet like the wind he is strong and moves across the Face of the Earth without anyone or anything to stop him or slow him down; a Great Lord who is a Powerful Warlord; a Great Ruler who is a Just Judge; a Noble Lord and Supreme Ruler; known as the Balanced One; the Harmonious One: Nima Ajaw Nakxit was his title; his sovereign name.

Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl was the Name of the Great Lord and Highest Authority of the Realm known as the One who Weighs the Word-Xa Jun Qʼatol Tzij; the One who Measures the Truth-Qʼatol Tzij thick with the power and authority of rule is his majesty; his sovereignty; thus the ʼnaming of his nameʼ Ajaw Nakxit.

Ajaw Nakxit: Lord of the Four Feet; Noble Lord Deer; Noble Traveler; Noble Knower of the Kingdom; like maize his flesh is the original sustenance of the First Animal People; the flesh of deer was formed and shaped by the Former; the Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol who forms and shapes the Deer from the essence taken from the Four Cardinal Direction; Four Colors of the Four the Four Roads; Great Strength and Balance of the Four Hoof of Deer; Powerful Leader; Strong Leader.

Ajaw Nakxit was Rajawal Aj Relebʼal Qʼij which made him the Noble Lord and Ruler of the Coming Out Place of the Sun; Relebʼal Qʼij who was himself invested with the names of entitlement bestowed upon him as the supreme authority who is thick with power and strength of rulership and majesty-tzatz rajawarem of all the lands giving him great sovereignty-tzatz rajawarem. For thick was his power and strength of the Four Corners; Four Sides where he ordered and balanced the harmony and strength of his divine power over the People; noble authority; sacred authority over the Pueblos who lived upon those lands that were his to rule as a benevolent Ruler.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Nakxit Quetzalcoatl was the Noble Lord who was the caring and kind benevolent Ruler; the Just Judge of all those who came before him in quest of his great power-qʼaqʼal and authority-tepewal that would provide and sustain them with his noble ways of rule through sovereign command and supreme control that made him the very embodiment of splendor and majesty in Rulership-Ajawarem-Nobility. Truly, Nakxit was a Noble Lord; a Majestic Sovereign; the Supreme Lord of the Realm.

For it was he Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl who bestowed rule and authority upon the Young Noble Lords who came before him to receive that which they traveled far and wide by walking while suffering and self-sacrificing along the way to acquire; to attain that which were signs of sovereignty and insignia of rulership that entitled and empowered them with the power and authority to rule as rulers in his majestic realm of noble sovereignty with its sacred ways of divine rulership.

These were the signs and symbols of all their Sacred Offices: Aj Popol who was the Highest Noble Lord and Ruler of the Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule; and AjPop Kʼamjaʼil who was the Lord Counselor of the Reception House Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule; Second-in-line to the Noble Lord and Ruler: AjPop.

So then they brought forth the images that embodied the essence of rulership and this is what they were: the signs and symbols of power and authority that were seen as the emblems of investiture that symbolized and signified the supreme sovereignty of the AjPop who was the Noble Lord and Ruler of the Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule; and, the AjPop Kʼamja known as the Noble Lord and Ruler of the Reception House Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule; he who was second in line to receive the rulership of the Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule.

Those were the names of the Noble Lords who ruled over the People of the Pueblos with supreme power and sacred authority.

The Great Lord; Nim Ajaw was there; he was the Noble Lord of the Kingdom known as, Ajaw Nakxit. It was Ajaw Nakxit who gave out all of the symbols and insignia of Nobles, Lords, and Rulers: Wachinel Ajawarem-the Emblems of Rule and Rulership of Noble Lords.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
It was Noble Lord himself Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl who fulfilled the task of bestowing power and rule upon the Young Lords of Kʼicheʼ who were the replacements of their Noble Fathers; the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl provided them with the sacred sustenance that would sustain them with power and sovereignty of Noble Rule and Divine Authority through his bestowal upon these Noble Sons of Noble Fathers with their signs and symbols, emblems and insignia of Nobles, Lords, and Rulers.

This is who they were now recognized to be as Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ through all they received in the form of emblems and shape of insignia that manifest their Noble Rule while it expressed their Sovereign Authority.

These sacred insignia and noble emblems were acknowledged by Lords and Vassals alike just as they were recognized by Rulers and Subjects as the sacred symbols of these Young Noble Lords Divine Rule and Noble Authority spoken of as: Wachinel Ajawarem.

These are the names of the Wachinel Rajawarem-the Symbols and Emblems of Rulership and Authority that embodied and imbued these Named and Entitled Lords with the power to rule as a Noble Lords; Noble Rulers. These then are the names of the symbols of Noble Rulers and their Noble Rule:

Muj: Canopy, Paladin-Throne; Bearer of Noble Lord as Sacred Burden

Qʼalibʼal: Jaguar Pelt Throne and Woven Reed Mat of Rule and Authority

Tzam-baq: Nose-bone driven through the septum as a sign of initiation

Subʼaq; Tzu bʼaq: Eagle Bone Flute of the Noble Lord and Ruler

Cham-Cham: Ceremonial Drum or Gourd Rattle of Ruler

Tatil: Resplendent black body paint-mineral dust; for ritual dance

Qʼanabʼaj: Gold Beads-Amber Beads-Yellow Beads; Gold Bead Necklace

Tzikwil Koj: Puma Fang Necklace, Puma Claw Necklaces; Canyon

Tzikwil Bʼalam: Jaguar Fang Necklace, Jaguar Claw Necklace; Mountain

Jolom: Owl Skull; Messenger of the Lords of Death; Ancestors

Pich Kiej: Deer Hoofs; Signs of the Nawal of Lord Four-Foot Deer-Nakxitl

Makutax: Deerskin, Jaguar-pelt Armband; Ballcourt-Warrior Insignia

Tʼotʼ tatam: Snail Shell Bracelet; Dance Costume; Ukʼuʼx Cho-Ukʼuʼx Palo
