source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Noble Lord Sweathouse-Kʼo Tuj Ja was a Nawal Ajaw for the sweathouse was the place of initiation; the sacred place of transformation; it was in the sweathouse where women and men found their true selves by entering into the fire of purification. It was in the name that oneʼs destiny was named; thus it was in the name given by the Divinatory Calendar that revealed the destiny of the Lord who bore that Calendrical Name.

Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz was like this as well; it was just his essence; his character; his nature that attracted the Mountain People to come in to be closer to him in order to follow him and listen to the ways of his speech in order to hear all he came to say. It was in his name that his essence; his character; his nature was revealed to the Mountain People who followed him wherever it was that he led them as their Guide and Protector; as their Provider and Sustainer; as their Nawal Ajaw who always knew what to do next.

This is why the mountain people, the canyon people ʼcame inʼ if they came in. They ʼcame inʼ because they were enchanted by these beguiling trickster being; these bewildering ancestral beings were as human as they were divine; as plant as they were animal; as celestial and they were terrestrial; a magical and they were mystical; but mostly they were as nawal as they were ancestral which made them Nawal Ajawabʼ who were Nawal Winaq. This is why the Mountain People; Canyon People came in to live close to these charismatic beings that had the power to transform into an infinitude of diverse and different things. Let us see what this means.

These were those whose names manifest their divine destiny and they are these Nawal AjAwabʼ named here; these were their names; their names that are named here Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz and Ajaw Kʼotuja; Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja known as Lord-Ajaw Sweat-Tuj House-Ja.

Ajaw Qʼukumatz-Lord Quetzalcoatl was truly a Nawal Ajaw; he was pure Nawal Winaq. And so it was said that Ajaw Qʼukumatz transformed himself in these ways:

For Seven Days he climbed into the Sky.

For Seven Days he descended into Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
For Seven Days he transformed into a Serpent; so that he took on the qualities of a Serpent-Kumatzil when he became as Serpent for Seven Days.

And, again for Seven Days he transformed into an Eagle; so that he took on the qualities of an Eagle-Kʼotal when he became an Eagle for Seven Days.

And, again, for Seven Days he transformed into a Jaguar; so that he took on the qualities of a Jaguar-Bʼalamil when he became a Jaguar for Seven Days.

When he transformed into a Serpent then he became a Serpent-Kumatzil.

When he transformed into a Jaguar then he became a Jaguar-Bʼalamil.

Truly his image became that of an Eagle; that of a Jaguar when he became an Eagle; when he became a Jaguar.

And so it was that for the next Seven Days he just Pooled-up as a Pool of Blood; so that it was only Pooled Blood that he did become.

This was when he just became a Pool of Blood for the next Seven Days; so that for Seven Days nothing but Pooled Blood did he become then; when he became a Pool of Blood of Pooled Blood for Seven Days.

All the Lords feared him; his presence alone caused them fear; so that when the Lords came near him they were made to feel fear before him.

For the one they held dear to them who was there with them was the one who caused fear within them; and so the Lords came to him, to bow to him, to then kneel before him for the cheer that he brought forth from within them.

For it was they, the Lords; one and all, who approached him trembling with fear yet he cared for them for the Lords were dear to him if only they would come close to come near him to know him for the Great Lord that he was who would come to guide and protect them by tending them by defending them like the maize in the milpa that they were to him; the Great Lord-Nim Ajaw: Qʼuqʼkumatz.

The Lords-ri Ajawabʼ sent out news to let others know of his great powers of transformation. The Lords sent word to let others know of his miraculous sort of nawal kind of magical type of changing and transforming nature that was his essence of change; this nature of transformation.  This is how his power began to grow when his power grew as a Nawal Ajaw.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This was the beginning of the rise of the Kʼiche Winaq-Kʼicheʼ People and the aggrandizement of the Kʼicheʼ Amaq-Pueblo Kʼicheʼ when Ajaw Qʼukumatz-Lord Quetzalcoatl showed signs of his great powers; when his great powers as a Nawal Ajaw where shown through his transforming nature as a Nawal Winaq.

This was when Lord Quetzalcoatl began to manifests his abilities to bring forth the transformation of the Sky-Earth all across the Kʼicheʼ Mountain-Plain-Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj as well as the Canyons-Siwan and Ravines-Siwan.

Ajaw Qʼukumatz was not forgotten by his grandsons and sons; he was not forgotten in their heart; he was not lost to them, for he was present in their remembrance. He was clear in their recollection of him as their Grandfather, Father. For the knowledge and experience of Ajaw Qʼukumatz passed on to them so that their knowledge and experience was that of their Father and Grandfather: Ajaw Qʼukumatz.

Never before had there existed a Nawal Lord such as him for Lord Quetzalcoatl-Ajaw Qʼukumatz was One Nawal Lord-Jun Ajaw Nawal of such a prodigious nature that he would never be forgotten.

For it was just magical transformation was his essence and this is what made him what he was and how he came to be remembered as Jun Ajaw Nawal.

He only did what he did to subjugate the Tribes. He did what he did to subdue the Pueblos for their well-being and transformation as a manifestation of his Nawal Character-Ukʼojeʼik Nawal; a demonstration of his Nawal Essence-Ukʼojeʼik Nawal which was a revelation of his Nawal Nature-Ukʼojeʼik Nawal to bring forth before the People of the Pueblos his Nawal Condition-Ukʼojeʼik Nawal so that they came to see and experience his Ancient Ancestral Way of Being as those who are spoken of as Nawal Winaq as he was known to be as a Nawal Lord-Ajaw Nawal-Nawal Ruler.

That is to say Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz-Ajaw Quetzalcoatl was seen by the Mountain Tribes as a Magical Transforming Lord who was a Magical Transforming Ancestor who was imbued with Miraculous Powers of Transformation.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
For Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz was known by all as A Magical Lord who was a Miraculous Lord who was the Noble Lord; Noble Ruler of his People of his Pueblo who he will change and transform through his Nawal Nature; Nawal Character; Nawal Essence; and Nawal Way of Being a Nawal Winaq.

This is who Ajaw Qʼukumatz was known to be as a Nawal Lord; this was his Ancient Ancestral Way of Transformation; his Ancient Ancestral Nature; his Ancient Ancestral Condition; his Ancient Ancestral Essence; his Ancient Ancestral Way of Being One Nawal Lord: Jun Ajaw Nawal.

It was the Ancient Ancestral Nature of this One Nawal Lord-Jun Ajaw Nawal that became the personification of himself as One Great Lord-Jun Nim Ajaw who became One Great Ruler-Jun Nim Ajaw who was known then as he is he is remembered today through our remembrance of Ajaw Qʼukumatz as Jun Nim Ajaw; Ajaw Qʼukumatz as Jun Nawal Winaq!

And so it was that this One Great Ruler was an Ancient Ancestral Being who in his essence was Jun Ajaw Nawal which was the nature of his being embodied as Lord Quetzalcoatl-Ajaw Qʼukumatz who became the One Great Leader known as the Principal of all the Citadels; the Head of all the Towns, la Cabecera de los Pueblos: Jolom Tenamit as it is said in Ojer Tzij-Ancient Word.

Ajaw Qʼukumatz became the Head of the Towns who was the Leader of the Pueblo: Jolom Tenamit. This is how he transformed into the One Great Ruler who was also the One Noble Lord of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ which to say Ajaw Qʼukumatz transformed into the One Nawal Lord-Jun Ajaw Nawal who was the Head of the Pueblo-Jolom Tenamit.

This then end the Naming of the Name of Jun Ajaw Qʼukumatz!

This is how it must be understood:  the Fourth Generation of the Kʼicheʼ Lords-Ajawabʼ Kʼicheʼ-Kʼicheʼ Rulers was that of the Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼ Kumatz, Plumed Serpent, Feathered Serpent known as the Lord Precious-Quetzal Twin-Coatl:  Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz took the position and place of two Noble Lords at once by taking the position and place of both the AjPop and the AjPop Kʼaʼma Ja. In this way he left his successors and replacements behind for those who would come to take these positions and place as Two Ruling Lords who were Twin Noble Lords; who were paired complements of one-an-other.

He left descendants just as he left his replacements and remembrances in the form of signs, in the shape of symbols; tracks and traces; marks and markers; ketal which is to say successors; retal which is to say replacements who are descendants.

Ajaw Qʼukumatz left his word, his truth, his tradition in the burning ancestral flame-kitzijel that he left behind as a burning remembrance and embodiment of himself which is the ancestral way of saying he left descendants-utzijel.

Those descendants replicated as they reproduced his ways of being. Just as his replacements were those who emulated in order to imitate his way by speaking and acting so that they spoke and acted like him when it came to speak and act like him.

His descendants who were his replacements-kʼexel became the ʼspitting imageʼ of their ancestors by replicating, repeating, reproducing his ways of being to then begin thinking and dreaming like him; to then begin forming and transforming like him in order to be like him in every way being and becoming.

This is the way of leaving oneʼs kʼexel which is what it means to leave oneʼs ketal; kitzijel.

In this way descendants-kʼexel became the replacements-kʼexel of their Father and their Grandfather too who they were born to replace by following in the footsteps he left on the path of life that led his descendants to great power and authority in order to guide and protect their People and their Pueblo as they became more and more powerful every day.

Ajaw Qʼukumatz left successors and descendants who were ancestral signs and symbols of ancestral remembrance-ketal, kitzijel which are two words that reflect one way of understanding ancestral replacements reflected in the face of oneʼs descendants.

The Most Important Remembrance and Gift of this Sacred Text:

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Ketal; Kitzijel; Kʼexel: the Very Essence of the Popol Wuj

Ketal: Their Sign; their Mark; their Track; their Trace; Their Trait; the Immortality of an Ancestor in their Descendant; this is the Sign that is the Mark made to be Followed on the Way

Kitzijel: Their Word; their Flame; their Truth; their Tradition; the Immortality of an Ancestor in their Descendant; this is the Word that is the Fire that Burns as the Flame of Eternal Existence

Ketal: Their Sign, their Mark, their Tracks, their Trace, their Traits of their Descendants and Descendancy; an Example Set; a Way to Be; a Way to Go; a Path to Follow; an Ancestor

Kitzijel: Their Word; Their Flame; Their Truth; their Story; their Tradition; News of their Descendants formed as signs painted on paper and shaped as letters formed into words written as writing that tells a story but also writing and images carved and crafted in limestone and wood

Tzij:  to strike or ignite a fire; to light a light; to tell a story; to give news; to explain; to speak; to provide knowledge; all that has to do with the word, truth, way, tradition

Etal: a marker, a sign of posterity, to indicate, to measure, a sign, a date, an inscription; to be known; a trace, a track, a trace to be followed, Ancestral footsteps walked by Descendant

The signs and symbols; script and images sculpted on limestone plates forming and shaping the stelae that told the sacred histories of the Holy Lords both Women and Men whose kitzijel was their ancestral remembrance passed on as a torch is passed on with an eternal flame; the burning ember; burning flame of the ancestors that is borne as the sacred burden of the descendants: kitzijel.

These signs; these symbols-ketal, kitzijel accompanied the painted pictures and written writing that were passed on to the descendants-kʼexel, ketal, kitzijel known as the replacements; kʼexel, ketal, kitzijel that were recognized by the ancestral traits-ketal, kitzijel.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These ancestral traits-ketal, kitzijel-ancestral characteristics are what identified the lineages in profile through the distinctive shape of the nose, form of the lips of the mouth, and set of the eyes as well as the shape of the forehead, chin, cheeks, ears, and top-knot of the hair this is what is meant by ketal, kitzijel.

These ketal, kitzijel were and are the principal traits and distinguishing marks of the ancestors worn with pleasure and pride upon the ancestral face of the descendants and their lineage: ketal, kitzijel.

Ketal, Kitzijel

These two words are signs that show as they signal the way in which the Maya are molded and modeled by the ideas of repetition and replacement of humans and maize. These foundational ideas that are embedded in these words that are metaphors-ketal, kitzijel are similar if not the same as the fundamental ideas of mimetic desire to repeat the speech and acts of the people who surround us. The Maya lived and continue to live by replicating the words and ways of the all the many beings in the world in which live with all the assorted ways of acting and speaking in that world that surround them. All humans do this yet the Maya transform it into mythic metaphors while practicing as a way of life; a way of life expressed in their religion.

This is why we must unravel to reveal the ancestral genius embodied in the words and ways of ketal, kitzijel for these to twins provide us with knowledge and wisdom that supports our desire to understand the essence of this Maya myth and its metaphors that come to life in the rites of initiation and the religious rituals that bring about transformation in the lifecycles of nature, culture, and individuals.

This repetition of rites of initiation is found in the desire to insure ancestral life is repeated perfectly through the Sign-Etal and Symbol-Tzijel that are spoken of here that reveal the repetitive nature of Maya ways-ketal and words-kitzijel that insure the ancestral return of the ancestral face through ancestral remembrance of ancestral ways.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This is rather simple yet complicated so either jump strait over to continue the mythic narrative or prepare yourself for a fascinating journey to be taken by us by our ʼentering the wordʼ of Maya Ancestors-Ojer Winaq  and their Maya Descendants-Ketal-Kitzijel-known as their Replacements-Kʼexel.

Ketal, kitzijel principal metaphor of the Maya sense of remembrance through the manifestation of ancestorsʼ most expressive qualities; most defining characteristics; most significant aspect of the ancestors nawal nature that was articulated in writing and expressed in painting; immortalized in carving and deified in sculpting in order to ensure the immortality of the ancestral essence left behind as a signs and symbols of remembrance and recollection known as: ketal, kitzijel.

Retal; Kitzijel of Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz

His descendants were many and it was through them that he was glorified in their remembrance of him and magnified in their memory of all he did; so that eventually his descendants manifest their sovereign power and majesty through their reverence of him, their Nawal Ajaw: Ajaw Qʼukumatz.

It was he who was a Nawal Kʼicheʼ Lord that was venerated by his daughters and sons; his subjects and vassals because of his magical powers of transformation.

This was when they hungered to leave their descendants the remembrance their fathersʼ traits in the ancestral faces of their replacement-retal and this they did by leaving behind a great many of their own ancient ancestral features-utzijel in the face of the descendants the left of their own; descendants that they bore and begot with their women; their wives who sought to give birth to a great many descendants.

This is what they did when they engendered many sons with their same facial features and same form of speech known as retal, utzijel so that they became many more than ever before in order to leave behind many, many sonsʼ of sons who were their grandsons: kimam.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
All of these grandsons shared their looks and language; their face and their speech so that the original sign and signature returned as their replica and replacement here on the Face of the Earth through the ʼspitting imageʼ that shown from the eyes, nose, ears, mouth, and teeth of their Grandson: Mam.

It was in this way that their ancestral traits were borne and begot on the faces of their Grandson; faces that were the direct result of their desire to bring forth the replacements of their Divine Ancestors who had died long, long ago.

Their ancestral image continued on as the sign; as the symbol of the living  remembrance of the original forming and shaping of the First Mothers; First Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo: Nabʼe Chuch; Nabʼe Qajaw Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

And so it was that many more descendants were made to sprout forth by both the Lords and the Vassals who will People and Populate the Face of the Earth.

These sons were engendered sons of the One Lord known as Tepepul spoken of as the ʼMountain Princeʼ who was known as ʼLord of the Mountainʼ Tepepul was his name. Tepepul; Iztak Yollotl are ʼCo-Regents or Co-Rulersʼ which is to say they are ʼTwinʼ Lords of Rule and Authority they complement and collaborate with one-an-other as Tepepul; Iztayol they are the successors-kʼexel of Ajaw Qʼukumatz. The second of two was Iztayol from Iztakyol from Iztak Yollotl known as White Heart, Bright Heart; Pure Heart, Shining Heart.

Iztayol was he, the unfortunate one; the unfortunate son of Noble Lords who was misused by the jealous and envious Ilokabʼ and their infamous plot to take power and rule from Ajaw Kʼotuja by killing him dead.

Tepepul and Iztayol were those who lived to perform the Noble responsibilities of the Lords through their power and sovereignty over the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom-Ajawarem-Realm for they ruled and reigned over a great territory with many groups of people, known as chinamit who lived in towns and villages known as tenamit.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
A tenamit was a well protected place with a palisade to embrace it just as a chinamit was this townʼs population who were its people. It was in these Tenamit-Citadels known as una Ciudadela  that the Chinamit-Pueblo grew to become many, many more People-Winaq-People who together as ʼOne Peopleʼ were  known as a  Pueblo-Amaqʼ and it was they who came to live in Great Walled Towns; Fortified Villages; and Stronghold Settlements surrounded by kʼoxtun-palisades that were built from wooden planks and spiked posts to protect the People of the Pueblo on all sides; for the Kʼoxtun encircled their Tenamit to enclose and embrace the Chinamit-Pueblo who were People-Winaq of the Pueblo-Amaqʼ.

Kʼiqʼabʼ and Kʼawisimaj: Kabʼawil Tojil

Kʼiqʼabʼ was one invincible Noble Lord of Great Strength who mobilized Many-Kʼi, Arms-Qʼabʼ and this is how destiny and naming in the Maya world are perfect mirrored reflections of one another in this case Kʼiqʼabʼ is  the strongest of all Kʼicheʼ Maya Warlords and Conquerors.

Kikʼabʼ-Lord Blood, this is a great name for a powerful and rather bloodthirsty Warlord who dedicated himself to harvesting captives who like IxKikʼ collects a net filled with heads by pulling one by their hair to then pull them forth as perfect heads with which to fill his One Big Harvest Net with sacred sustenance. Kikʼabʼ is a fine play on this name meant to mean many meanings.

Kikʼabʼ was he who collecting tribute to feed his Kabʼawil Tojil with the blood sacrifices required of him because of vast territory he acquired through great conquests through his ʼgreat strengthʼ and the ʼmany armsʼ that sustain him as Warlord who in turn was required to provide and sustain Tojil his Kabʼawil with a great harvest of sacrifice whose skull-heads were placed in perfect order on the skull wrack there in Qʼumaraq Aaj.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Sacrificial victims never want to go to their sacrifice which one is reminded of the Hero Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who must be goaded down the road to arrive before Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame in Xibʼalbʼa. That mythic image was a replica of the image of war captive being driven towards their sacrifice looking for a way to escape everywhere they are able. Tojil is the Kabʼawil who guides and protects this archetypal mythic figure who was an epic hero warlord and conqueror. It was because of the great achievement of Kʼiqʼabʼ Kikʼabʼ Kiʼkabʼ-Sweet Honey that his Kabʼawil Tojil grew in power as he grew in strength to grow in notoriety so that he grew in popularity so that many sons and daughters embraced him as their Kabʼawil to who they offered their own blood and sacrifice.

These are those who became the Fifth Generation of Noble Lords-Ro Le Ajaw and it was they who engendered yet another Generation of Lords; Lords who are named next by the naming of their names.

So that these who are those that are named next; these are those that are named by naming the names of the next generation; the next generation which is the Sixth Generation of Lords.

Both were Great Lords, they were glorious warlords and conquerors whose names are:  Kʼiqʼabʼ and Kawisimaj.

Kʼiqʼabʼ is the Great Lord-Nim Ajaw who is known today as Many Arms, Many Hands-Great Strength; and, Kawisimaj his Twin-like Co-regent and Co-conqueror known as Fire-Hardened Double-headed Planting Sticks; Fire-Hardened Double-headed War Spears.

Kʼiqʼabʼ and Kawisimaj are the names of the two Great Noble Lords who are the ʼgreat conquerorʼ and ʼgreat settlerʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom; the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom that these twin-lords expanded during their time of sovereign rule and authority over their Ancestral Realm of Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

They will change and transform their ancestorsʼ dominion through epic battles of conquest to conquer more and more territory to bring about extensive settlement through the sowing maize and cacao; indigo and cochineal; rubber and vanilla; cotton and henequen and much more throughout the massive territory they conquer to bring under Kʼicheʼ control.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
There was so much that was done by these two Noble Lords since much was brought to completion by these who are those known and named: Kʼiqʼabʼ-he of great strength to go to war; he of ʼmany arms, many handsʼ to sow the milpa who was paired with Kawisimaj-he of the double-headed spear to go to war; he of the double-headed planting stick to sow the milpa.

A great deal was accomplished by these two as it is said;  much was completed by these two Noble Lords of the Sixth and Final Generation of Ajaw Kʼicheʼ.

They made the Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ proud because truly they were also of a Nawal Essence; they were of a Nawal Nature who lived out the Nawal Way of being and becoming Nawal Ajaw on the Face of the Earth.

Their nawal nature; their nawal character distinguished them from others for they were those of great endurance; great strength. It was they who destroyed their enemy; it was they who decimated the countryside; they just demolished it by breaking it apart before they began breaking to pieces those places known as the Siwan-Tinamit; the Canyon-Siwan-Country; the Citadel-Tinamit-Town of the Small Pueblos-Chʼuti Amaqʼ; of the Large Pueblos-Nima Amaqʼ.

For it was they, these two Warlords; these two War Captains who broke apart the Kʼoxtun Towns with their Wooden Palisades; then they turn to smashing to bits to then tear to pieces the Canyon Country that was made up the Little Tribes-Chʼuti Amaqʼ; Big Tribes-Nima Amaqʼ of the Small Towns, the Big Towns; Chʼuti Tinamit; Nim Tinamit.

There was very little distance between these ancient defensible towns with their ancestral populations and their ancient defense works. They were all quite close together; those that were close to one another were the many walled cities and the fortified towns that known as the well defended strongholds of the Canyon Country.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
All of them were enclosed with protective palisades-kʼoxtun that protected these fortified citadels that were completely encircled by the warlords who then crushed them; for it was Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj who just smashed the Old Citadel-Tinamit Ojer. Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj simply demolished the Siwan, Tinamit with their superior strength and superior numbers of warriors and weapons.

There is the mountain territory of the Kaqchikelebʼ known as the Juyubʼal Qʼaqʼchekelebʼ the Mountain Place of the Kaqchikelebʼ spoken of in Nahuatl as Chichicastenango-ri Chuwi Laʼ, this is the place just on top of the surrounding ravines known as Above the Nettles today-ri Chuwi Laʼ wakamik.

There is the Mountain Place, the Mountain Territory of Rabʼinal or Juyubʼal Rabʼinalebʼ and there is the place known as ri Pa Maqʼ A-Where One Gathers Water on the River spoken of as Saqapulas where the white lime is found.

Then there is the Mountain Territory of Kaʼokebʼ or Kaweqebʼ known as Ujuyubʼ Kaʼokebʼ spoken of as Santa Maria Cauque.

Then there is the  Mountain Place known as  Saqabʼaja this is the territory of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo of San Andrés Saqabʼaja known as Juyubʼal  Saqabʼaja where the White Stone Houses of Sacrifices Saq Kabʼa Ja-White House of Sacrifice once existed as the Houses of the Divinity-Rochoch Kabʼawil where the Dawning Mountain-Saqiribʼal stands at the center of the Kʼicheʼ world. Then there are all the fortified citadels to the West known as: Tinamit chi kʼut Saqulewabʼ-White Earth known as Saculew; Chuwi Maqʼinaʼ-Above the Hot Springs spoken of as Totonicapán; Xelaju-Below the Ten Mountain-Xeʼ Lajuj Juyubʼ known as Xela; Chuwa Tzʼaq-Before the Temple Walls-Facing the Altar of Sacrifice-Momostenango-Pueblo of Altar Place of the Sacred Count of Days; Tzʼoloj Che-Place of the Elderberry Tree-Santa Maria Chiquimula.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
All of them rejected his authority; they just disrespected his rule; the authority, the rule of Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ giving cause for war to be made against Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ but they were not victorious in their war against Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ for he descended upon them to then fall upon them to destroy; to demolish; to decimate them there in their Canyon Country. For it was most certainly Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ who smashed them in their Great Walled Towns know to all as Tinamit.

The ones who he defeated are known today as: the  Rabʼinalebʼ, the Qʼaqʼchekelebʼ, and the Saqulewabʼ from Saculew-White Earth; then comes Chuwi Maqʼina-Totonicapán which is the place of ʼHot Waterʼ or Hot Sulfur Springs; then Xelaju-Quetzaltenango; next is Chuwa Tzʼaq-Before the Altar Walls of Momostenango; finally comes the naming of the name: Tzʼoloj Cheʼ-Elderberry Tree which is where Santa Maria Chiquimula continues to thrive on the very threshold of East and West between the two great territories of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Kingdom.

These are the places Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ made war against those who rejected his wish to govern them by subjugating them to his rule and authority. But it didnʼt happen like that because they didnʼt accept his offer to rule them as their Noble Lord; they didnʼt accept his subjugation of them through his power of rule that gave him the right to collect tribute from them.

So then it was Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ who conquered them; he just subjugated them to his rule and for this they despised him. They despised him because of the sovereign authority he held over them through his indomitable will and unquenchable thirst for power over others.

For this they made war on the Nim Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ; but it was they who were brought down low, humiliated by him to then be broken apart, just smashed to pieces by him; the People of the Canyon Country, the Palisade Pueblos of the Walled-off Cities; the Many Tinamit; the Naturally Defended Citadels; las Ciudadelas; the Kʼoxtun Towns and Fortified Fortresses; the Canyon Villages surrounded by deep ravines; all of them were defeated by Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The Pueblos of the Rabʼinalebʼ, Qʼaqʼchikelebʼ, Saqulewabʼ; they were brought down by him as well. They were cut-down like trees, the Tribes were felled; he knocked them over; he just broke them up; he just brought them to their knees; he just took them down to the ground.

Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ Ajaw Kawisimaj

Those who ended up subjugated were all the villages and towns who bowed down; knelt down low-mejlem, xukulem before this Great Lord of Great Strength: Nim Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ.

The warriors of Kʼiqʼabʼ conquered the people and the pueblos that lay far away from where they began their ordeal of conquest. Some of them died from the long distance of their journey that began so very far away; they were just finished off  and died before they were ever able to deliver the tribute asked of Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ Ajaw Kawisimaj.

When one group or two groups failed to deliver the tribute asked of them, their town would fall to Kʼiqʼabʼ the warlord and his powerful warriors and long distant merchants who collected the tribute that he demanded of them raise and collect from those People and Pueblos who he subjugated to his rule.

And it was that they did as his rule and authority required of them to do and quickly carried away the burden of tribute-patan that they delivered there before the presence of Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ and Ajaw Kawisimaj when that tribute was summonsed, when it was called for, when it was exacted from them, all of those who were subjugated to his extractive practices of demanding tribute from the subjugated cities and towns of the great Kʼicheʼ warlords and conquerors.

The Pueblos came to be oppressed in severe ways, for it was they who were enslaved; they were bled of their blood when they disobeyed; for when they disobeyed his requests it was they who were shot through with arrows against the trees.

Many times Kʼiqʼabʼ was forced to arrow the disobedient against the trees simply because the destiny that was once theirs was no longer theirs; for their destiny had become that of Kʼiqʼabʼ the Kʼicheʼ Warlord.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
For no longer did those towns where Kʼiqʼabʼ passed live lives in which they were born with a future, nothing became of their birth anymore because Kʼiqʼabʼ held their fate in his all-powerful hands; their destiny was clenched in his ʼfirm fistʼ that was his ʼunyielding graspʼ over the destiny of all those he subjugated to his rule thus was he named: Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ.

All of this came to be; all of this came to pass on account of the merciless severity of Ajaw Kiqʼabʼ who came up with the idea of a great rain of arrows that he let fly to let fall from the ʼmany handsʼ of the ʼmany armsʼ of his many archers who brought down a deluge of obsidian bladed arrows on the heads of those who resisted his rule.

This then was when Kʼiqʼabʼ made war on the Mountain People who thought they were safe behind their wooden palisades-kʼoxtun; kʼoxtun that were just those wooden-works of worked-wood that were formed and shaped to be carved and crafted into impenetrable protective barricades molded and modeled protect the People and their Pueblos from attacks coming in from the immediate surrounding by sealing the citadels off from any kind of outside invasion. The People of the Pueblos secured themselves within their palisade protected Pueblos to wait out the siege of Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ; Ajaw Kawisimaj.

Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ just went up and over to come down on the peopleʼs heads with a deluge of obsidian arrows from the sky above; to come crashing down upon the heads of the pueblos like a hail storm from the Heart of the Sky; a Great Storm that resound all around like lightning, like rain, like wind, like thunder to bring the villages down and the people asunder as innumerable obsidian blades went up into the heart of the sky to then hail back to down leaving the well protected strongholds completely and utterly destroyed and  demolished; towns in which nothing was heard except the distant roll of thunder; so that all there was left to do was conclude this tragic play with a final act of  plunder.

It was a sad, sad day for those who stood up to and resisted Kʼiqʼabʼ and his total rule over the Mountain Places and Canyon Country with all its well protected settlements, villages, and towns.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Especially those with thatch roofs that are not mentioned here but one can only imagine what lay in store for those people and pueblos who somehow provoked a firestorm from above by these most bellicose and imaginative Noble  Kʼicheʼ Warlords and Conquerors.

Qʼol Cheʼ known as the Arbol de Trementina

In their terror the Tribes threw themselves down in prayer and petition before the resin tree that stood there. It was just out of reverence and fear that they lay prostrate before the incense tree: Qʼol Cheʼ. Qʼol Cheʼ: Arbol de Trementina, this Tree of Flowing Sap; Tree of Flowing Blood, its wounds just told the story of devastation that came to pass there.

For this is where a proud Tinamit, once stood; this is where a confidant citadel once existed on the hot coastal plain known as Taqʼaj; a place that no longer stood as it stood before. That once proud town was now just a mound of rubble; a pile of stone that Kiqʼabʼ kept just as it was to teach everyone who lived there a lesson by leveling the place to the ground. Only a few stones here have been left unbroken, the rest are chopped-up in pieces as if split with an axe.

Today it can be seen there on the South Coast; there in the place known as Reed Mat Mound-Petate Juyubʼ or just Petatayubʼ for short, only today it is known as Ayutla, a place of pilgrimage, a place of remembrance of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq. It is right over there on the Costa Sur in Soconusco there on el Rio Suchiate.

It is just a pile of rocks that serves as a town marker, and called today by the name it was given as a reminder of what happened there: One Mountain of Stone-Jun Juyubʼ Abʼaj.

One can see it clearly today; the people look upon it in wonder when they pass by wandering how something like that could happen. People look on this place taking it in as proof of the strength and resolve of this Kʼicheʼ Warlord from the forgotten past; amazed by the pure fearless wrath of Kʼiqʼabʼ leaves one bewildered by the path of destruct he left in the memory of those who no longer remember these episodes of the Kʼicheʼ past that were a sure sign that the end was coming fast.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They could not kill him, nor could he be defeated; because, he was truly an invincible warrior-qitzij wi chi achij-truly he was a courageous conqueror that none could contain much less control.

He received tribute from all of the kʼoxtun towns-tenamit-villages with their fortifications and their surrounding Canyon Country and Mountain Places.

And then the Noble Lords-Ajawabʼ gather together to take council with one another in order to make plans so they would know what to do next and this is what they decided to do.

This then was when the Lords decided to control in order to collect tribute from all those that entered and exited the entrances and exits of every single one of their fortified towns and palisade villages as well as the surrounding countryside with its Mountain Places and Canyon Country.

It was not long before the entire territory was placed perfectly under the Lords control; making the Mountain Places and Canyon Country completely cut-off from all of their once neighboring citadel cities, garrison towns, and stronghold villages that were now firmly in the hands of the Great Lord; Nim Ajaw Kʼiqʼabʼ, the original Traditional Maya ʼStrong Manʼ or  ʼNimalaj Achiʼ whose preferred way was to strike fear in those who would not accept the sovereign rule of  he who was born to subjugate others to his total rule.

And then came the well-armed watchmen, the sentries of the warriors, and it was they who became the keepers and the care-takers; the sentinels and guardians of the Mountain People and Canyon Pueblos. It was they who organized the control of the lineages and their connection with those wild people of the hills around there where the mountain people lived and had lived since time immemorial.

The new way of watching the people of the mountain places and people of canyon country became a new way of controlling the enemy from the inside out. It was simply by cutting off the access between the pueblos and the canyons of the defeated towns and destroyed villages so that the coming and the going of the family members of the siwan-tinamit was now completely under the control of these all-seeing; all-knowing; all-powerful Kʼicheʼ Lords.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Remember the beginning of the recitation of the Ojer Tzij and the long discussion we had of the AjBʼis; AjNaʼoj; and the Ilol, Naʼol. Well sure enough we are moving far and away from the imaginal realm of the Nawal Winaq to wander further and further into the age-ending collapse of a completely overpopulated Mesoamerican world on the brink of deadly defeat and devastating destruction followed by a dreadful ordeal of death and disastrous dynastic demise; who would have ever imagined it coming to this?

The Sowing and Dawning is coming to its opposite in the Death and Destruction; Descent and Disintegration; Decline into Darkness and Degeneration into Dissolution.

We have come full circle; we are almost where we can begin dreaming of rebirth and return; revival and resurrection; renaissance and regeneration. This is where we are at 2025 with the Maya returning to their Sacred Book of Council: Popol Wuj.

No longer could the disobedient lineages of the hidden canyon be supported by the disobedient families of the villages who continued on with their resistance to the conquests and control of their ancestral strongholds and ancient settlements by those who we know so well by now as Kʼiqʼabʼ and Kawisimaj.

“If they return, then we shall make it so that they come in to live amongst the Pueblos in their great-walled cities,” they said, when all the Lords there arrived at an agreement on what to do next.

“This shall be our defense; as though it were an impenetrable wall; so too shall be our jealously preserved lineages who will stand-up against the enemy as our well built palisades-kʼoxtun of wooden planks and sharp wooded stakes.”

“Our fortresses will rise before us through the control of the movement of its people, may this be a show of our bravery-qoyowal-our courage; may this be a manifestation of our manly manhood-qachijilal-our mannish masculinity. So be it!” said all the Ajawabʼ-Lords; Rulers; Cacique de los Pueblos.

And so the leaders headed out when they went to the posts to which they were assigned; the places where each lineage prepared to confront the enemy warriors and rival captains of their traditional enemy.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This is when they were given their instructions; this is when they were named to go forth as warriors-ajlabʼal-soldiers to occupy the territory of the Mountain Pueblos-Juyubʼal Amaqʼ-the Mountain Tribes.

“You can get going now on account of the fact that this territory is now ours. Fear nothing! If there are guerrilla-ajlabʼal who continue to persecute you; those who come after you intent on killing you then just send for us, so we can return to finish them off; we will just come back to go after them until none are left,” they were told.

This is when Kʼiqʼabʼ gave them all their instructions; this is when they were advised on what to do next before the Captains-Qʼalel-Judiciales; Judges-Qʼalel-Magistrates and AjTzik Winaq; AjTzij Winaq, Mouthpiece of the Noble Lords-AjTzij Winaq-Crier-Speaker-Messenger of the Noble Lords who spoke on behalf of the Higher Ups; AjTzik Winaq those who announced and proclaimed that which the Noble Lords wish to make known to the Populous and its People.

Then they set-out in every direction; those known as the archers; those known as the arrowers; those who were spoken of as the Edge of the Obsidian Blade-uchiʼ chaʼ, uchiʼ kʼaʼm-the Edge of the Bow String.

They just scattered themselves all about up there on the mountain and down there in the canyon. Those who were the Grandfathers and Fathers of all the Kʼicheʼ people just scattered out and about the mountains; and, in and along the canyons.

Each of the Grandfather; each of the Fathers were assigned one of their mountains to defend and protect as guardians of the mountain-chʼajal juyubʼ.

They were those who walked all around the mountains and canyons as mountain scouts who were mountain lookouts who were war spies who were responsible to the eyes and ears of their Noble Lords.

They were those who came to be known as mountain lookouts that walked about with the mountain scouts looking all around the mountain places as well as in and out of their canyons and ravines.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
It was they-the mountain scouts-who were always ready to walk off to wherever they were called to go with their bow and arrows; arrows with their sharp-edged obsidian blades and bows with their tensely tightened strings.

It was they-the mountain lookouts-who walked about with their obsidian blade arrows ready to be notched on the edge of their bow-string of their tightly strung bows.

These were the guardians of the mountains. These were the care-takers of the canyons who walked their forest trails always at the ready; always walking on the edge of their obsidian blade arrows; always on the edge of their tightly strung bowstrings of their deeply bent bows of sentinel warriors known as uchiʼ chaʼ-uchiʼ kʼaʼm-chajal labʼal.

It was they who were those that moved all about as the mountain lookouts who were known as warrior scouts-chajal labʼal-warrior spies that walked all about on their forest paths to watch over their ancestorsʼ mountain places and canyon country with their well protected garrisons; with their naturally defended strongholds.

As mountain scouts they knew just where to go when they walked all about the many trees of the thick forest of their ancestral mountains; when they walked in and out of their peopleʼs hidden ravines and lost canyons.

They had no Dawn-Saqir of their own; nor did they have a Kabʼawil that was theirs; Mana jun ta Saqir wi; ma nay puch jun ta ukabʼawil.

They were those who just cut off the entrance and exit at the edge of the Noble Lordsʼ towns.

They were the ones who watched the way in and the way out of their Noble Lordsʼ citadels.

This is when they all left, all of those people of:

Aj WiLa; People of the Nettles

Aj Chulimal; People of Laguna Lemoa

Saqi Ya; People White River; Crystalline Water

Xajbakyej; People of the Deer Dance;

Chi Temaj; People of Beside the Bench; Chi Tem

Wajxalajuj; People of Eighteen Place; and just one more-xa jun chik

Aj Kabʼraqan; People of the Mountain Earthquake Quetzaltenango

Chʼabʼi Qʼaqʼ; People of Fire-Arrow of Jun Aj Pu-Volcán de Fuego

AjMaqʼ A; People of Saqapulas where they gathered the water

Aj Xoyabʼaj; People of Joyabaj; People of the Place of River Rocks

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
Aj Saqabʼaja; People of Saq Kabʼa Ja-White House of Sacrifice

Aj Siyajaʼ; People of Siya Ja; People of Sija; People of the Wild Cat River

Aj Miqʼina; People of Totonicapán; People of the Hot Water Springs

Aj Xelajuj; People of Quetzaltenango; People beneath Ten Mountain

Those of the Boca Costa and Costa Sur with its Torrid Hot Plain-Taqʼajal-Juyubʼal-Mountain Places are those that came forth with the information they had of the movement of all these many people who moved through from one place to another on their way up and down the mountainside.

They were the sentinels who were spies, the ears and eyes of the Noble Lords; they were the sentry who were the guardians and watchmen of the territory and the lookouts of the land who were mountain scouts that saw everything that happened up on the mountain to then report all that the People of the Pueblos did;  as well as what they said; and, were they went.

This was where and when they were sent out by Kʼiqʼabʼ and Kawisimaj to do what was asked of them by their Noble Lords who named them at this time with following names of Noble Entitlement:

AjPop: Noble Lord and Ruler of Noble Reed Mats of the Council House

AjPop Kʼamja: Noble Lord of the Reception House Noble Reed Mat

Qʼalel: War Captain of Power; Judge of Clear Vision, Magistrate

AjTzikʼ Winaq: Speakers, Criers, Messengers of the Higher-Up Authority

This was when there were Four Lords who gave orders to those who were sent out to watch the movement of the enemy warriors.

Kʼiqʼabʼ and Kawisimaj were the names of those Noble Lords who represented and stood before the Kaweq, they were two.

Keʼema known as the Weaving was his name of the Noble Lord who stood before the lineage known as the Nijaʼibʼ Kʼicheʼ.

Achaqʼ Ibʼoy known as the ʼYounger Brother of the Armadilloʼ was the name of the Noble Lord who stood before the lineage of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ which is to say it was Noble Lord Achaqʼ Ibʼoy who was the Noble Lord of the Ajaw Kʼiche-Lord Kʼicheʼ lineage.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
And, it was he who was their Noble Lord and Ruler: Achaqʼ Ibʼoy of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ was the way his name was named and the name of his position as a Noble Lord of the Lord Kʼicheʼ lineage: ʼAchaqʼ Ibʼoy-Younger Brother of the Armadilloʼ was his name.

And these are the names of the Lords who they summoned; these are the names of those who they sent for and those that they sent messages to as a summons.

These were those who were sent to give orders to those who were summoned there on each of the mountains to receive orders given by the Noble Lords. These were those who were summoned to receive the messages given to the Noble Lords-Nim Ajaw in order to do what they were instructed to do on the mountains according to the ʼcouncilʼ that was taken that became the ʼcounselʼ that was given by the Rulers; given by the Lords; given by the Ajaw.

And so it was that they sent their vassals to each of the mountains. The vassals they sent were their Engendered Sons-Kikʼajol who they sent to the mountain they were given; so that each engendered son was sent to rule over a mountain; the mountain given to him to rule was the mountain that he received as the Engendered Son of a Noble Lord and Ruler: Jun Ajaw.

And, then later on there came captives who were brought to the Lords, and there also came prisoners who were taken captive to be sent as slaves before those know as the Lords Ajawabʼ Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj, Qʼalel who were clear-seeing War Captains, Judges, and Magistrates who governed along with AjTzikʼ Winaq who were the Speakers that were the Criers that spoke for the Lords.

AjTzikʼ Winaq spoke in order to communicate all of that which was called upon to be spoken before those who were summonsed and sent for to listen to the messages that had been sent in order to be listened to and heard as the communications that the Noble Lords and Higher Ups delivered as communiqué ment to inform and instruct those who were their vassals and subjects-kal, kikʼajol-daughters and sons.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They made war, those known as the ʼedge of the arrow, the edge of the bow string; uchiʼ chaʼ, uchi kʼaʼmʼ those of the obsidian blade, those of the edge of the bow string; these were those who were specially trained warriors who took the war to those on the mountain; the mountain people were those who the specially trained warriors took their war to on the mountain with the sharp edge of their obsidian blade arrows; with the taught edge of the bowstring that were strung tight.

These were those who made war on the Mountain Places and Canyon Country where they took war to the Mountain People by engaging them in battle and conflict with their Obsidian Blades and Arrows; with their Bows and Bowstrings; these were once warriors of the Mountain Places.

They captured slaves, they took captives for sacrifice; and so it was that they enslaved those they captured while taking captives those they sacrificed before their Kabʼawil. They were courageous; these warriors who were ordered to make war on the Mountain Tribes in order to take captives alive. This was dangerous.

They grew in number as they grew in stature and status for the sacrifices they made of their lives; when they sacrificed their lives to make slaves of those they captured and taking captives for sacrifice; these warriors  grew in number as the Kʼicheʼ Warlords grew in strength and importance.

And because of this they were given status and recognition through their being given names to be given position of power and the stature of status for the courage and strength they showed in war.

It was dangerous this taking of captives; it took daring this capturing of slaves; and so it was that a warrior had to be bold, one had to be brave; neither slave nor captive gave themselves up easily.

It took courage to enter and invade the mountain places to make war on the mountain people to then begin taking them alive. And so these Kʼicheʼ warriors who captured slaves and took captives for sacrifice were greatly respected; they were held in high esteem as the sacred burden of their divine office grew in importance; and it did grow in importance.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
These warriors were much beloved by the Lords and so it was that they were recognized and remembered for what they did by having their rank and position assigned special status and special recognition by being granted special titles by the ruling lords and magistrates who sent them out to protect and watch over their realm, their kingdom while providing and sustaining the AjKʼixibʼ, AjKajbʼ with the sacred sustenance required of their divine office and that divine officeʼs sacred burden of sacrifice.

When they returned they delivered their prisoners, for those they had taken captive were handed over to AjKʼixibʼ, AjKajbʼ when they returned to Qʼumaraq Aj from the Mountain Places and Canyon Country where they were ordered to make war on the Pueblos in order to capture slaves and take captives.

So this was when the Lords gathered together in council with one another to establish the names and rank given as the official positions and noble offices of those who had provided service to those who gathered there in council:

AjPop: Noble Lord of the Council House Mat of Rule and Authority

AjPop Kʼamja: Noble Lord of Reception House Mat of Rule and Authority

Qʼalel: War Captain of Power and Clear Vision; Judge who weighs the Word of Truth and Tradition; Magistrate of the Governance of the Realm

AjTzik Winaq: Speaker; Crier of the message; Announcer and Messenger of the Noble Lordsʼ communiqué

This was when their thoughts; their understanding was brought forth before those gathered there in council:

“We must first take-up the sacred burden of office as representatives of each of the divisions of the Pueblo; first we must take-up the rank of the care-takers and safe-keepers of the lineages; we who have become the Protectors of the People that we have become as the Guardians of Villages-Chinamit-the Pueblos through our service given on behalf of the Great Houses of the Noble Lords!”

“I am the Noble Lord of the Noble Reed Mat: In AjPop!” said the leading New Lord who bequeathed status and entitlement upon himself.

“I am the Noble Lord of the Reed Mat of the Reception House: In AjPop Kʼama Ja!” said another New Lord who entitled himself with power and position.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
“Aj Pop-Noble Lord of Sovereign Rule and Authority is the cargo that is the sacred burden of divine office I shall receive just as you shall receive the noble rank and dignified position that comes next so that those who have lived and sacrificed themselves with the dignity of nobility may be shown the dignity of nobility inherent to the dignified noble titles and names received by us as signs and symbols of our now noble status and the inherent dignity comes with noble entitlement with it noble position and power,” said the Lords-Ajawabʼ.

This is what they said when they gathered together in council to bestow the emblems of dignified nobility; to bequeath the insignias of noble dignity upon themselves by naming their names with the hierarchical rank and order of the elite status intrinsic to the dignified titles, names and positions with which they were now named to be given in order to receive the dignity of distinction that was the noble distinction they deserved for the noble effort they made on behalf of their Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords and Lineages.

And so like them the Tamubʼ and Ilokabʼ were equal in status, in rank, and in position among these Three Divisions of the Kʼicheʼ. All of them were made equal in status and stature when they were named the name of their rank; when they were entitled with the position that bestowed upon them the distinction and deference; dignity and decorum; regard and respect; esteem and awe that was the position and rank bequeathed upon those of nobility as Noble Lords, Judges, Magistrates, Warlords, and War Captains.

This was when they made their choices; when they selected those to be named noble names conferring upon them rank and position; while being entitled with sovereign titles of entitlement bestowed upon their prized vassals and precious subjects of all their beloved territories.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This was when they bestowed upon them the sovereign titles of Qʼalel and AjPop to those who were shown noble status with its dignified distinction and distinguished deference before all other Daughters and Sons; Vassals and Subjects of the realm by being named noble names while being entitled with the great respect and high regard that comes with their entitlement as Supreme Magistrates and Noble Lords who governed and ruled as Councilors, Judges, Leaders, and Rulers of their particular citadel cities and protected towns and strongholds of their sovereign realm.

This was when their loyal subjects and devoted vassals received their names and entitlement as the Judges and Magistrates as supreme Rulers of the Land.

This was when the strong-armed Warlords and War Captains were recognized with noble status and royal stature bestowing upon them the position and rank they deserved as the First-born Sons, First-born Daughters of the realm; the First-born Vassals, First-born Subjects of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

They were those who were acknowledged as the chosen ones of the Noble Realm for their faithful service and selfless sacrifice shown to their Noble Lords as beloved vassals and beloved subjects of the Sovereign Realm of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

This is just as it was-and continues to be-the way of naming the names of noble titles of noble order, noble status, and noble position that is carried out to this very day.

But it wasnʼt here in the Kʼicheʼ where they began this practice of noble entitlement.  No, it was not from there that this noble tradition began.

This bestowal of power and authority upon the Engendered Sons and Engendered Daughters and the noble entitlement they receive was just the result of their being given noble titles that conferred on them entitled positions of noble rule and authority that came from the duties they performed.

This entitlement was bestowed upon the dutiful vassals and devoted subjects through their winning noble dignity and deference. Their naming and entitlement constitutes their being acknowledged for all they had done to be named and entitled with position and rank of nobility.

body:
These were those selected before all other as the first born daughters; first born sons of their territory who merited being recognized with the entitlement of nobility with its power and authority of sovereign rule.

Their newly won entitlement was only bequeathed upon those who proved themselves worthy of the recognition they received through their invaluable service and self-effacing sacrifice on behalf of their Noble Lords and their Kabʼawil.

All of which deserved the distinction they now received through their being named and entitled with the noble names and dignified titles of nobility. These titles; these names came with the dignity and decorum inherent to the entitlement and distinction of noble power. All of which was the nature and condition to the divine authority they now bore as their sacred burden upon their now regal shoulders.

This was the sacred burden of ancestral responsibility of rule and rulership they graciously carried as they made their way across their territory collecting tribute; acting as magistrates by judging the word and ways of their vassals and subjects while performing the role of guide and protector of  their handsome Mountain Citadels, finely-formed Canyon Fortresses, good-looking Garrisons, and well-built Strongholds surrounded on the four-corners and four-sides  with well-worked wood-works  of their wooden palisades: Kʼoxtun.

The Kʼicheʼ titles and names of noble entitlement and order were bestowed upon those of the Mountain Places and their First Born Children-unabʼe al, both girls and boys; both daughters and sons; the vassals, the subjects who were the chosen and the elect.

And then they summonsed them all. This then was when they sent for all of them, they sent for all of them to come away from there on top of each of their Mountain and Canyon Places known as their Mountain-Plain-Juyub-Taqʼaj.

body:
They sent their messengers to summons them so that they might come to one place; so that they might gather together in just one place to ʼName the namesʼ that would bestow upon all of them the noble dignity that was the deference and distinction of nobility in order to govern and rule as Noble Lords on the Mountain Places and in the Canyon Country.

These were just those Noble Lords who were yet to be acknowledged through their receiving titles of rulership through their being named as nobility; by their being given titles of entitlement, and powerful position in the noble hierarchies that would be inherited by those who were the Sons and Daughters of those who sacrificed their lives and well-being on behalf of the growth and expansion of their Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords at Qʼumaraq Aaj.

This is the lineage that goes back to the First Sunrise of the First Dawn of the Divine Daughters and Sacred Sons of the Saqil Al; Saqil Kʼajol Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

These were those who ruled with power that came from the Coming out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij; there in the East; there Beside the Sea where the Great Lord-Nim Ajaw sat upon his Jaguar Throne and Woven Reed Mats Noble Rule and Authority of the Council House of the Great Lord who was the Lord of the People of the Coming out Place of the Sun: Rajawal Aj Relebʼal Qʼij: Nacxitl Quetzalcoatl!

This comes from Tulan Tzuy-Wa the first and last word of this Ancient Ancestral Account of the Ancient Ancestral People: Nawal Winaq.

Xe Balax, XeKʼaʼmaqʼ is the name of the mountain where they went to meet together when they were raised-up in the chain of command by being recognized and awarded title, rank, and position designated by the sacred burden of divine office to which they were named and entitled.

They were shown respect by being named as nobility, selected, and designated to be given respect by being shown dignity through their entitlement as nobles by their being named with position of the power and authority to govern and rule through the practice of Naming the Names.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
There at Chulimal is where it was done, between Lemoa and Chuwila. This is how they created the noble hierarchy of the rank and order of governance through the entitlement, selection, and designation of those positions of power, rule, and authority known as:

Juwinaq Qʼalel: Twenty Judges of Clear Vision; Captains; Magistrates

Juwinaq AjPop: Twenty Noble Rulers named and titled as nobility

AjPop: Noble Lord and Ruler of the Council House Mat

AjPop Kʼamja: Noble Lord of the Reception House Mat

Qʼalel:  Judges of Clear-vision; Magistrate; Governor of the Realm

AjTzik Winaq: Speaker; Crier, Announcers of Counsel and Messages

Nimalaj Winaq: People of Notoriety; Principales of Guidance and Protection

All of them received their sacred burden, their ancestral cargos, and their entitled offices that bestowed on them the rank and order of the noble positions of hierarchy to designate and distinguish their noble dignity as the rulers and magistrates of the land.

AjPop: Noble Lords and Rulers who ruled the Land and its Pueblos

Qʼalel: Clear-sighted Captain; Even-minded Judge; Decisive Magistrate recognized as distinguished nobility devoted and dedicated to their lineage and its land; its People, and their Pueblo.

AjPop: Noble Lord and Ruler of the Council House Reed Mat of Rule

AjPop Kʼama Ja: Noble Lord of the Reception House Reed Mat of Rule

Qʼalel: Clear-sighted Judge and Judicious War Captain; Magistrate

AjTzik Winaq: Speaker; Crier of the message and ordinances of the Nobles

Julajuj Nim Chʼokoj: Eleven Masters of Ceremony; Masters of the Ancient Word and the Performance Ritual Drama, Dance, Song, and Recitation

Qʼalel Ajaw: Lord Judge, Noble Captains of War, Distinguished Magistrate

Qʼalel Saqikʼ: Lord Judge Saq ʼIkʼ, Noble War Captain of the Saq Ikʼ

Uqʼalel Achij: War Captain of the Uchi Chaʼ, Uchi Kʼaʼm; Arrow & Bow

RajPop Achij: Counselor of the Warriors; Guardians of the Borderland

RajTzʼalam Achij: Builders of Wooden Rampart Palisades;  Kʼoxtun

Utzʼam Achij: Front Guard of Merchant-Warriors; Spies and Mercenary

body:
The names of the Warriors-Achijabʼ entered there within the noble hierarchy and it was they who were given their noble titles-xekʼobʼik-when it came time for them to be named and entitled according to their official positions allocated to them upon their benches and the noble cushions of their sleeping places according to the hierarchy of their rank and order.

They were the First Born Sons-Nabʼeyal making them the Sons-Kʼajol of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq: Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Nation. This made these First Born Sons or Nabʼeyal the first among equals of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

They were those who saw and heard it all: Ilol rech, Taʼol rech-Seers of All, Hearers of All who were also recognized by their warrior position as ʼUchi Chaʼ, Uchi Kʼaʼm-the Cutting-edge of the Obsidian Blade; the Tight Strung edge of the Bowstringʼ as these master marksmen and archers were known.

These were those who were the elite warriors who watched for and listened to everything so they could guide the archers and bowmen who were the protectors of the Pueblo for they were the sheltering shield of the realm.

They were those seen as the protective wall that sealed-off the ramparts; they were those who just closed-off the wooden palisades that formed and shaped the wooden barricade; kʼoxtun that stood as the last line of protective defense before and behind the Kʼicheʼ Winaq.

And so they did the same, and just like this the Tamubʼ did as the Ilokabʼ, they selected and named the first of their subject, first of their vassals as the ʼPrincipalesʼ who were first among equals that were there in each of the territories to watch and protect the Kʼicheʼ Winaq in their realm, in their territory: Ajawarem Kʼicheʼ as the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom is known today as el Reino Kʼicheʼ.

They made titles for their first born boys, the first born sons, the engendered sons of theirs who were born on-top of each of their mountains and this is the origin of the Qʼalel who acted as the War Captain, Judge, and Magistrate and the AjPop who acted as the Noble Lord who acted as the Supreme Counselors of the Kingdom; these are the dignitaries that live in each of these places.

body:
This became the origin of the naming of the positions of entitlement of these men of rank; this became the way of distinguishing those of deference and distinction there on each of the mountain top citadels of today.

This was the origin of when they made their choices of supremacy in the choosing of the characteristic superiority of their Rulers, Captains, Judges, and Magistrates according to merit between those known as: Aj Pop, AjPop Kʼama Ja, Qʼalel and the AjTzik Winaq when the sons were given their titles that were passed down to them in perfect order according to their own particular day and its destiny.

Here then we shall recount the names of the House of their Deity: Rochoch Kabʼawil.  In truth it was just like this that the names of the Houses of their Kabʼawil were named in this way.

Nimaʼq Tzʼaq Tojil: Great Stonewall Temple and Stairs of Tojil

Nimaʼq Tzʼaq Tojil: Great Stone Temple and Stairs of the Kaweqebʼ

Awilix rech Nijaʼibʼabʼ: Great Stonewall Temple House of Awilix

Tzʼaq Rochoch Awilix: Great Stonewall Temple House of Awilix

Awilix Kabʼawil rech Nijaʼibʼabʼ: Awilix Deity of Great House People

Jaqawitz rech Ajaw Kʼicheʼ: Great Stonewall Temple of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ

Tzʼaq Rochoch Kabʼawil Jaqawitz: Great Stone Temple of Deity Jaqʼawitz

Jaqawitz Kabʼawil rech Ajaw Kʼicheʼ: Deity of Lord Kʼiche People

Tzʼutu Ja: Corn Tassel House is still visible this House of Corn Tassel

Kajbʼa Ja: House of Sacrifice is still its name; AjKajbʼ is Sacrificial Priest

They were Great Stone Temple Houses where their Kabʼawil was placed to receive the Sacred Sustenance of Ritual Sacrifice and the Worship given to them. The essence of the Kabʼawil was that of stone so too was the character of the Kabʼawil stone; so that the Temple Houses of the Kabʼawil were made of stone.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
The nature of their Kabʼawil was of stone and these stone Kabʼawil were worshipped by the Lords of the Kʼiche; AjAwab Kʼiche. They worshipped-qʼijiloxik their deity by ʼkeeping and countingʼ the Sacred Count of Days of the Divinatory Calendar that divined what needed to be given as sacrifice on the day when a particular kind of sacrifice was required to be to be given in order provide and sustain their Kabʼawil with the particular type of sacred sustenance that was the proper form of sacrifice given to feed those who called to be fed: the Kabʼawil.

And so it was that the Kabʼawil received the perfect offerings of sacrifice to make them satisfied and content in order that they in turn gave those who provided and sustained them with all they need with regard to their Milpa and its need for sun and rain; wind and breeze; clouds and lightning, thunder, and rainstorms.

In this way the Milpa grew thick with abundance creating great wealth for the Noble Lords who gave great feasts to make strong and valuable alliances with other People of all the other Pueblos.

And so it was the Kabʼawil were made content so the Lords of the Mountain and the Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Ukʼuʼx Ulew were made content to bring the rain and wind; warmth and sun; clouds and dew to make the Maize in the Milpa content.

And so the People of Maize of the Pueblo of Maize were made content with their great harvest nets filled with great loads of big heads of maize. With the harvest nets full the Noble Lords were made content and so they gave more and more sacrifice to their Kabʼawil in their Rochoch Kabʼawil. This is their story being told here.

They showed veneration to their Kabʼawil by invoking the ancient ancestral essence of stone that was the flesh of these Kabʼawil. The People worshipped them by naming their names and by doing so gave them praise and adoration.

They ʼKept the Daysʼ of their Divinatory Calendar and its ʼSacred Count-of-Daysʼ that told  them what to do and say next to form and transform the lives of the People of the Pueblos through their Kabʼawil that was provided for and sustained in their Rochoch Kabʼawil, the House of their Deity.

body:
The People of Pueblos entered first in the Rochoch Tojil to burn offerings before Tojil; then they provided and sustained the AjPop and AjPop Kʼaʼma Ja through ritual sacrifice that was brought forth through the invocation, incantation, and enchantment brought about through the ancestral practice of Naming of Names of the Nawal Ancestors and Kabʼawil of those who were AjPop and AjPop Kʼaʼma Ja-the Noble Lords of the Council House of the Woven Reed Mat of Rule and Authority.

It was then that they came before the Noble Lords to give their quetzal feathers-kiqʼuqʼ which were their way of providing tribute before the Lord; it was he who they provided for and sustained as both AjPop and AjPop Kʼamja.

It was through nourishing and nurturing the Kabʼawil of Stone in the Stone House of the Kabʼawil that the Noble Lords of the Council House Mat were venerated as the Great Lords and Magical Transforming Ancestors that they were; those who were known as Nima Ajawabʼ; Nawal taq Winaq these were those whose names were those known as Great Lords-Nima Ajawabʼ who were those known and named as:  Ajaw Qʼuqʼumatz; Kʼo Tuj Ja. It was they who through their nawal powers were able to change and transform the Face of the Earth for truly they were: Nima Ajawabʼ; Nawal taq Winaq.

Many towns were subjugated by these Great Lords that were Nawal taq Winaq, and it was they, the Nawal Winaq who were known and named as the Great Nawal Lords-Nim Nawal Ajaw: Nawal Ajaw ri Qʼuqʼumatz was one and the Nawal Lord Kʼo Tuj Ja was the other.

The two Nawal Ajaw known as Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj were another divine duo who were co-regents that ruled together as a pair of Noble Lords and Rulers who ruled ʼas ifʼ they were divine twins.

Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj were those who ruled as collaborative and cooperative companions to govern the People of the Pueblos of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

Kʼiqʼab-Nabʼey; Kawisimaj-Ukabʼ

body:
First came the strength subjugation of Kʼiqʼab and his ʼstrong armʼ of conquest that opened the road for his complement who came to settle the land. This was he who was Kawisimaj with his ability to establish settlements on the land by planting milpa after clearing the mountainside and valley floor with the axe and hoe to then set fire to clean the earth of the many obstacles and obstruction for the proper seeding of the maize seeds that were sown in the rich forest soil and ash of cleared and cleaned land.

It was Kawisimaj who came with his ʼsimaj-planting stickʼ with which he inseminated the earth with the sacred seed of the Ixim Winaq that sprouted forth as the descendant replacements-kʼexel of the ancestor whoʼs seed like ʼspittle-kʼexajʼ was just like that of Jun Junajpu. It was then that the tortoise shell earth sprouted forth with the milpa in the form and shape of all the many sprouts that came up and out of the ground. This is the story suggested but not told when the names of Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj are named.

It was these who were known as Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj that knew whether or not war was to be made; because everything was revealed before them clearly; they saw before them all that was to be seen; whether it was death; or, whether it was famine; or, whether they had go to battle in order to make war on another.

No matter what it was they knew what it would take place because they had a place to see it-Ilbʼal; there was a Council Book-Popol Wuj was its name.

This was their Book of Council that they consulted to know what needed to be done to bring their worked to completion by bring their lives to fruition through the seeing and knowing of the knowledge they looked for and found in their Book of Council that was their Council Book: Popol Wuj was its name.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
They were not like any other Lord; for great was their essence; immense their nature; vast their character. What was theirs in life was their ability to fast; they fasted there for a long time in their ancestorsʼ sacred buildings; for truly sacred was their burden of fasting; sacred was their self-sacrifice that was carried out by them in their Sacred Temple; in their Sacred Realm; for their Powers of Creation; for their Power of Sovereignty:  Loqʼbʼal Tzʼaq, Loqʼbʼal Ajawarem.

This was their ancient ancestral way of being in the world; this was their Nawal Way of becoming Nawal Ajaw through the change; through the transformation that comes through self-sacrifice that was their way of being and becoming Nawal Ajaw; Nawal Winaq in and upon the Face of the Earth-Uwach Ulew; there in and upon the  Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew.

For a long time they fasted when they humbled themselves; when they prostrate themselves before their Kabʼawil to suffer through self-sacrifice. They just punished themselves; they just gave sacrifice as penance; sacrifice as payment; sacrifice as tribute offered; tribute paid.

Xekʼajbʼik: they sacrificed themselves; they punished themselves; they brought themselves low to humble themselves before their Deity; their Kabʼawil.

And this then was their fast, 180 days they fasted and 180 days they prostrate themselves and burnt offerings-kekʼatonik-before their Kabʼawil.

This then was when they fasted there before their Kabʼawil for 260 days Oxlajuj Winaq; the Fast known as ʼThirteen Twenty-Oxlajuj Winaqʼ is the name of the Fast they fasted, Oxlajuj Winaq-Thirteen times Twenty days did they sacrifice themselves; they lay face down; they prostrate themselves while they sacrificed their burnt offerings; burnt offering of sacrifice that they burnt before Tojil; they burnt their sacred offerings there before their Kabʼawil Tojil.

Xa Munil-Only Fruit; Xa Tulul-Just Zapote; Xa AjAche-Just Matasanos;  Xa Qʼinoom chikilo-Just Jocotes fruit did they suckle; they ate no sustenance molded and modeled from Maize; no Sacred Sustenance formed and shaped from ground maize did they take; just fruit was all they ate; that is all they took; they just suckled fruit.

body:
When they practiced sacrifice for Three-hundred and Forty days they humbled themselves through punishment-kʼajbʼik; though penance-kʼajbʼik; through blood-letting-kʼajbʼik sacrifice upon their altars of sacrifice before their Kabʼawil there in the House of their Deity-Rochoch ri Kabʼawil.

They did not eat for Three hundred and forty days-Wuk lajuj Winaq-just Seventeen times Twenty days did they prostrate themselves face-down before the Earth before the Sky. This was their fast known as Wuklaj-Seventeen, this is when they took it slow when they made their fast; this was when they did not eat anything but fruit; for the fast of Wuklaj-Seventeen they just suckled Jocote-Qʼinoom Chikilo.

Truly-qitzij they carried out great vows; this was the sign of their intentions before the Kabʼawil as the Noble Lords of the People who were the Pueblo; this was an indication of the spiritual essence of the Holy Lords.

They didnʼt sleep with any woman then; they kept to themselves by staying alone; just keeping themselves company by staying all alone with themselves; they fasted while remaining in the house of the Kabʼawil.

They gave sacrifice, the performed acts of worship and adoration every day; they just burnt offerings-xa kʼatonik, and they just lay themselves down upon the ground as they prostrate themselves before their Kabʼawil.  This was all they did when they made the fast known as Wuklaj-Seventeen.

They just stayed there in the dark of night; they just stayed there in the light of day. Their hearts wept just as their bellies wept when prayed and petitioned for the light and life of their daughters-kal and of their son-kikʼajol; for the blessing-usaq and health-ukʼaslem. This was when they prayed and petitioned for: usaq, ukʼaslem, kal, kikʼajol.

They made prayers of petitions for their Rule as Noble Lords of their People; they made petitionary prayers for the Sovereignty that was theirs to Govern over their Kingdom; to Rule over their Realm: Ajawarem.

This was when they raised their Face to the Heavens; this was when they lifted their Eyes to the Sky above-Chi Kaj-and the Heart of the Sky: Ukʼuʼx Kaj.
