source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
This then is their petitionary prayer that they performed as they pleaded for their beloved People, precious Pueblo; the Sons, the Daughters; the Vassals, the Subjects to satisfy all their hunger and need made known through their plea; their petition; their appeal presented here before the Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Earth.

Aqʼaroq! At Oobʼ uQʼij, at Juraqan, at Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ulew

“!Aqʼaroq! At Oobʼ uQʼij,

at Juraqan,

at Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ulew!

At yaʼol rech qʼanal, raxal,

at pu yaʼol miʼal, kʼajol!”

“Chatziloj, chamaqʼij uloq a raxal, a qʼanal!

Chayaʼ taj ukʼaseʼik, winaqirik  wal, nukʼajol.”

“Chipoqʼ taj, chiwinaqir taj,

Tzuqul awe, Kʼool awe,

Sikʼi awe pa bʼe, pa jok, pa bʼe yaʼ, pa siwan,

Xe cheʼ, xe kʼaʼm;

Chayaʼ kimiʼal, kikʼajol!

Ma ta ja bʼiʼ il, tzʼap, yan, kʼexo.

Ma ta chok kʼaxtokʼonel chikij, chikiwach!”

“Me pajik, me sokatajik, me joxowik, me qʼatowik.

Me qajik rekem bʼe, rajsik bʼe;

ma ta ja bʼik pakʼ toxkʼom chikij, chikiwach.”

“Keʼayaʼ taj pa raxa bʼe, pa raxa jok!

Ma ta ja bʼi kil kitzʼap akʼwil, awitzmal!”

“Utz taj kikʼojeʼik tzuqul awe, kʼool awe chachi, chawach.”

“At Ukʼuʼx Kaj, at Ukʼuʼx Ulew,

At Pisom Qʼaqʼal, a puch Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz;

Pam Kaj, upam Ulew, Kaj Tzʼuq, Kaj Xukut.”

“Xa ta Saq, Xa ta Amaqʼ upam chachiʼ, chawach, at Kabʼawil!”

Lord of the Five Days: Jobʼ Qʼij

This then is the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords pleading their plea; making their petition through this prayer performed before their Kabʼawil in order to make their appeal from their ancestral heart to request the sacred sustenance of their People while clearing their road of all possible obstacles of every snare, trap, lust, longing, deception, and desire that will make them fail, falter, to then fall into the depravations placed on oneʼs path by the deceptive play that is the way of the trickster deity mentioned here; the deceiver; the mocker of men; the deceiver of women who one must stay clear for he-she is the one who causes fear that is prayed to be free of  here.

body:
Give the Spark of Inspiration and Powers of Creation

to Children of Mothers; Children of Fathers;

You who give Daughters of Fathers; At yaʼol Miʼal;

You who give Sons of Fathers; At yaʼol Kʼajol

Giver of the Spark of Life; Kʼaseʼik

You who bring forth the Peopling of the Earth; Winaqirik

Bring forth the Daughters of Women; Sons of Men!

Chayaʼ taj Kʼaseʼik, Winaqirik Wal, Nukʼajol!

May you Give us the Vassals and Subjects of the Realm!

May you Give Us Daughters and Sons of the Pueblo!

Giver of life of Children, At yaʼol Miʼal;

Giver of life to Sons, At yaʼol Kʼajol

Giver of Daughters of Fathers; At yaʼol Miʼal;

Giver of Sons of Fathers; At yaʼol Kʼajol

That they may multiply, may they grow to become many

Chi Poqʼ taj chi Winaqir taj

Those who are Providers may they Provide for You; Tzuqul awe

Those who are Sustainers may they Sustain You; Kʼool awe

Those who invoke may their invoke you; Sikʼij awe

May they invoke you upon the path; pa bʼe

Calling upon you on the wide roads, pa jok

May they invoke you along the river, pa bʼe yaʼ

Under the trees, under the vines; Xe cheʼ, Xe kʼaʼm

Give them their daughters, give them their sons;

chayaʼ kimiʼal, chaya kikʼajol;

May there be no evil; Ma ta ja bʼiʼ il

May there be no wrong-doing

Nor knotted traps, tzʼap

Nor secret seduction, yan

No changing one for another; kʼexo

May there be no deception of one thing for another;

Ma ta ja bʼiʼ kʼexo;

May there be no Bait and Switch in the Marketplace

No tricky exchange under the table

May there never be Tricksters in front or behind you

Ma ta chok kʼaxtokʼonel chi kij, chi kiwach!

That your daughters and sons not be accused; ma pajik

May they not be found guilty; ma pajik

That they not be wounded; me sokotajik

That there be no knee-scrapping lust; me joxowik

May they not be falsely judged; me qʼatowik

May they never fall on their way down the road;

Me qajik rekem bʼe; rajsik bʼe

May they never stumble climbing up the road;

May there be no obstacles placed on their path;

May there never be problems set on their way;

May they never be stopped from behind;

May they never be blocked from upfront;

At Ukʼuʼx Kaj, at Ukʼuʼx Ulew, at Pisom Qʼaqʼal, a puch Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz; pam kaj, upam ulew,  kaj tzʼuq, kaj xukut.

This was when the Lords fasted after they invoked their Kabʼawil in order to pray out their petition; this was when they begged and pleaded their  needs when they sowed and seeded all the many thing they needed as they raised their face to the Sky and their eyes to the Heavens.

The Noble Lords and Rulers fasted for nine times twenty days-Bʼelej Winaq-180-Days; this was when they fasted for thirteen times twenty days-oxlajuj winaq-360-Days, and when they fasted for seventeen times twenty days-wuklajuj winaq-340 Days too!

Great was there fasting, so great  that they cried out with all their heart for the divine providence that brought forth the success and prosperity of their daughters and sons.

This was when they wept for all of their women and for all of the children when they felt the weight of their responsibility when they carried out their ancestral cargos of their sacred burden of power and authority.

This was when they wept for their rule and sovereignty that was their divine office that was theirs to  carry-out and perform on behalf of the People; on behalf of the Pueblo; that which was the destiny of each of their Noble Lords; Noble Rulers: Ajawabʼ.

This was in the Sacred Light of the Sacred Life-Loqʼbʼaʼl Saq Kʼaslem recognized by the Noble Lords and Rulers that had come down to them from the very beginning at the sowing; the rooting of the Forming; the Shaping.

body:
This was the precious life; precious light of the Noble Lordsʼ that was shown appreciation from the beginning; from the origin of their Sacred Rule; Divine Sovereignty: Loqʼbʼal AjAwarem. This was the Lordship that was the Rulership of the Kingdom:

AjPop,

Aj Pop Kʼamja,

Qʼalel,

AjTzikʼ Winaq.

They entered there as Co-Regents as Co-Rulers who were companions; they came in two-by-two as twin rulers-kakabʼ. So it was that they came in there as coupled companions;  two-by-two-kakabʼ as pairs when they took turns governing the Pueblos of the Kʼicheʼ so that they as came to their Noble Rule two-in-two when they substituted one another as Rulers of the Pueblos. This is how it was when they began to rule as Co-Regents who were Co-Rulers who were Twin-like Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

This was when they sacrificed themselves to the goverance of the Pueblos and all the Kʼicheʼ People. These rulers gave of themselves completely for the support and maintaince of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblos.

There was only one origen from which their rule came forth; it was just from one begining that originated thier ancestral truth that was their ancestral tradition of those who provided the sustenance to maintain the Kʼicheʼ Lords; just one root of origin was the one way of providing sustenance and support; just one root of origin was the one word of humility and obedience of those who were the Providers and Sustainers of the Peopleʼ when they gave sacred sustenance and ritual sacrifice to maintain the Noble Rulers and their Kabʼawil.

There was just one root to the one word; of the one way of those who were the Providers and Sustainers of the support and maintance of the Kabʼawil for it was they who feed and sustained their People, their Pueblos; those who had to be fed were fed by those who were their Kabʼawil.

This One Root of the One Word, One Way; the One Root of the One Truth, One Tradition came from the Many Trees People; Many Trees Pueblo known as the KʼicheʼWinaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ who were sown and rooted in the Place known as Kʼicheʼ  it was only from here did their origin branch out to the other lineages.

body:
And so it was that from under the power and authority of the sacred word was it done since it came from the Lord Kʼiche-Ajaw Kʼicheʼ; and, likewise was it done by the Tamubʼ and Ilokabʼ together with the Rabinal, Qʼaqʼchikel, AjTzʼikin Ja, Aj Tujala Ja, Uchʼabʼa Ja.

Thus began the tradition of providing sacred sustenance as well as the support for the Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ by  providing and sustaining them with the care and concern that comes with their being provided with their sacred sustenance while being supported with the necessary support and maintance.

This is how it began there when it then became the tradition and way of everywhere else in the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom: the Noble Lords were both provided for and sustained by the Kʼicheʼ People of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. For it was said this came from the very origins of their Sovereign Rule; of their Noble Reign.

Each group  arrived there to serve their month in Kʼicheʼ; that was when it was done by all of them; that is how the Kʼicheʼ came to rule and govern those who they came to rule;  for those who they ruled were obliged to provide for them as their Noble Lords who in turn provided them with Noble guidance and Noble protection for the People of the Pueblos they governed as Sovereign Rulers.

Those Kʼicheʼ Lords happily received those who were appointed to be their providers, sustainers-tzuqul, kʼool-nourishers, nurturers of  their Kabʼawil for they had done so much for them. Tzuqul, Kʼool were those who gave blood sacrifice to nourish, nurture the Kabʼawil; they were those who sacrificed blood to be given as sacred sustenance.

Their fasting was a punishment that was a penance  made by the Noble Lords so that it was not in vain that they ruled over all others. For it was they who gave sacrifice as payment for the debt of their power; the power theyʼd been given in exchange for the sacrifice given by them; the power they were given was the fire-sovereignty they received from the Kabʼawil of Tulan Tzuy-Wa and that fire-rulership they now possessed to rule with power and authority over the People-Winaq of the Pueblos-Amaqʼ.

body:
The punishment they suffered in their fasts showed they had not won their rule through sorcery with its beguiling and bewitching of others through conjuring in the shadows; through bewitching in the darkness; they did not steal away their rule-ajawarem-sovereignty; nor  their power-qʼaqʼal-strength because they came with a cost; majesty-tepewal-glory was won through suffering pain and the punishment of blood sacrifice; it was just suffering and sacrifice that the Noble Lords attained their rule-ajawarem and power-qʼaqʼal and majesty-tepewal-glory.

It wasnʼt for nothing that they went down to subjugate the citadels in the canyons and fortified villages of the Small Pueblos, Large Pueblos to collect tribute from them.

And a great tribute they collected because a great payment they were made to pay; those of the Siwan, Tinamit; those of the Chʼuti Amaqʼ, Nim Amaqʼ they came bearing their tribute so that  there came turquoise-xit and silver-puwaq; and there came handfuls of jade beads-kajqʼabʼ raqan-jade beads by the handful that were measured by the handful; handfuls of gold beads tuwik raqan-gold beads by the handful that were measured by the handful; and there came precious jade jewelry-chi kuwal and along with all of this came the fine emeralds-yamanik-precious stones that became finely crafted jewelry that the Noble Lords wore as their adornment and embellishment.

There came penachos that were beautiful feather crest worn on the head; feather headdress known as crests that were formed and shaped from lovely turquoise-blue cotinga feathers-raxon and bright green resplendent quetzal plumes.

This finely crafted quetzal plumage framed the feathers of these highly prized headdresses; this was the precious feather work of the Small and Large Pueblos of the Canyon Citadels. These feather crests were created and crafted so that they stood straight up on the crown their Noble Lords heads; it was all delivered up as Tribute: Patan.

The tribute of all the tribes came before the twin rulers who ruled as couples; two-in-two-kakabʼ that was spoken of as Co-Regents; Co-Rulers: Nawal Ajawabʼ Qʼuqʼumatz, Kʼo Tuj Ja or Kʼotuja.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
And so too did the Tribute-Patan come before Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj and those who ruled with them through the power and authority given to these Noble Lords through the titles they received and the names they were given with the rule that comes with those noble names and titles.

These were the Noble Rulers of the Mat, Noble Rulers of the Reception House Mat along with their Judges, War Captains, Magistrates, Speakers, Criers; and many others not named here by title.

So that those who are named are named by their titles: ri AjPop, AjPop Kʼamja, Qʼalel and AjTzikʼ Winaq. These were all noble positions of entitlement; these were the names of nobility that were given to show dignity and deference; distinction and difference between the Vassals and Lords; Subjects and Rulers.

These were those who formed and shaped the hierarchy of the People of the Pueblo through the naming of the names of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

And so it was that the Kʼicheʼ Lords did what all entitled Lords are called to do. It was not just a little that they came to do those who were the Kʼicheʼ Lords.

It was not just a few more Tribes-Amaqʼ that they, the Noble Lords, went out and conquered; because it was not such a very long time that passed before many more groups of People and divisions of the Pueblos were brought into the service of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq.  It was they who were those of the Mountain Pueblos who were brought in to serve the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

It was they, the People of the Tinamit who were the Pueblos of the Siwan that came in to Kʼicheʼ bearing the sacred burden of the Nobleʼs tribute in their kakaxtle. Those of the Siwan; Tinamit that bore on their back the tribute they carried in their merchant carrying-frames-kok which was the tribute required; the tribute requested from them by the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ. It was the Siwan; Tinamit-Canyon Country; Outlier Towns who were ordered to have their great loads delivered as Patan-Tribute to the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords.

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
It was they, the branches of the Pueblos, who received great suffering and it was they who were persecuted by their power and majesty; the splendor and supremacy that was the greatness and grandeur of the Kʼicheʼ Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

The grandeur and greatness of the Kʼicheʼ did not come all at once; it didnʼt sprout forth all of the sudden; their power was created through the sacrifice and suffering of the Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ. Their power and glory that was their sovereign majesty came with a One Great Lord: Jun Nim Ajaw.

Their great growth and aggrandizement was created by a Nawal Ajaw known as:  Nim Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz he who is known and named: Great Lord Quetzalcoatl. Thus was the beginning of the remarkable growth and development of the Kʼicheʼ.

Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz was the root and origin of their grandeur; of their greatness through his service to the Sacred Burden of Rulership and the responsibility that he took as the sovereign rule over the Pueblos and their People. So let us then name the names of the Kʼicheʼ Lords and Kʼicheʼ Nobles as if one were naming the names of a Sacred Bundle of Noble Lords and their Noble Entitlement with the dignity and decorum; deference and distinction that comes with the naming of the names of their ancestral names while naming the names of their noble titles.

So here is where we shall innumerate; here is where we shall name the names of the generations of the Noble Lords.

We shall innumerate the names by naming the names of all the Noble Lords, names that we shall name here by naming each of their names in order, until all of their names named. This is how we shall Name the Names of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords; Generation by Generation; Lineage by Lineage until all the Names are Named.

This then, is the descent of order, of the orderly descent of Noble Rule, of the Noble Lords:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ,

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ,

Majukʼutaj,

Ikʼi Bʼalam

These are the First Grandfathers-Nabʼe Qamam and the First Fathers-Nabʼe Qajaw, when they stood before the Dawn at the Coming Out Place of the Sun; there at the emergences of the Sun; the Moon, and the Star.

body:
This was when the Our First Grandfathers-Nabʼe Qamam and Our First Fathers-Nabʼe Qaqajaw watched and waited for the appearance that was the emergence of their Sun; their Moon, and their Star: Ikʼoqʼij.

This was when the Sun, the Moon, and the Star showed their face to make their appearance at the Place of Emergence there Beside the Sea in the East.

This then is the descent that is the order of the Lordship, Rulership that we shall begin here, right at the root, as the lords entered to rule as Companions-Kʼulukʼuj-Complementary Collaborative Lords as Twin Lords; Coupled Lords; Paired Lords of the People of Maize: Kʼulukʼuj Ajaw.

These were the Divine Ancestors who were the First Grandfathers that were the rulers of Great Walled Cities-Tinamit-Finely Finished Fortified Towns. These Co-Rulers who were Co-Regents succeeded one another as Noble Lords in perfect succession; one after the next the Kʼicheʼ lineages ruled as Sovereign Lords with noble power and divine authority; each one of the Noble Lords entering in perfect order as Sovereign Rulers who manifest as the Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo..

This is how they appeared in succession as Noble Lords of Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ: Ajaw Kʼicheʼ.

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ was the Root of the First Generation-Uxe Nabʼal of the Kaweqibʼ.

Kʼo Kaʼibʼ also Kʼokawibʼ was the Second Generation-Uka Le after Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

Bʼalam Kʼonacheʼ became the Aj Popol of the Third Generation-Rox Le.

Kʼotuja, Istayul are of the Fourth Generation; Ukaj Le.

Qʼuqʼkumatz, Kʼo Tuj Ja is the Root of the Fifth Generation-Uxeʼ Nawal Ajaw Roʼ Le.

Tepepul, Iztayol was the Sixth Ranked-Waq Tas.

Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj was the Seventh Change-Waq Jal of Lordship of this Nawal Ajaw.

Tepepul, Ixtayubʼ are the Eighth Generation-Uwajxaq Le in the lineage of Rulers.

Tekum, Tepepul were the Ninth Generation-Ubʼelej Le of Noble Lords.

Wajxaqi Kʼaʼm, Kʼiqʼabʼ were the Tenth Generation-Ulajuj Le of Noble Lords.

Wuqubʼ Noj, Kawatepech were the Eleventh ranked Lord-Ujulajuj tas Ajawabʼ.

Oxib Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi were the Twelfth Generation of Lords-Ukabʼlajuj le AjAwabʼ.

Maize Lord Lineage: Jun Nal Ye; Jun Ixim; Jun Ajaw, Yax Bʼalam

source: Popol Wuj: Translation and Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (Grove Press manuscript, October 24-27 2025)
body:
First Fathers: Nabʼe Qajaw; Xpeyakok, Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej

“Xchiwachin uwach jujun chu jujunal Ajawabʼ Kʼiche. This my dear reader is one last serious play-serio ludare on the Maize Lord Jun Nal Yeh which comes through the writing as a secret sort of sacred language of Tzuy-Wa that seems to say here is the appearance of the face of the First Fathersʼ Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are being invoked in order to be made ʼpresentʼ just as we are invoking the names of the First Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ by saying we will start at the very root by naming each of their names in pairs in order of their appearance. 					And the First Lords of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq are named in pairs as: Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu sure enough the ingenious scribes write this little funny and strange little phrase that says:  xchiwachin uwach jujun chu jujunal Ajawabʼ Kʼiche which translated as “their faces shall appear one by one, jujun, each one of ʼallʼ the Lords of the Kʼiche”ʼ that sounds like the Ancient Ancestral Lords Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu will appear as the One Lord Jun Ajaw the Classic Maize Deity know in the Classic Period as Jun Nal Yeh: Jujunal sounding  very similar. It probably is just the way the sentence naturally appears but jujunal is also a choice the Maya Scribes make out of any number of other possibilities: serious play-serio ludare.

And so you there you have it, magic nawal language of Tzuy Wa that says the Face of the Earth was ʼcleared off to seed each of the seeds of each of the teeth of the Maize Deity, known as the Maize Lord Jun Nal Yeh who has teeth like the Ground White Maize Teeth of Ground White Bone of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who was a the First False Maize Father yet is played with as a Maize Deity through his false maize teeth. Amazing people, the Maya and how they are able to pull together every last hair to bring forth the sprouting and dawning of the Maize People.

body:
Xpiyakok merits mentioning as well because it is up through his tortoise shell back as a an Earth Deity that the Maize sprout will come shooting forth as Jun Nal Yeh comes back to life after being left for dead somewhere in Xibʼalbʼa. For it is from Xpiyakok that the rooting of this naming should begin with the Father of the Fathers of Junajpu, Xbʼalamkiej but we will leave that for you to ʼfigure outʼ so time when you donʼt have to name the names of the Kʼicheʼ Ajaw. “Xchiwachin uwach jujun chu jujunal Ajawabʼ Kʼiche”

And it was they, Oxib Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi-Three Deer, Nine Dog who ruled when the Warlord and War Captains of the Castilian Conquistadores known as  el Adelantado Don Pedro de Alvarado yet known as the Sun in Nahuatl: Tonatiuh-Donadiu.

This is the Castilian Conquistador who burns to death the Two Last Lords of the Kʼicheʼ. Some say they were ʼhung-ximʼ or were they just ʼboundʼ by the Castilian People. What is importance is the Traditional Maya way of death as you know so very well would have been burning them in a great stone oven to have their ashes scattered like jade along the waterʼs edge of the Motagua River  that snakes its way down through the Kʼicheʼ until it reaches the Caribbean Sea.  I cannot help but think the Kʼicheʼ Maya saw a New Sunrise over their Kingdom with the fall of their Sun and the Rise of Castilian Sun-Donadiu as mention before.

Tekum, Tepepul paid tribute before Castilians. They had already been engendered at the thirteenth generation of lords.

Don Juan de Rojas, Don Juan Cortes were the Fourteenth Generation: Ukaj lajuj Ajawabʼ. They were engendered heirs of Tekum Mam and Tepepul.

Oxib Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi; Three Deer, Nine Dog were the Ukabʼlajuj le AjAwabʼ

Oxib Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi were the Twelfth Generation of Noble Lords and they were killed-ixkamik on 4-Kʼat Marzo 9, 1524.

body:
The perfect day to be immolated in the stone oven of sacrifice on the sacrificial fire burning their on the Archetypal Day of the Sacred Fire Kajibʼ Kʼat which Four Harvest Net but also Four Sacrificial Fire and the Four of the Four Corners, Four Sides; Four Cardinal Directions to assure the rebirth of the Kʼiche Rulers; Kʼicheʼ Lords; Ajaw Kʼicheʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

And this is the descent of the descendants, and these are the succession of the successors of the generations as well as the rank and position of Rule and Authority before the Kawiqibʼ Kʼicheʼ.

The Kingdom-Ajawarem with its Rulership of the Lords is here names as those who are the Noble Lords of the Council House Mat and the Reception House Mat of the Kaweqibʼ Kʼicheʼ: ri Ajaw AjPop, AjPop Qʼamja chuwach Kawiqibʼ Kʼicheʼ; before the Kaweqib Kʼicheʼ.

Here we shall tell further of the Great Houses and their town lineages. Here they are the naming of the Great Houses-Nim Ja; these are the Great Houses of the each of the Noble Lords are the AjPop, AjPop Qʼamja.

These are the names of the Nine Towns with the Nine Great Houses of the Pueblo-Chinamit of the Kawiqibʼ

These are the names of the rulers of each of the Great House-Chi Nim Ja.

Ajaw AjPop: Noble Lord Chancellor; Noble Lord Councilor; He has One Great House-Jun Nima Ja that is a Holy House, Sacred House-Kʼu Ja;

Kʼu Ja-Sacred House; Holy House is the name of his Great House-Nima Ja.

Ajaw AjPop Kʼaʼm Ja-Noble Lord of the Reception House Mat

Tzʼikina Ja ubʼiʼ Nim Ja-Bird House is the name of the Great House of AjPop Kʼaʼm Ja-Second-in-Line to Receive Rule has a Great House

Nim Chʼokoj Kaweq, Jun Nim Ja-Great Scribe; Master of Ceremonies of the Kaweq has One Great House

Ajaw Aj Tojil, Jun Nim Ja-Lord Storm, Lord Thunder: Tojojila, Tojojil; has One Great House

Ajaw AjTojil kʼo Jun Nim Ja; Lord Storm, Lord Thunder One Great House

Ajaw Aj Qʼuqʼumatz, Jun Nim Ja-Lord Quetzalcoatl; the Plume Serpent has One Great House

Popol Winaq Chi Tʼuy, Jun Nim Ja-Council Book of the People of the Noble Red Mat has One Great House

Lolmet Kejnay, Jun Nim Ja-One Great House Overseer of Cotton Storage

Popol Winaq pa Jom Tzalatzʼ xkuxebʼa, Jun Nim Ja-Council House People of the Ballcourt; Noble Rulers of Council Mat; Chief of the Thin Walled Ballcourts has One Great House

Tepew Yaki, Jun Nima Ja-Mexican Majesty Yaki-Méxica Conqueror

These were the Nine Town; Citadels; Chinamit of the Kawiqibʼ

Thick with the children of women and thick with the children of men were the children that were born there in the Great Houses that were the children born to them; many were their engendered sons that were well ordered and named after the Nine Great Houses.

Here then is the ordering of the Nijaʼibʼabʼ with their Great Houses of the Nine ʼGreat Housesʼ People; ʼGreat House-Nijaʼibʼabʼ Winaqʼ.

We will first tell of the succession and sequence of the rulership that begins at the very root; the very beginning; the very origin of the sowing and dawning of  the Nijaʼibʼabʼ-the very root of the very beginning of the light of Kʼicheʼ Dawn; Kʼicheʼ Sun.

This is the origin of this lineage and generation-leʼ of Kʼicheʼ People who were engendered by this First Father:  Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ was the First Grandfather, Father.

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; Nabʼe Mamaxel, Qajawixel-First Grandfather, Father;

Kʼo Akul, KʼoʼAkutek, Uka Leʼ;

Kʼo Chajuj, Kʼo Tzibʼaja, Rox Le;

Bʼelejebʼ Kej; Ukaj Leʼ chik;

Kʼotuja; Roʼ Leʼ Ajaw

Bʼatzʼa; chi kʼut Uwaq Leʼ chik

Istayul;  chi kʼut Uwuqʼ Leʼ Ajaw;

Kʼotuja;  chiwi Uwajxaq Tas Ajawarem

Bʼelejebʼ Kej; Ubʼelej Tas

Kema, chuchax chik, Ulajuj Leʼ;

Ajaw Kʼotuja; Ujulajuj Leʼ

Don Christowal, chuchaʼxik, xajawarik chuwach Caxtilan Winaq.

Don Pedro de Robles, Ajaw Qʼalel wakamik.

Now all of the Noble Lords come from the lineage of the War Captains and Magistrates Qʼalel Ajaw whose descendants were also Judges shall be named here.

And next we shall name the names of each name of the names of the rulers of the Great House; these are their names named here:

Ajaw Qʼalel, Unabʼe Ajaw chuwach Nijaʼibʼabʼ, Jun Nim Ja.

Ajaw AjTzik Winaq, Jun Nim Ja

Ajaw Qʼalel Qʼamja, Jun Nim Ja

Nima Qʼamja, Jun Nim Ja

Uchuch Qʼamja, Jun Nim Ja

Nima Qʼamja, Jun Nim Ja

Nim Chokoj Nijaʼibʼ, Jun Nima Ja

Ajaw Awilix, Jun Nima Ja

Yakolatam, Jun Nima Ja

body:
Are kʼut Nim Ja ri chuwach Nijaʼibʼabʼ

These then are the Great House of the Great House People: Nijaʼibʼabʼ

And now these are the names of the Nine Citadel of the Nijaʼibʼabʼ as it is said. Are ubʼinam wi Bʼelejebʼ chinamit chi Nijaʼibʼabʼ, chuchaʼxik.

And many more were the lineages of the Lords, many were the towns of each of the Lords; we named the names of those that are named here, there are more names to name.

This is the naming of the Lord Kʼicheʼ Noble Lords, this is the naming of the names of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ of the Lord Kʼicheʼ lineage of Majukʼutaj and Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ.

Waʼ Mam, Qajaw; Here is the Grandfather, the Father:

Majukʼutaj, Nabʼe Winaq-the First Man

Kʼo Ajaw, ubʼiʼ Uka Leʼ Ajaw; Noble Lord is the name of the Second Generation Lord

Qʼaqʼlakan;

Kʼo Kosom;

Kʼo Najkun;

Wuqubʼ Aj,

Kʼo Kamel,

Kʼo Yobʼakojʼ;

Winaq Bʼam; Creators of Beauty, Beautifiers

Are kʼut AjAwabʼ ri chuwach Ajaw Kʼicheʼ; are uleʼel, utasel puch.

These are the names of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ and their generations of Noble Lords and their rank.

These are the name of the Lords who stood before the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ. These are their generations and their ranks. And these are the names of the Noble Lords here in the Great Houses. There were only Four Great Houses.

The Noblemen of the Lords-AjTzik Winaq Ajaw ubʼi Nabʼe Ajaw-is the name of the First Lord, he had One Great House: Jun Nima Jaa.

Lolmet Ajaw ukabʼ Ajaw, Jun Nima Jaa-The Overseer of the Cotton Plantations of the Lords who was the Second Noble Lord, he had One Great House.

Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw, Jun Nima Jaa-Great Lord Master of Ceremonies was the Third Noble Lord and he had One Great House.

Jaqawitz was the Fourth Lord with a Great House-Jaqawitz kʼut ukaj Ajaw, Jun Nima Ja,

There were Four Great House before the Lord Kʼicheʼ Lineage-Chi Kajibʼ kʼut Nim Ja chuwach Ajaw Kʼicheʼ.

These are the Three Great Masters of Ritual Drama; Ritual Recitation; Ritual Performance who were honored as Fathers of all the Kʼicheʼ Lords:

Are kʼu ri e Oxibʼ chi Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw!

They gathered together as just one the Three Great Masters of Ceremonies-Nim Chʼokojibʼ; these were those known as the Mother-Fathers of the Word, the Scribes; the Orators, the Storytellers, Writers, Painters, Illustrators-xa jun chikikuch wi kibʼ e Oxibʼ chik Chʼokojibʼ; these three Masters of Ceremony; Nim Chʼokojibʼ were the three Noble Lords who were the Masters of the Ancient Word and Masters of the Performance of the Ancient Word: Ojer Tzij.

They were hereditary. They were Mothers of the Word, Fathers of the Word-e Uchuch Tzij, eʼ Uqajaw Tzij. Great was their essence; great was the nature of their knowing.

These were the three Chʼokojibʼ- Oxibʼ Chʼokojibʼ and they were those who wrote the Popol Wuj these are their names, the names of the rank and position:

Great Scribal Lord of the Kaweq People-Nim Chʼokoj chuwach Kaweqibʼ

Great Scribal Lord of the Nijaʼibʼ the Great House People was the Second in line of the Noble Lords of the Nim Chʼokoj then-Nim Chʼokoj chuwach Nijaʼibʼ, Kabʼ Nim Chʼokoj kʼu ri.

Great Scribal Lord of the Lord Kʼicheʼ Lineage was the Third Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw Lineage of Scribal Masters of Ceremony of Kʼicheʼ Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word-Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw chuwach Ajaw Kʼicheʼ, Rox Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw; Uchuch-qajaw Ojer Tzij.

Chi Oxibʼ kʼut ri Chʼokojibʼ-Three Masters of the Ritual Performances of the Spoken Word; Masters of Ritual Recitation of the Ancient Word, Ancestral Story; Ojer Tzij also known as the Mother-Fathers of  the Word, each in their own lineage.

Truly, this is just the essence of the Kʼicheʼ. There no longer is a place to see it; no longer is there an instrument to enliven ones imagination of the Ancient Word known as  Ilobʼal re-for no longer is there a place to see the Pictorial History-Ilobʼal re that tells this ancestral story that once seen to be contemplated on a  Painted Manta-Ilbʼal re-Painted Lienzo upon which to see the words and ways of the Divine Ancestors and Kabʼawil is no more; for there no longer is a ʼplaceʼ to see what is written here as the spoken word. There was the First One; there was the Ancestral Book of the Noble Lords; but it is now lost and gone.
